We want the UK to follow suit with its own equivalent law.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Give police stronger powers to tackle motorcycle theft & increase penalties We want the Government to give the police more powers to tackle this without fearing any consequences.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Add Assault of a Roadworker to the Crime and Policing Bill The Crime and Policing Bill, includes a specific new offence of assaulting retail workers. Given the increasing levels of abuse, verbal and physical, towards road workers and we think they should be added to the legislation.
label: Home Office

text: Legislate for the statutory regulation of 'Counsellor' and 'Psychotherapist' Legislate to make ‘Counsellor’ and ‘Psychotherapist’ protected titles regulated by the HCPC. The Government should also review how this could include influencers and life coaches offering mental health services, ensuring all are subject to mandatory fitness-to-practise oversight.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review the police response to assaults on mental health nurses We want more protection for mental health nurses in cases of assault. Review the official action taken after an assault, to ensure that the assault and abuse of mental health nurses is taken seriously. Review how Operation Cavell has been applied to mental health nurses.
label: Home Office

text: Don't send troops to Ukraine to support peacekeeping Reports suggest that the UK may consider sending troops to Ukraine to support peacekeeping. We think doing this would risk escalation.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Ban 20mph speed limits with limited exceptions We believe anti car sentiment has become rife and 20mph speed limits are becoming commonplace in many towns and villages which just slows traffic and causes more congestion. There should be a national policy so 20mph limits are only used as the exception, e.g outside schools.
label: Department for Transport

text: Abolish the Working Group on Anti-Muslim Hatred/Islamophobia Definition We think the Working Group risks giving special status to one group, and we are concerned that a definition could limit free speech and silence concerns. Current laws protect everyone equally. We believe the process is secretive and undermines democracy.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Ban trades unions from donating money to political parties Introduce legislation to prohibit trades unions from donating funds to political parties, directly or indirectly. Unions represent members with a wide range of political views, yet their collective funds are often used to support a single political party.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Petition for Parent/Child Parking Badges for children up to age 13 I call on the Government to introduce a parent/child parking badge for parents or guardians with children up to age 13.
label: Department for Transport

text: Revoke the BBC Royal Charter, abolish the TV Licence Fee & privatise the BBC Abolish the mandatory TV licence fee and revoke the BBC’s Royal Charter. Legislate to transition the BBC into a private corporation, as they did with BBC Studio's. We believe the BBC should compete independently in the media market without state funding & Royal Charter rights, akin to BBC Studios.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Pause and review the use of EdTech in schools and early years settings Pause all pupil-facing 1:1 device and EdTech use in schools and early years settings—except for children with specific technology needs—unless and until reputable, independent assessments confirm both net educational benefit and no unacceptable safeguarding, health or wellbeing risks for children.
label: Department for Education

text: Extend the NHS Learning Support Fund to fully include pharmacy students Pharmacy students complete mandatory NHS placements and can face high travel and living costs but are excluded from many aspects of the NHS Learning Support Fund. We ask the Government to extend the NHS Learning Fund to fully include MPharm students to ensure fairness & encourage entry into the NHS.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reform UK Bail Law: Require Passport Surrender for Serious Criminal Charges Make passport surrender an automatic bail condition to protect victims’ families, uphold justice and restore confidence in the courts. Prevent criminals absconding while on bail for serious crimes. Currently making this a bail condition is at the discretion of the judge.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Legislate to protect ILR applicants from retrospective changes Keep the 5-year ILR route for people already in the UK and do not apply new settlement rules retrospectively. Future changes should apply only to new arrivals. We support waiting up to 10 years for access to public funds if the 5-year ILR pathway is protected.
label: Home Office

text: Nationalise the UK water industry I would like to see the government make plans to gradually nationalise the UK water industry.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Increase funding for transgender healthcare to reduce waiting times & train GPs Increase funding to help reduce transgender healthcare waiting times to 18 weeks. Fund training for GPs in identifying and diagnosing gender dysphoria, prescribing hormone replacement therapy and monitoring bloodwork.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Abolish early release for sex offenders and murderers I am a survivor of serious sexual abuse as a child and was raped as an adult. I would like the Government to change the law where anyone sentenced for rape or murder should not be eligible for early release on licence.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Make Carbohydrate content mandatory on restaurant and pub menus. Require all restaurants, café's and pubs with 250+ employees to clearly display carbohydrate information on menus, alongside calories and Allergens.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Make it a criminal offence if tenants don't pay rent Tenants who refuse to pay rent should be made to face criminal charges similar to theft.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Make admissions to children's indoor play centres zero-rated for VAT We want the Government to permanently zero rate VAT from admissions to children's indoor play centres to make active play more affordable, improve access for families and support children's health, well-being and development.
label: HM Treasury

text: Fund a medical cannabis trial for children left without NHS access since 2018 When medical cannabis was rescheduled in 2018 to allow specialist prescribing, many patients were left behind without NHS access. Families call them the “Forgotten Children of 2018”. Many rely on this treatment to control life-threatening conditions but must pay privately or go without.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Add Crohn’s & Colitis to the NHS prescription exemption list Add Crohn’s Disease and Ulcerative Colitis (IBD) to the Medical Exemption Certificate list in England so people with lifelong inflammatory bowel disease can receive free NHS prescriptions for essential ongoing medication.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text:
Require social housing providers to allow XL bullies with exemption certificate We think local authorities should not be allowed to exclude XL bully owners with a certificate of exemption from Social Housing.
We think they should be required to remove No XL bullies clauses from Allocation policies
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Add a tick box for "Cornish" in the 2031 census for national identity question  To add a "Cornish" tick box to the 2031 census for the question on national identity. Instead of Cornish people being forced to write it in the "Other" category.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Fund routine screening for bacterial vaginosis (BV) during pregnancy. BV has been associated with increased risks of pregnancy complications, including preterm birth. earlier identification and treatment of BV may help reduce avoidable pregnancy loss and improve outcomes for mothers and babies.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Allow mortgage interest to be deducted when calculating taxable rental income. Allow mortgage interest to be treated as a deductible business expense when calculating taxable rental income, in line with standard UK business taxation principles and generally accepted accounting practice, helping support stable rental supply and avoid upward pressure on rents.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Mandate independently-monitored CCTV in all dairy farms and slaughterhouses We demand the Government mandate independently-monitored CCTV in all UK dairy farms and slaughterhouses.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Specify China under Enhanced Tier of the Foreign Influence Registration Scheme We urge the Government to specify China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region under the Enhanced Tier of the Foreign Influence Registration Scheme. We believe this could help to protect British democracy.
label: Home Office

text: Create an independent early years funding review We ask Government to establish an Independent Early Years Funding Review Body. Similar to the School Teachers’ Review Body, it could take evidence from providers, parents and experts and recommend fair funding rates based on actual costs, not political decisions, for the Government to respond to.
label: Department for Education

text: Abolish the basic State Pension, increase the new State Pension and pay to all. We think the government should abolish the 'basic State Pension', put all our elderly onto the new State Pension, and increase the new State Pension to a good percentage of average earnings.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Mandate that free roaming pet cats must be neutered Change the law around free roaming pet cats so that all free roaming pet cats must be neutered. I also think rescue centres should be given powers to charge pet owners the vet bills that come with un-neutered cats fighting and mating.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Secure the release and return of British nationals arbitrarily detained in India There are British nationals being arbitrarily detained without conviction in Indian jails for many years, with many concerns about their treatment. We believe the UK Government must secure the release of all British nationals that are arbitrarily detained & return them to the UK.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Fund more Physician Associates roles in the NHS We want the Government to urgently fund more Physician Associate (PA) roles in the NHS. We believe that without immediate action, trained PAs will remain jobless, and the profession will be at risk.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: End concurrent sentencing for heinous crimes We think concurrent sentences is not justice. We urge lawmakers to end concurrent sentencing and require consecutive sentences for violent offences. Stand with us—sign this petition for true justice.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban prisoner segregation for periods of more than 15 days Ban the use of segregation in prisons for continuous periods longer than 15 days.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Require candidates for MP to be registered to vote and residents of the UK  Currently, a candidate for MP is not required to be registered to vote or be resident in the UK. We ask the Government to require candidates for MP be registered to vote and residents of the UK.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Extend the kinship care allowance pilot to all local authorities Support all local authorities around kinship care, not just 10 pilot local authorities. Kinship carers have struggled for way too long and do it for love, only love doesn’t pay the bills or the extra cost of bringing up a child. How can you Choose 10 local authorities around? Choose them all!
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Create a National Disability Hate Strategy for the UK Develop and fund a National Disability Hate Strategy, co-produced with Disabled People’s Organisations, to tackle disability hate crime, online abuse, discrimination, public stigma and improve awareness of visible and hidden disabilities.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Review traditional and social media regulation  Review media regulation, including social media, to consider the introduction of stricter regulations to ensure truthful reporting, accountability and integrity across all platforms, including newspapers, TV and online.  The review should also look at how many outlets can be owned by one person.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Fund access to tirzepatide on the NHS to help people with PCOS We urge the Government to fund access to tirzepatide on NHS for patients suffering from Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Hold a national referendum on introducing Digital ID We believe Government plans for Digital ID represent the most radical change in our governance since universal suffrage. We want the  Government to put this plan to the people via a referendum before proceeding with what we feel is a monumental shift in how we are governed.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Decide on any change to the commission payable on the sale of a Park Home We feel that the Government has delayed making a decision, following a report commissioned by them, for 30 months on any changes to the commission that has to be paid to a Park Owner on the sale of a Park Home. We don't believe there is reason for this continuing delay.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Include British Citizens Studying Medicine Abroad in NHS Training Prioritisation The Government should work to ensure the inclusion of British citizens who studied medicine abroad in NHS specialty training prioritisation, regardless of graduation date, so they are not treated the same as overseas applicants without UK ties.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Urgently review NHS approach to shared care agreements for ADHD Urgently review the current approach to shared care agreements (SCAs) in England. We think a review could help ensure all SCAs are reviewed individually and fairly and not refused. We want better integration of privately diagnosed patients into NHS pathways, and continuity of care.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Create a Ukrainian ILR route & ensure time on Ukraine visa schemes count to ILR Create a dedicated route to ILR for Ukrainian refugees and ensure that their time on Ukrainian visa schemes (Homes for Ukraine, Family and Extension) count towards obtaining Indefinite Leave to Remain.
label: Home Office

text: Reassess the classification of Cannabis and decriminalize it. We believe the Government should re-evaulate Cannabis' classification as a class B drug. We think that by legalising the drug in a controlled way across the country the tax could assist in paying off the country's debt and help repair the ongoing economic difficulties the UK faces.
label: Home Office

text: Require local authorities to provide 90 minutes of free parking in town centres Introduce a law which requires all local authorities in England to provide a minimum of 90 minutes of free parking in town and city centres to help support economic growth and high street businesses.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Increase funding for co-operatives in the UK International Development Budget In the UN Year of Co-operation, we think the UK Government should commit to raising the importance of co-operatives with world leaders and show leadership by doubling the proportion of funding allocated to co-operative development as part of the UK's International Development budget.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Stop DWP additional spouse payments in overseas-registered polygamous marriages From April 2026, the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) permits people in the UK in specific, legally recognized, overseas-registered polygamous marriages to receive additional benefit payments, with rates for "additional spouses" increasing to £125.25 per week.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Remove all sanctions on Syria After over a decade of conflict, we believe the fall of the Assad regime has brought new hope for Syria. The Syrian people need the world’s support to heal and recover— we consider that lifting sanctions is a critical first step toward a brighter future.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Commit to not deploying British Troops to Ukraine Following recent speculation, we don't want the Government deploying British troops to Ukraine, even as part of a potential multinational force following a ceasefire or peace deal.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Higher minimum penalties for death by dangerous driving  I want people who have committed death by dangerous driving due to drugs to permanently have their licence removed and never have chance to reapply, and longer sentences for death by dangerous driving with a minimum of 20 years without parole.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Publish updated statistics on Armed Forces Veteran suicides annually We ask the Government to publish annual suicide data for armed forces veterans. We think this could help ensure transparency, improve mental health support, and  prevent further loss of life by understanding the true scale of the issue.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Ban wind farm onshore asset development on green belt land We want the Government to ban wind farm onshore asset development on green belt land. We don't think local authorities are enforcing the National Planning Policy Framework to protect the greenbelt from inappropriate development when brown belt land is available and offers regeneration opportunities.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Stop mileage tax on electric & plug-in hybrid cars & reduce public charging VAT To remove the planned mileage tax on electric and plugin-hybrid cars, and to equalise VAT on public charging to 5% to support adoption.
label: HM Treasury

text: Reform Carer’s Allowance rules so carers can earn more without losing support Many unpaid carers balance demanding caring responsibilities with the need to remain financially secure. We believe the current limit allowable for carers to earn is set way too low. It makes it difficult for carers to work, take on a second job, or rent out property to supplement their income.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Suspend Climate Change Act targets & undertake a full national impact assessment We call on the Government to temporarily suspend the legal duties to meet the UK's statutory carbon budgets and 2050 Net Zero target under the Climate Change Act 2008 until Parliament has considered an independent national assessment of their full costs and impacts.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: The North Of England A1 Safety Guarantee: Action Immediate Protection. Commit to continuous dualling of the A1 through the north of England to the Scottish Border. Implement immediate, interim safety upgrades —including junction visibility & hazard warnings—to prevent fatal collisions & stop dangerous traffic displacement through local rural villages.
label: Department for Transport

text: Ban technology that enables pharmacies to auto renominate EPS patients in bulk We want the government to explicitly ban NHS system suppliers, by law, from providing any technology that may enable pharmacies to switch patient EPS nominations without informed and current consent, or in bulk using automation, and make it illegal for pharmacies to engage in this practice.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reduce national speed limits on single carriageways Reduce the national speed limit on single carriageways usually found in rural areas from 60mph to 30mph.
label: Department for Transport

text: Grant Rivers and Rias in England Legal Personhood Recognise Rivers & Rias (Drowned River Valleys) in England as living entities with rights to 'their' own voice by creating a system to appoint Lead Legal Guardians & Guardian Groups for each River & Ria in England to enforce 'their' rights.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Do not reduce the Right to Buy discount Stop the reduction of the Right to Buy discount. The Government have said the maximum discount will be reduced to £16,000–£38,000 depending on the tenant's location. We think this is unfair because some people's only way only to get on the housing ladder is via Right to Buy.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Issue new guidance on teachers’ early retirement rights The state pension age will change to 67 in 2028 and therefore minimum early retirement age will change to 57. Teachers with final salary pensions who started teaching before the pension changed to career average have a given early retirement age of 55 rather than this being tied to state pension age
label: Department for Education

text: Fund NHS COVID boosters for Clinically Vulnerable people – keep covid boosters 'Protect the NHS' and 'Save Lives' by continuing to fund NHS COVID boosters for Clinically Vulnerable people, including most previously shielded as CEV, rather than limiting them to over-75s, care home residents and those with severely weakened immune systems.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text:
Distinguish pets from other types of property in civil and family proceedings We want legislation to: 
1. Make a pet's welfare the paramount consideration when Courts resolve disputes over their ownership and possession. 
2. Recognise a pet's true value as being the value to its owner, not just its open market price. 
3. Require Court cases regarding pets to be expedited.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Make it Law for Water Companies to Object When Sewage Systems Are Over Capacity We urge the Government to legally require water companies to object to planning developments once the sewage system is over-capacity. This could stop new developments proceeding without confirmed infrastructure upgrades.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Amend Equality Act to define the terms woman and man not based on biological sex We believe trans women are women and therefore deserve the same rights as cis-gendered women, and that trans men are men and therefore deserve the same rights as cis-gendered men. We think the rights of human beings are being stripped away by defining people based on biological sex.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Create a fast-track system for benefit claims for cancer patients We believe the benefits application system for cancer patients is not fit for purpose. We think it is over-complicated, upsetting, and adds high levels of stress. We would like the Government to create a fast-track system for all of those cancer patients who are seeking benefits.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Adjust the £10 DWP Christmas Bonus introduced in 1972 to reflect inflation Adjust the Christmas Bonus given to benefit claimants, from £10 - when it was introduced in 1972 - to reflect inflation (approx £180 in 2025). Make the uplift only available for British citizens, who have been claiming benefits for a minimum of 6 months.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: End the ban of care workers bringing dependants to the UK End the ban on care workers being able to bring their dependants to the UK. Allow them to sponsor spouses, children, or other dependants, even if their sponsorship is issued after 11 March 2024.
label: Home Office

text:
Write off Armed Forces Pension overpayments. Veterans are being told that they have to pay thousands back to the MoD after a disastrous pension error occurred, estimated to be around £5.1 million. 
I’m calling for the MoD to have the pension overpayments written off, as the Veterans were not at fault for the incorrect calculations.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Government to advise monarch to refuse/cancel state visits with hostile powers The Government should advise the Monarch against facilitating a ceremonial head of state visit where a foreign state is engaged in hostile activity - whether economic, diplomatic, military or otherwise - that is directly contrary to UK interests and/or the rule of international law.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Recognise Palestine as a State and seek immediate ceasefire in Gaza  We believe it is imperative the UK Government acknowledges the rights of all Palestinian people and seeks to implement an immediate ceasefire in Gaza. Their suffering must end; they deserve basic human rights. Palestinians should live without fear and make decisions about their future.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Review family court system to help prevent post-separation abuse We want the government to review the family court system to help prevent post-separation abuse. This should look at training on coercive control, protections for abuse survivors, and strict limits on use of “parental alienation” claims that we feel can silence legitimate safeguarding concerns.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Define Anti-Palestinian Racism (APR) & launch an inquiry into APR We urge the Government to adopt a definition of Anti-Palestinian Racism (APR) that is based on the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (ICERD), & to launch an inquiry into APR and its impacts upon politics, the media, and disinformation & dehumanisation.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Reverse decision to pause decisions on asylum applications from Syrians We think the decision is inhumane and may be at odds with our requirements under international law — asylum is a human right and an international obligation as recognised in the 1951 Geneva Convention on the protection of refugees. There also wasn't a vote in Parliament on this decision.
label: Home Office

text: Ban all e-bikes & electric scooters in public Fully ban e-bikes and electric scooters in public, in order to prevent accidents and stop people from using them to commit crimes.
label: Department for Transport

text: Fund & mandate early intervention plans for minors who deliberately harm animals I ask for the Government to fund and mandate early intervention plans, which include assessments and education, for minors who deliberately harm animals in order to recognise cruelty as behaviour that requires action, support and prevention.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Repeal the Hong Kong Economic Trade Office Act 1996 Pass legislation to close the Hong Kong Economic Trade Office in light of the lack of autonomy Hong Kong now has from Beijing, by introducing legislation to repeal the Hong Kong Economic Trade Office Act 1996 through, for example, a Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office (Revocation) Act 2026.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Retain 5 Year ILR & Citizenship Route, Delay Public Funds Access Until Year 10 Retain the 5-year path to ILR and British citizenship for Skilled Worker migrants, but extend the no recourse to public funds period to 10 years. We believe this would balance and uphold the UK’s promise to migrants to make it their home via 5-year ILR path while easing pressure on public resources.
label: Home Office

text: Introduce presumed liability for civil cases from road traffic collisions Introduce presumed liability for civil cases relating to certain road collisions, to shift the burden of proof. It would mean when vulnerable road users, e.g cyclists & pedestrians, claim against a more powerful road user (a driver), the driver would be presumed liable unless they prove otherwise.
label: Department for Transport

text: Require Independent Scrutiny Before Passing any Education Laws Affecting Rights We ask Parliament to require no education legislation affecting parental rights, religious freedom, or home education be enacted without an external independent review—appointed by cross-party agreement, based on sound evidence and consultation with affected minority communities.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Allocate annual funding to accelerate breakthroughs in MND research  We want the Government to allocate annual regular funding for the purpose of research, clinical trials, all stages of trials, in order to prolong the lives of MND patients in a meaningful way. We want innovative research to be prioritised. MND is life limiting still.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Scrap the planned 2029–2039 Asylum Support and Accommodation programme Cancel the Home Office Asylum Support and Accommodation Programme procurement (2029-2039). Shift focus from long-term housing to rapid enforcement. We want to protect taxpayers from multi-billion corporate contracts, ease pressure on local public services & enforce strict contractor accountability.
label: Home Office

text: Fund Breast Cancer Screening from Age 40 & Alternative Screening Options We urge the Government to fund breast cancer screening at 40+, as thousands under 50 are diagnosed yearly. Early screening can save lives and lessen the need for aggressive treatments. Invest in alternative screening, including options for dense breast tissue, to help ensure no one is overlooked.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require a trained FLO to be assigned to families bereaved by suicide We would like Jason's Law to be introduced which would Require all police forces to assign trained Family Liaison Officers to every family bereaved by suicide, which could help ensure consistent support, communication, and guidance during investigations, inquests, and the immediate aftermath.
label: Home Office

text: Introduce new penalties for repeated breaches of SEND law We call on the UK Government to introduce enforceable penalties where local authorities, schools, academy trusts and responsible bodies repeatedly breach their legal duties to children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).
label: Department for Education

text: Remove people on the terror watch list from the UK In 2020, the Home Office said there were over 40,000 people where MI5 judged there was some risk of them re-engaging in terrorist activity. We think people on this list who are in the UK should be deported, to keep people in the UK safe.
label: Home Office

text: Introduce a Statutory Levy on Bookmakers to Fund Greyhound Welfare We call on the UK Government to introduce a statutory levy on bookmakers to secure reliable funding for greyhound welfare.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require all meat to be labelled to indicate the method of slaughter, as such We want the Government to create a law requiring all meat to have a label, such as a simple ‘RS’ (Religiously Slaughtered.) or 'NRS' (Not religiously slaughtered), that states whether it has been religiously slaughtered or not.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text:
We call for harsher sentencing for causing death by careless driving. • We want the maximum sentence raised from 5 to 20 years.
• We want driving licences to be suspended pending investigation outcome, and only reinstated if there are no charges brought.
• We want consecutive sentences where there are multiple fatalities.
• We want a review of judicial guidelines.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Increase funding for Early years providers. Increase funding for early years settings. We believe early childcare is fundamental to all children and giving them the best start. Save our nurseries and Preschools. We believe early years education is crucial to set the foundations.
label: Department for Education

text: Ban restrictions on overnight parking for motorhomes and campervans Recent years have seen local authorities increase restrictions on overnight parking, which we think massively decreases the appeal of taking to the roads and staying off-grid. We think this ignores the impact of visitors on the local economy and the freedom of individuals.
label: Department for Transport

text: Stop giving homework to primary and secondary school students I think that the government should ban all homework for children aged 4-16. This is because children go to school for an average of 6.5 hours a day and then get home and have to do more work, this being homework.
label: Department for Education

text: Introduce Full Statutory Regulation of the Funeral Industry by Spring 2027 Legislation needs to be introduced urgently to ensure the prevention of any Funeral Director malpractice including the hoarding of the deceased, degrading storage of the deceased including ashes and preventing the lawful burial of the deceased.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Introduce a Long-Term Visit Visa for Parents of British Citizens and ILR Holders We urge the UK Government to create a long-term visit visa for parents of British citizens & ILR holders. This visa would allow extended stays beyond the current six-month limit, with applicants providing proof of private health insurance or paying an NHS surcharge to mitigate public health costs.
label: Home Office

text: Mandate anti-racism training for all staff in nurseries & primary schools Mandate all nursery and primary school staff in England to complete accredited anti-racism training, including how to recognise, address, and prevent racism in early years and primary school settings.
label: Department for Education

text: Expel all US military personnel and close all US military bases in the UK We call on the UK Government to cancel all UK-US agreements that permit US personnel and bases to operate in the UK, in order to prevent the UK from being used as a base for any unilateral military action.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Allow up to 10 days authorised school leave per year without fines Introduce national school attendance rules to allow parents to take children out of school for up to 10 days per year for family leave where attendance is otherwise good, including flexibility for families with children with SEND, without fines or prosecution.
label: Department for Education

text: Reduce the sound of fireworks to under 80 decibels for humans and animals I think fireworks are being used more frequently throughout the year and are becoming a nuisance. I want the government to mandate that fireworks should be reduced to below 80 decibels so they are safer for humans and animals.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Ban the use of generative 'AI' in all creative sectors Ban any creative product (books, artwork, television, cinema, music, etcetera) from being published if it was created using generative 'AI' at any step in the creative process.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Change the oath of military and the police Because we feel the present oath of allegiance is out of date and is not fit for purpose in protecting our democracy. Many people in Britain are dissatisfied with our democracy and so we believe we need this change of oath to restore confidence in our democracy again.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Increase funding for IVF & fertility treatments to increase access. We believe that we are in a fertility crisis. We worry that many people may be being denied access to medical treatment for infertility due to inconsistent restrictions and criteria that we believe are unfair. We feel this level of inequality and inequity needs to be urgently addressed.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Make assaulting a security worker a standalone offence Security workers play a vital role in maintaining public safety, but can face violence and abuse while performing their duties. Despite their critical role in protecting businesses, venues, and the public, security workers lack the legal protections afforded to emergency workers and shop workers.
label: Home Office

text: Offer healthcare workers on tier2 visa ILR after 2 years instead of 5 years Healthcare workers are meant to have lived in the UK for at least 5 years before they can apply for ILR. With the work they do and the demand for their skills world wide, they deserve to get residency status much quicker. Most healthcare workers are working under extreme pressure in the UK.
label: Home Office

text: Stop social media posts being shown with dogs that have cropped ears We call on the Government to make social media platforms ban future posts and remove existing posts that show dogs with cropped ears.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Introduce the death penalty for certain child sex offences Introduce legislation to reinstate capital punishment and make the death penalty the mandatory sentence for the most serious child sexual offences, with no lesser sentencing options.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Pause Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill for consultation with children I believe decisions about children should include children. I want the Government to ask the Children’s Commissioner to consult children on the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill, and pause the Bill until the consultation finishes, including on data privacy & protecting the home as a safe space.
label: Department for Education

text: Mandate monthly welfare updates and photos for owners of all seized dogs I am campaigning to mandate monthly welfare reports and photos for seized dogs I think this is essential to ensure accountability, uphold humane standards of care, and enable timely intervention to prevent suffering.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Increase full-time Carer's Allowance to at least £800 per week We want the government to pay all full-time carers at least £800 per week. Carers should be valued within society and we think their worth should be reflected in the help and benefits they receive. Carers can receive £83.30 a week, however they must provide care for at least 35 hours a week.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Exempt all nurseries from Employer NI Contributions We believe that if costs incurred from the planned increase to employer National Insurance Contributions and National Minimum wage are not mitigated, nurseries will have to increase fees parents pay, reduce staffing (and thereby the number of places offered), or close due to no longer being viable.
label: HM Treasury

text: Protect the Function of the Architect in UK Law Protect the function of architects under UK law, not only the title. Review legislation and procurement to ensure that work affecting building safety, design quality, and regulatory compliance must be carried out or overseen by appropriately qualified and regulated architects.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text:
legislation for accountability within NHS, Police, CPS and findings of Inquiries We ask the UK government to introduce legislation requiring enforceable measures for the NHS, police and CPS where serious failings or neglibence are identified.
This should include a statutory duty for organisations and individuals to act transparently and honestly during investigations
label: Cabinet Office

text: Stop driverless cars coming to UK Stop driverless cars from being introduced in the UK. We think they will threaten the jobs of over 300,000 private hire and London black cab drivers. We want the Government to block the rollout of autonomous taxis and protect drivers’ livelihoods.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review implementation of Public Service Pensions and Judicial Offices Act 2022 Launch a review into the implementation of the Public Service Pensions and Judicial Offices Act 2022 to investigate Government compliance with the requirements of the Act. We believe the Government has not provided the resources required to deliver what was required by the PSPJOA2022.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Ensure that student nurses are paid for their placement hours We want the government to ensure that student nurses are paid for their placement hours. With the rise in living cost, even with the training grant and maintenance loans, we feel it is increasingly hard for student nurses to live.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Stop PIP Cuts: Protect Support for Disabled People We call on the UK government to reverse the changes to Personal Independence Payments (PIP). We think these cuts unfairly target disabled people who rely on PIP for essential support. We would like fair and compassionate welfare policies that protect, not punish, the most vulnerable in society.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Allow UK Hospitality Businesses to Reclaim 10% Food Costs Against quarterly VAT We call on Government to allow hospitality businesses to reclaim 10% of their food costs against their quarterly VAT bill. We believe this would help businesses remain viable, protect jobs & sustain local communities, and that this could support thousands of independent businesses.
label: HM Treasury

text: Reduce the maximum decibel limit on fireworks from 120 to 90 We think the current noise limits were likely created based upon neurotypical healthy adults. The limit should take into account neurodiverse people and animals that have higher sensitivity to noise.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund a National NHS Railcard for Healthcare Staff Fund a National NHS Railcard to give healthcare staff discounted rail travel. This card could be similar to existing railcards for young people, veterans and seniors. We think this would ease commuting costs, support retention, and encourage public transport use.
label: Department for Transport

text: Require restaurants to offer a non-religiously slaughtered meat option Some food establishments only offer meat that has been religiously slaughtered. I believe this could isolate some of the population who do not eat religiously slaughtered meat.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Set up an independent inquiry into the UK’s involvement in the war in Gaza We urge the Government to set up an independent inquiry into the UK’s involvement in the war in Gaza, including arms sales, military support, and political actions. We believe the public deserves transparency, and that a democratic country should be accountable for its role in conflicts.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Provide funding for body armour for frontline operational ambulance staff Provide funding for body armour for frontline operational staff who wish to be equipped with it for use at their discretion, in the same manner body worn cameras are sometimes deployed, and fund adequate training.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Abolish the deadline for the purchase of new petrol and diesel cars We believe that those purchasing new cars should be allowed to exercise complete freedom of choice in making their choice of vehicle.
label: Department for Transport

text: Allow Charities to continue to re-home adult dogs with historic injuries We ask Parliament to include an exemption in the Animal Welfare (Import of Dogs, Cats and Ferrets) Act 2025 allowing registered charities and responsible rescue organisations to continue to rehome adult, healthy dogs with historic injuries or mutilations to the UK.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require NHS to offer base line X-rays for children born with a limb difference Limb different children have unusual anatomy. Without a baseline X-ray on NHS records, some A&E doctors can’t tell what is an injury & what is the norm for that child. We want every limb different child to have a baseline X-ray at diagnosis, stored and easily accessible
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Honour maintenance loans and childcare grants for existing weekend students  To allow existing students to continue studying weekends with student finance loans and grants for the rest of their studies. The Government should allow us as students to continue our studies in weekends with funding as we signed up for it that way.
label: Department for Education

text: Legalise Cannabis Use and Sales for Adults over 18 The conversation around cannabis in the UK has changed dramatically, and one thing is crystal clear: it's not going away. Despite current prohibition, a vast illicit market thrives, operating without any regard for public safety. Dealers don't check ID, meaning under 18s have easy access.
label: Home Office

text: Statutory paid leave for parents whose child is undergoing cancer treatment I’d like the Government to provide statutory paid leave, in the same way as maternity and paternity leave, for parents whose child is diagnosed with cancer and need to assist them with their care.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Offer MenB vaccine to under 22s born before 2015 We want the Government to introduce a catch-up MenB vaccination programme for people under 22 born before 2015 who were not routinely offered the vaccine, ensuring equal protection against meningococcal B.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review care for sickle cell patients within the NHS We consider that there is systemic poor care and racial disparities in NHS healthcare for sickle cell patients, and that there needs to be a review into this.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Pass a law which bans the reselling of practical driving tests We urge the Government to pass a law which bans reselling practical driving tests and makes this practice illegal. We believe the lack of availability for booking a driving test in the UK is because people are openly booking and reselling practical tests.
label: Department for Transport

text: Launch a public inquiry into UK arms exports to Israel and suspend all licences We call on the Government to immediately establish a public, judge-led inquiry into British arms exports to Israel and to suspend licences during the investigation. Many are concerned that Israel has violated international law, and the inquiry should look at the role of UK components.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Stop the cancellation of Local Elections to help uphold democracy The Government must reinstate all cancelled local elections now.  Local communities need fair, timely elections, not political decisions made behind closed doors. We believe cancelling democratic votes without a national emergency is dangerous and undermines trust.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Set a maximum 6‑month diagnosis target for endometriosis With diagnosis of endometriosis taking on average 8-10 years, I am calling for a national 6‑month diagnosis target, supported by mandatory GP training, a clearer NHS process for assessment and referral, and increased investment in specialist services.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Do not house illegal migrants in private rentals, deport them immediately Don't house illegal migrants in private rental accommodation. Instead, I want the government to immediately return them to their home country or last safe country they travelled from. I think they've no right to enter via boats or other means without applying for and achieving a warranted visa.
label: Home Office

text: Instruct NHS England to revoke adoption of the IHRA definition of antisemitism In October, the government asked NHS England to adopt the IHRA definition of antisemitism, without public consultation. Serious concerns were raised by Doctors in Unite and over 23 other organisations. We think the definition has serious flaws threatening freedom of expression and political debate.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban the sale of helium balloons I'm calling for the sales on helium balloons to be banned. April 2024 we tragically lost our son Joshua on his 8th birthday, due to him unintentionally inhaling helium from his birthday balloon.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Regularly assess & consider the economic benefits of EU Customs Union membership We want the Government to commission independent bodies to regularly advise how joining the Customs Union could benefit Britain's economy. We want Parliament to regularly consider how that would advance Government's strategic goal of stimulating UK economic growth.
label: HM Treasury

text:
Ban the wearing of face-coverings during marches and protests We think citizens are increasingly concerned about safety, identity, and transparency and we think they are alarmed by the potential risks or intentions posed by participants wearing face-coverings during protest marches.
 
We want the government to ban face-coverings during marches and protests.
label: Home Office

text: Act on UN Commission findings of Genocide of Palestinian Children The UN Commission of Inquiry found Israel is committing genocide against Palestinian children. We urge the UK Government to formally recognise these findings and act on its legal obligations under international law.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Make mental health support standard for parents of seriously ill children Parents of seriously ill children should be offered proactive mental health support from diagnosis, through treatment, and in grief. Unlike perinatal parents, they get no dedicated help. We want this support made a standard part of every child’s care.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review 5-year residency limit for Moldovans to exchange their driving licences Review the 5-year residency limit for Moldovan citizens in the UK to exchange their licences and consider the introduction of a fair transition period so no one is left out, to ensure equal rights and no division in the community.
label: Department for Transport

text: Exempt all military families from school fines — let them be with family. We call on the government to exempt military families from school attendance fines. Military parents often live away from home and are deployed for weeks or months at a time. These families make extraordinary sacrifices. They deserve flexibility and compassion when spending precious time together.
label: Department for Education

text: Review how to turn the MHRA into a fully transparent, patient first regulator We believe the MHRA should be independently reviewed. This should cover approval and surveillance processes, funding & accountability. It should consider how to ensure the transparency of decisions, prioritisation of patient safety, and how to ensure there aren’t conflict of interests.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require every primary school to have a published plan for outdoor free play We call on the Government to require every primary school in England to publish a plan for outdoor free play at breaktimes and lunchtime, and for the Department for Education to produce statutory guidance defining what quality provision looks like, with Ofsted required to inspect against it.
label: Department for Education

text: Introduce Romanian into the GCSE Curriculum Require the Government to approve Romanian as a GCSE subject, and help fund exam development and the training of  teachers, to allow students to study and sit Romanian GCSE alongside other modern foreign languages.
label: Department for Education

text: Amend the 28-day rule for the Carer’s Allowance for carers giving hospital care Amend the Carer’s Allowance rules so unpaid carers continue to be paid their allowance after 28 days if they are still providing essential care in the hospital and require NHS trusts to confirm in writing when they cannot meet a patient’s needs and when an unpaid carer must stay and provide care.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Cap Academy Trust CEO Pay and Protect School Funding for Children Conduct a value-for-money review of academy trusts; give Local Authorities greater powers to intervene where leadership and standards fail; introduce a CEO pay cap aligned with headteacher pay, capped at 2% above the highest-paid head; and require independent oversight of contracts.
label: Department for Education

text:
Make a dog injuring or killing a cat a specific offence
 Make it an offence for a dog to kill or seriously injure a cat, whether in public or on private property. Introduce penalties for negligent dog owners and compensation for cat owners that reflects the emotional impact & distress caused plus vet bills or cremation costs.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: ​Keep 5-year Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) for those already granted asylum. ​Exempt all individuals already granted asylum or humanitarian protection from any proposed changes to increase the ILR qualifying period. Maintain the 5-year route to settlement for these groups to ensure fairness, aid integration, and honor the established commitment.
label: Home Office

text: We call for a referendum before extending voting rights to 16 & 17-year-olds We call on the government to hold a national referendum before extending voting rights to 16 and 17-year-olds in general elections.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: The Government must get the East West Rail Line passenger service running ASAP The East West Rail Line was due to open last December for passenger services. It’s still not running. The Government needs to break the deadlock between Chiltern Railways and unions. There needs to be effective negotiation to resolve differences and find a solution. Services need to run urgently.
label: Department for Transport

text: Establish a single, powerful, independent statutory regulator for all news media The Government must create a single, independent statutory regulator covering print, broadcast, and digital news media. This regulator should have the legal power to enforce truth and factual reporting via a mandatory code of conduct for journalists and prohibit the reporting of opinion as fact.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Establish a bank holiday on the Monday after Remembrance Sunday We call on the Government to establish a Veterans & Community bank holiday on the Monday that falls after Remembrance Sunday.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text:
Penalties for Local Authorities if their EHCP decision is overturned at Tribunal Many parents appeal to the SEND Tribunal, where Local Authority decisions are, in 98% of cases, overturned. We think this process denies SEN children access to appropriate education and costs the taxpayer millions.
We think this is a common experience.
label: Department for Education

text: Deport people with dual nationality who are found guilty of raping children We think the Grooming Gangs scandal is possibly the biggest scandal in our country's history. It is time for a tough approach. We are calling for foreign born nationals with dual nationality who are found guilty of raping children to be deported.
label: Home Office

text: Allow radio operators to install antennas & masts without planning permission Reform planning laws to allow licensed amateur radio operators to install antennas and masts without planning permission, to support innovation, skills, and emergency communications.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Require a vote and consultation before implementing the new UK–EU Reset Deal Require a full vote in Parliament and public consultation before implementing the UK–EU Reset Deal signed in May 2025. We think the deal includes major policy shifts and must not proceed without democratic consent. We think doing so would undermine public trust in authority
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Repeal the 2000 and 2006 Terrorism Acts and review other legislation We urge the Government to repeal the Terrorism Acts of 2000 and 2006, and for it to commission a review into how other existing legislation could provide the necessary safeguards for society.
label: Home Office

text: Increase HMRC Mileage Allowance to 70p per mile The 45p per mile mileage allowance has been static for fifteen years. Since April 2011, prices in the UK have increased by around 49.2% according to the Bank of England. We want the allowance to increase to 70p a mile.
label: Department for Transport

text: Introduce stricter minimum penalties for acts of animal cruelty. We want the Government to introduce stricter penalties for animal cruelty. Current punishments can often just result in suspended sentences or fines. We think the government should introduce stricter minimum penalties, including prison sentences, to help deter abuse and ensure justice for victims.
label: Home Office

text: Fund a scheme for 20 Years’ service Medals for PCSOs. Some police officers get a 20 year service medal for their service to their force and community and I feel that PCSO’s should also get the recognition in the form of a 20 years’ service medal, for their commitment to our late queen, current King and the communities they serve in the United Kingdom.
label: Home Office

text: Fund free GCSE exams for all home-educated children We want the Government to fund free GCSE exams for all home-educated children. We believe that they should be free as parents already pay tax, and that decisions to not enrol in mainstream schools, as it can often be too much for many children, should not mean they are denied access to GCSE exams.
label: Department for Education

text: Grant free British citizenship to Europeans with settled status We urge the Government to grant Europeans who have settled status in the UK with British citizenship on request, without any cost in money.
label: Home Office

text: A2 motorcycle licences to upgrade to an A license automatically after 2 years To revert to the automatic update of an A2 license to a full A license after 2 years of riding.
label: Department for Transport

text: Stop building solar/wind farms until a cost-benefit analysis is made public Publish a thorough nationwide cost-benefit analysis of the construction of solar and wind farms, and make the subsequent report public. Analysis must include environmental, economic, social, and health costs, and include comparison of alternative energy e.g. nuclear.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text:
Review & Reform the Probation Service, apologise & enshrine Victims Code in law We call on the Government to
1. Formally apologise to the families of those killed by individuals under the supervision of the Probation Service.
2. Commission a review into the Probation Service.
3. Enshrine the Victims Code of Practice in law
4. Reform the Probation Service based on the review
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Reduce the home building targets to 200,000 houses per year. Lower national homebuilding targets to an achievable level for local councils, builders and infrastructure providers, rather than what we think are arbitrary numbers. We think changes in housing targets need to be in small, workable increments.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Reinstate Post 16 transport for disabled young adults Reinstate Post 16 transport for disabled young adults. Personal Transport Budgets do not work for all families.
label: Department for Transport

text: Fund more permanent NHS roles for newly qualified student nurses  We want the Government to guarantee employment for newly qualified student nurses by providing funding to ensure there are more permanent NHS roles, improved workforce planning, and that graduates can transition directly into secure employment to support patient care and NHS staffing.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Seek agreement with the EU to accept pet passports for UK-EU travel Seek to negotiate an agreement with the EU to allow UK residents who hold valid EU Pet Passports to use them for travel without needing an Animal Health Certificate (AHC). This would allow UK residents to travel with pets to the EU without repeated high fees and complex admin.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Legislate to enforce timely payment of workplace pensions We call on the Government to legislate for timely payment of workplace pensions, including a guarantee of the first payment to be paid within 31 days of someone retiring. This period must commence on the agreed date of retirement, including the payment of lump sums.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Apologise for the Balfour Declaration and fund the teaching of its legacy We ask the Government to issue a formal apology for the Balfour Declaration and Britain’s actions in Mandate-era Palestine, and to commit to funding educational initiatives that acknowledge this history. This should include public resources and curriculum support reflecting Britain’s role.
label: Department for Education

text:
Allow test-free A2 to A motorcycle licence upgrades after two years We should allow automatic A2 to full A licence upgrades for retaining an A2 licence for 2 years. 
 
The test for A2 and A are the same, and while the type of motorcycle is different, we feel the test doesn't address the extra power allowed on a 35 kW+ motorcycle.
label: Department for Transport

text: Provide funding to support Breast & Cervical Cancer Screening for Disabled Women We want the government to increase funding to ensure every facility is properly equipped to provide equal care. All women, regardless of disability, should be able to access cancer screenings without fear of exclusion, humiliation, or inadequate care.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Government to fund vorasidenib for NHS patients We call on the Government to fund vorasidenib for NHS patients with IDH-mutant low-grade glioma, notwithstanding the NICE decision on whether to so or not.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban the residential use of artificial grass We urge the Government to introduce a ban on both the use and sale of artificial grass in residential settings. This should include prohibiting its installation in private gardens and outdoor spaces, as well as restricting retailers from selling it for domestic use.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Fund a full bursary and maintenance fund to train Learning Disability Nurses At a time when the demand across health and social care is so high, numbers entering the LD nursing profession are too low. To halt this decline, support the profession with a full bursary and maintenance fund. Now is time for action.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban puppy yoga, puppy Pilates and other “puppy cuddle therapy” We call for a ban on puppy yoga, puppy Pilates and other “puppy cuddle therapy” to help in bringing an end to an alarming rise in the number of businesses offering alternative therapy classes which use puppies as part of their sessions.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Introduce a higher, sector-specific Minimum Wage for HGV Drivers (C, C+E). While the National Living Wage has increased, "middle wages" for HGV drivers have stagnated. We call on the Government to conduct a review into HGV driver pay. The goal is to restore the shortened pay gap between HGV roles and the National Living Wage.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Repeal all religious exemptions Repeal all religious exemptions in law. Ensure laws relating to public safety, animal welfare, and other legal obligations apply equally to all individuals and organisations, regardless of religion or belief.
label: Ministry of Justice

text:
Stop Charging Early Years Nurseries Full Business Rates 1) Classify nurseries as educational providers — not commercial premises
2) Exempt nurseries from business rates (like schools and academies)
label: HM Treasury

text: Conduct a review of political news regulation by Ofcom Conduct a review of policy at Ofcom. We think that political news reporting on all channels has become unrepresentative of the public vote at the last general election and that political reporting using the ‘due weight’ policy is allowing extreme growth in far right coverage.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Introduce British Sign Language (BSL) to all primary school children Use digital platforms to introduce BSL to all children within primary schools. Studies suggest sign-language use improves spelling, reading and language skills for all. It promotes inclusion of hearing-impaired children, supporting better educational, employment, and mental health outcomes.
label: Department for Education

text: Reform the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991 to remove breed bans and introduce licensing We ask the Government to reform the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991 by removing breed-specific provisions and introducing a universal, behaviour-based dog licensing system that replaces the current framework and applies equally to all breeds, with proportionate enforcement and owner accountability.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Define "Significant NHS Experience" as 2-3 years for Training Prioritisation Define significant NHS service for medical training prioritisation as two years’ NHS service for entry to core specialty training and three years’ NHS service for entry to higher specialty training. We believe this will uphold fairness and protect the NHS workforce.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review support for ARFID and fund national treatment pathways ARFID (Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder) affects thousands across the UK, yet support remains inconsistent - creating a postcode lottery that must end. Around 1.25 million people have an eating disorder, 5% ARFID, yet many cannot access appropriate care.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Keep 5-year ILR for Health and Care visa holders to protect the NHS Healthcare professionals have been on the frontline during national crises & ensuring the continued functioning of vital services. We think extending ILR timeline undermines their contributions. Instead keep the ILR requirement and reduce the workforce shortage and avoid uncertainty on their future.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Make it a criminal offence for MPs to deliberately mislead the public We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation—similar to the Senedd Cymru Wales (Member Accountability and Elections) Bill—to create a criminal offence for all election candidates who knowingly make false or misleading statements during campaigns, and for MPs while in office.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Allow licences to be issued to wildlife rehabilitators to release grey squirrels We ask the Government to amend the Invasive Alien Species (Enforcement and Permitting) Order 2019 to allow Natural England to issue licences to wildlife rehabilitators to release rehabilitated grey squirrels.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Review medical testing standards & process: use optimal ranges & cellular tests Review whether symptomatic patients should be assessed using optimal ranges and cellular tests instead of standard reference ranges and serum tests. We are concerned that current tests might fail to reflect cellular or neurological dysfunction.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require care workers to have advanced level of English language proficiency We call for higher standards in English language for care workers. We think there should be a minimum of 1 year's training, working alongside a fully experienced carer, including an English test with no multiple choice questions. The elderly need to be able to understand what is being said to them.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund a trial for children and young people denied NHS access to medical cannabis We call on the Government to support children and young people on private prescriptions for drug-resistant epilepsy, still unable to access medical cannabis on the NHS, despite it being legally available in the UK since 2018, by establishing a funded observational trial.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Allow British Citizens by Descent to upgrade their citizenship Allow Citizens by Descent to upgrade their citizenship after a period of UK residency, so they can pass on citizenship to their children born abroad without further requirements.
label: Home Office

text: Increase Statutory Paternity Leave to a minimum 12 weeks paid leave for fathers Amend employment law to extend Statutory Paternity Leave to at least 12 weeks for fathers, paid at a meaningful rate. This should be a protected entitlement separate from maternity leave and not dependent on Shared Parental Leave. with protection from workplace discrimination and financial penalty.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Increase penalties for motorbike and e-bike theft & enable self-defence We want the Government to introduce harsher penalties for vehicle theft—especially when filmed for social media—and reform self-defence laws so victims are not unfairly prosecuted for protecting their property from thieves.
label: Department for Transport

text: Fund post-surgery bras/breast protheses voucher scheme for all women post cancer I would like the Government to fund a voucher scheme for all women for post surgery bras and breast prosthesis, giving ladies a choice. This would expand the current scheme to enable all women to access support, regardless of their age or income.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Create a trauma-informed task force to develop a strategy to address trauma  We think trauma is an unaddressed public health issue, with no nationwide strategy to address it. We feel a coordinated, cross-sector, trauma-informed response is essential. We urge the Government to develop a trauma-informed taskforce to create a more compassionate, effective, equitable system.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund screening for neurodivergent conditions in schools & teacher training Fund screening for all children for neurodivergent conditions in primary and secondary schools; and fund compulsory teacher training relating to neurodivergent conditions.
label: Department for Education

text: Tag and trace all illegal immigrants We believe the Government response to illegal immigration has been weak. We are concerned about the illegal immigration and the lack of information about past criminal activity of some illegal immigrants in their native country. We believe enough is enough!
label: Home Office

text: Require inquests into the death of a child by suicide to be private We want the government to change law in relation to the death of a child by suicide. We think that all inquests involving these children should be conducted privately, shielded from the public and the media.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Reverse the ban on XL Bully dogs We urge the Government to reverse the ban on XL Bully dogs, as we believe the problem is with owners not the dogs themselves. We believe a ban on a dog breed due to some undertrained dogs is wrong and discriminatory.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Add specific content on men’s mental health to RSE & health guidance for schools Statutory guidance for secondary schools on mental health should be expanded to include more specific content about men. This should include the importance of men opening up and breaking traditional stereotypes that young men are being forced into by presences online.
label: Department for Education

text: Review the safeguarding and welfare of artists in the entertainment industry We think large entertainment companies should be held accountable and responsible for the welfare of their artists. We implore the Government to review safeguarding and welfare measures used in the entertainment industry.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text:
Review slaughterhouse regulation and welfare protections We want the government to review slaughterhouse oversight.
 
- More accountability for facilities & individuals found in breach of animal welfare laws
- Increased transparency of inspections & enforcement actions
- Review the role, structure & accountability of the Food Standards Agency
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Review regulations on Battery Energy Storage Systems Review the regulations on Battery Energy Storage System systems, including how close they can be built to homes, schools and hospitals, and rules around safety.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Classify reindeer as domesticated farm animals and end Zoo Licensing requirement Reclassify reindeer as domesticated farm animals and remove the requirement for keepers to meet zoo-level geological enclosure standards. Establish fair, practical welfare regulations suited to reindeer kept by trained, responsible handlers.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Make a statutory requirement for schools to have a bereavement policy for pupils A bereavement policy is necessary for well-being but should not be watered down or muddied by a mental health policy as grief is significantly different. We believe the policy for it should encompass a pupil passport for the longevity of a child's entire education to support learning and retention.
label: Department for Education

text: Introduce a mid-term referendum on whether to hold an early General Election We urge the Government to allow the public to decide if they think the Government is fulfilling its obligations and pre-election pledges by holding a midterm referendum within a six-month window of either side of the mid-term of that Parliament.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Extend Statutory Maternity Pay and Leave for Twins, Triplets and Multiple Births Extend Statutory Maternity Leave and Statutory Maternity Pay for mothers of twins, triplets and other multiple births. We believe maternity entitlements should reflect the additional care, financial costs and practical demands associated with raising multiples.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Make Stamp Duty payment flexible Introduce Stamp Duty Land Tax payment flexibility: buyers choose between paying in full at completion or spreading the cost over 2-5 years via government-backed scheme. This could reduce upfront barriers to homeownership. Similar to other HMRC payment plans.
label: HM Treasury

text: Don’t tax people on any overtime they work. Don’t tax people on anything over their normal working hours. I don’t think it’s fair that we get taxed on this, overtime can be optional and we still get taxed.
label: HM Treasury

text: Launch an independent review of NHS wheelchair services  I’m calling on the Government to launch a full, independent review of NHS wheelchair services. We feel too many disabled people may be be let down by delays, poor assessments, unsuitable equipment, and a lack of accountability. We need urgent reform to ensure dignity and fair care.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Introduce random alcohol & drug testing within the House of Commons We want the government to introduce random alcohol and drug testing within the House of Commons
label: Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

text: Allow Visa applicants to pay health surcharge in instalments  If someone applies for a five-year visa, they currently must pay £1,035 per year upfront, totalling £5,175. We think applicants should have the option to pay the Immigration Health Surcharge in instalments instead of the full amount upfront for the entire visa duration.
label: Home Office

text: New legislation; ensure informed consent is always given to avoid patient harm. Update the law to ensure informed consent is mandatory before ALL medical and cosmetic surgeries/procedures/treatments, and before prescriptions are written. Legislation must ensure all known risks are declared to the patient. Failure to comply resulting in needless injury must be prosecutable.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Government to fund access to portage services by all Local Authorities We call on the Government to fund all Local Authorities to provide portage services in every area, as we believe this will ensure a young child with developmental delay and disability can have more successful outcomes.
label: Department for Education

text: Introduce the Right to Breastfeed and Express at Work We call on the UK Government to align UK employment law with Article 10 of ILO Convention No. 183 by introducing a statutory right to paid breastfeeding and expressing breaks, together with suitable workplace facilities.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Mandate that murderers start their sentences in category A prisons I would like the Government to mandate that those convicted for murder should begin their sentences in category A prisons. I believe they should do this to help protect our society.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: End the use of the term child prostitution in official documents and UK Laws We call on the Government to remove all references to child prostitution or any other variation of the term prostitution in relation to children. The language used matters and impacts victims for life.
label: Home Office

text: Withdraw involvement in war on Iran and seek diplomatic resolution We ask the UK government to publicly declare non-support for any US/Israel military action against Iran. Use diplomatic channels to urge restraint from both governments. Withdraw any military or intelligence support to the conflict and urge peaceful solutions.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Add peas, lentils and chickpeas to the UK’s list of major allergens. We want the Government to update food labelling laws to add peas, lentils and chickpeas to the major allergen list. These ingredients are increasingly used in foods and can cause severe allergic reactions. They should be clearly highlighted in bold on labels and menus to improve safety.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Screen for Vasa previa in the NHS Update NHS guidelines to make screening for vasa previa mandatory during the routine mid-pregnancy anomaly scan, using colour Doppler where needed. Ensure all NHS trusts follow a consistent national policy so no baby dies from this preventable condition due to lack of detection
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Publish the economic impact of removing or raising the £100k tax cliff edge Model and publish the economic impact of removing or raising the £100k taxable income cliff edge. The loss of personal allowance and loss of entitlement to free childcare hours means those who earn over £100k face a disproportionately high marginal tax rate. Between £100-£125k this can exceed 100%.
label: HM Treasury
