text: Repeal the Coronavirus Act 2020 We want the act fully repealed. Temporary provisions lapsed in 2022, but we feel its framework lingering risks future democratic overreach. We think repeal restores normal oversight, ends emergency-era controls, & reflects lessons learned. We believe temporary measures should not outlast their need.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Mandate default and activated parental control on all consumer home routers Most home routers include an option to add parental controls. We ask the Government to require all home routers to have the parental control functionality and for it to be activated by default, blocking adult content in the home while allowing parents to change or disable settings if they choose.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Review children's critical care decision law We urge the Government to review laws around critical care decisions to ensure parents are central in decision-making for critically ill children.  We want NHS bodies to be required to consult parents as equals, be required to get a second opinion from an agreed upon specialist and offer mediation.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review Government's approach to redacting Polish Military Records held by MoD I think descendants of members of the Polish Forces who fought alongside the UK in World War II, should be able to access UNREDACTED Records of their ancestors who served. I believe that the Government should review how descendants can access this information.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Ban service charges on inherited retirement properties while vacant The Government should ban retirement-housing operators from charging service charges after a leaseholder's death. Estates must not be billed while a flat is empty, in probate, or stuck on the slow resale market common in this sector. We believe this unfair financial burden should end.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Fund improvements to secondary care community mental health services  We think supporting patients with a qualified & compassionate workforce that have sufficient time & resources to provide effective support is essential & cost effective.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Commit to a referendum in May 2028 asking the next government to rejoin the EU Polls show that many people of the UK believe leaving the EU was a mistake. It is time politicians stopped ignoring the views of the people. The government needs to consult the people about what to do next.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Referendum changing the UK from constitutional monarchy to a democratic republic We think there should be a referendum on the future of the monarchy & the type of government they want to be part of. Stay as a constitutional monarchy or become a true & secular democratic republic. We think it's time we became a democratic republic, it's long overdue.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Increase dual carriage and motorway speed limit to 80mph We want the Government to increase the speed limit on dual carriage and motorway to 80 MPH.
label: Department for Transport

text: Mandate whole-life sentence for knife-related murders & stricter penalties We believe Parliament should amend sentencing laws to introduce mandatory whole life sentences with no possibility of parole, to ensure consistent punishment, public protection, and deterrence.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Provide funding to help the television industry and support TV freelancers The British TV industry has faced a decline in recent years, leaving some freelancers jobless for long periods, unable to support their families, and exiting the industry.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Referendum on illegal migration. We believe that only a referendum would give a voice to public opinion. We think the current situation regarding irregular migration is unacceptable and a burden to the taxpayer. We feel many people among the UK public believe this is a crime against their rights and interests.
label: Home Office

text: Create a government-owned, free software for Making Tax Digital (MTD) With the roll-out of Making Tax Digital going ahead, HMRC must provide an in-house, government-developed, fully-functional software that allows easy and confident compliance with MTD. Self-employed people should not be obliged to hand data to private companies.
label: HM Treasury

text: Require schools to notify parents if a pupil is distressed by results feedback We want the Government to create specific statutory guidance that must be used by educational establishments. This is to prevent the risk of pupils taking their own life after having been distressed whilst receiving feedback on their academic results and/or future subject options.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund a national pro-building stimulus package to get Britain building again Fund support package to encourage house building, including simpler, faster, cheaper rules-based planning consent process powered by AI, and financial incentives for people to buy/improve their homes, incentivise careers in building & construction, accelerate training and talent attraction.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text:
Protect sports bodies from coercive legal actions over inclusive trans policies 1 Legislate to give protection to British sports bodies and charities from legal actions that are intended to intimidate them in abuse of the British legal system
2 Until legislation is in place provide funding to all charities and sport bodies who receive such legal actions to help resist them
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Create a coordination body for Nationally Significant Energy Projects (NSIPs) We call on DESNZ to create a central body that adopts a strategic framework to assess projects collectively and ensure they proceed without environmental harm. We believe energy project cumulative impacts are a big issue, and a body is needed to coordinate competing schemes and explore alternatives.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Make reproductive coercion a standalone criminal offence Make reproductive coercion a standalone criminal offence, including forced or pressured abortion, pregnancy coercion, and contraception sabotage, to improve recognition, reporting, victim protection, and prosecution in England and Wales.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Stop all overseas spending including foreign aid The UK has a massive debt and we believe it is in decline, with a very high tax burden on its citizens. We think it is the duty of the UK government to put its citizens and the UK first and it is irresponsible to spend taxpayer's money on any overseas project.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Launch a public inquiry into concerns about free speech in the UK We would like Government to launch a public inquiry into free speech in the UK, including criminal offences relating to social media posts.
label: Home Office

text: Make helmets legal requirement while riding a bicycle or scooter on public roads My brother Riley died following a fatal collision in 2021. I believe my brother would still be with us today if he was wearing a helmet. Make it a legal requirement to wear a helmet when you are on a bicycle or scooter.
label: Department for Transport

text: Establish mandatory training to tackle medical misogyny in the NHS  We want the government to make comprehensive training in women’s health and sex-specific medicine mandatory for all healthcare professionals, in order to tackle what many see as a culture of medical misogyny in the NHS.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Adopt the "citizen advance": 28-40s may take £12,500 advance & delay retirement We call on the government to adopt the Social Market Foundation proposal allowing 28-to-40-year-olds to take a £12,500 advance in exchange for delaying retirement by one full year.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Make child maintenance evasion a criminal offence It would be child neglect if a parent providing full time care failed to provide a child with food, clothing or shelter. Yet, when a parent deliberately avoids child maintenance, depriving their child of those same essentials, it is not treated the same. It should be made a criminal offence.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Appoint independent body to bar elected officials with discriminatory views  If information comes to light indicating that a candidate/elected official may hold views that could harm people with protected characteristics, as defined by the Equality Act, an independent adjudicator should be empowered to investigate & if appropriate, remove them from the ballot paper or office
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text:
Increase funding and review children’s mental health system Many families with children suffering from mental health difficulties feel as though there is not enough support in place from services such as CYPMHS and CAMHS.
Increase funding and review the children’s mental health system.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Increase funding for Botox treatment for Sphincter of Oddi Dysfunction on NHS Various world-renowned gastroenterologists have been supporting patients who suffer with the debilitating condition of Sphincter of Oddi Dysfuncrion. (SOD) by using Botox to paralyse the sphincter.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund offer of toxicology test for repetitive symptoms unexplained otherwise I would like parliament to put in place funding, to ensure everyone is offered a toxicology blood test if they go to the doctor or A&E and are not getting any answers for their symptoms. For people who have attended more than once for symptoms unexplained otherwise.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Change speeding penalties to 1point for up to 25MPH on a 20MPH road We feel that the current penalty of 3 points for speeding in 20mph areas is disproportionate. We think the current penalty treats these drivers the same as other drivers who speed at much higher limits.
label: Department for Transport

text: Introduce legislation restricting nonsurgical aesthetics to medical doctors only We believe the lack of regulation in aesthetics, including Botox, fillers, fat-dissolving, and liquid BBL, can lead to harm, with poorly trained practitioners sometimes causing severe complications and unnatural results.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Legally require absent parents to undertake medical testing if child is unwell We call on the Government to make it a legal requirement for absent parents to present themselves if requested by a medical professional, for medical history or a blood sample if it can benefit the living child in determining why the child is so unwell.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text:
Improve statutory paternity leave in the UK to better support families. 1. Extend statutory paternity leave to a minimum of six weeks.
2. Increase statutory paternity pay to full income replacement.
3. Make it a legal requirement for employers to offer flexible arrangements to employees taking paternity leave (e.g. taking in chunks)
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Do not recognise the planned December 2025 election in Myanmar Do not recognise any election held by Myanmar’s military in December 2025. We believe the Government should condemn it as illegitimate, continue to press for the release of political prisoners and support a genuine, UN-backed democratic process.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: New policies on deporting legal and illegal migrants & full ECHR withdrawal Some research has suggested that the share of the British population that is White British may be a minority by the end of this century. We believe that reasonable concerns about this are dismissed as racism. We want the government to take the following steps in response.
label: Home Office

text: Fund access to tumour treating fields devices for glioblastoma patients Fund access to tumour treating fields (TTF) devices like Optune for Glioblastoma patients. Other countries have and we think it's a disgrace that UK citizens are not able to access it on the NHS. Huge amounts are paid for other cancer medicines, so this type of treatment should be funded too.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Hold a referendum on banning housing developments in the green belt Let the country decide what happens to its own green belt and historic villages and towns. Call a referendum on banning housing developments on green belt land.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: We call on Government to urgently revise the mobile phone in schools guidance We believe schools cannot meet statutory safeguarding duties under ‘Keeping Children Safe in Education’ while allowing students to carry smartphones. Smartphones pose risks including distraction, sharing harmful content, cyberbullying, and non-consensual photos and recording of students and staff.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund menopause support being added to the NHS Health Checks for women over 40 Taking place every five years from the age of 40, we think that NHS Health Checks are the perfect opportunity for the majority of women to see a healthcare professional before perimenopause starts to learn more about what to expect, and then again during and after menopause for continued care.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Prohibit the Use of Mobile Devices During Formal Parliamentary Proceedings We want the House of Commons to adopt rules to restrict MPs from using mobile phones and tablets during formal parliamentary proceedings. Clear guidance and appropriate sanctions should ensure compliance and maintain professional standards.
label: Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

text: Establish Complaints Commission for Social Care, Health, Education & Benefits Establish an Independent Complaint Commission for health, social Care (Adult & Child), education & benefits, who can legally force services to take action. We don’t think current complaint mechanisms and arrangements are good enough.
label: Cabinet Office

text:
Close the Borders!
Suspend all immigration for 5 years We believe our country is facing serious challenges both from legal and illegal migration, and think the only way to deal with this is to suspend all immigration temporarily for 5 years.
label: Home Office

text: Fund access to Holistic Needs Assessment for all NHS cancer patients & follow-up As a 45-year-old battling cancer, I know it is the toughest ordeal many will face. It's as much a mental battle as it is physical. We believe the NHS should ensure mental health support. So we're calling for funding for Holistic Needs Assessments for all NHS cancer patients.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Allow Licensed Raw Milk Sales in Supermarkets Change current regulations in England to allow licensed producers to sell unpasteurised milk in supermarkets, with strict safety testing, proper refrigeration, clear labelling for consumers, and systems to trace products back to the source if needed.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Review accountability for incorrect decisions regarding the removal of a child Review how officials, including judges, social workers, CAFCASS and police, can be held accountable for incorrect decisions regarding the removal of a child from a parent's care, including in cases where a parent's mental health is severely impacted.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Change the law so all investors can vote their shares Change UK company law to ensure nominees, including investment platforms, are required to pass on voting rights and information to beneficial owners of shares or their advisers. This would allow investors or their advisers to vote their shares without obstacles or additional charges.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Include Wales in the Union Flag I urge the Government and Parliament to recognize Wales's integral role within the UK by updating the Union Jack to include Wales. I am calling for an official review and redesign process that engages experts, stakeholders, and the public to ensure Wales's rightful place on our national flag.
label: Wales Office

text: Ban solar panels in countryside fields or farmland The countryside gives us food. We're currently unable to feed ourselves as a nation. Insects pollinate, their habitat is being destroyed by construction. Solar panels add to this massively. Thousands of acres being handed over to them.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text:
Implement measures to reduce child poverty It’s not OK that almost a third of UK children (4.5 million) live in poverty. I want the Government to:
-Lift 620,000 children from absolute poverty by removing the 2-child limit and the benefit cap
-Increase child-related benefits in line with inflation or average earnings (whichever is higher)
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Protect Cats: Make Reporting Cat Accidents a Legal Requirement I want cats to have the same protections as dogs, under section 170 of the road traffic act 1988 - so that it is the law to report any accident involving a cat.
label: Department for Transport

text: Archie’s Army Law - Rights for parents with a child in critical care by injury We want the government to give parents rights to be fully involved in all decisions taken for their child by the medical profession and give them the right to seek independent expert medical advice and include it in decision making.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review the UK’s policy toward the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus We believe that the UK's policy not to recognise the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TNRC) has left Turkish Cypriots, including British citizens, isolated for over 4 decades. We think this should be reviewed, to help end exclusion and help ensure fairness and equality for all Turkish Cypriots.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Halt the Pylon Network Expansion & support underground & undersea cabling We, the undersigned, urgently call on the UK Government to immediately halt and reassess the proposed expansion of the national grid network, which we believe could threaten irreversible harm to our natural environment, wildlife (including protected birds and bats), and rural communities.
label: Department for Education

text: Require headstones to be laid flat & legislate for regular safety checks Require all headstones to be laid flat and properly secured to the ground. We think there should be rules set out in legislation about how headstones are safety checked and the frequency of these checks.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Remove VAT on all veterinary care services & fund new support for vet services Remove VAT on all veterinary care services. Increase funding for veterinary services, including means-tested support for low-income pet owners struggling with veterinary bills, funding for registered rescues, and subsidised neutering to cut unwanted litters and long-term rescue intake.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Amend Dangerous Dogs Act to recognise and fund rehoming of non-dangerous dogs We call on the Government to amend the DDA1991 to allow non-dangerous dogs deemed prohibited under Section 1 to be recognised as such, and for their rehoming through approved rescues under a behaviour-based licensing system to be funded.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Improve the Financial Assistance Scheme for pensioners We call on the Government to change the parameters of compensation set out in the Financial Assistance Scheme to end what we see as a miscarriage of justice inflicted on former workforces who lost their pensions when their pension schemes being lost due to employer insolvency.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text:
Make "Stolen Valour" a Criminal Offence We would like the Government to make the act of "Stolen Valour" a Criminal Offence. Stolen valour involves falsely claiming military service, rank or medallic recognition.
 
We would like the offence to include the wearing of uniform and/or medals not awarded to the individual.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Implement an "HSE Owned Legal Register for Electricians" We want a register owned by the Health and Safety Executive, like the Gas Safe scheme. We think such a register would enforce standards and ensure only registered electricians can purchase and install electrical equipment. We think voluntary schemes like NICEIC and NAPIT lack any legal authority.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Make all World War 2 veterans exempt from Tax and Care costs Our WW2 veterans are owed by us all. There are only 8 thousand alive. We need to look after them. No Tax on their Pensions at all. Their Care costs are free, paid by the Government.
label: HM Treasury

text: Fund improved care and support for individuals with FASD. Foetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD) is a disability affecting both children and adults, but there is a lack of awareness among healthcare professionals and the public. Consequently, individuals with FASD can struggle to access appropriate care and support services.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Lower financial requirement for Spouse Visa from £29,000 back to £18,600 I think that the £29,000 is discriminatory and feels that the message it is trying to get across is that if you are earning less than £29,000 annually you are not allowed to be with your family. I don't think this is what fairness and equality constitutes. This prevents families being together.
label: Home Office

text: Grant Protected Status to UK Trig Points Grant UK trig points protected heritage status, recognise them as nationally significant, create a national register, and ensure their preservation through listing, monitoring, and maintenance by bodies like Historic England and Ordnance Survey.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Review & Regulate Veterinary Care so it's Affordable & Accessible  Review and regulate veterinary care to ensure its affordable and accessible to all. Vet costs rose 60%+ from 2015-2023 with more increases since. Costs vary regionally but basic consultations can cost £65+ and some costs like advanced scans may exceed £1000, unaffordable for many.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Clarify Grey Belt policy for land adjoining nationally protected nature sites. Clarify how Grey Belt policy should apply to land adjoining Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs), ancient woodland and other nationally protected nature sites to ensure consistent application.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Ban dynamic ticket pricing for live events Ban the use of dynamic ticket pricing for concerts and live events. Cap price increases above a fixed face value and require transparent pricing before checkout. Introduce these protections to help keep events affordable for fans.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Don't lower the voting age to 16 We urge the Government not to extend the voting franchise to 16 and 17 year olds in all UK elections, including general elections. We think that the voting age should exist in line with the age of adulthood.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Retain the 5-Year ILR Route & Fund Faster Decisions on Syrian Asylum cases We call on the UK Government to retain the current five-year route to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) for recognised refugees and to fund quicker processing and decisions of Syrian asylum claims.
label: Home Office

text: Give trans people legal access to single-sex spaces of their acquired gender We want the government to give trans people legal access to single-sex spaces of their acquired gender. We feel that the recent supreme court ruling could undermine trans people's access to single-sex spaces and make them vulnerable.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Ban the use of aversive dog training tools I would like the Government to ban the use of aversive tools such as electric shock collars, prong collars and invisible fencing due to the possible physical and mental harm caused to animals. I believe trauma and cruelty is unacceptable. Legislation on this topic has still not been enacted.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Mandate a 72-hour period before formal acceptance of a dog surrender document The Government must institute a non-waivable 72-hour cooling off period before requesting a signature for any relinquishment form offered in lieu of seizure of a dog.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Reform NHS wheelchair quality framework to make waiting times legally binding I want the Government to reform the NHS wheelchair quality framework to make it legally binding for ICBs to provide services within the 18 week deadline, including assessments, repairs and replacements, and to establish consistent quality standards across England.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Provide funding to make 25% of all public loos stoma friendly Set aside funds for local councils to make 25% of all public loos stoma friendly to create a safe space for ostomates to manage their bags. Needs to include a narrow-shelf, and hooks to hang stuff on.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Hold a Royal Commission on reform of the Westminster voting system Establish a Royal Commission immediately on the voting system to recommend changes be introduced at the next General Election.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Stop the introduction of driverless cars Stop the introduction of the commercial use of driverless taxis and other driverless passenger transport services, and protect the livelihoods of over 400,000 licensed private hire and Hackney carriage drivers by preventing their replacement with autonomous vehicles.
label: Department for Transport

text: Legalise cannabis for adults, take action on past convictions, fund compensation Legalise cannabis for adult use, require that criminal records for non-violent cannabis offences be expunged, require a review of past convictions and driving disqualifications, and establish and fund compensation for people who have been harmed by prohibition.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Fund a time-limited childcare scheme for all parents with cancer Fund a national, time-limited funded childcare scheme for parents undergoing active cancer treatment to cover nursery and before/after-school care during treatment and short-term recovery. Eligibility would not depend on employment status.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Introduce Independent Auditing of Police Complaints in England and Wales There is no routine, systematic and independent audit of police complaints. Around 85–90% are handled by the forces complained about, while only a small fraction reach the IOPC.
label: Home Office

text: Stop Commonwealth Citizens voting in UK general elections unless mutual rights The UK Government must end voting rights for Commonwealth citizens and replace them with fair, reciprocal agreements - if British citizens can’t vote in their elections, their citizens shouldn’t be allowed to vote in ours.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Keep 5 year route to ILR for Existing Ancestry Visa Holders We petition to keep the 5 year Indefinite leave to remain (ILR) route for current Ancestry Visa holders who are already living in the UK.
label: Home Office

text: Fund Emergency Shelter to anyone Homeless during all named storms. We urge Government to fund local authorities so that Severe Weather Emergency Protocols (SWEP) can be activated during all named storms & severe weather events, not just freezing temps; protecting rough sleepers from extreme wind, rain & cold to ensure no one is left vulnerable outside.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Detain all migrants that enter the UK illegally Detain all migrants that enter the UK illegally in detention centres. We think existing MOD bases could be used for this. Hotels are not to be used. Only process asylum applications for those arriving with documents and proof of no convictions.
label: Home Office

text: Expand free school meals provision to cover all school children I would like the Government to expand free school meals to cover all school children up until the end of sixth form.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund free lifelong NHS prescriptions for organ transplant recipients Update the medical exemption criteria to make all post-transplant maintenance medications free on the NHS in England, ending the geographical inequality with the rest of the UK and preventing costly graft failures.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Exempt Afghan women from the study-visa suspension and reinstate routes to study Create an immediate exemption to the current suspension of study visas for Afghan nationals, so Afghan women and girls can obtain UK education visas (including university, foundation and English pathways) with appropriate safeguards, and publish clear guidance for applicants and institutions.
label: Home Office

text: Abolish Estate management fees on New build estates for freehold properties Abolish Estate management fees on New build estates for freehold properties,
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Introduce mandatory life sentences for child sex offences I would like harsher sentencing introduced for what are the worst of all crimes in my opinion. I feel that child sex offenders are treated with leniency and this feels to me to be a grave injustice.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Make species-specific training, advice and care mandatory for pet shop staff. Pet shops in the UK may give outdated or harmful advice, leading to poor care and preventable illness. There is no legal requirement for species-specific knowledge. We call on the Government to make these training and care standards mandatory.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Set a firm launch date for Alternative Student Finance (ASF) and the LLE We call on the Government to publish a dated timeline for the launch of Alternative Student Finance (ASF), confirm exactly how it will work alongside the Lifelong Learning Entitlement (LLE), and guarantee that students who take out standard loans for 2026 can transition onto ASF without penalty.
label: Department for Education

text: Stop all foreign aid I would like the Government to stop all foreign aid. I believe the recent amount of £15 billion is unaffordable.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Outlaw fireworks for the general public Outlaw the sale and/or possession of Fireworks for all but accreditted/professional pyrotechnicians.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Referendum on the UK to be neutral on Ukraine and end all bilateral agreements We urge the Government to hold a national referendum on the UK being neutral in the war between Ukraine and Russia, and withdrawing from all bilateral agreements with Ukraine. We believe in peace and that the UK's involvement in foreign wars must end.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Make 12 July 2027 a Bank Holiday for 1100th anniversary of the birth of England Make Monday 12th July 2027 a bank holiday in England to commemorate the 1100th anniversary of the birth of England, so that all the people of England celebrate this occasion. The Government should also support organising celebrations for that day.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Increase the £100k childcare income cap in line with inflation Increase the £100,000 per-parent childcare eligibility income cap to restore its original real-terms value, and automatically uprate it each year in line with inflation to prevent further fiscal drag and unfair loss of childcare support.
label: Department for Education

text:
Ban egg hatching programs in schools and nurseries We request:
- The immediate ban of all egg hatching programs in schools and nurseries.
- The development and promotion of alternative educational resources that communicate similar concepts without involving live animals.
label: Department for Education

text: Review practice and introduce licensing and regulation for dog professionals We want the government to review and strengthen legislation and licensing requirements for dog daycare, boarding, walking, and training services. Promote responsible business practices and provide dog owners with the reassurance that anyone caring for their pet meets the highest welfare standards.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Reverse the state pension age back to 60 for women & 65 for men Stop working people to death
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Make a law to protect ILR from abolition and retrospective changes We want the Parliament to introduce primary legislation that guarantees Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) as a permanent route to settlement. ILR must not be abolished, withdrawn from holders, or replaced with visas. Any changes to ILR should apply only to new entrants from the date of implementation
label: Home Office

text: Amend laws permitting telecommunications infrastructure installation We believe small businesses across the UK are increasingly harmed by telecommunications infrastructure installed under permitted development rights, often without meaningful consultation or proper consideration of visual impact, access, or long-term commercial harm. We call for Government action.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Regulate lifeguard provision and require them to use coloured flags I would like to the Government to regulate lifeguard provision at all major beaches. This would be done at beach towns with 25,000+ residents. I think it is paramount to make our beaches as safe as possible.
label: Department for Transport

text: Increase minimum sentences for drug supply offences Drug supply should not be considered a victimless crime. Aggravating factors such as supply to vulnerable people and minors should be given greater consideration.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: School Minibus Safety - Remove Section 19 Exemptions for Schools We call on the Government to remove Section 19 exemptions for schools in the Transport Act 1985, so children and young people are only driven by qualified, professional drivers, and that minibuses are maintained to commercial standards, by requiring a full Public Service Vehicle Operator’s Licence.
label: Department for Transport

text: Overhaul and Enforce Reforms to Water Park Safety Regulations We believe comprehensive Emergency Plans, CCTV Operatives & lifeguards trained for underwater rescue should be mandatory and strictly enforced at all waterparks. We believe it should be with urgency that the relevant authorities pass this into law without delay.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: End all EU fishing rights in UK waters until France stops small boats We urge the Government to end all EU fishing rights in UK waters until France stops small boats coming to the UK. We believe it is costing far too much money and cannot continue. If this is done, the Government could have more money to spend on other services and crime may decrease.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Count all accrued residence under the Long Residence route toward the new system Provide transitional protection to migrants (who arrived pre-2021) and are nearing settlement via the current 10-year route by recognising all previously accrued continuous lawful residence counted under Appendix Long Residence toward the 10-year qualifying period of the new Earned Settlement system
label: Home Office

text: Support families by bringing nannies into the 15/30 hours free childcare scheme We would like the government to support more families by including Ofsted nannies in the 15/30 hours free childcare scheme. Nannies are a critical pillar of the childcare sector and their inclusion could maximise the options available to working parents and drive UK productivity.
label: Department for Education

text: Do not apply ILR qualifying period changes retrospectively to ILR applicants We, the undersigned, call on the UK Home Office and Government to ensure that the recent changes to the qualifying period for Indefinite Leave to Remain announced on 20 November 2025 are not applied retrospectively to individuals who are already on the route to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR).
label: Home Office

text: Regulate outbound medical tourism: mandatory accreditation, insurance, aftercare Government should create an accreditation body for overseas medical providers advertising to UK patients, require them to offer complication insurance and UK-based aftercare, allow only accredited providers to advertise in the UK, and set up a national database to track clinical outcomes.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review child maintenance service (CMS) process for accepting reduced payments Currently, a paying parent can reduce their CMS payments by adding a partner’s child as a “relevant child,” even if that child is not biologically theirs and already receives support from their own parent. We want the Government to review this process.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Automatic fast track benefits for anyone diagnosed with a terminal illness. I call on the government to automatically fast track anyone diagnosed with a terminal illness, not just those in their final year of life, so they can get essential financial support. We think this would give people financial stability at the end of life & remove the financial stress & worry.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Review how the rights of trans athletes are respected in sports We call on the Government to commission a review into trans athletes’ participation in sports, looking at how to balance fairness and inclusivity, based on scientific research. Trans people face exclusion from sports at various levels. We believe this is a violation of human rights.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Abolish the effective Tax rate of 60% on income between £100,000 and £125,140 We want the Government to abolish the effective Tax rate of 60% on income between £100,000 and £125,140, replacing it with a Tax band of 45% on income over £100,000 and removing the tapered withdrawal of Personal Allowance.
label: HM Treasury

text: Ban all convicted child sex offenders from using social media I would like the government to introduce a law that prevents all convicted child sex offenders from using social media. It’s been proved time and time again that social media is used by paedophiles to target and groom vulnerable children.
label: Home Office

text: Fund access to GLP-1 medications on the NHS for women with PCOS/PMOS Fund NHS access to GLP-1 medication for women with PCOS/PMOS, especially those with obesity and insulin resistance.  We believe this could help treat debilitating symptoms, support weight loss, improve metabolic health and fertility, & reduce physical and mental health impact of the condition.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban abortions after 12 weeks Ban abortions after 12 weeks. Babies can survive after 21 weeks, and we believe it is wrong to be able to have an abortion after 12 weeks.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban Drop-off charges at airports We think it does not make any sense to ask passengers to pay when they are dropping-off their loved ones.
label: Department for Transport

text: Require independent investigations of police officers accused of sexual offences Legislate to require every allegation of a sexual offence against a serving or former police officer, and every allegation of abusing a policing role for a sexual or intimate relationship, to be investigated by an independent body established by law. This could be called Harriet’s Law.
label: Home Office

text: Hold a referendum on stopping immigration into the UK for 30 years We demand the Government call a referendum on immigration, in order to address people’s concerns by a public vote. We want the referendum to be about whether we agree to end immigration into the UK for 30 years.
label: Home Office

text: Make parents legally responsible for their children's crimes against wildlife There have been multiple reports of children torturing and killing wild animals. Change the law and prosecute the parents for their children's crimes.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Reclassify Ketamine as a Class A drug We believe that ketamine use is a rising problem amongst the 18-30 age range, and feel that the damage it can cause to people’s bodies can be rapid and detrimental. It’s appearing that ketamine can make visible and detrimental damage to people’s bodies within a very short timeframe.
label: Home Office

text: Launch a public enquiry into Veterans UK We believe there needs to be a public inquiry into Veterans UK, including the war pensions claim system.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Amend Law so Definitions of Man & Woman Include Transgender and Intersex People We want the Government to amend the law so that legal definitions of “woman” and “man” are inclusive of transgender and intersex people, and not restricted to biological sex. We think this would ensure full legal recognition and equal protection for all under the law.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund more Clinical Psychology Training places and accessible alternative routes Urgently increase funded clinical psychology training places, expand permanent Assistant Psychologist roles, review barriers to the Doctorate pathway and create other routes so the profession is accessible to graduates from all socioeconomic backgrounds, to help tackle the mental health crisis.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Grant visas & scholarships for Palestinian students, collaborate with Gazan Unis We demand that the Government extend the Gazan student evacuation policy that ended on the 31st December 2025 indefinitely, grant further scholarships for studies and facilitate twinning partnerships between UK and Gazan Universities.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Stop medical appointments counting against school attendance We believe children shouldn’t be marked down as absent for hospital or GP appointments. These are authorised absences but still lower attendance records. We urge the Government to create a separate code so medical care doesn’t impact students’ attendance records.
label: Department for Education

text: Make all manufactured gluten-free foods VAT-free & help reduce their cost Manufactured gluten-free foods are essential for people with coeliac disease and intolerance, yet they are often very expensive. We call on the Government to remove VAT and seek to reduce production costs to ensure fair pricing and access to necessary dietary products.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Add veterinary medicine to second-degree tuition loan exemptions We ask the government to add veterinary medicine to the list of second-degree courses eligible for tuition fee loans. This would align it with medicine and dentistry, remove unfair financial barriers, and help address the UK’s critical veterinary workforce shortage.
label: Department for Education

text: Review highway code for vulnerable road users and fund a tv awareness campaign We feel the Highway Code updates don’t go far enough for vulnerable road users. We believe the 2-metre distance when passing cyclists, horse riders or carriage drivers cannot be proven. We also feel the police do not enforce the code and we are not taken seriously enough when reporting incidents.
label: Department for Transport

text: Strengthen protection of DA victims and how their testimony is treated in court Introduce Tianne Olivia's Law so evidence given by domestic abuse (DA) victims while alive is not dismissed as hearsay after death. Improve monitoring of high risk perpetrators, and prevent future deaths. Fund support when victims leave the perpetrator.
label: Home Office

text: Fund Memorial for Gaza Children Honouring Peace, Compassion We ask the Government to fund a memorial to honour Gaza’s children lost to conflict. We think this memorial would promote peace, compassion, and reflection, complementing existing monuments that uphold justice, humanity, and equality.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Protect Disability Benefits: Stop Changes to PIP and Universal Credit We urge the government to stop the cuts to PIP and UC. We think they will disproportionately harm disabled people. We think they should ensure PIP rises with inflation and that disabled people on UC are not financially penalised for being unable to work, not make it harder to access vital support.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Increase funding for NHS cancer care to make patients access treatments quicker The government should provide more funding to ensure faster cancer diagnosis and treatment by reducing waiting times for biopsies, scans and chemotherapy. Guarantee patients timely access to life-saving care through increased investment, staffing and resources, so delays do not cost lives.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban meat and dairy advertising We think billions of animals suffer in factory farms while meat and dairy ads hide the cruelty. Ban meat and dairy ads to support humane, sustainable, plant-based choices. The less people see these advertisements, kinder choices can be made. Help to save animals lives by stopping advertisements.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Ban higher car insurance premiums for over 70s based on age Parliament must review the exclusion of financial services from the age discrimination provisions of the Equality Act. We think over 70's should not routinely, based upon their age, be charged more for car insurance than any other sector of society.
label: HM Treasury

text: Fund improved aftercare, support & advice for mothers after caesarean sections We call on the UK Government to fund improved post-caesarean aftercare across the NHS including standardised scar-care, abdominal rehabilitation, pelvic health & mental-health support. With caesareans accounting for around 45% of births (& increasing) mothers require consistent, specialist aftercare
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Scrap ILR B2 English requirements for people already in the UK on family visas Scrap B2 level English requirements for ILR for people who are already in the UK on family visas. We believe the B1 requirement should remain place for people already living in the UK in this route. The B2 requirement only apply to applicants arriving after 2025.
label: Home Office

text: Enact military, diplomatic & economic sanctions on Israel for attacks on Lebanon The UK Government should enact military, diplomatic and economic sanctions against Israel unless they stop their attacks on Lebanon, end their invasion, and withdraw from Lebanese territory. We believe Israel should also pay compensation for the destruction of civilian infrastructure.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text:
Increase the annual cash ISA allowance to £25000 per annum We want the Government to increase the cash ISA annual allowance.

We want allowances increased as we feel they have remained stagnant for sometime.
label: HM Treasury

text: Make directly threatening action based on a constituency’s voting record illegal We believe that voters should feel free to vote for whatever candidate they prefer, and not be guided by threats of Government action in the constituency based on the voting record of that constituency, and that therefore making such threats as a part of political campaigning should be illegal.
label: Cabinet Office

text:
Introduce the mandatory neutering of cats by 6 months of age.
 We are calling on the government to introduce the mandatory neutering of cats by 6 months of age unless they are registered as licensed breeding cats. Some animal charities are being overwhelmed with abandoned cats and kittens.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Establish a Pathway to Permanent Settlement for Ukrainians in the UK Provide a pathway to permanent settlement (Indefinite Leave to Remain) for Ukrainians under humanitarian schemes who are already contributing to the UK economy but are forced to live in uncertainty for almost 5 years many with no place to return due to destroyed homes or hostile territory occupation
label: Home Office

text: Improve maternity pay and financial support for working families We want the Government to improve financial support for families by increasing statutory maternity pay to reflect living costs, reviewing Universal Credit income thresholds so working families are not excluded, and extending access to the Sure Start Maternity Grant or an equivalent payment.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Suspend licences after fatal or serious road collisions Introduce a law requiring immediate suspension of a driver’s licence after a road traffic collision causing death or serious injury, pending a full investigation, with a right to appeal.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review the prescribing and sale of topical corticosteroids We ask the government to review prescribing protocols and over-the-counter availability of topical corticosteroids. We believe that topical corticosteroids have been over-prescribed and irresponsibly prescribed for decades – leading to what is known as ‘Topical Steroid Addiction’.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Hold an inquiry into the status of the Sino-British Joint Declaration We call on the Parliament to hold a formal inquiry and investigate whether the JD is void or not as a signatory of the treaty, as we believe there is no evidence that China has acted to ensure the JD abides by the peremptory norms of international law, or “jus cogens.”
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Require a, "no confidence," vote on the ballot for all elections/referendums. To give the people of the UK the option that no candidate/party/issue on the ballot represents their convictions. A "no confidence" vote should encompass general elections, by-elections, local elections, and referendums.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Legalise and regulate cannabis for adults across the United Kingdom Introduce laws to legalise and regulate cannabis for adults in the UK. This should include licensed production and sale, strict age limits, product testing and labelling, restrictions on advertising, and taxation to fund the NHS, education and addiction services.
label: Home Office

text: Immediately pause the early release scheme and establish a review In July 2024, the Government announced that sentences for serious violent offences of four years or more, as well as sex offences, would be automatically excluded from the new early release scheme. What we were promised has now changed and some of the most violent offenders are set to be released.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Apply proposed changes to the ILR qualifying period to those already here Apply the proposed changes of increasing the qualifying period for settlement (ILR) from 5 years to 10 years, outlined in the recently released immigration white paper, to the migrants currently in the UK.
label: Home Office

text: Review the issuing of hormone prescriptions for transgender individuals by GPs I believe the government should launch a review into the ways that GPs work alongside NHS gender clinics to issue prescriptions for hormones.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund a public health campaign to reduce the stigma of suicide Fund a multi-year campaign which should include mass media, social media, workplace toolkits, promotion in schools and universities, media collaboration and clear support signposting. Over five years, this should include development, pilots, evaluation and targeted campaigns for high risk groups.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Increase the personal tax allowance threshold to £20,000 The personal allowance has been frozen while living costs have risen, meaning workers pay more tax in real terms. Increasing it to £20,000 would put more money into millions of workers’ pockets, helping with rising bills and supporting low and middle earners.
label: HM Treasury

text: Reduce maximum weekly working hours to 32 & introduce statutory overtime pay Amend the Working Time Regulations to reduce the legal maximum baseline working week to 32 hours from 48 hours, maintaining current pay levels (100:80:100 model). Make it a legal requirement that any hours worked beyond 32 hours a week be paid statutory overtime across all sectors.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Resolve delays in renewal of COS for Skilled Worker visas The Government should urgently address delays in renewing Certificates of Sponsorship (CoS) for Skilled Worker visas, including clear updates on renewal delays, published processing times, priority for care workers, and an expedited route and support channel for urgent UK-based cases.
label: Home Office

text: Cease and ban all UK trade with Israel due to its occupation of Palestine We urge the UK Government to cease all trade with the State of Israel concerning the Occupied Palestinian Territories (oPt) and ban UK businesses from trading with Israel in this regard. We believe Palestinian-led businesses in the oPt should have direct UK trade without Israeli involvement.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Remove inheritance tax on all estates and their property worth under £1 million Change the inheritance tax threshold from all estates from £325,000 to £1 million, so that no inheritance tax is levied on estates and the property within them up to a value of £1 million.
label: HM Treasury

text: Ban 3G rubber crumb on new artificial pitches and display health info notices We call on the Government to ban the use of rubber crumb infill on all new 3G artificial football pitches, and to require clear health information notices to be displayed at existing 3G pitches that use rubber crumb infill. Also to require the removal of rubber crumb from all existing 3G pitches.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Ban plea deals in serious sexual offence cases against children & the vulnerable We want the government to change the law so that plea bargains are not allowed in cases of serious sexual offences against children or vulnerable people. We think the CPS should be required to pursue charges that reflect the full severity of the crime.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Adapt EYFS and KS1 Literacy Curriculums to be inclusive for Non-Verbal children We want the current phonics screening test, the early years and the Key Stage 1 curriculum frameworks to be adapted to make them inclusive for children with oral communication challenges.
label: Department for Education

text: Introduce a Minister of Mental Wellbeing for Young Adults Introduce a Minister, with their own team and department, focused on the mental wellbeing of young adults in the UK, decreasing indices such as suicide and self-harm rates, and increasing the overall optimism amongst the youth of this country.
label: Department for Education

text: Introduce Legislation to make Verbal Abuse toward Police Officers an offence We believe that to some it's become acceptable that police officers get verbally abused and are considered too hardened to experience Harassment, Alarm of Distress for Public Order Act offences. They are public servants worthy of protection from abuse. Make it an offence to verbally abuse officers.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Exclude land used for primary food production from being designated grey belt Explicitly exclude any land used for primary food production (Grade 1, 2, and 3a agricultural land) within the greenbelt from the definition of grey belt in the National Planning Policy framework (NPPF).
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reverse the Tax Treatment of Double Cab Pickup Trucks in the 2024 Autumn Budget We call on the Government to reverse the recent decision announced in the 2024 Autumn Budget to reclassify double cab pickup vehicles with a payload of one tonne or more as cars for certain tax purposes.
label: HM Treasury

text: Provide funding for a review of the efficacy of Pineal Gland Surgery  We would like the government to fund a review to explore the extent to which surgical intervention can alleviate the symptoms experienced by individuals with pineal cysts.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Change the speed limit for single-carriageway rural roads from 60mph to 30mph Rural roads are the most dangerous roads for all kinds of driver and speed is the problem. A study of single-carriageway rural roads estimated that a 10% increase in average speed results in a 30% increase in fatal and serious crashes.
label: Department for Transport

text: Animal cruelty & Neglect cases at Court  should be charged per animal. We believe that each animal's suffering from Abuse/Cruelty or Neglect, should be charged to reflect this. One charge per animal. We also request that  sentencing guidelines  reflect single charge per single animal. Every animal deserves justice and stronger sentences will act as a deterrent.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Allow international travel while an ILR application is pending Allow people with valid leave to remain who apply for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) to travel outside the UK and the Common Travel Area while their application is pending without it being treated as withdrawn. With eVisas, their valid immigration status and leave period can be easily verified
label: Home Office

text: Ban large solar farms on high-quality farmland and mandate BESS safety zones We demand legislation to ban large solar on farmland classed as Best and Most Versatile farmland.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Private pensions to remain excluded from someone's estate for Inheritance Tax We ask the Government to reverse the planned change in April 2027 to include someone's Private pension into their estate estimate for Inheritance tax. In our view this disproportionately penalise single or unmarried couples due to £325k individual tax allowance (plus £175k if house goes to children)
label: HM Treasury

text: Allow clinical and biomedical scientists to use patient group directions. Patient Group Directions are already used safely by nurses, pharmacists and allied health professionals. We want the Government to extend this framework to trained and statutory regulated clinical scientists and biomedical scientists, with suitable governance, training and competency frameworks.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Repeal the Public Order Act 2023 We want the government to repeal the Public Order Act 2023 which established several criminal offences in relation to protest. We think it is fundamentally undemocratic.
label: Home Office

text: Review how Home Office deals with applications for ILR due to domestic violence I think that the Government allows claims of leave to remain because of DV too easily. People can apply for indefinite leave to remain (ILR) because of a relationship breakdown due to domestic violence or abuse, if their partner was a British citizen or settled in the UK.
label: Home Office

text: Introduce ban on keeping wolves in captivity We call on the Government to enact a legislative ban on keeping wolves in captivity including all zoos and wildlife parks.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Negotiate UK-wide recognition of older person's bus passes I think senior citizens living close to the English, Scottish & Welsh borders are disadvantaged in how many local bus services they can use. Bus services run across borders and I think it would be easier and fairer if the bus pass covered the whole journey, and return, on all of these services.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review FCDO procedures for supporting investigations into British deaths abroad  We believe the UK government should take a more active role in ensuring that deaths of British nationals abroad are properly examined.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Allow conjugal visits for prisoners in England and Wales Allow prisoners to have conjugal visits with their partners. We think this will put less strain on relationships and might also help keep prisoners in check as they could lose rights for certain visits if misbehaving.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Mandate parental CCTV access in childcare settings after safeguarding incidents We call on the Government to introduce a legal right for parents to have clear, timely CCTV access in all childcare settings and nurseries within a set timeframe, following a safeguarding incident involving their child.
label: Department for Education

text: Cancel student debt for NHS staff after 5 years’ service Write off the student loans that NHS staff such as midwives, doctors, nurses, theatre staff, radiographers, physiotherapists have to take on in order to work in the NHS, after they have completed five years’ service.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Repeal the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991, introduce new laws on penalties & education We want the 1991 Act to be repealed and replaced with new legislation mandating education on dog ownership at a young age, and specifying harsher penalties for any owners mistreating their dogs or who fail to prevent their dogs acting dangerously out of control and harming the public.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Shorten residency period for undocumented migrants to apply to regularise status Allow undocumented people in the UK to regularise their status based on a shorter residency period, enabling all migrants here over 5 years to apply for ILR, then citizenship, and those here under 5 years to apply for secure residency, upholding the human rights of these integral members of society.
label: Home Office

text: Review Local Government Reorganisation decisions This petition asks the government to review recent Ministerial decisions on Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) particularly in relation to the size and practicality of councils in rural areas.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Introduce measures to ensure fair pay for rideshare drivers Some firms can charge drivers commission fees of 25% or more of each fare. This can leave drivers struggling to earn a fair and sustainable income. We think this model places an unfair burden on drivers, who are essential to our transport infrastructure but we feel lack basic rights and protections.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text:
Require schools to include both skirts and trousers in female uniform policy Require school uniform policy to allow girls the right to wear skirts or trousers.
 
I think control over the wearing of either item contravenes the Equality Act 2010 through direct discrimination of women.
label: Department for Education

text: Enable self-employed to include childcare costs in allowable expenses We want the Government to allow those who are self-employed to deduct childcare costs from their taxable profit and therefore be included in allowable expenses. We think these deductions could increase productivity, earnings, and ultimately tax revenues.
label: HM Treasury

text: Mandate diabetes awareness training for all childcare professionals & educators Recently, my world was turned upside down when a family member was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes. One thing that struck me deeply was the realisation that so many childcare professionals and educators lack adequate training to recognise the symptoms of type 1 diabetes.
label: Department for Education

text: Ban holiday companies raising prices in school holidays. Put restrictions on holiday companies so that they are unable to raise prices of holidays so much during school holiday times.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Lift the ban on new UK oil & gas exploration licences to improve energy security With ongoing wars pushing up global energy prices and increasing reliance on volatile imports, we call on the Government to immediately lift the ban on new oil and gas exploration licences, approve viable projects and support domestic drilling to secure affordable energy for families and businesses.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Continue PR for severely disabled adults instead of costly CoP Deputyship Amend the law so Parental Responsibility continues beyond 18 where a capacity assessment between the ages of 16-18 confirms the young person severely and permanently lacks capacity, with oversight safeguards, removing the need for families to apply for costly, Court of Protection Deputyship.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: More funding for Lipoedema and Lymphoedema care on the NHS Currently there is no treatment for Lipoedema or Lymphoedema available within the NHS. We believe we need more funding for training and for more specialists in all parts of the country, along with the treatments such as liposuction to be funded on the NHS
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Investigate the claims of £22 Billion black hole Investigate the alleged £22 Billion black hole Labour is claiming the previous Government left and previous government denies. We think an investigation will sort out the true facts.
label: HM Treasury

text: Add Endometriosis to NHS Medical Exemption List for Free Prescriptions We want the Government to add endometriosis to the list of qualifying long-term medical conditions that entitle patients in England to Medical Exemption for free NHS prescriptions. Endometriosis is a recognised incurable chronic inflammatory condition that requires lifelong medical treatment.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Mandate that all Council and Parliamentary Candidates have an Enhanced DBS check At the moment it is not mandatory for prospective council candidates or Parliamentary candidates to have an Enhanced DBS check.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Increase funding for ARFID treatment We think that everyone who needs it should be able to access treatment for ARFID. I think funding should be increased for the treatment of ARFID.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reintroduce capital punishment for child murder, rape and abuse offences We want the Government to pass a law to reintroduce capital punishment for the most serious crimes against children, including child murder, rape, and extreme abuse.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Provide more funding and aid for children's education in Gaza We ask the Government to provide funding and support for teachers and educators in Gaza to help children access education, ensuring they have the chance of a future once the war has ended. They need new schools that are safe, and teachers to teach them, who aren't worried about being hurt or killed.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: The Government should block all trade with Israel including the blocking of arms We think Israel's illegal settlements and disproportionate military actions against Palestinians violate international law and are widely condemned. We believe the UK must take stronger a position.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Introduce Statutory Menstrual Leave For People With Fibroids and PCOS We urge the Government to introduce statutory paid menstrual leave of up to 3 days per month for people with fibroids and PCOS, similar to Portugal’s model. We believe leave should come with strong workplace protections, be confidential and require a single annual medical certificate.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Ban Trawling in All Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) in UK waters Ban all bottom and pelagic trawling within all UK Marine Protected Areas to safeguard vital marine ecosystems & ensure these protected areas are truly safe for nature. We think this would support biodiversity, aid climate resilience by protecting carbon stores & benefit sustainable fishing practices
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text:
Collect and publish data on companion animal euthanasia Currently there is no accurate data on the euthanasia of companion animals available in England.
 
Commercial companies given contracts by local authorities in relation to stray animals are not subject to freedom of information requests.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Call a public inquiry into any foreign influence on UK politics & democracy It’s clear that we have numerous issues with covert foreign interests attempting to influence British political parties. In order to ensure British democracy is preserved by the next election, we believe we should understand how embedded foreign interests are in British politics.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Fund awareness, care and treatment of Stiff Person Syndrome Provide funds to improve awareness of Stiff Person Syndrome (SPS), recognise the value of patient lived experience, increase access to specialist care, remove unnecessary barriers to clinically appropriate medications, including treatments not routinely available in the UK.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require independent adjudication for private toll penalties We call on the UK Government to require that all penalty charges issued by privately operated toll roads with statutory enforcement powers are subject to independent adjudication by an approved tribunal.
label: Department for Transport

text: Introduce a Bereaved Parent Support Framework following the death of a child We call on the Government to introduce a national Bereaved Parent Support Framework, including improved transitional financial support and proactive bereavement care in the form of GP contact within 14 days of a child's death and dedicated bereavement support for surviving siblings.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Create a new independent regulatory body for vets Create an independent regulatory body overseeing vets. We think incompetent or negligent vets are not being dealt with appropriately and we believe the veterinary sector in the UK is not adequately regulated. We think animal welfare is at risk.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Introduce a 2% wealth tax on assets over £10 million & tax reform We urge the Government to launch a 2% tax on assets over £10 million and implement tax reform measures such as closing loopholes in non-doms and inheritance tax and reducing taxes on regular working people. We think this could raise billions of pounds per year for public spending.
label: HM Treasury

text: Introduce stronger welfare regulations for pet care services  We want the Government to introduce a Pet Care Regulations Bill to mandate licensing for all commercial pet care services, including pet sitters and dog walkers, groomers & trainers, and require welfare training, enhanced DBS checks, public liability insurance and an animal cruelty public register.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Mandatory trauma-informed training and standards in the family courts service   We call on the Government to ensure mandatory trauma-informed training and standards for all professionals whose assessments influence decisions in the family courts, including judges, CAFCASS officers, social workers, and court-instructed medical experts.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Review and introduce safer prescribing regulations for topical corticosteroids We ask the government to urgently review and implement stricter, safer, and more regulated prescribing protocols for topical corticosteroids - used for skin conditions such as eczema. We believe that topical corticosteroids have been over-prescribed for decades, leading to horrific side effects.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Increase support and awareness to help IPF sufferers Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is life limiting. There is no cure, it's caused by scarring on the lungs which gets worse, breathing reduces, you end up reliant on oxygen & death is inevitable. Once diagnosed we experienced in our case no real support at all.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund temporary suitable housing for children with life-limiting illnesses We urge the Government to pass a law which funds temporary housing for children with life-limiting illnesses if their homes can no longer meet their needs. We believe that under no circumstances should a child remain in hospital for a lengthy period if they are able to be cared for at home.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Pass an act for tartan woven in the Highlands, similar to Harris Tweed Act 1993 Create an act that legally recognises tartan cloth woven in the Highland region following the precedent set by the Harris Tweed Act 1993. A Highland-based authority could be established to manage the use of the act and it could be supported by with a newly formed working group.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text:
Halt the new vaping duty tax, help protect small British businesses & consumers We call on the government to reconsider the introduction of a flat-rate duty on all vaping liquids, which imposes a tax of £2.20 per 10ml of e-liquid plus VAT.
This tax is set to come into effect October 2026. The tax covers not only finished e-liquids but also concentrate.
label: HM Treasury

text: Lower the English language test exemption age for BNO visa holders from 65 to 60 We propose allowing individuals over 60 to provide proof of active participation in ESOL courses in place of a formal test when applying for settlement. This adjustment would offer more support to elderly BNO visa holders.
label: Home Office

text: Review rules, policing and harm of marches We want Government to review stricter permits for and costs of policing disruptive marches, penalties for organisers of protests where antisemitic or extremist activity takes place, and the policing, economic and community harm caused by protests.
label: Home Office

text: Extend NHS Learning Support Fund Eligibility to fully include MPharm Students We ask the Government to fully include MPharm students in the NHS Learning Support Fund. We believe pharmacists are essential to NHS services, including Pharmacy First, yet many pharmacy students receive less support than other healthcare students despite completing clinical placements.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund NHS access to Lecanemab & Donanemab to slow dementia/Alzheimer's symptoms We call on the Government to fund NHS access to Lecanemab & Donanemab on prescription for those with early-onset dementia, Familial Alzheimer's Disease and those who are asymptomatic, but carry a genetic mutation that will result in early onset Dementia.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Make it mandatory for the NHS to offer scans at 9-10 weeks Introduce early mandatory scanning at 9-10 weeks to help reduce miscarriages going undetected. 1 in 4 women suffer a miscarriage. 1-5% of these are known as a "missed miscarriage", which averagely happens between 6-9 weeks and are only detected at the 12 week scan.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Repeal Net Zero targets & Climate Change Act. Stop Renewable energy expansion We think Government MUST immediately revoke ALL Net Zero Targets & The Climate Change Act 2008. Since this became law numerous scientists up to Nobel Laureate level have jointly declared "There is NO climate emergency". The raised energy prices are impacting the UK's living costs & economy.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Pause & review the Children’s Wellbeing & Schools Bill regarding home education Pause and review the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill to amend it and ensure home education is not over-regulated, that parental rights are respected, and that any changes are evidence-based and developed in consultation with home-educating families.
label: Department for Education

text:
Help to return Ukrainian children that have been forcibly taken by Russia This petition calls on the UK Government to:
 
Work with international partners to identify and repatriate these children to their families and homeland.
 
Provide increased resources to Ukrainian and international child protection agencies working to find and return abducted children.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Require all employers to include parental leave policies in job listings Require all employers to include parental leave policies clearly in job listings. Some studies show only a small percentage currently do so. Making it a legal requirement could help ensure fair access to information. We believe without it, discrimination, unfair withdrawal of offers could result.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Require all doctors to receive perimenopause training & GPs to have specialists We urge the Government to require all doctors and UK medical students to take mandatory perimenopause training and ensure every GP practice has at least one senior medical staff member trained to support, listen to, and properly help women experiencing perimenopause.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Deploy the Royal Navy to help stop illegal immigrants entering the UK We think that UK national security is the number one job of the UK government. We would like the Government to deploy the Royal Navy to help stop illegal immigrants entering the UK.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Commit to Protect Rights to EOTAS/EOTISC for Children & Young People with SEND In any SEND reforms, maintain the legal right to education other than in school for children & young people whose needs mean no school or college placement is appropriate. Retain the SEND Tribunal’s power to order EOTISC and specify the provision required for a child’s individually assessed needs.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund full clinical trials naltrexone to treat cancer Some studies have shown naltrexone may inhibit cancer. There have never been full clinical trials to investigate this. I would like the government to fund full trials in order to get this drug licensed.
label: Department of Health and Social Care
