text: Fund free civil legal support for survivors of sexual violence Create a Government-funded scheme that provides free, specialist civil legal support for survivors of sexual violence. This should cover legal advice, representation, and essential case costs, ensuring survivors can pursue civil claims regardless of income or financial barriers.
label: Ministry of Justice

text:
Revise and make statutory the Voluntary Code of Practice for Food on the Go
 On behalf of a group of councils, we ask the government to issue a clear, enforceable, evidence-based statutory framework to help businesses manage litter consistently, reduce environmental harm, and create fair and proportional responsibility, in partnership with local authorities and volunteers.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Ban All Knives including ceremonial knives in Schools Introduce a clear policy banning knives of any kind in schools, including religious or ceremonial blades. Schools should remain completely weapon-free environments so pupils and staff can learn and work safely.
label: Department for Education

text: Make school libraries statutory in all secondary schools We think all secondary schools should have a school library with a dedicated full-time librarian, and that this needs to be compulsory for all secondary schools and not simply an optional "bolt-on" depending on how individual headteachers feel about libraries and literacy provision.
label: Department for Education

text: Keep the state pension at 67 for those born before 1977 Leave the state pension qualifying age as it stands at 67, for those born prior to 1977 and have planned their retirement accordingly.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Fully fund specialist glasses for visually impaired children We call on the Government to fully fund clinically necessary specialist glasses and tinted lenses for all visually impaired children through the NHS.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Seek professional drivers’ exemption to Schengen restrictions on length of stay We believe a professional drivers’ exemption from Schengen restrictions from the 90/180 day rule to those who are transporting goods or people between the UK and EU on a return journey is needed, and would be grateful for support in raising this issue in Parliament and with EU members.
label: Department for Transport

text: Make British Summer Time (BST) permanent year-round We call on the UK Government and Parliament to keep the UK on British Summer Time (BST) permanently—by ending the bi-annual clock changes and remaining one hour ahead of GMT year-round.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Reverse the visa brake on Study Visas for citizens from Myanmar  Allow Myanmar people who meet the visa requirements for studying in the UK to be able to come and benefit from a UK education and contribute to the UK and Myanmar now and in the future.
label: Home Office

text: Stop child sex offenders living near schools & within victims’ communities Children deserve to feel safe in their homes, schools and communities. Allowing convicted offenders to live close to schools or within the same town as their victims can cause fear, trauma and undermine public confidence in safeguarding measures.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Require all owned cats to be neutered by six months of age unless exempted Require all owned cats to be neutered by six months of age, with exemptions for cats being kept for breeding by a legally recognised and licensed breeder, or medical grounds by veterinary surgeons. Their neutered or exemption status should be recorded on the cat’s microchip database record.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Fund access to lipreading classes, and classify as Health and Wellbeing course Lipreading courses can be essential rehabilitation for anyone who has lost some or all of their hearing. Therefore the Government should fund access to them and ensure they are classified as health and wellbeing courses rather than leisure activities, to recognise their importance.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Hold public inquiry on safeguarding system and training in family courts We think the Family Courts and social services, Cafcass, CPS are failing to safeguard children, overlooking evidence and allowing harmful practices. We want a public inquiry into accountability, what we see as systemic failings and bias, and effects of current procedures on child and family welfare.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Stop road tax on zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) from 2025 We believe that charging road tax on ZEVs risks undermining the UK’s commitment to reducing carbon emissions and reaching our net-zero targets.
label: HM Treasury

text: Stop the deduction of carers allowance from people's Universal Credit award Stop the deduction of Carers Allowance from the carers Universal Credit award, it shouldn’t be treated as an income.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Reduce the Motability Drive Smart age limit from 30 to 25 I want the government to reduce the Motability Drive Smart age to 25 and under because Motability already allows access to certain cars at 25. It’s inconsistent to set 30 for Drive Smart. Aligning policies ensures fairness and equal access for all drivers.
label: Department for Transport

text: Direct the UKHSA to monitor COVID infections that occur in particular settings Ensure that the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) monitors, and reports on, the numbers of COVID infections that occur in healthcare settings through its routine surveillance programmes, and advises on how to prevent and control infection in establishments such as hospitals, care homes and schools.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Cap income used to calculate Child Maintenance to Minimum Wage over a 40hr week We call on the UK Government to introduce a fair and sustainable cap on the income figure used to calculate CMS payments. We propose that the maximum weekly income considered for CMS assessments be limited to the equivalent of the National Minimum Wage multiplied by a 40-hour working week.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Mandate working a/c and heating systems on all new public transport vehicles Heatwaves are becoming increasingly more frequent, so let's get working air conditioning and heating systems made a legal requirement before a new public service vehicle can go in to service.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review the enforcement policy guidance for LAs to protect mobile home owners. We call on the Government to review its enforcement policy guidance for Local Authorities, associated with the Mobile Homes Act 2013, to strengthen protections for residents living in Park Homes from the malpractices of rogue ownerships.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Repeal changes to immigration visa & settlement requirements announced 1/07/2025 We want the government to cancel all changes to the immigration and visa policy as set out on 01/07/25, effective 22/07/25. The new rules cut many eligible job roles, raised the salary threshold, and require that sponsored jobs have a university degree.
label: Home Office

text: Remove the 28 day time limit from the unduly lenient sentence scheme for murder There is no time limit on grief, families of murder victims should be allowed to apply outside of the 28 day time limit to appeal a murderers sentence given the trauma they have endured during the murder investigation and subsequent trial.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Make it law to have working parking air conditioners in all HGVs Pass a law to make it mandatory for all Heavy Goods Vehicles to have a fully working Parking Air Conditioning unit installed. HGV drivers’ lives can be at risk when parked up due to record breaking temperatures and we believe existing laws are not sufficient to prevent this.
label: Department for Transport

text: Rule out BBC licence fee being linked to council tax There have been reports of the licence fee being linked to council tax, following a media interview from the BBC Chairman that covered future funding. For the reasons stated below, this petition asks that the Government should rule this out.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: The Northern Ireland Troubles Bill should be withdrawn We believe the Troubles Bill contains provisions which current and former service personnel will find insulting and should not be proceeded with.
label: Northern Ireland Office

text: Provide more funding for further biomedical research and education on CFS/ME We want the government to provide more funding for further biomedical research and education on myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME)/chronic fatigue syndrome. ME Association UK estimates there are currently over 250 000 people in the UK with ME/CFS. Please help me and others who are suffering with ME/CFS.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Stop mental health, ADHD & autism services review. Adopt report recommendations Scrap the review into rising demand for Mental Health, ADHD & Autism services. Instead fund & implement the recommendations of the 'Time to Deliver' (Autism Act Committee) & ADHD Taskforce Part 2 reports. This would help end systemic failure, poor health outcomes, & inequality in Autism & ADHD care.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Do not implement Age-Based Eye Testing for Drivers Over 70 Years of Age Withdraw proposals for mandatory eye or health tests applying only to drivers aged 70+. Some older drivers already renew licences more frequently and self-declare medical conditions, while some reports show that people aged 70+ are among the safest drivers on the road.
label: Department for Transport

text:
Fair funding for Early Years Care: To allow quality, training, and transparency 1. Increase, publish and properly allocate funding to match the actual cost of delivery
2. Funding to support, train and retain skilled early years professionals
3. Allow providers to charge fair fees if funding doesn't meet the cost of delivery
label: Department for Education

text: Direct the UKHSA to monitor COVID infections that occur in particular settings. Ensure that the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) monitors, and reports on, the numbers of COVID infections that occur in healthcare settings through its routine surveillance programmes, and advises on how to prevent and control infection in establishments such as hospitals, care homes and schools.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Devolve The Crown Estate In Wales We are calling on the Government to devolve the Crown estate from Westminster to Wales, like it was devolved to Scotland in 2017. We believe that the appointment of a Crown Estate Commissioner doesn't go far enough, and that a radical change is needed by devolving the Crown Estate.
label: Wales Office

text: Ban banks from denying service to sex workers because of their work Many sex workers are being denied banking services, including account closures and mortgage refusals, because their lawful work is labelled “high risk". Other sectors considered "high risk", such as gambling, have managed to negotiate terms for banking. Why should the sex industry be any different?
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Extend parental bereavement leave after the loss of a child. Currently UK bereavement leave for parents after the loss of a child is two weeks. We believe this is not enough time to begin to grieve or plan and have the funeral before returning to work. We want to get the law changed so parents have more time to grieve after such a huge loss.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Introduce a benefits payment card that can be used for essentials only To ensure that welfare money is being spent on essentials to help those in need, introduce a payment card that can only be used for things like food, clothes, school supplies etc. We are concerned that the tax-payer could be funding non-essential items for those who rely on the state for support.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Hold a public inquiry into organised political disinformation & hate speech Launch a public inquiry which investigates the sources, funding & networks behind any organised political disinformation campaigns, examines how hate speech may be weaponised for political gain, and recommends reforms to hold politicians and organisations accountable for undermining democracy.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Cap of £10,000 per individual donor to political parties Currently anyone can give an unlimited amount to political parties. The cross-party Committee on Standards in Public Life has recommended a cap of £10,000 per individual donor.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Lower the age for invites to regular mammograms to 40. Currently the age for routine mammograms to start is 50. I believe this should be lowered to 40.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Motability to maintain higher mileage options for disabled people Require Motability to maintain higher mileage options for disabled people who need to travel more than 30,000 miles in three years and not to proceed with the changes planned for 1 July.  We believe these changes will risk restricting access to work, healthcare and essential independence.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Issue guidance so carers continue care visits for disabled patients in hospital We call on the Government to issue guidance ensuring that hospitals allow care workers to continue their care visits to disabled patients whilst they're in hospital.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Send the navy into the channel to help stop illegal migrants entering the UK Send the navy into channel to help prevent illegal migration from boat crossings.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Review and strengthen mandatory allergy training for all food industry staff We want the Government to review and strengthen allergy training for all food industry staff, including front-of-house and kitchen roles, to ensure safe handling, clear communication, and better protection for allergy sufferers.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Reverse the DfE rules that restrict agency social workers’ pay and movement Reverse new DfE rules that cap agency social worker pay, restrict movement, and impose conditions that push workers into permanent local authority roles.
label: Department for Education

text: Negotiate a youth mobility scheme with the EU We would like the Government to negotiate a youth mobility scheme with the EU. We believe this would expand opportunities for school children and young people to take trips, study, teach and volunteer abroad. We think this should include passport and visa free school trips.
label: Department for Education

text: Hold a referendum: Replace FPTP with Proportional Representation through STV Legislate for a UK-wide referendum on the voting system for House of Commons elections, with two options: Replace First Past the Post with proportional representation using the Single Transferable Vote (STV) system, or keep First Past The Post. Include a potential timetable for implementation.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Change the law to tell parents if their child threatens suicide to a doctor We urge the Government to change the law to give parents the right to be informed when their child presents to a doctor threatening suicide.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Increase funding for MND research Many people are being diagnosed with MND. More Government funding for research is needed.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Mandate that schools use trans students' chosen names and pronouns. Some schools fail to acknowledge the preferred names and pronouns of trans pupils, which can lead to misgendering, distress, and a lack of acceptance in the educational environment.
label: Department for Education

text: Introduce new legal protections for access to purchased video games Introduce new legal protections requiring video games sold in the UK to remain accessible to consumers who have purchased them. This could involve a requirement to provide physical versions or equivalent permanent ownership options for software.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Make 'Tragedy Chanting' at football stadia a specific criminal offence I want the government to legislate to eradicate the vile, triggering act of mocking death on the football terraces of Britain. I wish for the government to make 'Tragedy Chanting' a specific criminal offence
label: Home Office

text: Pause pylon projects and bring in regulations to provide community support We want the Government to pause all pylon projects until regulations have been brought in providing independent support for affected communities. The regulations should provide for an independent consultation on such projects with funding for a community advocate & assistance from technical experts.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Allow Dental Therapist & Hygienist roles (3213) to be filled by migrant workers We call on the government to reverse the decision to classify SOC code 3213 as below RQF Level 6, so that employers can still offer sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa route. If NHS practices are unable to continue to fill vacancies with migrant workers, services may suffer drastically.
label: Home Office

text: Stop the importation of honey bees into GB from the EU via Northern Ireland We want the Government to close what we see as a loophole potentially allowing unchecked honey bee imports from NI into Great Britain. We believe full inspections, destination tracking, bee inspectors in NI, and prioritising local bee breeding are needed to help protect UK bee health.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Make it mandatory for food services to provide detailed carbohydrate information In educational and professional environments where food is served people with T1 Diabetes need to be able to manage their insulin intake with confidence. Carbohydrate information needs to be available in restaurants and in school. It seems discriminatory to not provide this.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Introduce measures to protect digital ride-share drivers from exploitation We believe digital ride share drivers face growing exploitation from platform companies. They can take big commissions while paying little to drivers. Drivers work long hours but can earn less as fares and profits rise. Drivers now demand government action to end this unfair system.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review the EHCP process. Timescales are not being met which is distressing. The EHCP process has set timescales. Some assessments are currently not meeting the 20 week timescale. We believe in some cases it is taking a year or more. We think children in need are being let down by a broken system. We believe more families may need to go to tribunal causing additional stress.
label: Department for Education

text: Stop DWP powers to receive universal credit claimants bank account information I want the parliament to reconsider recent powers is has given DWP under universal credit to require banks to carry out certain checks linked to benefit eligibility for vulnerable people. I want them to consider rescinding these powers especially where they appear to be being used inappropriately.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Abolish the 'tooth tax': remove VAT on children's toothbrushes and toothpaste. Abolish the 20% VAT on children's oral care products like toothbrushes and toothpaste. Make these essential items zero-rated for VAT (like children's clothing). With an estimated 4.3 million children in poverty, this could ease pressure on families and reduce NHS costs from preventable tooth decay.
label: HM Treasury

text: Require GPs to send any patient with a lump for further testing I want the Government to put in place a law that if any lump in any part of the body is found, it will be looked at in a 2 week timeframe. This could be known as Melissa’s Law.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Hold a referendum on the abolition of the British Monarchy We believe that the monarchy, in its current form, is an archaic and cynical institution, deeply entrenched in the fabric of the UK, yet seemingly more focused on preserving its wealth and position rather than representing the values of modern society.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Raise the Personal Allowance for pensioners from £12,570 to at least £25,000 We want the government to raise the Personal Allowance for pensioners (the income you do not have to pay tax on) from the current rate of £12,570 to at least £25,000.
label: HM Treasury

text: Make it legal to carry regulated non-lethal self-defence products. We believe threat of violent crime can make many feel unsafe. We ask Parliament to review weapons laws and allow adults to buy, possess and use regulated non-lethal self-defence items. The framework should cover product approval, licensed retailers, safe-use guidance and heavy penalties for misuse.
label: Home Office

text: Ban all Fox and Stag Hunting with Dogs - including Trail Hunting The Government said they'd ban hunting, we think now is the time to stand by this promise & ban all forms of hunting with dogs. We think allowing trail hunting hasn’t worked to prevent live animals being harmed and killed by hunts.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Add Brazil as an eligible country for driving licence conversion We think it would be beneficial to Brazilians to have their driving licences exchanged for British equivalent licences. We feel this makes sense with the lack of driving tests available in the country and the amount of Brazilians with full Brazilian driving licences living here.
label: Department for Transport

text: Reform the Dangerous Dogs Act (DDA) 1991: keep the public safe We urge the Government to reform the DDA 1991. Whilst S3 applies to all breeds, we believe it's discriminatory due to the existence of S1 which targets specific types based on appearance. We want this replaced with a behaviour-based approach, and to prioritise education for safety and fairness.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Extend the two year limit on theory tests for PDIs and extend pink licence time Change the time limit to allow for all attempts at the pt2 and pt3 before the theory runs out due to long periods of waiting times for Potential Driving Instructors (PDI). Extend the pink licence to reflect waiting times of tests due to backlogs.
label: Department for Transport

text:
Prohibit police officers from having sexual relationships while undercover
 Ban undercover police officers having sexual relationships as part of their undercover work. Ensure full and early disclosure is made to victims.
label: Home Office

text: Funding for specialist police to tackle antisocial behaviour on illegal e-bikes Funding to be made available to police forces to tackle illegal off road electric motorbikes and anti social behaviour. This funding could be used for specialist motorbike drone units designed to catch and prosecute those involved in the behaviours outlined above and make our communities safer.
label: Home Office

text: Referendum on the TV Licence Hold a simple yes or no referendum on whether the TV Licence should be abolished.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Make secondary schools teach about endometriosis, vaginismus & hormonal cycle We urge the Government to require secondary schools to teach about endometriosis, vaginismus, & the hormonal cycle. We feel this will increase accountability for the lack of education on women's health—both in health sector research and educational systems—by raising awareness.
label: Department for Education

text: Pause and review the net zero renewable energy development drive. Review net zero, and the associated planning practice and policy across central and devolved governments of the UK. We think local environment and local communities should be given greater priority in decisions.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Require panels of lay people to review abattoir CCTV footage for potential abuse Since 2018, it's been mandatory for CCTV to be installed on all areas of abattoirs where animals remain alive. The recordings made being available to "official vets" only. This has not ended reports of animals being abused prior to slaughter, most of these reports coming from unofficial sources
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Ban LED vehicle headlights or regulate bulb wattage We think LED headlights are dangerous and need banning, or a lower limit on the wattage of the bulbs in all vehicles needs to be enforced. We are concerned that LED headlights are far too bright and blinding to oncoming traffic and could easily cause an accident.
label: Department for Transport

text: Drivers who hit cats in their car should stop and take the cat to a vet To change the law: require drivers who accidently hit a cat in their car to stop and take the cat to the vet.
label: Home Office

text: Establish a Royal Commission on assisted dying The Government should establish a royal commission on assisted dying to deeply consider the matter.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Exempt Global Talent and 'highest skilled worker' visas from 10-year ILR rule Exempt all existing TIER 1 high-skilled visa holders and their replacement visa types (including Global Talent, Investor, Innovator Founder, Entrepreneur), and their dependents from the 10-year ILR rule. Preserve 3 and 5-year ILR and 12-month citizenship timelines
label: Home Office

text: Change free childcare scheme to direct payments into Tax-Free Childcare accts We believe the 30 hours free childcare has failed, and that it doesn’t take account of variety of needs or types of settings available. There are reports that settings are starting to pull out. We want the Government to offer a subsidy paid directly into Tax-Free Childcare account for parents.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reinstate study visas for Sudanese students and fully protect their education The UK suspended Sudanese study visas citing a surge in asylum claims. However, we believe most students are genuine and law-abiding. We think this blanket ban denies education, punishes lawful students, and disrupts futures. Parliament must reinstate visas and protect students’ right to study.
label: Department for Education

text: Implement a 2% wealth tax on individuals with net assets exceeding £10 million Create an asset register and apply a 2% annual tax on individuals with net assets over £10 million. Introduce safeguards, like an exit tax to prevent assets being moved offshore. We think these measures, particularly for real estate, would help ensure the policy is fair and effective.
label: HM Treasury

text: Expand home university fee eligibility to UK residents without settled status This petition is to make UK residents regardless of immigration status or timeline eligible for home university fees. All immigrants living in the UK should have the right to a fair education at higher level in England.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund Long Covid compensation scheme Fund a long covid compensation scheme (like the covid vaccine compensation) for people who have caught covid and are now living with long covid, some with debilitating effects.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Approve and implement the EHRC guidance on meaning of sex in the Equality Act The Supreme Court has issued a ruling relating to the definition of sex in the Equality Act. We want the Government to immediately approve and implement the resulting guidance produced by EHRC. We think the delay is untenable.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Require airlines offer alternatives to boarding passes displayed on smartphones The Government should require all airlines to let passengers travel without mobile app or smartphone. Passengers must be allowed to print boarding passes before arriving at the airport, unless all passengers, including app users, are required to check in at the airport for document or visa checks.
label: Department for Transport

text: Require bars/pubs to have CCTV covering areas surrounding toilets I believe it should be a requirement for CCTV to cover all areas of the venue. This includes stairwells/corridors leading up to toilet facilities to monitor the safety of customers.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Require civil harassment orders to be disclosed in enhanced DBS checks I’m calling on the government to close the DBS loophole by ensuring civil harassment orders, such as court-issued undertakings, are disclosed on Enhanced DBS checks to better protect children and vulnerable people from individuals under legal restrictions.
label: Home Office

text: Make Drama a mandatory subject in the National Curriculum for Key Stage 3 We ask the Government to make Drama a mandatory subject within the National Curriculum for all pupils in Key Stage 3 in England, and provide appropriate curriculum time, guidance, and support for its delivery.
label: Department for Education

text: Make Addressing the Climate Emergency a Statutory duty for Councils We want the UK government to introduce legislation that makes addressing the climate emergency a statutory duty for all local authorities. By legally requiring councils to prioritise climate action, we think this would ensure that vital environmental policies become integral to local governance.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Review of Gender Identity and LGBT Education in Schools Initiate a formal review of how gender identity and LGBT content is introduced and taught in state-funded schools.
label: Department for Education

text: Remove VAT on veterinary fees for pets Following reports of some pet owners not being able to afford vet fees, we believe it is time for the Government to remove VAT from veterinary fees for pets so that it is no longer charged on animal health care which is essential for their health.
label: HM Treasury

text: Lower the age that someone can be considered a victim of domestic abuse The law defines domestic abuse as abusive behaviour by one person towards another, where both people are 16 or over. We think this should be changed. Our daughter Holly, aged 15, was murdered by her ex-boyfriend and we think this case should have been looked at in the context of domestic abuse.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Referendum on whether to abolish the Welsh Parliament I believe a referendum in Wales is needed on whether to abolish the Welsh Parliament.
label: Wales Office

text: Create secure safeguarding children’s risk register Create a safeguarding register to which police, education, health, councils and other agencies can input information they collect about people who may pose a risk to children. Parents should be able to request information from this register, with independent oversight.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Remove NPPF Paragraph 11(d) and Footnote 8 to Help Protect Green Spaces Remove Paragraph 11(d) and Footnote 8 from the National Planning Policy Framework to help stop developments proceeding where they may be contrary to local plans. This would help restore a genuinely community-led planning system and strengthen protection for green spaces.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Fund a national awareness campaign of suicide in the construction sector We want an open and honest debate about this silent killer which we feel has been ignored in the sector. We want heightened public awareness, as we believe current legislation is not fit for purpose.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text:
Reset the Windrush Compensation Scheme with free legal assistance for victims We call on the Government to:
1. Move the Windrush Compensation Scheme out of the Home Office to a fully independent body.
2. Provide guaranteed, non-means-tested legal assistance for all claimants.
3. Expand the scheme to include all losses, like military pensions.
label: Home Office

text: Invoke Article 15 of the ECHR- to help tackle illegal migration Notify the Secretary-General of the Council of Europe of a "public emergency threatening the life of the nation". Effective immediately.
label: Home Office

text: Legally recognise non-binary as a gender Non-binary isn’t a legally recognised gender in the UK. We urge the Government to legally recognise non-binary as a gender and people who identify as non-binary in the UK. This proposal would include an X marker on UK passports for non-binary people.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Referendum on UK sovereignty over the Chagos Islands. We call on the Government to hold a referendum on the transfer of UK sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius. We believe the Government should consult the public on continued UK sovereignty over the Chagos Islands.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Fund supported living for all autistic adults We call on the government to fund supported living for autistic adults and including those without intellectual disabilities (ID) who cannot sustain education, training, or employment without specialist help.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Require large housing development applications to be made as full applications Require all large (25+) housing development applications to be full detailed applications, not outline which feature an artists impression and vague description of what’s planned. The current system can prevent crucial infrastructure need from being correctly assessed, e.g Schools, health, transport
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Fund more training for police in dog control matters. We think more funding is needed for police officers to be thoroughly trained in dog behaviour and handling. We feel more training in expert handling, i.e. using tranquiliser guns, could prevent distress or danger to dogs and the public. We think that training in breed identification is essential.
label: Home Office

text: Establish dedicated independent statutory SEND regulator for Local Authorities Establish an independent statutory dedicated SEND regulator with powers to monitor, investigate and enforce Local Authorities’ compliance with their legal duties towards children and young people with SEND.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Make organ donation consent made prior to someone’s death binding We call on the Government to legislate so that a person’s registered decision to donate is legally binding and cannot be overridden by family members after the person’s death.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review the Access to Work Scheme Investigate how the Access to Work scheme is operating. This review should ensure the scheme offers fair and timely support for all disabled people seeking employment.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text:
Ban client side scanning (CSS) of private communications on personal devices We ask the government to:
- Prohibit any requirement for client side scanning on consumer devices.
- Reaffirm its commitment to safeguarding democratic freedoms, protecting human rights, and preserving the security of its citizens’ digital communications.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Ban holiday companies from charging higher prices in the school holidays We think the government needs to ban holiday companies from charging higher prices for trips and flights during school holidays. We think it's shocking that nothing has already been done about this. Some families struggle to afford to take their children on holiday, especially abroad.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Align pay for general practice nurses with Agenda for Change framework Align pay scales and reviews for general practice nurses in England with the Agenda for Change framework. Currently I believe we have unfair pay and unfair value for those of us trying to prevent the emergencies and hospitalisations.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text:
Allow artistic swimming as a GCSE and A-level option for PE coursework. Current coursework options for GCSE and A-Level PE include many options, but do not recognise Artistic Swimming as one, even though it is a skilled Olympic sport.

Not having it as an option prevents artistic swimmers from being able to count their specialist sport as part of their skills.
label: Department for Education

text: Adopt the Yogyakarta Principles into UK law to ensure LGBTQ+ rights are upheld Amend domestic legislation to incorporate the Yogyakarta Principles as binding human rights standards, require government agencies to align policies with sexual orientation and gender identity rights, and allocate resources for training, monitoring, and civil society engagement.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Call for a Public Inquiry into Systemic Issues in Children’s Social Care Some families report treatment received from social workers during assessments (etc) is often punitive, blame-based, & shaped by narratives that are narrow, biased, oppressive, & lack context. We feel assessments frequently fail to reflect the full circumstances.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Prevent the prosecution of veterans for historical offences. I would like the government to prevent members and former members of the armed forces from being prosecuted for alleged historical offences, sometimes decades after the events in question take place.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: New independent, judge-led national Inquiry into the scandal of the Rape Gangs We think the current grooming gangs inquiry has failed. Several survivors have resigned from its panel and there have been calls for the resignation of the Safeguarding Minister. Two prospective Chairs have walked away from the process. The new public inquiry must be fully independent.
label: Home Office

text: Launch a public inquiry into the SEND system in England We call on the Government to launch a statutory public inquiry, under the Inquiries Act 2005, into the provision of SEND services in England following whistleblower allegations, which have led to wider concerns from many about the existence of systemic failures within SEND services.
label: Department for Education

text: Impose a lifetime driving ban for causing death or injury by dangerous driving Any driver/rider who causes death or injury by dangerous driving should receive a lifetime ban from driving/riding. If subsequently caught driving/riding, they should receive a substantial custodial sentence.
label: Home Office

text: Allow care worker visa holders to change employer We want the government to replace the current visa scheme for care workers, where care worker is bound to the employers who have sponsored their visa, to a new scheme which allows the visa holders switch jobs freely still within the health sector without the risk of losing their visa.
label: Home Office

text: Do not introduce pay-per-mile road charging for UK drivers Many people depend on driving for work, education, and family life, with no viable public transport. We think a pay-per-mile tax would unfairly hit many families, shift workers and parents supporting children’s sports.
label: Department for Transport

text:
Compensate people excluded from Government COVID support schemes 1. Acknowledge the financial hardship faced by taxpayers excluded from government support during COVID

2. Provide fair & equitable redress to those taxpayer who received nothing
label: Cabinet Office

text: Cap Child Maintenance payments at £200 per child We want Child Maintenance payments to be capped to a maximum of £200 per child – rather than to be based on pre-tax income – and to be reduced according to the proportion of days’ care given by the paying parent.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Publish list of all accommodation used for illegal immigrants & asylum seekers Publish a full list of all hotels and other facilities currently used to house asylum seekers and illegal immigrants, broken down by region and local authority, including numbers accommodated and cost to the taxpayer.
label: Home Office

text: Introduce measures to protect women at risk of domestic violence Mandatory Real-Time Domestic Violence History Checks: public bodies including the police, courts, probation services and local authorities must check for known domestic violence or coercive control histories before allowing shared housing, child contact, or release from custody.
label: Home Office

text: Ban international licence holders from driving if they fail UK driving test Pass a law where if international licence holders fail their UK driving test, they will be banned from continuing to drive in the UK unaccompanied as we believe they have no demonstrated competence.
label: Department for Transport

text: End the Safety Valve programme and provide funding to cover SEND deficits We ask that the Safety Valve programme, which gives funding to local authorities who put plans in place to reduce school deficits, is ended. We believe it incentivises cutting support for vulnerable children, and we want funding to cover local authority deficits to be provided without condition.
label: Department for Education

text: Ensure the Red Arrows fly a British-designed and built aircraft The Red Arrows represent British engineering, skill and national identity. We believe this iconic team should continue to showcase British aerospace excellence by flying a new British-designed and built aircraft when their existing aircraft are retired.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Legalise Regulated Non-Lethal Self-Defence Tools Rising knife crime and violent attacks can leave citizens vulnerable when police cannot arrive instantly. While some self-defence can be legal, the public lacks practical tools. Legalise self defence tools such as pepper spray to help save lives of men, women and children.
label: Home Office

text: Allow Registered Nursing Associates to vaccinate under PGDs Please update the Human Medicines Regulations 2012 to allow Registered Nursing Associates to vaccinate under PGDs. This modernisation would boost vaccination capacity, reduce pressure on nurses and prescribers, and strengthen protection amid falling herd immunity.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Scrap the TV Licence Scrap the TV Licence and make BBC pay per view
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Introduce statutory paid leave for 1 parent if child too ill for school/nursery We call on the UK Government to give one parent per household a statutory right to paid leave when their child is too ill to attend nursery or school, with pay and requirements equivalent to Statutory Sick Pay (SSP).
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Cap Child Maintenance: 10% of a paying parent’s basic salary excluding overtime We want the Government to cap child maintenance payments at 10% of a paying parent's basic salary, excluding overtime. We also propose a minimum payment of £210 per month for parents in full-time employment – which is roughly 10% of the minimum wage based off a 40hr week, minus any deductions.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Make those convicted for domestic abuse ineligible for early release I want the Government to change the law so that people convicted of serious domestic abuse offences must serve their full prison sentence instead of being released early.
label: Home Office

text: Increase the incentive for employers employing an apprentice to £2,000 Raise the employer incentive for employing an apprentice to £2,000, as it stands the current £1000 incentive split over 365 days equates to just over £19 a week.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Higher tax on income of £400,000, and exit tax if they move to another country Tax people with an income of 400,000+ more severely.
label: HM Treasury

text: Financially redress 3.8m taxpayers excluded from Covid-19 financial support We want the Government to establish a fair financial redress scheme for the 3.8 million taxpayers excluded from Covid-19 financial support, reflecting the support received by comparable taxpayers and businesses.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Require all think tanks to disclose their donors, funding, and media spending Research bodies and representation of specialist interests is important when making policy. However, think tanks go beyond merely brainstorming ideas and presenting data and arguments. They can push stories and PR to media outlets to influence the public before policy is made.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Seek to negotiate a freedom of movement arrangement with the EU   We call on the UK Government to seek to negotiate and secure UK participation in the EU freedom of movement framework or equivalent reciprocal arrangements. This would allow eligible UK residents and European nationals to live, work, study and travel freely between regions.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Mandate GPS location, time details and photo for all parcel delivery companies Mandate that all parcel delivery companies provide recipients with GPS location recorded at delivery, time, estimated GPS accuracy & a map showing the delivery location alongside the proof-of-delivery photo. This should only be available to the intended recipient and comply with UK data protection.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Detain all illegal migrants until a decision is made over their status We urge the Government to immediately detain all migrants who enter the UK illegally. We believe this will make our towns and cities safer.
label: Home Office

text: Make it mandatory for drivers to provide Driving Licence to get insurance We request the government to take immediate steps to amend existing legislation to mandate the provision of valid driving licence details by all individuals, irrespective of their nationality or immigration status, when applying for vehicle insurance.
label: Department for Transport

text: Stop allowing the US to use British bases for any action against Iran The UK claims that it is only taking defensive action in the Israel-US & Iran war. We think that letting the US use British bases does not align with this claim, that it is not in our interest and does not support peace in the region. Stop the US use of bases in all capacities, including defensive.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Harsher punishments for sex offenders and bans near schools We urge the government to enforce harsher penalties for sex offenders, including longer sentences, mandatory rehab, and a ban on living near schools or child-centric areas.
label: Home Office

text: Criminalise pretending to be a member of the armed forces or a veteran I want the Government to make it a specific criminal offence for any person to pretend to be serving or to have served in His Majesty’s Armed Forces.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Ban the sale of catapults and carrying catapults in public We urge the Government to make carrying catapults in public places illegal, so that the police can arrest those carrying, especially in areas of known wildlife. We also urge the Government to ban the sale of catapults the UK, so they are not so easily accessible to children!
label: Home Office

text: Cap airport drop-off and pick-up fees at £5 across UK airports Introduce legislation to cap airport drop-off and pick-up charges at £5 across all UK airports and prevent any further increases. The Government should regulate these charges to ensure they remain fair and reasonable for passengers, drivers and transport providers.
label: Department for Transport

text: Seek to rejoin the European Union Single Market and start discussions now I would like the UK Government to start discussions with the European Union to seek to rejoin the EU Single Market and to make rejoining the EU Single Market a priority for the UK Government, and to set itself the aim of rejoining the Single Market within 12 months.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Ban solar panels on farmland & require new build homes to have solar panels Ban ground-mounted solar panels on fertile farmland and make it law that all new-build houses have solar panels installed. We think solar panels should be installed on rooftops, car parks and farm buildings, which should be subsidised by Government. Farmers could benefit from the additional income.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Add Morocco to the list of 'designated countries' for driving licence exchange Driving licence holders from 'designated countries' can exchange their non-GB driving licence for a British licence. We urge the UK government to add Morocco to this list of designated countries.
label: Department for Transport

text: Make defibrillators, bleed kits and their cabinets VAT free for all I would ask the government to make the purchase of defibrillators, bleed kits and the cabinets they are housed in all VAT free. Certain organisations can purchase defibrillators with no VAT, I ask the government to make this the case for everyone and extend it further to include bleed kits.
label: HM Treasury

text: Keep the Graduate Route (PSW Visa) at 2 years for international students We call on the UK Government to keep the full 2-year Graduate Route (3 years for PhDs), dependant rights for taught postgraduates, and consult student communities before future changes that could impact international education and mobility.
label: Home Office

text: Teach severe autism, non-verbal needs and sensory crises in PSHE⁠ We want the UK Government to mandate teaching about severe autism, non-verbal communication, sensory overload, and dysregulated behavior in the national PSHE curriculum.
label: Department for Education

text: Urge Israel to permit regular humanitarian access to all Palestinian prisoners We believe Israel is obliged to respect international humanitarian law under the 1949 Geneva Conventions which includes facilitating access by the International Committee of the Red Cross to all Palestinian detainees. We feel it's unacceptable that Israel continues to refuse access.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Make destroying or vandalising the Union Flag a criminal offence We feel that our flag and its colours represents us as a nation and is what our ancestors fought two World Wars and died for.
label: Home Office

text: Add intersex to the Equality Act as a protected characteristic We want the government to make sex variations a protected characteristic under the Equality Act.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Create an independent clean air monitoring system for incinerators We want the government U.K. wide to create an independent ‘clean air monitoring system’ linked to the Environment Agency who can enforce any and all breaches where they occur, for communities near incinerators.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Fund the creation of a single National Police Trust using proceeds of crime We urge the Government to fund the creation of a National Police Trust with a committee that oversees grant funding for police charities and not-for-profit organisations which support the UK's police workers and their families including the bereaved.
label: Home Office

text:
Automatically suspend PR when a parent is convicted of child murder/serious harm Current legislation ensures the automatic suspension of parental responsibility (PR) in cases where one parent murders another.
 
However, there is currently NO automatic suspension of PR when a parent is convicted of seriously harming or murdering their child.
label: Home Office

text: Criminalise homophobia and transphobia We urge the Government to criminalise all homophobia and transphobia by introducing fines to punish transphobia and homophobia. We think these fines should be between £75 to £100 and should incrementally increase if the person is repeatedly transphobic or homophobic.
label: Home Office

text: Create a national welfare team to oversee kennels holding seized dogs We want the Government to create an independent national welfare team to monitor kennels used by police forces. This should include checking that staff are trained to meet the welfare standards in the Animal Welfare Act 2006 and reporting those who fail to meet those standards for prosecution.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Prioritise NHS training based on experience, not immigration status Amend the Medical Training (Prioritisation) Bill to prioritise doctors based on length and quality of NHS service, not merely immigration status, ensuring experienced NHS doctors are fairly considered for specialty training - overall supporting workforce retention and patient safety.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Add more female scientists to the National Curriculum We would like the Department for Education to add more female scientists to the National Curriculum and make it mandatory for every exam board to include them in the specification.
label: Department for Education

text: Give parents the right to claim tax refunds for children's education expenses As education is compulsory and fundamental in a society, parents should receive tax refunds for taxes paid on uniform, materials, tutoring, and school fees during all mandatory years education (5-16). It could help state school pupils, homeschooled and private educated children.
label: HM Treasury

text: Referendum on English Independence We call for a referendum on full English independence from the UK due to what we believe is the enormous financial burden which the nations of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland place on tax-payers in England.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Public inquiry into the selling of Family Asset Protection Trusts. We think some people are being mis-sold "Family Asset Protection Trusts". We think the Government needs to protect citizens, introduce harsher punishments for miss-selling, and support victims.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Mandate Ethical Rehoming for Lab and Breeding Animals by 2025 Mandate rehoming of lab & breeding unit animals as default by end of 2025. We want partnering with accredited rehoming orgs & a rehoming database, funded by licence fees & grants. We want to end unnecessary euthanasia & independent outcome monitoring for an ethical future.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Include Martial arts as an individual sport in the Examinable PE GCSE Broaden the GCSE PE practical criteria to include martial arts. These disciplines require immense technical skill, physical fitness, and mental discipline. Including them ensures that dedicated student-athletes in these fields are not disadvantaged compared to those in traditional sports.
label: Department for Education

text: Update building regulations to require more women’s toilets in public buildings. Update building regulations to require more women’s toilet facilities in public buildings, taking into account longer usage times, children accompanying mothers, and delays caused for others waiting. Apply updated standards to new buildings and major refurbishments.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Remove non-qualifying status for leasehold flats We call for the Government to amend the Building Safety Act to remove the qualification status once the remediation has been done and the EWS1 has been issued. We believe the qualification status is totally irrelevant once the remediation is done.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Mandate CCTV in any educational setting that cares for children with SEND Children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities should be protected in education settings at all times. We believe there should be CCTV to ensure that the right care is always given. We think this needs to be regulated both in specialist provisions and in mainstream school settings.
label: Department for Education

text: Include more sports options for GCSE PE I feel that a lot of the sports chosen for GCSE PE are not available in more deprived areas, limiting the options for working class children to consider taking a GCSE in sport.
label: Department for Education

text: Ban all gambling ads from social media, TV and all other platforms We urge the government to ban gambling ads across all platforms (Social Media, Youtube, TV, Radio, etc). We believe that these adverts fuel addiction, harming individuals, families, and future generations. Gambling addiction is a serious public health issue with devastating and lasting consequences.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Increase funding for rare cancer research & treatment I was diagnosed with a rare cancer in 2022, since then I have met other patients in the same situation.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund Specialist Care & Automatic NHS Continuing Care for dementia patients We urge the UK Government to provide funding to ensure every dementia patient stays under specialist care and receives automatic NHS Continuing Healthcare. We think no one should face the heartbreak of dementia without proper care, support, and compassion.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require dating apps to ensure ID and DBS checks on users & ban violent offenders I believe to better protect the public from offenders, the Government should legislate to require dating apps and websites to make it mandatory for users to undergo ID and DBS checks to open an account, and require them to implement permanent bans on users who have committed violent offences.
label: Home Office

text: Change interim driving disqualifications from 6 months to until sentencing. We think anyone convicted of a driving offence should have a full driving ban until sentencing, with no exceptions, so there is no chance of that person being able to drive whilst waiting for sentencing.
label: Department for Transport

text: Reform Child Maintenance Service, strengthen processes to protect paying parent Reform CMS by calculating maintenance using net income, tax maintenance as income for the receiving parent, allowing reductions for denied contact, mandatory auditable arrears explanations, cease liability at 16, ensure due process before deductions, prosecute false declarations by either parent.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Review regulation around hysterectomies in private hospitals We believe there should be a review of the regulation around hysterectomies in private hospitals, to ensure that the hospitals have all necessary equipment and appropriately trained staff to deal with emergency complications. If they don't, they shouldn't be able to do it.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Create a 'Homes for Palestine' Sponsorship and Visa Scheme We want the Government to start a scheme that allows Palestinian people living in Gaza or the West Bank to obtain entry to the UK under sponsorship, independent of whether they have family in this country or not.
label: Home Office

text: Grant UK citizenship to anyone with Indefinite Leave to Remain or Settled Status Some political parties are proposing deportation or a change of rights to people with ILR or settled status. Millions of people could be affected.
label: Home Office

text: Make accurate medicine barcodes (GTIN) mandatory to protect patient safety Errors in medicine barcodes (GTIN) mean pharmacists and hospitals bypass safety systems and rely on manual checks. We believe this increases risks for patients and wastes NHS time and money. Making accurate barcode data mandatory would protect patients, reduce errors and save millions.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text:
Continue funding Level 7 NHS Apprenticeships -Clinical Associate Psychologists We are asking the Government to continue providing funding for the L7 Apprenticeship course “Clinical Associate in Psychology”

This is in response to discussions being held within Government regarding plans for the Government to stop/change how some level 7 apprenticeship courses are funded.
label: Department for Education

text: Reform UK Energy Standing Charges Shift all non-infrastructure costs off electricity standing charges onto company profits or general taxation. Require Ofgem to separate policy levies from true network costs, make suppliers absorb bailout and policy expenses, and ensure foreign-owned firms reinvest profits into UK infrastructure.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Replace 'hysterectomy' with 'uterectomy' in NHS patient materials Direct NHS England to adopt 'uterectomy' as the primary term in all patient-facing materials, consent forms and clinical guidelines, replacing 'hysterectomy' - a term we believe is rooted in misogyny, not anatomy.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Debate NetZero policy so UK gas production isn’t replaced with foreign imports. The UK Government should review its Energy & Climate policies to ensure they don’t increase the importation of hydrocarbons, simply outsourcing emissions. This practice would contradict the spirit of the UK's commitment to achieving Net Zero by 2050 and undermine global climate leadership.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Do not roll out digital IDs We do not want digital IDs. We are concerned about total control by the government. Do not spend our money on this system!
label: Home Office

text:
Legalise recreational cannabis & release those convicted of cannabis offences. Change existing laws to allow for the use of cannabis.
Review all those convicted of cannabis offences, and release all non-violent offenders to appropriate community placements.
Enforce an 18 or over stance for cannabis use (excluding prescribed use).
label: Home Office

text: Fund high-quality, non-partisan political and citizenship teaching resources Youth Parliament UK urges the Government to invest in high-quality, non-partisan lesson resources that any teacher can use. It’s vital students are taught the skills for informed and active participation in society, but too often teachers don’t have the support, leaving students without consistency.
label: Department for Education

text: Scrap Mandatory Advice and Guidance for Primary Care Referrals On the 1st April 2026, NHS England introduced mandatory advice and guidance for GPs and primary care professionals. This means clinicians must get advice and guidance from secondary care colleagues before referring patients, which we think removes their ability to make direct referrals.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Introduce new rules and protections from development in rural green heartlands We believe that the South West — Devon, Somerset, Dorset, and Cornwall — stands at a breaking point. We are concerned that our cherished green fields, productive farmland, and close-knit rural communities are being swallowed by unchecked urban expansion.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Include Child Maintenance as Income in Universal Credit and Means-Tested Benefit Child maintenance payment is not counted as income for Universal Credit, allowing some to receive maintenance payments and benefits. At the same time, paying parents must meet their obligations even where those payments reduce their overall household income below the Universal Credit threshold.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: More funding to diagnose & support individuals with ADHD & provide training  Provide funding for spotting and diagnosing ADHD in adults and children, and for support and medication to be easily accessible upon diagnosis. We believe funding should also be provided to educate medical & education professionals to help eradicate stigma/stereotyping.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Only provide foreign aid for national disasters and emergencies We spend 0.5% of Gross National Income (GNI) on Foreign Aid a year. The Autumn Budget confirmed the UK would spend £13.3 billion in aid for 2024/25 and £13.7 billion in 2025/26.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Form a centralised microchip & DNA database for dog breeding, care, and welfare  We believe that the practices of both licensed and unlicensed breeders have resulted in many dogs and puppies suffering from serious health and welfare issues.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Start a government "do not drop litter" campaign We think the streets are overrun with litter. We think we need a national litter campaign to stop people dropping litter and inform them about prosecution if they're caught.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Ban Fur Imports into the UK We ask the Government to ban the import and sale of all fur products in the UK. Fur farming is banned here due to cruelty, yet imports support suffering abroad. We believe that this ban would align UK laws with ethical and environmental responsibility, closing the loophole that fuels the fur trade.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Grant Chagossians a referendum to decide the future of Chagos Islands Grant Chagossians a referendum to decide the future of Chagos Islands, making any arrangement on sovereignty of the Chagos islands subject to a consultative referendum by the Chagossian diaspora living in the UK, commonwealth, and overseas territories.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Review regulation of animal boarding and licensing conditions A review should consider introducing a new framework for paid pet care including minimum standards, more efficient checking of licences and enforcement of online platforms. There should be more alignment between devolved governments. These changes could be known as Molly's Law.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Fund NHS dyslexia assessments Dyslexia affects many people yet NHS assessments are unavailable. This leaves access limited to those who can pay or navigate complex systems. The government must ensure free, early assessments for all to support education, wellbeing, and equal opportunity.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Abolish council tax and fund local councils from national taxation We call on the Government to abolish council tax and replace it with fair funding for local councils through national taxation, as we feel council tax has become unaffordable for many households during the cost of living crisis.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Categorise all air rifles as firearms and require owners to be licenced Currently some air rifles can be purchased by anyone over the age of 18. Every year wild animals and pets die or are permanently injured by air rifle bullets. All air rifles should be treated as firearms and subject to the same rules as owning a gun. They are not toys.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Amend microchip rules to prevent stolen pets being re-registered without consent We call on Defra to amend The Microchipping of Cats and Dogs (England) Regulations 2023. Databases must not transfer keeper registration for a lost or stolen pet if the original keeper is contactable and has not given consent. This could stop thieves or finders re-registering pets in their name.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Review bereavement policies for pupils sitting GCSE and A-level exams I want the government to review the grading and expectations set by the Joint Council for Qualifications, for pupils that have lost a close relative immediately before starting their GCSE or A-level exams.
label: Department for Education

text: Reform the British Spouse Visa System Many British citizens and their spouses face huge costs, with the initial visa application costing £4,951(including the healthcare surcharge), the extension application priced at £3,845.50, and the settlement (ILR) application at £2,885. Over five years, families may have to pay more than £11,000.
label: Home Office

text: Require processed meat products to have a carcinogenic warning label We call on the UK Government to introduce mandatory, front-of-pack cancer warning labels on processed meat products sold to inform consumers that regular consumption can increase the risk of bowel cancer.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Allow elderly disabled people to claim the state pension early We think that any disabled person aged 60 who has been unemployed for at least 5 years should be given the choice to retire and claim the state pension immediately.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Fund free access for all home educated children to GCSE examinations Fund free access for all home educated children to GCSE examinations. Access should be allowed through a private exam centre or other education setting. The cost should fall to government, not on the parents or carers.
label: Department for Education

text: Regulate the brightness and type of vehicle headlights allowed Online discourse indicates that a growing number of drivers are adversely impacted by the proliferation of excessively bright LED headlights, which impair the vision other road users.
label: Department for Transport

text: Increase the tax free overnight allowance for HGV and PCV drivers to £50 We ask the government to increase the overnight allowance for nights away from home creature comforts. This allowance has not increased since 2014 and even if it matched inflation would now be £45.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review the NHS decision to make smear testing every 5 years if HPV negative  The NHS are changing the smear tests for women aged 25-49 from every three years to every five years if they are HPV negative. We think this should be reviewed. Some women get cervical cancer without having HPV. We think women are going to suffer as a result of this change.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Provide funding to the NHS to offer full STI screening at beginning of pregnancy This petition is calling for the Government to provide funding to the NHS so that full STI screening can be offered as part of routine testing at the beginning of a pregnancy.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ensure Section 20B sets deadline for final service charge after notification Establish a statutory 6-month deadline for final service charge invoices following any notification under Section 20B of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Restrict voting rights to British citizens who are long-term residents I would like the Government to restrict voting rights to eligible British citizens who have resided in the UK for a minimum of ten years.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Temporary Ban on agricultural use of sewage cake In order to protect our land, we’re seeking a temporary ban of the agricultural use of sewage cake until better testing and treatment of waste can be proven. We call on all farmers after this harvest to refuse to accept any more until things change.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Do not bring in the new Ecodesign Regulations on tumble dryers in the UK Don't make heat pump tumble dryers effectively the only new models legally permitted for sale. The proposed ban undermines the purpose of the UK Right to Repair Regulations. Set up an independent taskforce of experienced appliance engineers to assess the cost/benefit ratio of the ban on UK consumers
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Capital punishment for officials guilty of treason, corruption, misconduct We believe for too long our government and institutions have had officials who don't have the country's or the public’s best interest at heart. We think serious action is needed to prevent treason, corruption, and misconduct in public office. Those found guilty should face capital punishment.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Impose Financial Sanctions Against The UAE There have been a number of reports that the UAE is supporting the Rapid Support Forces in Sudan. I would like for the UK government to impose sanctions against the UAE because of this. I hope these sanctions could help allow peace to reign in the region.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Ban councils from discharging housing duty if person refuses long distance offer Ban local councils from designating people as “intentionally homeless” and relieving themselves of their duty if someone refuses an offer of housing more than 90 minutes away. Councils should be able to make long distance offers, but such offers would not discharge their duty.
label: Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

text: Licence the sale of Class F3 and above fireworks & only allow sales at set times I'd like the Government to bring in legislation to license the sale of the bigger classes of fireworks and only allow sale of the bigger fireworks at specific times ( Bonfire Night, Xmas, Dewali ect) to stop the anti social use of the bigger fireworks that continues all year around
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Launch a review of UK fishing laws We urge the Government to launch a review of fishing laws, which looks into giving UK boats and anglers fair access, restricting foreign super-trawlers and fish stock management. We believe protecting our waters, rebuilding fish populations, and supporting coastal communities should be the priority.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Mandate offer of Group B Streptococcus screening for all pregnant women Mandate offer of Group B Strep (GBS) screening for all pregnant women at 35–37 weeks, provide funding for NHS-wide access to testing and antibiotics during labour to those who test positive to help prevent serious newborn infections.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Explicitly exclude sex offenders from accessing children’s data under CWS Bill We call on the government to add a category of exclusion to the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill to prevent child sex offenders from accessing the increased amount of data that could be collected stored and shared if the Bill becomes an Act amounting in some cases to a child’s daily whereabouts
label: Department for Education

text: Require all ICBs to offer 3 NHS-funded IVF cycles We call on the Government to require all ICBs to offer 3 NHS-funded IVF cycles. We want an end to what we believe is a postcode lottery we believe fertility treatment should be fair, equal, and based on medical need, not where you live. We believe everyone deserves a chance to build a family
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Sever diplomatic, trade, and other relations with Israel and impose sanctions Government should sever diplomatic relations with Israel, suspend all imports from and exports to Israel (including of military equipment & components), impose tight economic sanctions, cancel any contracts with Israeli firms (including UK subsidiaries) & cease any intelligence sharing with Israel.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Review and strengthen protections for children online Review protections for children online. This should include how social media companies are held responsible for identifying grooming behaviour, reporting suspected exploitation, and improving safeguards to prevent predators contacting children.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Recognise Police Special Constables under s50 of the Employment Rights Act 1996. Special Constables are fully trained and warranted officers, who hold regular employment and on their days off join local police teams to be a visible presence, make arrests, deter crime and enhance safety – all without pay.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: First aid kits a legal requirement for public use at public venues Make it a legal requirement for cafés, restaurants, and public venues to have an adequate first aid kit accessible for public emergencies and not only legally required for employee use. Currently it is ‘recommended’ a first aid kit is available for the public but it isn’t a requirement.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Fund local community litter crews and fund education around littering Create and fund local “Litter Crews” in every community to help reduce litter, improve public spaces, and run education programmes that encourage people not to litter.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Require DBS checks for all staff in Soft Play centres. We want the Government to amend safeguarding legislation so that all staff working in Soft Play environments are required to undergo DBS checks, ensuring consistent child protection standards across all childcare and play settings, and closing what we see as a clear safeguarding gap in current law.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Make genetic testing available from 12 weeks pregnant. Make genetic testing an option from 12 weeks pregnant.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Create a public register of domestic abuse offenders We think that domestic abusers should be put on a register like sex offenders are. We want there to be an easily accessible website where individuals can search by either name or location, to find those who has been convicted of domestic abuse against previous partners.
label: Home Office

text: Pass a law that triggers an early General Election via a public petition Right now, only the Prime Minister can request an early General Election. We believe the public should also have a clear democratic mechanism to do so.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Create new route to appeal CPS decisions to drop rape or child abuse cases We want the Government to create a new and more affordable route for victims and families to appeal a Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) decision to drop rape and child abuse cases. This should apply to both current and past cases.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban the manufacture, import and sale of Rawhide as a dog treat Rawhide dog chews can pose a serious risk to animal welfare, such as choking, blockages and illness. We ask the UK Government to ban the manufacture, import and sale of rawhide dog chews. Safer alternatives exist, and a ban could protect pets and prevent avoidable harm.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
