text: Mandatory Prison for Drivers Who Conceal Accidents or Obstruct Investigations We are seeking a minimum sentence of a jail term for drivers who are proven to have purposely looked to avoid justice after killing someone in a road traffic collision.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban the sale and use of high-frequency and ultrasonic animal deterrents We call on the Government to introduce legislation to ban the sale, supply and use of all ultrasonic and high-frequency sound devices marketed or used as animal deterrents. These products should be removed from sale and existing units withdrawn from use entirely.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Suspend fuel duty and VAT on fuel until the Iran conflict ends Suspend fuel duty and VAT on petrol, diesel and domestic gas until the Iran conflict ends to reduce the impact of rising global oil and gas prices on UK households and businesses.
label: HM Treasury

text: Ban the sale of Israeli products until Israel ends its military actions in Gaza Israel has bombed Gaza, an enclave of over 2 million people, for more than 18 months. Cutting-edge military hardware is harming civilians, with thousands dead and many of the survivors starving. We believe we should act with our wallets and ban the sale of Israeli products in the UK.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Scrap legal aid for all convicted criminals and recent immigrants Scrap all legal aid for all immigrants and convicted criminals. We think legal aid should not be available for immigrants who have paid less than 15 years tax and that repeat offenders should not have access.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban the use of piercing guns / hand pressure piercing devices We believe piercing guns are incredibly dangerous and should be prohibited to prevent the ongoing danger to the public. We believe piercing guns are a severe infection hazard as they can’t be fully sterilised, increasing the risk of cross contamination and the spread of life-threatening diseases.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Hold MPs accountable for misleading statements and apply sanctions Introduce a statutory mechanism to investigate and sanction MPs who make demonstrably false or misleading statements in Parliament or public communications. This should include an independent body empowered to review evidence, issue corrections, and apply proportionate penalties.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Ban artificial intelligence-produced imagery and art from being copyrighted For many artists, graphic designers and animators out there, I feel the rise of artificial intelligence taking over their jobs has grown to be a major concern. I think the thought of copyrighting AI imagery is a ludicrous idea, since we think it could be stealing other copyrighted artwork.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Mandate antenatal discussion of low-dose aspirin in pregnancy across NHS I am asking the Government to mandate maternity services routinely discuss aspirin with pregnant women so they can make informed choices with their healthcare providers. This should not be only discussed after loss and should be available to all parents expecting babies regardless.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund the inclusion of music therapy in community mental health support We believe government plans to expand community mental healthcare support are vital to improving access, outcomes and quality of life for service users. The Government should fund the provision of music therapy services, offering an evidence-based route to support that transcends words and language.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require CCTV in all nursery & child-minding settings Require CCTV in all nursery and child-minding settings with the minimum requirement to have CCTV at entrances and exits.
label: Department for Education

text: Establish a Strategic Digital Assets Reserve Create a Strategic Digital Assets Reserve to manage UK’s digital assets, such as 61,000 Bitcoin from seizures. Appoint a unit responsible for stewardship, audits, transparency, and market monitoring for strategic opportunities in the national interest.
label: HM Treasury

text: Review UK arms exports to UAE & consider sanctions Sudan faces a severe humanitarian crisis, with civilians suffering widespread displacement and harm. We ask the Government to review arms exports to the UAE to ensure full compliance with export controls, increase transparency, and consider sanctions linked to the Sudan conflict.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Protect Military Families: Mandate 6ft Fences In Gardens We urge the government to mandate the installation of 6ft fences in all military family housing to enhance security, privacy, and well-being. We request the standardisation of 6ft fencing in ALL military housing, Ensure that all new and existing military homes have 6ft fences as a minimum standard.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Review the Regulation of Pet Insurance Premium Increases and Consumer Choice We believe that many pet owners face huge & unsustainable rises in their monthly pet insurance on renewal far above inflation & income growth with limited transparency or ability to switch providers due to even minor pre-existing conditions leaving many effectively locked into their current insurer.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Include GMC accredited degrees from UK medical campuses outside of the UK The Medical Training (Prioritisation) Bill should be amended to include GMC accredited medical degrees from UK medical campuses outside of the UK within the definition of UK Primary Medical Qualification.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Make the teaching of criminal offences & their consequences compulsory in school We want the government to include criminal law within the national curriculum for all schools within PSHE. We want students to be taught what is illegal, thinking/reasoning around crime and how to avoid criminal situations as they get older.
label: Department for Education

text: Apply the Human Rights Act retrospectively I think the Government should legislate for full retrospective application of the Human Rights Act.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Require Parliament’s vote & an impact assessment on the UK-US trade deal We are concerned the UK-US trade deal could be implemented without a vote, consultation or impact assessment. We believe it affects food, farming, health, and data standards. We believe Parliament must be allowed to assess its consequences and vote before any further changes are made.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Start mining British coal again for the environment and heritage sector We call on the Government to start mining coal again. A small anthracite mine, which we think could bring the cost of fuel down enormously for heritage sites and be considerably greener, as it wouldn't need to shipped from the other side of the world.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Review foreign travel advice for Libya I kindly request the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office review its travel advice regarding travel to Libya.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Don't put an extra duty on vape products We think that putting duty on vaping products of £2.20 per 10ml will lead to people smoking again. This is adding potentially £22 per 100ml liquid on top of the price. We think this is extremely excessive. We think it's an unfair duty on a product that contains no tobacco.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Classify Organised Grooming and Rape Gangs as Domestic Terrorism under Law Organised rape gangs operate through systematic sexual exploitation, coercion, violence, & intimidation, primarily targeting vulnerable children and young people. These crimes are not isolated offences but coordinated, ongoing campaigns that instil fear, silence victims, to undermine public safety.
label: Home Office

text: Ban generative AI music software in the UK The UK music industry has generated £8 billion in yearly revenue to the UK economy. We are concerned AI-generated music is threating the livelihoods of professionals in Britain’s music sector, we call on the Government to ban generative AI music software to protect British jobs.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: 30yr minimum sentence for all cases of murder & manslaughter involving a knife We call for the introduction of a mandatory minimum sentence of 30years for murder & manslaughter cases where a knife or sharp object was used. We want knife crime laws changed with tougher sentencing for crimes of murder & manslaughter involving knives and sharp objects.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Abolish quarterly Making Tax Digital submissions for self-assessment We want the Government to abolish the requirement for quarterly tax submissions under Making Tax Digital, introduced this April by HMRC.  We believe it is difficult enough doing annual submissions and now to be forced to submit tax calculations 4 times a year is more than many of us can bear.
label: HM Treasury

text: Introduce specific safeguarding regulation for extracurricular activities Introduce safeguarding legislation and regulation for extracurricular activities. Ensure all staff and volunteers are trained, vetted, and members of an accredited awarding, governing or regulated body to safeguard vulnerable individuals.
label: Department for Education

text: Stop the State Pension retirement age rising to 67. Make it 65 Let people have the choice whether to retire or keep working. Many people have been working since they were 16. We think a state pension retirement age of 65 for all is ample enough
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Fund access to abiraterone in England for high-risk prostate cancer patients Abiraterone has been available in Scotland and Wales for two years for high-risk patients whose cancer has not yet spread but not in England and Northern Ireland. I want the government fund abiraterone for men in England, giving them the treatment they deserve and has been proven to work.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text:
Remove the automatic right of bishops to sit in the House of Lords
 The Archbishops of Canterbury and York, and the Bishops of London, Durham and Winchester, together with 21 other diocesan bishops, have an automatic right to sit in the House of Lords.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Make it illegal to sell, buy and use fireworks other than silent ones Change the law so that we can no longer buy non-silent fireworks, sell them or use them.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Don't increase defence spending to 2.5% of GDP & change approach We urge the Government to not increase defence spending to 2.5% of GDP. We believe increasing military spending would exacerbate international tensions and make the UK involvement in wars more likely, which could put all of us in the UK more at risk.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Remove VAT from all children’s swimming lessons We want the Government to remove VAT from all children’s swimming lessons to keep them affordable and accessible. We believe swimming is a vital life-saving skill, not a luxury, and high costs can prevent many children from learning to swim safely.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Require CCTV in all early years settings Change the law so that all early year settings are required to have CCTV
label: Department for Education

text: Allow disputed landlord service charges be paid to courts for better justice Make it possible for tenant/leaseholders to pay disputed service charges to a court. The funds will then only pass to landlords if they can prove the charge's legitimacy within a specified timeframe. Otherwise, the money returns to the tenant/leaseholder.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Incorporate the UNCRDP into domestic law and appoint a Secretary of State Incorporate the UN Convention on the Rights of a Person with Disabilities into domestic law by creating a National Disability Living Act (NDL), appoint a Secretary of State for disabled lived and within 10 years meet all UNCRPD obligations, publishing annual reports on progress.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Stop members of the Government and Parliament from attending WEF meetings We call on the Government to not allow any ministers or members of Parliament to engage with the World Economic Forum.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Increase Personal Income Tax allowance to £14,000 to cover the State Pension Raise the income tax personal allowance from £12,570 to £14,000 to cover the State Pension. This will put all State pensioners, including older pensioners who have paid into SERPS or the State second pension, on an equal footing until the end of this Parliament.
label: HM Treasury

text: Deport any migrant who is guilty of committing a sexual offence Pass a law which automatically deports any migrant who is identified and guilty of committing any sexual offences, including sexual activity with a child.
label: Home Office

text: Review the way media outlets inc online/social media report about suicide deaths Conduct a review with the aim to protect the welfare of families left behind after someone dies by suicide and consider what legislation is necessary.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: £1 tax on top division football league tickets to fund community 3G pitches Currently, many football games are getting postponed due to the weather affecting grass pitches. I call on the Government to impose a £1 tax on every top division football league ticket to fund community 3G pitches for grassroots teams in bad weather conditions via a “Let The Kids Play fund.”
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Make keeping horses tethered with no shade, food or drink a specific offence Many horses are left with no shade, very little water or food tethered in open fields. Some hardly have any grazing and when in severe weather conditions all they do is walk in circles all day. Keeping horses tethered outside with no access to shade, food or drink, should be made a specific offence.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Lower the bowel cancer screening age to 25 Lower the bowel cancer screening age from 50 to 25. There is a huge increase in younger people being diagnosed with bowel cancer with one in every 20 cases being in someone under 50.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban all face coverings at all protests and demonstrations Face coverings at protests allow individuals to hide their identity, making it harder to prevent and investigate crime, disorder, and intimidation. We call for a clear, universal ban on face coverings at protests to ensure accountability and public safety.
label: Home Office

text: Revoke The Selective Licensing of Houses (Additional Conditions) Order 2015 We think the Selective Licensing of Houses (Additional Conditions) (England) Order 2015 should be revoked immediately by the Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government and not implement new schemes or renew any schemes currently in effect.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: End the 2023 £476m deal with France to stop the migrants crossing the channel Stop paying the French Government the money that we believe isn’t being used effectively to stop the migrants. We believe that the French are in effect reneging on the 2023 agreement.
label: Home Office

text: Fund Level 7 Apprenticeships for over 21s if a MSc Is Essential for Career Entry Instead of capping funding for Level 7 apprenticeships for those over 21, we urge the government to distinguish between career entry and career progression and continue funding level 7 apprenticeships (regardless of age) in fields where an MSc is the minimum qualification for starting a career.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund more support for armed forces veterans when they leave We are calling for the government to fund more support for armed forces veterans when they leave the military, particularly in relation to their recovery from accident and injury and the Armed Forces Compensation Scheme.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Give BSL, Cornish, Irish, Scots, Gaelic & Welsh UK-wide language protections We call on the UK Government to give Cornish, Irish, Scots, Scottish Gaelic, Welsh and BSL the same official language protections that exist in the constituent nations of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Mandatory life sentences for repeat child sexual offenders to protect children Introduce mandatory life sentences or whole-life orders for repeat child sexual offenders, and remove eligibility for early release. Ensure sentencing reflects the lifelong harm caused and prioritises protecting children from repeat offenders.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Reverse restrictions to landlords’ finance cost relief. We call for the Government to remove the restrictions on the tax relief that buy to let landlords are entitled to claim on their mortgage interest. We believe removing it may entice landlords back to the market, increase availability and make rents more affordable.
label: HM Treasury

text: Strengthen Hate Crime Laws for Disabled People & Recognise Their Vulnerability Disabled people can face high levels of hate crime causing serious physical and emotional harm. We urge the UK Government to strengthen hate crime laws, introduce tougher sentencing, fund improved police and CPS training, and fund increased support for disabled victims as they are more vulnerable.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Remove Visa Requirements for Jamaican Citizens Visiting the UK For over 20 years, UK visa rules have kept many Jamaicans from visiting loved ones here. My family, like many others, has missed weddings, births, and final goodbyes. Jamaica’s Windrush generation helped build the UK—now we ask for the same trust and welcome in return.
label: Home Office

text: Lower bowel cancer screening from 50 to 40—save more lives, detect cancer early. We are calling for bowel cancer screening to start at 40 instead of 50. Bowel cancer can affect younger people, and early detection saves lives. Lowering the screening age could help find cancer sooner, improve treatment outcomes and give more families precious extra years together.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text:
Fund mandatory endometriosis training for all NHS staff We think every person with endometriosis is being failed.
Endometriosis diagnosis can take 8-10 years not because it is a complex process, but because we feel we are ignored by every medical professional we encounter. Even when diagnosed, we feel professionals do not understand the condition.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Call referendum on introducing death penalty for certain offences We call on the Government to conduct a referendum of whether to introduce the death penalty by hanging for offences of: treason, murder, rape and terrorism.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Review how to better weave nature and wellbeing into the curriculum Review how to make nature and wellbeing core parts of the curriculum — not optional. We think this, a "living curriculum", would transform outcomes for children, especially those with SEND and mental health needs. With a new curriculum in 2028, the evidence, and workforce we have, we should act now.
label: Department for Education

text:
Strengthen consumer protections on new build homes Consumer protections should be strengthened by requiring developers to: 
1) Meet stricter quality control standards before sale.
2) Refund 10% of the home's value if it falls below a set standard
3) Cover the cost of alternative accommodation if buyers are not happy.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Make Perimenopause Training Mandatory for All UK Doctors Perimenopause affects millions of UK women, yet many are dismissed or misdiagnosed. We call for mandatory training for all doctors and at least one trained specialist in every GP practice to ensure women are properly recognised, supported and treated.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Mandate maximum 12 week dental waiting time for SEN children & increase funding Mandate a maximum 12-week wait for SEN children requiring urgent dental care under sedation or general anaesthetic. Provide emergency funding to increase surgical capacity and ensure Integrated Care Boards are held accountable for delays that leave vulnerable children in prolonged pain.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Prison Officer Occupation code 3314 to be added to Immigration Salary List Urgently include occupation code 3314 (Prison Officers) in the Immigration Salary List to help enable sponsorship for recently recruited Prison officers to ensure staff retention and avert further staffing crisis for prisons.
label: Home Office

text: Match the funding rate of childminders of 2-4 yr olds with current under 2s rate Increase the hourly funding rate for 15/30hr early education & childcare places for 2-4-yr olds to the same level currently paid for under 2s. I believe current rates are financially unsustainable, contribute to some childminders leaving the profession, & lack of quality/flexible childcare places
label: Department for Education

text: Apply the same energy efficiency legislation to all property - not just rentals The UK government has announced plans to significantly increase energy efficiency standards for privately rented properties. Owner-occupied properties would not be required to meet the same requirements, which we think creates an unfair and illogical situation from an environmental standpoint.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Legislate to allow social services to force visits to non-engaging households We would like the Government to change the law to enable social services to force visits & gain forced access to the households of non-engaging families, to ensure children’s welfare & living conditions are verified, and to avoid families enduring pain & suffering that many families have experienced
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Give Wales the same funding per person for the rail network as England We feel that the Welsh rail network is treated as second class compared to England. The nation has 11% of the entire UK's rail network, has 5% of the UK's population but receives just 1% of rail infrastructure funding.
label: Department for Transport

text: No more tax rises in this Parliament We think the tax rises in the 2024 Autumn budget have been self-defeating, with unemployment rising. We think they will likely result in less tax revenue and lower growth. We believe that tax payers of all degrees pay enough already and the government needs to spend the money more wisely.
label: HM Treasury

text: Do not sign a trade deal with the USA We urge the Government to not sign a trade deal with the USA
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Fund free bus travel for school pupils, college students and apprentices We believe the Government should fund free bus travel for school pupils, college students and apprentices. The cost of travelling to education or training can be a barrier for young people and families. Free travel could improve access to learning, training and employment opportunities.
label: Department for Transport

text: Allow State Pension to be passed to children, long-term partners, and dependents We ask the Government to change State Pension inheritance rules so that individuals can nominate a beneficiary such as their child, long-term cohabiting partner, or carer – or offer them a lump sum – so it is not just a spouse or civil partner inheriting from the pension as at present.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Require disabled toilets to have a fold down shelf for stoma users There are often no facilities for stoma users in disabled toilets. Leaving us using the floor or the top of toilet seats for our appliances. This is not sanitary. I would like a legal requirement of a fold down shelf. This allows the shelf to be folded up so there is no impact on wheelchair users.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Repeal the Public Order Act 2023 & Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022 We urge the Government to repeal Public Order Act 2023 and the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022. We believe these acts have prevented people from taking part in legitimate protest and may lead to the criminalisation of people for going to meetings to plan protests.
label: Home Office

text: Hold a public referendum on whether to hold an early general election Call an immediate referendum to allow the public to decide whether there should be an early general election.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Reduce child maintenance, exclude overtime & introduce no contact, no payment We want the government to review and reduce child maintenance rates, stop including overtime in calculations, and halt payments when contact is denied or contact does not exist, especially if there is a new parental figure.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Ban air fresheners & scented products in public spaces We want the Government to ban air fresheners, scented candles, and fragranced products in public buildings and enclosed public spaces. Scientific evidence shows these products can contribute to indoor air pollution and pose health risks to the public.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Amend the Ancient Monuments Act 1979 to ban building on all scheduled sites. Parliament must amend the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Areas Act 1979 to mandate a total ban on Scheduled Monument Consent for any permanent above-ground construction. This should apply to all list entries where archaeological deposits exist, removing discretionary executive powers.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Ban homework in all schools Stop all schools setting children homework. They already spend over 6 hours in school 5 days a week. We think homework causes children stress, tiredness, and exhaustion.
label: Department for Education

text: Criminalise Repeated Non-Consensual Photography and Recording in Gyms We want the Government to create a specific criminal offence for repeated non-consensual photography and filming in gyms and leisure facilities, giving police clear powers to investigate and prosecute those who repeatedly target individuals without their consent.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Allow employees to deduct living expenses from salary before it’s taxed. I’d like to propose that the Government allow employees to deduct essential living expenses—such as rent/mortgage, utility bills, food, council tax and childcare—from their income before it is subject to tax.
label: HM Treasury

text: Introduce national social care tariffs so councils pay the true cost of care Introduce transparent national social care tariffs so councils pay the true cost of care, ending the hidden shifting of costs onto private households and care providers when local authority fees fall below the cost of delivering safe services.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Formally recognise the killings of Bengali people in 1971 as genocide. We call on the UK Government to formally recognise the killings of the Bengali people of East Pakistan in 1971 as genocide - so that nearly 1 million British Bangladeshis, and the generations carrying this history, are no longer left without an answer.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Change England’s disabled bus pass so it can be used at any time on weekdays We urge the Government to change the English national concessionary travel scheme (ENCTS) so the disabled bus pass can be used at any time, including before 9:30am on weekdays.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review The Number Of Asbestos-Linked Lung Cancers The HSE states that the ratio of mesothelioma deaths to other asbestos-related deaths is 1 to 1. Some research suggests that deaths from asbestos linked lung cancer are much greater than deaths from mesothelioma. We believe this may hide the scale of UK asbestos deaths and current asbestos risks.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Funding for Gastric Pacemaker Treatment for Gastroparesis Patients I urge the government to fund gastric pacemaker treatment for gastroparesis patients.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund reconstruction surgery and psychosexual therapy for FGM survivors We urge the Government to support FGM survivors by providing funding to make reconstructive surgery and psychosexual therapy accessible within the NHS. Many survivors face untreated pain and trauma, facing barriers from high costs and limited NHS resources.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Inform disabled people of high success rate for PIP appeals at tribunal We believe the Government should make it clear on the Personal Independence Payment (PIP) application form that 69% of people who appealed their PIP decision in 2023/24 won at a tribunal.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Immediately deport foreign nationals who break the law Immediately deport foreign nationals who break the law back to their country of origin. If a jail sentence is required, return them to the country of origin. Why should we put up with people who disrespect our laws & way of life!!!
label: Home Office

text: Abolish the Energy Profits Levy We think this punitive tax is dismantling the UK’s offshore oil and gas industry, especially in Scotland, accelerating job losses and forcing early decommissioning, despite oil now trading at a lower level
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Review UK policy treatment of bio-based chemicals and materials Reducing reliance on fossil resources is seen as vital for national security and resilience. We call on the UK Government to conduct an urgent review of how bio-based chemicals and materials are treated across UK policies, regulations and taxation including how their biogenic carbon is accounted for
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Require elected officials to keep comments open on official social media We think elected officials must keep comments open on official social media to foster dialogue, transparency, and accountability. We believe disabling comments stifles public feedback, blocks democratic participation, and silences constituents’ voices, undermining trust and parliamentary democracy.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Ban churches from being given a use as another religious building I want the government/parliament to put in place planning rules to ban churches being converted into other religious buildings.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Government to reverse delay on mayoral elections in the UK The Government has recently delayed mayoral elections until May 2028 in Greater Essex, Norfolk and Suffolk, Hampshire and the Solent, and Sussex and Brighton.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Ban travel insurance premium hikes & refusals for people in clinical trials Ban travel insurance companies vastly increasing premiums, or refusal to cover people who partake in clinical trials, which may make it impossible for them to travel without resulting in substantial additional costs.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Bring down driving test wait times The wait time for learner drivers to get a driving test is unacceptable, we need more examiners, reward them accordingly and incentivise them to do more tests.
label: Department for Transport

text: Mandate Mental Health Training for All School Staff Who Work With Children Require all staff working with children in schools to receive mandatory training to identify children in mental health crisis through behavioural changes, not just physical signs, so early intervention supports development and wellbeing.
label: Department for Education

text: Make it a criminal offence to collect street donations if not a charity We are concerned about bogus charity collections on our streets. Some operations that claim to be charitable are run as a "for profit" business with very little of their collections used to help anyone.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Chemical castration for all rapists and sexual abuse offenders We want the Government to make a law where all those found guilty of rape and sexual abuse, including child sex abuse are chemically castrated. We think it would make the UK a safer place for women and children.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Commit to not removing the presumption of parental involvement The Government has said it has reviewed the presumption of parental involvement, and will publish its findings. We think the Government should clearly commit to not removing the presumption.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Give students a legal right to access school toilets when they have their period Young people who have periods during school hours are sometimes denied access to toilets. We feel that this prevents young people from having a period with dignity, causing shame. We propose young people with periods, by law be given a right to access school toilets.
label: Department for Education

text: Increase maritime enforcement to intercept and return boats to France. We call for the Government to strengthen maritime border enforcement to intercept small boats attempting to reach the UK. We think this policy should ensure that intercepted individuals are returned to France, with collaboration improved to effectively address ongoing migration challenges.
label: Home Office

text: Fund free music tuition for all secondary school children aged 11-16 in England We urge the Government to full fund 1:1 music instrument lessons for all children aged 11-16 in all secondary schools in England. We believe this could close the “cultural capital gap” by ensuring all students can access these lessons regardless of their household income.
label: Department for Education

text: Make the most of our own natural resources. Allow companies to drill gas and oil Allow companies to drill gas and oil in our own country and in the North Sea, stop relying on energy from other countries. We can be self sufficient.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Fund NHS preceptorships for unemployed Physician Associates Fund a national NHS preceptorship programme for unemployed qualified Physician Associates, providing paid supervised NHS employment and a clear pathway into permanent NHS roles while maintaining patient safety and clinical competence.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require prison sentences to be served consecutively, not concurrently We want the government to change the law so that prison sentences for crimes can only be served consecutively, not concurrently.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Amend Public Order Act 1986 to include protections on the grounds of disability As it currently stands, the Public Order Act 1986 protects against inciting hatred on the grounds of race, religion and sexual orientation but not of disability. I want the Government to amend that legislation to extend the protections under that Act to disability.
label: Home Office

text: Remove the statute of limitations for medical negligence for long-term damage Remove the time limit that is required to file any lawsuit that is related to medical negligence for long-term damage.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Support newly qualified physiotherapists: Review barriers to NHS jobs We think newly qualified physiotherapists are struggling to get NHS jobs due to experience requirements and internal-only adverts. Some apply for assistant roles or private jobs but may be rejected for being overqualified or lacking NHS experience. We want a review and better support into practice.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require freeholders to allow fixed AC with external units in leasehold flats Require freeholders to allow leaseholders to install safe, compliant fixed split air conditioning with external condenser units unless they can justify reason to refuse it. Freeholders and managing agents should not refuse by default and must give evidence-based reasons for refusal.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Regulate podcast platforms to prevent the spread of misogyny and harmful content Strengthen regulation of podcast and social media platforms to meet minimum editorial standards, strengthen oversight & prevent algorithmic promotion of harmful content, in order to delegitimise misinformation and dangerous ideologies which endanger not just women and protected groups, but everyone.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Do not implement a ban on the use of aversive dog training tools For the government to not introduce a ban on the sale or use of aversive dog training tools including electronic collars.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Expand the winter fuel allowance to other vulnerable people. Instead of means testing the winter fuel payment for pensioners, we think all over 60s, those with cancer or long term sick patients should be entitled to £100 per month for each of gas and electricity from Oct to Jan paid directly to the energy company, or £200 per month for all electric homes.
label: HM Treasury

text: Allow Veterans of the Armed Forces to claim their state pension at the age of 60 I would like the Government to allow Veterans of the Armed forces to receive their state pension at the age of 60 in recognition of their service to the country.
label: HM Treasury

text: Lower the state pension age to 65 years old Lower the state pension age to 65.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Require re-development of empty properties in an area before building new There are many empty properties needing re-development these should be incentivised for redevelopment prior to green and grey land within the area being approved for planning and development of new estates.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Longer sentences and disqualification for drug/drink drivers who injure someone The current law for serious injury by dangerous driving is a maximum of 5 years. I think that when this is caused by a drink and/or drug driver, the sentence should be made harsher, with an automatic disqualification for life to make our roads safer.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban the sale of glue traps The sale of glue traps should be banned in line with the current ban on their use under the Glue Traps (Offences) Bill 2022 in order to protect animals and wildlife and limit their suffering caused by such traps.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Ban police from using lethal methods when dogs are out of control We want the government to require police to use non-kill methods with out of control dogs. Stun not gun.
label: Home Office

text: Review employment law awareness and enforcement in private Early Years There are concerns that employment rights are not being enforced in the private early years sector, both by level 2 and 3 qualified staff, and managers and leaders. We therefore call for a review of employment law awareness and enforcement of the law in the Early Years sector.
label: Department for Education

text: Review Dangerous Dog Act 1991 and bring in dog ownership license and dog tagging I want the Government to review Dangerous Dogs Act to bring in stricter penalties for out of control dogs, and require by law that all dog owners hold a dog owner license and that all dogs are tagged.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Make water companies statutory consultees in housing development planning We call on the UK Government to make water companies statutory consultees in all housing development planning applications. This would ensure that no development can proceed unless the relevant water company confirms that adequate water supply, wastewater, and drainage infrastructure is in place.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Stop all state benefit payments to non-British citizens I would like the Government to cease all state benefit payments and support to people who are not British citizens.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Ban the use of all pest control methods against pigeons Ban the use of any pest control on pigeons, as we believe it is cruel and should be against the law.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Psychosis: increase research funding into diagnosis, prevention and medication We think the government should direct more research funding to determine the underlying causes of psychosis, develop preventative treatments and evidenced diagnoses. We want more investment to accelerate the introduction of more effective medications with fewer serious side effects.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Bring the teaching of Key Word Signing in to all nurseries and schools Key Word Signing is very common in special education settings, but we believe it needs to be brought in to all nurseries, primary schools and secondary schools, being taught alongside languages. In our view it has the potential to become a universal language and everyone would benefit.
label: Department for Education

text:
Review levels of pay for Teachers' Maternity Leave We want the Government to review levels of pay for Teachers' Maternity Leave, to make those levels align with other sectors, like the prisons, fire and civil services. We believe teachers deserve:
26 weeks full pay 
13 weeks at 90% pay
and the rest at statutory maternity pay levels
label: Department for Education

text: Require Protection for Cultural Identity of Gypsy & Traveller Children in Care Require local authorities to prioritise placement of Gypsy and Traveller children with Gypsy and Traveller foster carers where safe and appropriate, and by provide better cultural awareness training for social workers.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Make Road Traffic Safety a mandatory part of the National Curriculum I petition that the Department of Education includes Road Safety awareness as a mandatory part of the National Curriculum. There are statistics suggesting a disproportionate number of young people are either killed, sustain life changing injuries or are seriously hurt on the roads.
label: Department for Transport

text: Create a task force to find the asylum seekers the HO has lost contact with Urgently create an ICE-style task force to locate the missing asylum seekers lost by the Home Office. For public safety, national security, and system integrity, we demand immediate action to track, verify, and resolve these cases.
label: Home Office

text: Amend Section 27 of the Road Traffic Act 1988 to include all public highways The existing Act deals with keeping dogs on a lead whilst on a road 'designated' by the local authority, but such roads are very rare and this legislation is seldom used.
label: Department for Transport

text: Ban trail hunting Ban trail hunting as it can be another excuse for fox hunting.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Retain current ILR rules for dependants already living in the UK Retain current ILR rules for dependants already in the UK. We believe the proposed 10 year waits and separate evaluations are unfair, risk family separation, and cause hardship. We think families who have lived here for years should progress together towards settlement.
label: Home Office

text: Automatic Clare's law checks when notice of marriage is given to registry office Such an alliance with registry offices will hopefully prevent the physical and financial abuse that can be prevented by alerting a woman to the fact that she is about to marry a known abuser.
label: Home Office

text: Respond fully to The Law Commission's recommendations on Surrogacy The Law Commission of England & Wales published its joint report with the Scottish Law Commission in March 2023, with recommendations for a robust new system to govern surrogacy. The Government gave an interim response on 8 Nov 2023. We want the government to publish a final response.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Change the law to allow public to carry and use pepper spray for self-defence Legalise carrying and using pepper spray for self-defence from age 16 or 18, with approved types only used against immediate threats. The Secretary of State should regulate standards, sales, and storage, and set penalties for misuse. This could ensure safety while protecting personal security.
label: Home Office

text: Launch a railcard for those over the age of 30 covering all of the UK. The Government should create a railcard for those over the age of 30. It seems unfair and unjust that people aged 16-30 may get a railcard, but after this cut-off it is not possible to get a railcard unless you are 'senior', travelling with another person, or part of another group, such as veterans.
label: Department for Transport

text: Give students the legal right to unrestricted toilet access in school We are concerned about “zero-tolerance” toilet policies in schools which can force children to wait for escorts or deny toilet breaks and can cause physical harm (retention/bowel distress). We believe it violates the Equality Act, and we call for a legal right to toilet access at all times.
label: Department for Education

text: Do not introduce digital driving licences We do not want the Government to introduce digital driving licences, and we would like to preserve the card and paper form that already exists as we believe it is sufficient. We believe this could be a slippery slope to compulsory digital ID, etc.
label: Department for Transport

text: Stop taxis operating outside their licensing area Taxis operating outside their licensing area (cross-border taxis) can create challenges for commuters, operators, and drivers. We believe they disrupt the transport system, causing unfair competition and confusion. As a driver, I’ve seen the frustration and income losses caused by this practice.
label: Department for Transport

text: Get rid of the reception baseline assessment I want the Reception Baseline Assessment (RBA) to be scrapped so that teachers can focus on what really matters in those crucial first weeks of school, getting to know our children as individuals. Instead of administering a test that we think provides no helpful insight.
label: Department for Education

text: Strengthen suitable environment criteria for dogs under animal welfare act We would like the Government to update the code of practice for the welfare of dogs with stronger criteria set for a suitable environment for dogs, including temperature based shelter and no tethering/caging which restrict a dog's movement.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Review licensing affecting captive bred bird exhibitions DEFRA has made it nigh on impossible to hold a sale and or exhibition of captive bred birds. We see no evidential reasoning or public consultation so I would like parliament to debate the reasoning behind this decision.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Ban business from not accepting cash payments Protect people who may not have a bank account from not being able to purchase items via cash
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Legalise assisted dying for terminally ill adults Introduce legislation to legalise assisted dying for mentally competent adults suffering from terminal illnesses or incurable, painful medical conditions. Current UK law denies individuals the right to a peaceful death. We believe citizens deserve dignity to a peaceful & insufferable end of life.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reinstate capital punishment for those convicted of sexually abusing of a child Change the law to allow for the death penalty to be imposed to anyone convicted for raping or sexually abusing a child or vulnerable person.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban the sale of secondhand and unroadworthy cars to underage drivers Make it a legal requirement at the point of sale of a secondhand vehicle to request proof of age and photo id, update the current V5C, and develop a seller portal via the DVLA vehicle check system. Failure to follow this process should lead to a prosecution or a fixed penalty for the seller
label: Department for Transport

text: Ban carrying religious, cultural & ceremonial bladed & pointed items in public I believe that the carrying of religious, cultural and ceremonial bladed & pointed items in public should be treated the same as the carrying of all other bladed & pointed items.
label: Home Office

text: Ban removing Rescue Back Up details from pet microchips & make them permanent Rescue Back Up details registered on microchips can be removed by authorised external users like alternate rescuers, without informing the original rescue organisation.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Create an Independent Cruise Passenger Regulator and Strengthen Consumer Rights We want the Government to establish an independent statutory regulator to protect UK cruise passengers, with powers to set and enforce minimum consumer standards covering cancellations, significant disruption, compensation, complaints, denied boarding and unfair treatment.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Reduce state pension age to 60 to create jobs for young people Reduce the state pension age to 60 years old. We think this change could create jobs for young people, reduce sickness and healthcare costs for older adults in the workforce, and reduce workforce strain due to sickness amongst older workers.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Ban UK Border Force from picking up migrants in the Channel We urge the Government to prohibit UK Border Force vessels from picking up and collecting migrants from the English Channel, and to only detain them once they land in the UK.
label: Home Office

text: Provide funding to make more NHS dentists available I want the government to provide funding and encourage dentists to reopen their lists for NHS patients.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Create a specific offence to prevent harassment of people breastfeeding The Breastfeeding etc. (Scotland) Act 2005 makes it an offence to prevent/stop a person feeding a child milk in a public place.
label: Home Office

text: Provide urgent ring-fenced funding for counsellors in every school in England The government promised in their election manifesto that they would provide access to specialist mental health professionals in every school. I want ring-fenced funding for this to be rolled out urgently. I think all schools should be able to offer what can often be a life saving provision.
label: Department for Education

text: Remove the VAT on Period Swimwear and Sportswear We want the Government to remove the 20% VAT on period swimwear and sportswear. We think these essential products are unfairly taxed as luxury items, creating barriers for women and girls to stay active during their periods.
label: HM Treasury

text: Stop individuals in non-fault accidents being charged more for car insurance I would like the government to require the motor insurance industry to change their policy procedures and not penalise innocent drivers who have been hit by other people's driving mistakes.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review and mandate DNA testing to end honey fraud and protect real producers. We urge the Government to bring forward regulations that mandate DNA testing to ensure honey purity. We believe that current tests fail to detect widespread adulteration.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Increase the Carer’s Allowance to equal 35 hours at minimum wage I want the Government to appreciate unpaid carers who can’t work and to increase the Carer’s Allowance so it equals the minimum wage. Many unpaid carers are only paid around £333 a month for a minimum 140 hours care every 4 weeks, which works out around £2.50 an hour.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Fund access to GLP-1 medications through the NHS for women with PCOS Studies highlight the effectiveness of GLP-1 medications for women with PCOS. We think funding access to GLP-1 treatments, without restrictive BMI criteria or tier system barriers, would improve care and outcomes for these patients.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban the use of Prong collars and Electric Shock Collars on Dogs and Cats in UK Ban the use of Prong Collars & Electric Shock Collars for use on Dogs and cats in the UK. We believe they are inhumane, inflict pain, fear and anxiety leading to potential physical and psychological damage, while punishment tools can increase aggression leading to more bites and risk to the public.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require councils to pause council tax bills for three months  We want the Government to require councils to pause council tax bills for three months as we feel they are not delivering on the jobs we pay for such as collecting bins, fixing pot holes and keeping the streets clean.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Review comprehensive pain relief & sedation options for hysteroscopy We call on the UK Government to review the use of pain relief and sedation options to help ensure that women undergoing hysteroscopy are routinely offered appropriate options, including gas and air, conscious (partial) sedation, or full sedation where requested or clinically appropriate.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review safeguards to stop marriage fraud – to protect UK citizens from Visa scam We call on the Government to review UK immigration law to ensure there are no loopholes or ways to exploit regulations to enable marriage and relationship-based immigration fraud, to better protect UK citizens from online grooming.
label: Home Office

text: Do not seek closer ties with the EU I do not want the government to seek closer ties with the EU. I think they should  consider the democratic vote of 2016. I feel that seeking closer ties with the EU amounts to reversing Brexit through the back door.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Give all parents the legal right to participate in their child’s funeral I want Parliament to pass a law to give both parents the right to attend their child’s funeral unless legally prevented, and for Government to provide statutory guidance to funeral directors to protect these rights.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Urge for an international inquiry into Hong Kong & review current HK policies We believe the Wang Fuk Court fire exposed serious concerns about safety, accountability, and the ability of Hong Kongers to seek truth without fear. As a signatory to the Sino-British Joint Declaration, we feel the UK must promote transparency and protect fundamental freedoms in Hong Kong (HK).
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Require the accuser in rape cases to hand over their phones to the police In some rape cases the accuser may withhold evidence in the form of texts and messages. We think the accuser should be required to hand over their mobile devices to the police. In some cases if the police had asked for the accusers phones we think they would of quickly seen that the accuser is lying
label: Home Office

text: Exempt Student HMO’s from Renters Rights Act 2025 We believe Student HMO’s should be exempt from the Renter’s Rights Act 2025 as these properties are run on a totally different business/rental model compared to professional and private rentals.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text:
Hold a referendum on restoring the Death Penalty for murder We call on the Government to hold a referendum on restoring the death penalty for murderers.

We question why taxpayers should pay to keep convicted murderers in prison. We believe that justice betrayed is justice denied.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Review the RE curriculum to ensure equal depth in teaching all major religions Review the Religious Education curriculum in all schools to ensure all major religions are taught with equal depth and respect. I believe Christianity should still be taught, but religions like Sikhism, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism and Buddhism should receive more meaningful and balanced coverage.
label: Department for Education

text: Justice for ESN Survivors: apologise and fund financial compensation In the 1960s, hundreds of black children were labelled as "educationally subnormal" and wrongly sent to schools for pupils who were deemed to have low intelligence. We want the government to apologise to those affected.
label: Department for Education

text: Ban fireworks in residential areas to prevent stress to people and animals Ban the use of fireworks in residential areas which is causing stress to vulnerable people and animals.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Regulate Foot Health Practitioners to require supervision by HCPC podiatrists. We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation to regulate Foot Health Practitioners (FHPs), requiring that they do not practise independently and may only provide foot care services under the clinical supervision or governance of an HCPC-registered podiatrist.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reduce income taxes on earnings under £50,000 and increase personal allowance Reduce the current basic tax rate of 20%, to 10%, for those earning under £50,000 a year, and increase the personal tax-free allowance to £15,000 a year.
label: HM Treasury

text: Stop illegal migrants from accessing financial support We want the Government to stop financial support for illegal migrants. We think this is a waste of tax payers' money.
label: Home Office

text: Ban Reselling Tickets for Above Face-Value and Dynamic Pricing We believe the Government should implement a new law that forbids the resale of tickets for any event for above face value and also bans "Dynamic Pricing".
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Recognise reputational abuse as a distinct form of abuse in the law We call on the Government to introduce legislation recognising reputational abuse, including reputational sexualisation, as a distinct form of abuse in law.
label: Home Office

text: Extra funding for SEND holiday clubs Provide funding to allow more holidays clubs for SEND children, so parents can go to work!
label: Department for Education

text: Provide funding for all pregnant women to have an ultrasound for CHD Fund congenital heart disease (CHD) screening during pregnancy to ensure early detection of life-threatening conditions. Identifying CHD via ultrasound enables timely interventions, better delivery planning, access to specialized care, improving survival and quality of life for affected babies.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require all employers to include parental leave policies in job listings Require all employers to include parental leave policies clearly in job listings. Some studies show only a small percentage currently do so. Making it a legal requirement could help ensure fair access to information. We believe without it, discrimination, unfair withdrawal of offers could result.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Restrict transport of asylum seekers from MoD sites to local towns We want the Government to end what we see as unnecessary taxpayer-funded transport from MoD asylum sites to local towns & cities. Transport contracts already operate from Wethersfield & Crowborough. Future MoD sites should provide minimal offsite travel & provide services onsite wherever practical.
label: Home Office

text: Fund travel reimbursements for families of children with lifelong conditions Provide funding for travel reimbursements for all families of children with lifelong conditions who are attending specialist centres for their conditions, similar to the scheme for paediatric cancer patients.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban the production and sale of small animal cages We think that almost all cages that are produced and sold in pet shops are far too small for all animals, particularly the ones they are marketed to.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Impose financial penalties when parent is killed due to dangerous driving We want courts to be able to order those convicted of killing a parent through drink driving, drug driving, dangerous driving or hit-and-run offences to pay ongoing financial support for the child. This could be known as "Butler’s Law".
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Do not postpone the local elections Local elections are held so that local people can have a say on local issues. We think that the postponement of some of the local elections would prevent citizens from voicing their opinions on local issues.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Legislate implementation of the Aviation Accessibility Report recommendations There have been many incidents of airports and airlines delivering substandard access and assistance to disabled passengers. These were highlighted in evidence to the Aviation Accessibility task and finish group who have made recommendations to rectify and prevent such issues.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review law on disability-related dismissals and employment tribunals Review law on employers disciplining or dismissing staff for disability-related absence. Review if employment tribunals are making reasonable adjustments, the speed of responses, and treatment of harassment cases and evidence examination. Mandate disability training for judges and panel members.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Switch to proportional representation for general elections We think the First Past the Post system is becoming increasingly obsolete as the UK continues to move away from a two party system. We are now in a place where the party who may gain the most seats at an election could be the most unacceptable to the majority. We must protect our democracy.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Review access to, and funding for, NHS powered wheelchairs Too many ambulatory wheelchair users are denied NHS-powered wheelchairs because they can walk short distances. We want eligibility to be soundly based on clinical need, safety and independence, not just on walking or standing ability.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text:
Ban balaclavas except for winter activity use We want the government to introduce legislation that clearly defines restrictions on wearing balaclavas in public, with exemptions for winter activities.
 
There could be penalties for non-compliance, and guidance issued to ensure public understanding and adherence.
label: Home Office

text: Introduce stricter regulation for pet cremation I want stricter rules such as requiring those who carry out pet cremation to have license, compulsory inspections, mandatory identity tags on pets, storage standards, staff training and respectful handling. We also think there should be CCTV requirements covering all key areas of the crematoria.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Raise the age of compulsory education in England to Six & reform Early Education We urge the Government to raise the age of compulsory education in England to six, and reform early years education by prioritising play-based, developmentally appropriate learning, and requiring teacher training courses to include core modules on child development and attachment theory.
label: Department for Education

text: Review need for a national standard of care for children with cerebral palsy NHS England introduced a Cerebral Palsy Commissioning Framework in 2025, but it has only been piloted in some Integrated Care Boards and not adopted nationwide.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Stop fines for taking children out of school on holiday Stop fines for taking our children out of school on holiday. Where does the money actually go when we are fined for taking our children away and showing them different cultures? Scrap the fines!
label: Department for Education

text: Make international GPs automatically eligible for ILR after completing training We urge the Government to make international medical graduates (IMGs) who complete GP training in the UK and receive a Certificate of Completion of Training automatically eligible to apply for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR), reducing visa barriers and helping retain skilled doctors in the NHS.
label: Home Office

text: Suspend all UK foreign aid to nations that refuse to take back illegal migrants Publish a list of countries blocking citizen returns, suspend UK aid until compliance is met, make aid legally conditional on cooperation with UK immigration, report annually to Parliament, and detain illegal migrants until asylum or deportation for public safety.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Stop the Data (Use and Access) Bill We want Parliament to stop the Data (Use and Access) Bill. Concerns have been raised that the Bill could make it easier for personal data to be used without fully informed consent from the data holder.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Hold an inquiry into Healthcare Professionals dying by suicide. To help us understand potential reasons for healthcare professionals dying by suicide. To make recommendations to governing bodies and workplaces on how to reduce suicides and improve staff mental wellbeing, and ensure adequate funding is in place to carry out the recommendations adequately.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: State that biological males must not be housed in women’s prisons I want the government to unequivocally state that biological males should not be housed in women’s prisons.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Make hedgehog highways mandatory on all new fencing. Hedgehogs travel around one mile every night through our parks and gardens in their quest to find enough food and a mate. We can make their life a little easier by removing the barriers within our control. For example, by mandating the use of holes/hedgehog friendly gravel boards on all new fencing.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Establish a national alert system for missing autistic & vulnerable people The Government should introduce a national alert system which alerts every phone in a county when an autistic or vulnerable person goes missing.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Don’t change agricultural & business property relief for inheritance tax We urgently call on the UK Government to stop the planned changes to inheritance tax reliefs that threaten working family farms and rural businesses—the heart of our rural communities. We believe these reforms could inflict irreparable harm on rural heritage and food security.
label: HM Treasury

text: Increase the DWP Christmas bonus for benefit claimants to £20 Increase the amount given for Christmas bonus. Increase the amount to £20
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Give vets powers to seize animals if there is neglect or abuse & punish owners If an animal is brought to a vet, we think they should be able to make the decision that due to the severity of neglect they will seize the animal. We think the owner should be fined, added to a register and unable to obtain animals in the future.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text:
Link the personal tax free allowance to a cost of living/ inflation index. 1 Remove 2028 lock on personal allowance
2 Benchmark to a cost of living index similar to state pension
3 Review and amend annually
label: HM Treasury

text: Vehicle recall: Courtesy car, compensation, cost cover & repair time limit Require car manufacturers to provide courtesy cars or compensation when issuing ‘do not drive’ recalls. We think support must include alternative transport, cover for ongoing costs, and compensation for stress and inconvenience. Set a legal repair time limit.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Review and remove judicial immunity for judges & magistrates Launch a review into all laws, rules and conventions that grant judges and magistrates judicial immunity and legislate to remove judicial immunity for judges and magistrates.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Fund a mandatory NHS wide digital patient record across all NHS hospitals Patients may experience fragmented or delayed care because NHS trusts use different record systems. We want a single mandatory NHS-wide digital patient record to help prevent errors or lost information, and stop patients being triaged or treated without full medical history across all NHS hospitals.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Develop, publish, and implement a new National Dementia Strategy Since the national dementia strategy published under the 2010-2015 Government, we have no dementia strategy in this country.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reverse Abortion Decriminalisation in England and Wales We urge the UK Government to reverse abortion decriminalisation in England and Wales, voted by 379 MPs on 17 June 2025. Many believe this undermines life. Reinstate penalties under the 1861 Offences Against the Person Act to protect unborn children.
label: Home Office

text: Change the law to allow dogs and cats to travel in airplane cabins into the UK We ask the Government to change the law to allow dogs and cats to enter the UK in the aircraft cabin under strict health, safety, and airline regulations. We believe pet owners should have the freedom to choose cabin or cargo travel based on their pet’s size, needs, and airline policies.
label: Department for Transport

text: UK to refuse to recognise Palestine. UK to supply Israel with military support We believe recognition of Palestine is contrary to The Montevideo Convention on the duty and rights of States....recognition we believe contravenes the convention and international law. We believe recognition will reward terrorists now and in the future.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Include 'Indo-Caribbean' as an ethnic group on Government documents We ask the UK Government to include “Indo-Caribbean” as an ethnic group option on Government documents, alongside existing categories, so people of Indian-Caribbean heritage can accurately identify their ethnicity and be better represented in UK equality data.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Fund free Meningitis B & ACWY vaccines on the NHS for all I do not think that private medical companies should be able to charge hundreds of pounds for Meningitis B & ACWY vaccines. I think they should be provided free for everyone of any age on the NHS.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Apply to rejoin EASA and obtain a reciprocal agreement on licensing Apply to rejoin the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) and obtain reciprocal licensing agreements to allow the airline industry to grow and undo the lasting effects from having left the agency.
label: Department for Transport

text: Introduce a public misconduct register for police accountability & transparency Legislate to introduce a public misconduct register for police found guilty of misconduct or gross misconduct, including bullying and discrimination. We think this should be known as 'Isabelle’s Law'.
label: Home Office

text: Fund research on the symptoms of Gilbert’s Syndrome Gilbert’s Syndrome is classified as a harmless condition, however we are concerned that some patients are experiencing debilitating symptoms that are dismissed. We want the government to fund more research into this condition and its symptoms, which could inform clinical guidelines.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review the child maintenance service Review the child maintenance service.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Fund a pancreatic cancer screening programme There is currently no routine screening programme on the NHS for pancreatic cancer, which is detected in far too many cases when it is too late to be cured. This affects thousands of families. It is one of the deadliest cancers, yet there is no nationwide, routine screening programme.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review DVLA’s performance & processes, increase funding & create governing body We want the government to conduct a review of the DVLA's performance and processes to make sure everyone is treated fairly & equally.
label: Department for Transport

text: Strengthen laws on ending the use of Listed assets I ask Parliament to strengthen Planning Laws and require any organisation wanting to end use of a Listed asset to provide valid Planning reasons to the Planning Authority if they wish to end the function of a Listed asset.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Government to review funding and regulations for Medical Fitness to drive Increase Grant Funding to Driving Mobility Centres to prevent further centre closures.  Extend the responsibility to declare a medical condition to the DVLA to include any medical professional who confirms the diagnosis. Enhance control of the regulatory management of Driving Mobility Centres.
label: Department for Transport

text: Students with 90%+ attendance to be able to go on holiday during term time We think that if a child maintains 90%+ attendance parents have proven their commitment and should not be fined or prosecuted for brief absences. In our view, enforcement should target persistent low attendance below 90%, where a child’s education is genuinely at risk, not responsible families.
label: Department for Education

text: Launch a review into job shortages facing new qualified midwives & fund support We urge the Government to launch a review into job shortages for newly qualified midwives, and increase funding for more Band 5 jobs and general support for newly qualified midwives to ensure a clear pathway to employment for them.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund all GP surgeries to provide blood tests to patients with chronic illnesses I want the government to put in place funding to ensure that patients with chronic conditions who need regular blood tests for the rest of their lives can get them in their own community, at their own GP surgery.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review NHS approach to shared care for ADHD medication. We would like the Government to review the NHS's approach to shared care for ADHD medication in England.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review NHS policy on masks, safe air & ventilation to protect vulnerable  Vulnerable people — those with cancer, immune compromise, or chronic illness — should feel safe in NHS settings, not fearful. We’re calling for a 'do no harm' standard: an automatic right to treatment by FFP2/3 masked staff, safe air and ventilation in every setting and stronger infection control.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require NHS to start priority triage & discharge pathways for dementia patients Make NHS hospitals implement priority triage and faster discharge pathways for people with dementia when the medical condition is treated & home or community care is available. Formally recognise that delay in discharge can cause rapid deterioration and should be treated as a clinical risk.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Introduce mandatory business and entrepreneurship in secondary curriculum I am deeply concerned that, in 2025, we continue to deliver a national curriculum designed for the traditional career paths of the 1980s rather than the technologies and opportunities of today.
label: Department for Education

text: Declare a Bank Holiday in 2025 for the 80th anniversaries VE Day and VJ Day I would like the Government to declare a special Bank Holiday in 2025 to commemorate the 80th anniversaries of Victory in Europe (VE) Day and Victory over Japan (VJ) Day, marking the end of World War II in Europe and the Pacific.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Make defibrillators mandatory in all types of gym or exercise establishments Make it a legal requirement for defibrillators to be available in all types of gym or exercise establishment.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban the Nazi salute, like in Germany, and Austria Please pass legislation that bans the Nazi salute, and condemns individuals, and punishes repeat offenders with fines or imprisonment.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Fund specialist chronic illness flare-up centres in every county Fund dedicated, county-level chronic illness flare-up centres to manage acute flares for conditions like PoTS, Crohn’s, and Colitis. Hubs could offer rapid access to IV fluids, anti-nausea medication, pain management, and direct-to-ward admissions to reduce A&E wait times and infection risks.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Abolish the Energy Profits Levy & review the tax regime for North Sea energy Abolish the Energy Profits Levy and launch a review of the current tax regime on North Sea energy to make it more predictable, so that there is more support securing domestic oil and gas production and efficient use of UK resources.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Nationalise all water companies We want the government to bring all water companies into public ownership.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Give Early Parole or Deportation for Certain Life Prisoners in the UK The UK stands for justice and human rights, yet many life-sentence prisoners remain in custody for excessive periods despite clear evidence of rehabilitation and reform. We ask the Ministry of Justice to introduce a structured review process allowing tariff reductions, early parole or deportation.
label: Home Office

text: Raise the maximum price for MOT tests for the first time since 2010 The maximum price for an MOT test has not increased since 2010, despite a rise in many other business related costs since then. We believe this has caused many small businesses to go under, sometimes more often than is necessary.
label: Department for Transport

text: Mandate suspension of police officers under investigation for serious injuries Change the Police Conduct Regulations 2020 to make suspension mandatory for any officer under investigation for incidents causing serious injury. This should apply automatically where an independent review finds evidence of a cover-up or the withholding of material evidence.
