label: Home Office

text: Hold a referendum on the abolition of the monarchy. Hold a referendum over the abolition of the monarchy.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Make people with cancer and unable to work automatically entitled to PIP Being unable to work due to having cancer does not give you the automatic right to claim PIP, but why shouldn’t it? We think people in these circumstances should be automatically entitled to PIP. Instead they may face an added stress of having to fight the system as well as fight cancer.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Require all owned cats to be neutered We call on the Government to introduce mandatory neutering for owned cats and to create legal protections and enforcement options to safeguard cat welfare. Cats are one of the most common pets in the UK, yet we feel they have far fewer legal protections than other animals.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Introduce a 30% tax on all non-stun slaughter produce From field to fork, we believe the treatment of animals should be carried out in the most humane way possible.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require green rooves and solar panel shelters in all car parks Require all car park operators to build green roof and solar panel parking shelters which could reduce the need to use farmland for solar farms and support biodiversity.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Stop changes to the large programme uplift funding to protect our education  The Large Programme Uplift (LPU) has been changed to only support the transition of students to "Priority Sectors" of industry. This Programme is being used by many state schools to support a variety of academic goals, not just "math".
label: Department for Education

text: Raise the maximum charge for an MOT to £87.17 for cars & £47.12 for motorcycles The maximum charge for an MOT test has not increased since 2010, despite a rise in business costs. Independent garages can be forced to close due to not earning a living wage. In line with inflation since 2010 the maximum fee for a car MOT should be raised to £87.17, and for a motorcycle to £47.12.
label: Department for Transport

text: Scrap student loan interest rates in England I would like the government to abolish the interest rate on student loans, or stop universities from charging tuition fees at all.
label: HM Treasury

text: Fund Covid booster vaccines for all, with priority for Long Covid sufferers Long Covid can ruin lives and cause financial hardship so we believe the Government must try to prevent new Covid infections. We want free Covid booster vaccines for all and Long Covid sufferers should be a prioritised group.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Abolish inheritance tax We believe inheritance tax destroys family wealth for future generations and destroys opportunities of further investment into the UK. We believe it is inhumane and incredibly unfair. Many people work all their lives to build wealth, only for it to be taxed by the Government.
label: HM Treasury

text:
Ban bottom trawling in all UK waters & ratify UN High Seas Treaty Ban bottom trawling in all UK waters- not just within Marine Protected Areas (MPAs).
Phase out industrial bottom trawling by 2030, ratify the UN High seas treaty - before the September 2025 General Assembly.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text:
Seek to expel the USA from the UN using Article 6 of the UN Charter We want the Government to invoke Article 6 to seek to expel the USA from the UN.

Article 6 of the charter allows for any member, including Security Council members, to be expelled for persistent violations of UN principles. Expulsion is decided by the General Assembly after a UNSC recommendation.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Change waste classification laws so pet ashes can be buried with owners We want the Government to change the law to permit pet ashes in human graves by ending their classification as waste so that families can be buried with their beloved pets.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Link small business rates to profitability instead of property value. The Government should reform business rates, so small and micro businesses are assessed based on actual profitability rather than property rental values. We believe this would create a fairer system that reflects modern trading conditions and supports financially vulnerable high-street businesses.
label: HM Treasury

text: Make a specific offence for a taxi driver to have sexual contact with a customer We want it to be illegal for anyone who drives a passenger vehicle for hire or reward (where they are directly compensated for each journey they undertake) to make or suggest sexual contact with any customer connected to their trade.
label: Department for Transport

text: Mandate emergency hydrocortisone IM injection training in schools Mandate emergency hydrocortisone IM injection training in schools for pupils with Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH). Parents can't leave hospital without this training, yet schools can opt out of it. Change DfE guidance to mandate similar training to that for the use of EpiPens.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Stop taxing UK citizens on the state pension British citizens who have, though out their working life, paid National Insurance & tax, should not then be taxed on the state pension regardless of other earning/pensions.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Commit £30m to community cycling facilities We believe that community cycling facilities help children, families and adults become active, improving health and wellbeing while reducing pressure on the NHS and that existing programmes have delivered proven results. Government backing is needed to expand this model across the UK.
label: Department for Transport

text: Create a national SEN Qualifications Regulator & SEN Qualifications Framework We believe young people with SEND/EHCPs currently have no dedicated qualification framework or regulator to ensure fair progression, recognised outcomes or equal access to vocational and academic pathways.
label: Department for Education

text: Investigate safeguarding & social care referral practices for SEND children We urge the Government to investigate safeguarding and social care referral practices for SEND children to prevent any possible misuse of safeguarding, ensure duties under Section 47 of the Children Act 1989 are upheld, and ensure schools adopt trauma-informed practices before safeguarding actions.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Lower the age for invites to regular mammograms to 30 We think the recommended age for routine mammograms should be lowered from 50 to 30. We believe this change could increase early detection, offer better health outcomes, and save countless lives
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban isolation rooms/booths in schools Ban isolation rooms/booths in all schools immediately. Replace punitive isolation with trauma-informed, therapeutic behaviour support. Mandate national monitoring and enforcement. Prioritise children’s mental health and rights under UNCRC Article 28.
label: Department for Education

text: Establish an electoral process and MP to represent UK Overseas Citizens Establish an MP  for the 5 million British citizens living overseas, who currently rely on former constituencies, aligning the UK with countries like France and Italy, which offer direct parliamentary representation for expats.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Standardised aftercare information and follow-up after endometriosis surgery We want the Government to ensure national mandatory, standardised post-operative aftercare guidance for patients undergoing endometriosis surgery, with information tailored to the severity and extent of surgery.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Increase funding for Multiple System Atrophy training, awareness & diagnosis  Increase funding for greater professional training, public awareness and earlier diagnosis for Multiple System Atrophy (MSA) to ensure better patient and family support across the NHS.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Add professional employment mediation into the employment tribunal ADR process Stop the plans to recruit more Tribunal Judges and Tribunal Members and instead implement professional mediation before judicial mediation which we think could resolve most issues. Invest the saved money into addressing the root cause by developing key resolution skills within organisations.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Regulate veterinary practices to help make them more affordable About 57% of households in the UK have a pet, yet we think veterinary prices are through the roof. With the cost of living increasing, we think there should be a limit on how much profit a veterinary practice can make from selling medications and completing procedures.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text:
Make 'Tragedy Chanting' online a specific criminal offence I wish for the Government/Parliament to legislate to make the act of Tragedy Chanting/Posting on-line a specific criminal offence.
Provide police and the CPS with the powers to prosecute such triggering and traumatising acts.
label: Home Office

text: Collect and Publish statistics on crimes committed by illegal immigrants Collect and publish statistics on crimes committed by illegal immigrants, additionally categorise those crimes by nature eg, Sexual, Violent, Terrorism, Theft, Fraud etc.
label: Home Office

text: Require local authorities to remove all flags from street furniture Require local authorities to promptly remove flags that have been put up illegally in public spaces (under the Highways Act 1980), and encourage anyone wanting to display a flag to do so on their personal and private property.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Ban all forms of conversion therapy Since 2018, successive UK governments have promised a ban on conversion therapy and have yet to pass legislation against the practice, which many experts have said amounts to "torture". We believe the current government needs to act immediately to ban anti-LGBTQIA+ conversion therapy.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review access to cash in rural areas, require FCA to reform rules and criteria Review access to cash in rural areas and require the FCA to reform its rules, and LINK’s criteria, so more rural communities like the Highlands can have banking hubs. It must better reflect rural issues: ageing populations; limited internet access; and geography to help stop financial exclusion.
label: HM Treasury

text: Drop the state pension age back down to 60 Instead of increasing the retirement age every two years it needs to stay at 60 years old to allow individuals to enjoy their retirement with the time that they have less
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Require venues to have full, up to date accessibility info on their websites. To improve disability rights, there should be a legal requirement for all venues, businesses and shops to publish easy to find accessibility information on their websites and/ or social media, even if it means stating they are not accessible.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Ban the sale, ownership and access to smartphones for children 16 and under We believe the UK is failing in its duty to safeguard its youth from the adverse effects of unmonitored smartphone use. We believe a ban for children 16 and under could help protect future generations from exploitation, radicalisation, harassment, addiction, misinformation and disinformation.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Make parental alienation a criminal offence We believe the government should make parental alienation a criminal offence, to deter separated parents from alienating children from the other parent. Parental alienation is where a parent manipulates their child to go against their other parent.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Hold MPs Accountable: By-Elections if They Lie or Mislead the Public 3 Times I want MPs held fully accountable for lying or misleading the public in any context - on social media, in interviews, speeches, or Parliament. Each lie could incur a fine, be logged in a public register, and if an MP accumulates three lies, a by-election could be triggered to protect democracy.
label: Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

text: Allow sentence reductions for rehabilitated Extended Determinate prisoners -EDS- We want the Government to review Extended Determinate Sentences (EDS) and allow sentence reductions for prisoners who demonstrate sustained good behaviour and rehabilitation. Any changes should apply to those currently serving EDS as well as future sentences.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Require formal recording and government monitoring of assaults on teachers Create a national system requiring schools to formally record assaults against teachers and school staff. The Government should monitor and publish this data to understand the scale of the issue and support policies that improve staff safety.
label: Department for Education

text: Require all MPs to publish their tax returns by law I think this would help ensure transparency, and should include information for the public to see on how much money MPs earn, where their income comes from, and whether they pay the correct amount of taxes.
label: Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

text: Publish a detailed plan to tackle illegal migration and stop boat crossings We want a clearer and more detailed plan from the Government to tackle illegal migration and stop the dangerous boat crossings. We want the Government to clearly set out what their strategy is. We think it's time for transparency and action. Sign this petition and hold them accountable!
label: Home Office

text: Require airlines to amend stored API data between outbound and inbound flights Following the UK's full implementation of ETA on 25/02/2026 and the EU's full implementation of ETIAS in 2027, please require all airlines operating flights to the UK to allow dual nationals to amend advance passenger information (API) data between outbound and inbound flights.
label: Department for Transport

text: Reinstate the hard shoulder on all motorways We think it is in the public interest with regard to road safety and saving lives to re- instate the hard shoulder on all motorways that have had it removed or have been changed to four lanes.
label: Department for Transport

text: Make it a legal requirement for public event venues to use subtitles/captions Make it a legal requirement for public entertainment services, e.g sports stadiums, concerts & shows, etc. to use subtitles, increasing the inclusivity of the entertainment sector. Whether this be on a big screen or a handheld device that can be requested by individuals who may require it.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Independent environmental impact assessment for data centres & make AI opt-in Require independent environmental impact assessments before any data centres are approved end the designation of data centres as "critical national infrastructure". We also call for AI to be opt-in, not built into everyday online services by default, so the public is not forced to fuel this boom.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Ban social media influencers from promoting/advertising cosmetic surgery I want the Government to make it illegal for social media influencers to promote or advertise cosmetic surgery. We believe this could help prevent often vulnerable individuals seeking plastic surgery, especially from cheap providers abroad.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Require sanitary waste bins in all toilets regardless of gender Change UK law to make it a legal requirement for businesses, public places and all social places with female, MALE and unisex restrooms to provide a safe and hygienic means for the disposal of sanitary waste to prevent environmental harm and maintain public health and hygiene standards.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Allow care workers to access 5-year ILR route like other health and care workers Change settlement proposals so all care workers can earn settlement after 5 years like other health and care workers on Skilled Worker Visas. We believe care is skilled, essential work that helps people live safely, out of hospital, and their family to stay in work.
label: Home Office

text: Pause immigration until Home Office processes all pending asylum applications Pause all legal and illegal immigration until those who are already in our country are processed correctly. Our resources are already stretched. We don't feel the present Government is doing enough. Enough is Enough!
label: Home Office

text: Require restaurants to list all ingredients in their food when asked I would like it to be law for all restaurants to be required to show customers all of the ingredients in the food when asked. To help customers who have allergies that aren't one of the main 14 allergies.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Childless to be eligible for Residence Nil Rate Band for inheritance tax Ensure that the childless have the same IHT allowances as those who have children, and benefit from both the 'Residence Nil Rate Band' of £175,000 and the Nil Rate Band of £325,000.
label: HM Treasury

text: Ban Live Facial Recognition (LFR) in all public and private spaces We call on the Government to ban the use of Live Facial Recognition (LFR) surveillance in all public and private spaces. This includes by private companies and in retail spaces unless strictly for national security or immediate prevention of terrorism, with strict oversight and judicial approval.
label: Home Office

text: Public inquiry into child deaths following family court cases We think we need an inquiry into the deaths of children following family court cases.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Cap donations to political parties & politicians at £500 yearly, for each donor Cap all donations to political parties and politicians at £500 per year, for each individual person or organisation making the donation—including unions and companies.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Extend FOIA to any private company providing services under government contract I would like the government to extend the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) 2000 to any private companies, including utility companies, providing a service under government contract.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Mandatory 50% female jury representation for trials of rape & violence vs women Selective randomisation of the jury would enable at least 50% female representation on trials involving rape & violence against women, domestic violence & intimate partner abuse.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Update on consultation on Overseas Dentist Provisional Registration Route We urge the UK Government to publish the responses and next steps to the consultation on overseas dentist provisional registration route. The consultation closed in May. We think the Govt must clarify why progress stalled, provide a clear timeline, and prioritize resolving NHS dental shortages.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Bring the Parking Code of Practice into law, as per the 2019 Act of Parliament. I was pursued by a parking company for an alleged parking violation. When it went to court, the claim was dismissed. I now want the Government to bring back the Parking Code of Practice to help protect motorists, after it was withdrawn in 2022.
label: Department for Transport

text: Launch a review into improving social housing provision for families Launch a review into reforming social housing so families with young children aren’t trapped in unsafe, overcrowded flats. The review should look into creating fairer allocation rules, offering suitable downsizing options for older tenants, and ensuring families have access to a safe, healthy home.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Ban family houses from being converted into Houses of Multiple Occupancy (HMOs) Introduce legislation to prevent property developers & private landlords from converting family homes into HMOs, especially ex-council homes. We think that there is already a dearth of family homes for low-income working families, & by converting them into HMOs, the situation is being made worse.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Cut VAT, Slash Beer Duty, reform business rates and cap energy costs for pubs We urge the Government to cut VAT for pubs to 10% or less, reduce beer duty, reform business rates, introduce an energy cap, and address unfair wholesale pricing. Without urgent action, thousands of pubs face closure—threatening jobs, communities, and local culture.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Ban animal testing, require use of alternative testing and invest more in this The government should ban animal testing, and require and invest more in the use of cruelty-free alternatives like AI and human cell research. We believe we need stronger laws to protect animals from painful experiments, forcing companies to use safer, modern scientific methods and not harm animals.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Government to support the Elections (Proportional Representation) Bill We call on the UK Government to support the progression of the Elections (Proportional Representation) Bill, ensuring time for a Second Reading in the Commons. Even if a vote were to fail, this is an important issue and deserves open debate and a free vote in both Houses.
label: Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

text: Family parking space badges for children up to 5 & fines for illegitimate use Create a badge system similar to blue badge, that will allow families with little children up to 5 years old or pregnant mothers, to be the only ones allowed to use parent parking. Introduce fines for individuals who break the rules and park there without a child under 5 or being pregnant.
label: Department for Transport

text: End the mandatory meat requirement in English school meals Remove the mandatory requirement in the Requirements for School Food Regulations 2014 requiring maintained schools and academies to serve meat or poultry three days per week. We believe this rule conflicts with environmental goals and health guidance on reducing meat consumption.
label: Department for Education

text: Remove the right for convicted sex offenders to appeal their sentence As the law stands convicted sex offenders and child predators are entitled to appeal their sentences should they feel the sentencing is to harsh. I wish to remove their right to appeal their sentences.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Change rules so parents with 50/50 shared care don’t pay child maintenance I think we should stop forcing parents with 50/50 shared care to pay maintenance to the other parent. This rule needs changing.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Review care and support given to women facing ovary removal Women facing ovary removal deserve clear information about surgical menopause, guidance on HRT/ alternatives, and proper follow-up care. Surgical menopause must be recognised as distinct from natural menopause, with individualised support reflecting its sudden, severe impact of hormone deprivation.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reopen British oil and gas fields using taxpayer funds for UK use only We think Britain has huge gas and oil resources that we are not utilising. We have very low storage capacity for those we import.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Review NHS PTSD diagnosis and treatment pathways The Government should conduct a review to look at introducing national PTSD diagnosis and treatment standards, including: assessment within 8 weeks, improved GP trauma awareness training, recognised PTSD referral pathways, faster access to appropriate specialist treatment and support.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require licensed venues to offer free anti-spiking drink covers to patrons Amend the Licensing Act 2003 to make anti-spiking drink covers a mandatory licence condition for all venues serving open drinks in England and Wales. Covers should be available free of charge, on request, to any patron.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Urge UN to send peacekeepers into Gaza & the West Bank We urge the Government to call on the UN to send peacekeepers to enter Gaza and the West Bank to help protect civilians there.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Fund state support for young people aged 18-25 who leave the care system We believe care should not end at 18. Each year, over 10,000 young people leave care in England and are pushed into independence without family support. We call for funding for extended supported accommodation, financial support, and long-term mental health care so no care leaver struggles alone.
label: Department for Education

text: Raise the personal tax allowance to the state pension rate Always raise the personal allowance to ensure state pension is free from tax.
label: HM Treasury

text: Formally recognise the killing of Armenians in 1915-1923 as genocide We are calling for the Government to formally recognise the killing of an estimated 1.5 Million Armenians by the Ottoman Empire from 1915-1923 as genocide. The Government states that "any determination as to whether genocide has occurred is a matter for a competent national or international court".
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Require NHS autism diagnoses to include assessment of level of support needed Autism varies greatly. Some autistic people live independently, while others are non-verbal, unsafe without supervision, self-harm, or need lifelong care. We want NHS autism diagnoses to include a clear, nationally standardised assessment of support-need levels.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Protect graves of all UK military veterans from reuse under new burial proposals Amend proposed reforms to burial law to permanently protect all UK military veterans’ graves from reuse, regardless of CWGC or MoD status, and create a national register allowing families to designate and safeguard graves of those who served.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Create community right to buy for empty pubs that are Assets of Community Value We call on the Government to pass a law where pubs designated as an Asset of Community Value that are empty for 6 months or more, and where the owner refuses to sell or rent out the asset at an independently assessed fair market value, automatically trigger a community right to buy at market value.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text:
Introduce national heatwave resilience strategy & legal protections Create a national heat resilience strategy with legal protections for excessive indoor temperature in workplaces and homes.

Britain increasingly faces dangerous summer heat, but there is no legal maximum workplace temperature in the UK, and many buildings are ill-equipped for heatwaves.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Require coercive control awareness training for some sectors We call upon the UK Government and Parliament to implement requirements for coercive control awareness training for all professionals working in these sectors - healthcare, education, social services and police forces.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Count waiting time from Covid-19 Home Office delays toward ILR 5-year residence We call on the UK Government to count Home Office delays during the nearly two-year Covid-19 pandemic toward the 5-year residence requirement for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR), ensuring fairness for long-term residents affected by delays beyond their control.
label: Home Office

text: More regulation for home-based childcare: nannies, maternity nurses & tutors We believe that this sector needs more regulation. Anyone can call themselves a nanny, maternity nurse, or tutor without qualifications, training, or background checks. This can put children at risk.
label: Department for Education

text: Extend the classic car tax exemption to 35 year old vehicles I think the classic car collectors are focusing not only on cars built in the '50s and' 60s but also modern classics of specific heritage such as specialist imports from other countries. These vehicles are routinely on show at classic car events yet many owners pay high rates of vehicle excise duty
label: HM Treasury

text:
Cap service charges & require publication of how they are calculated and spent We urge the government to:
1. Cap service charges fairly, in line with existing rent controls
2. Require transparent publication of how these charges are set and used.
We think this is needed to help protect tenants from unfair costs and keep housing affordable and fair.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Introduce a law preventing copyrighted work being used to train AI We believe that creatives need to have ownership over their work. We think there should be a legal opt out scheme that could allow creatives to protect their work
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Ban cheap renewable energy from being charged at the price of expensive gas Mandate energy providers to stop charging the same price as expensive gas for much cheaper renewable energy. We think they should pass any savings on to consumers, rather than keeping them as profit.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Issue a statement committing to no new drilling licenses for oil or gas We ask the Government to abide by the 2024 Labour manifesto and commit to no new drilling licenses for North Sea oil or gas. This summer has been another warning of extreme weather ahead. We believe the science is clear; to ensure climate security any remaining reserves must stay in the ground.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Fund free parking for key workers at their places of work I want to speak about fairness, recognition, and practical support for the people who keep our communities running: our key workers. Key workers are not a luxury. They are a necessity. They are nurses, paramedics, teachers, social workers, carers, police officers, firefighters and support staff.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reform nurse education funding, cancel debt & reinstate bursaries Abolish tuition fees for nurse training, reinstate the NHS nursing bursary, and forgive existing student loan debt for nurses working in the NHS.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Commission a Treasury Review On The Practicalities Of Levying A Wealth Tax. We believe the government should study the practicalities of a tax on wealth. This should include studying wealth taxes internationally and the work of think tanks, to consider appropriate thresholds and percentages. This could also consider an exit tax designed to reduce tax avoidance.
label: HM Treasury

text: Require energy companies to offer analogue meters  We want the Government to require energy companies to offer analogue meters for those who cannot have or do not want smart meters.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Grooming gang national enquiry to name officials and consider failures to act To ensure that the culture within the Crown and Public Service, including but not limited to the Police, Social Work, Teaching, plus amongst elected officials, is one of accountability.
label: Home Office

text: Review digital exclusion in NHS GP practices and produce national guidelines We call on the Government to review NHS GP services to ensure elderly and vulnerable patients can access health services without being disadvantaged by digital-first systems.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund a COVID-19 Booster Vaccination for All NHS Healthcare Workers We call on the Government to fund routine COVID-19 booster vaccinations for all NHS healthcare workers, regardless of age or underlying conditions.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Stop price increases by water service providers failing environmental standards The Government to direct Ofwat to block price rises by water providers until they meet strict environmental & service standards, including binding pollution targets, independent monitoring, stronger fines, & a ban on executive bonuses until performance & customer trust are restored.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: End Section 24 taxation against private individual landlords We ask the Government to abolish Section 24 finance cost restrictions for private individual landlords and apply the same tax treatment and mortgage interest deductibility rules that currently apply to limited companies and corporate landlords.
label: HM Treasury

text: Inform patients if vaccine was developed from aborted human foetus cell lines Call on the UK Government to ensure that information leaflets relating to vaccines state whether they were developed using cell lines originating from aborted human fetuses so that patients can make an informed decision, based on their conscience, whether or not to accept these vaccines.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Enable disabled bus pass users to travel during peak times across England We call on the Government to change the English National Concessionary Travel Scheme (ENCTS) so disabled bus pass users can use their pass before 09.30 am, and provide the necessary funding to local councils.
label: Department for Transport

text: Require NHS settings to address fragrance exposure as a patient safety risk Require NHS organisations to introduce fragrance awareness measures, including signage, staff guidance, and consideration of low to zero fragrance areas to reduce preventable reactions in sensitive patients.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Parents/guardian legal right to prevent use of their deceased child’s image I want parents or guardians to have the legal right to stop people using a dead child's name or picture to make money, mock them, provoke others or glorify violence and to be able to get that content removed when the family has not agreed to it.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Ban all public airports from charging drop-off and pick-up fees We believe the Government should ban public airports from charging drop-off and pick-up fees by making it a condition of their license to operate as an airport.
label: Department for Transport

text: DEFRA Pursue UK Wide Monitoring & Publication of Farmed Salmon Safety & Welfare We call on DEFRA to pursue collaboration with devolved administrations to monitor and publish a comprehensive annual UK Farmed Salmon Safety & Welfare Report collating data from various regulators and organisations.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Allow all dependent children of Skilled Workers to pay home tuition fees We are concerned the proposed changes to ILR routes could significantly affect the hopes and dreams of many dependent children of Skilled Worker visa holders, possibly hindering their goals, postponing their degrees due to high international tuition fees and entering lower skilled jobs.
label: Home Office

text:
Exempt hospices from increase in employers’ national insurance Hospices support the NHS in providing end of life care and support to those with life limiting illnesses.
The NHS and the public sector have been exempted from the increase in employers NIC increase. We think the same should apply to hospices.
label: HM Treasury

text: Do not extend the BBC licence fee to streaming services There are widespread reports that the Government is considering extending the BBC licence fee to include subscribers of streaming services that are not owned or run by the BBC. We believe this is a wholly unacceptable proposal.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Introduce a Kannada language GCSE Kannada is a language spoken by millions in Karnataka, southern state of India. There are Kannada speaking skilled workers in UK and other parts of the world. We request Government to recognise support and encourage Kannada language learning in schools, by creating a Kannada GCSE.
label: Department for Education

text: Maintain the £3 bus fare cap permanently As of the budget, we think that working people on lower incomes or who live in rural communities will suffer as a consequence of the decision to raise the bus fare cap to £3. We think bus fares should be permanently capped at £3 after December 2025.
label: Department for Transport

text: Calculate child maintenance based on net rather than gross pay I think the current child support system is unfair to working parents. I would like the Government to change the system so that payments are calculated based on net take-home pay rather than the current gross pay.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Review and strengthen enforcement of welfare laws for animals in street begging We want the UK Government to review and strengthen enforcement of animal welfare laws by supporting routine checks and microchip scanning of dogs used for begging, and giving authorities powers to remove animals at risk of fear, distress or exploitation.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Eliminate VAT on hot takeaway food We urge the Government to eliminate VAT on hot takeaway food.
label: HM Treasury

text: Fund advanced testing for UTI and improved support for UTI sufferers We call on the Government to fund more advanced testing for UTIs and to make it available via the NHS. We also want more funding for improved support for those suffering with recurring UTIs, and a review of support for those affected in workplaces.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require psychological injury assessments in coercive control cases Require mandatory psychological injury assessments in coercive control cases, ensuring trauma is formally recognised and sentencing reflects the real harm caused. Psychological abuse destroys lives, the justice system must treat it as serious injury. These changes could be known as Skye's Law.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban synthetic fragrance chemicals from public spaces and enforce full labelling We want the Government to ban the use of synthetic fragrance chemicals and ambient scenting in public spaces, and introduce mandatory full-ingredient labelling including health risks on all fragranced consumer products.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Reverse application of 20% VAT to independent schools With the recent policy decision to apply 20% VAT on independent schools, we believe this additional burden on tax paying parents has had significant impact on the education system & caused the closure of schools with great history, legacy & value.
label: HM Treasury

text: Review of guidance parents receive after a Patau’s syndrome diagnosis I ask the Government to conduct a formal review and consideration of updates to the guidance parents receive if their baby is suspected of or diagnosed with Patau’s syndrome, to ensure they are always accurately informed that some children may survive Patau’s syndrome, and that outcomes may vary.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Anti-social behaviour in social housing: Review police response and enforcement I call on the Government to review police response to anti-social behaviour in social housing & enforcement when tenants engage (but not limited to) threats, intimidation & repeated harmful behaviour. I believe there should be clearer limits on out-of-court disposals & faster action from the police
label: Home Office

text: Introduce statutory regulation and enforcement for managing agents & freeholders Introduce mandatory statutory regulation of managing agents and freeholders, including licensing, enforceable professional standards, financial penalties for breaches, powers to suspend or ban repeat offenders, and automatic cost sanctions where leaseholders are forced into tribunal action.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Stop sending military aid to Ukraine The Government should cancel all Military aid to Ukraine as we believe it is a waste of Economic resources. We think we could instead spend any money saved on our military to help ensure our children's future.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Ban the release of balloons and sky lanterns Sky lanterns and balloon releases present hazards to animals. While I am sympathetic to those who have lost a loved one, I believe there are many alternative and longer lasting ways to remember them, e.g. tree planting.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Introduce a mandatory 15-minute grace period in all car parks The Government should require all council and private car parks to adopt a single, mandatory grace period of 15 minutes. This rule should replace all existing “grace” and “consideration” periods to create one clear, universal standard.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review the UK-US Extradition Treaty We call on the UK Government to review the UK-US Extradition Treaty to ensure that the rights of British nationals are protected.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Hold a referendum on replacing First Past the Post with proportional voting We call for a referendum with the question: “Should the UK replace First Past the Post with a system of Proportional Representation?” We think it should be held before the next scheduled General Election. If passed, we think the new system should be designed by a non-partisan expert panel.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Fund the NHS to create a national database for NHS medical records I would like the Government to fund the NHS to create a national database for NHS medical records so they are able to be accessed at hospitals across the country without the need for contacting other hospitals.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Improve mental health services for neurodiverse young people We call on the Government to increase funding for NHS Child and Adolescents Mental Health Services to enable early diagnosis, intervention, treatment and support for children who are neurodiverse. We believe CAMHS requires more funding to improve staffing, treatment and care problems.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review extended determinate sentencing: reductions for rehabilitated prisoners We'd like Government to review the use of extended determinate sentences (EDS) and consider allowing sentence reductions for prisoners who’ve completed their custodial term while demonstrating excellent behaviour and real rehabilitation.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Send flotilla of ships with aid to break Israel’s blockade The UK government should heed the call to break the blockade on Gaza. It should work with other governments around the world to send a flotilla of ships with guarantees of British and international protection.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Reform the way PIP assessments are conducted for deaf people We think PIP claims for deaf people should be assessed through the form, with no telephone or face to face consultations.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Stop the EV Pay-Per-Mile Tax Cancel the planned pay-per-mile road tax for electric vehicles. We want to stop unfair double-taxing of drivers who already pay a premium VED surcharge on family-sized EVs and hybrids.
label: Department for Transport

text: Stop deducting carer's allowance from income based welfare Currently carer's allowance affects income based welfare. Carer's allowance is deducted from income based welfare like universal credit and Income based ESA.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Legislate a statutory maximum temperature for classrooms and fund school cooling We want the government to establish a statutory maximum classroom temperature and provide ring-fenced grants to fund air conditioning in schools that breach this limit. We are concerned that schools cannot afford this vital safety equipment without central funding.
label: Department for Education

text:
Remove or extend the 6 month time limit on prosecution for summary offences
 Currently, summary offences must be laid before a court within six months of the offence. Once that time passes, no matter the evidence or the harm, justice is simply gone, and legal action cannot be taken. A review of this rule is urgently needed.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: To prohibit adults without a child from entering designated children's areas We propose that UK law prohibits adults from entering or interacting with children in designated children's areas, such as playgrounds, unless accompanying at least one child.
label: Home Office

text: Change the requirements of how often MPs attend a Parliamentary sitting. To set requirements for MPs to attend the House of Commons and to hold constituency surgeries on a minimum number of occasions throughout the year.
label: Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

text: End mileage tax on EVs & plug-in hybrid cars and reduce VAT on public charging Remove the planned mileage tax on electric and plug-in hybrid cars.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill’s impact on non-school settings Ensure the Bill does not require full-time non-school settings, including youth clubs, enrichment programmes, and religious or cultural centres, to adhere to the Independent School Standards if they are not providing full-time academic education in place of a school.
label: Department for Education

text: Illegal immigrants entering this country to have DNA taken We think it should be mandatory for illegal immigrants entering this country to have their DNA taken.
label: Home Office

text: Stop all non-British citizens from voting in elections We believe all non-British citizens, including illegal and legal migrants who are not British citizens, should not be allowed to bolster the vote of any representative in office, by any electoral party, and as such, should be barred from being on the electoral roll and being able to vote.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Hold a rejoin EU referendum now We call for a referendum on whether the United Kingdom should rejoin the European Union after the Brexit referendum, giving the public a fresh, informed choice based on current realities and future needs.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Recognise Cultic Abuse in Statutory Safeguarding Guidance Update statutory safeguarding guidance to explicitly recognise cultic abuse alongside other forms of abuse, with clearer guidance for identification, response and referral across children’s and adults’ safeguarding frameworks.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Launch a review of eligibility for the Rural Fuel Duty Relief Scheme At a time of ongoing cost-of-living pressures, we want the Government to urgently review eligibility for the Rural Fuel Duty Relief Scheme to ensure fairness, consistency and equal treatment for remote, rural and island communities, including those in Argyll.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Amend the Firearms Act to allow licensed defensive tasers for female adults 18+ Amend the Firearms Act 1968 to create a regulated licensing category for specialist defensive tasers, enabling lawful possession by female adults aged 18+ with mandatory training and safeguards, to support personal safety in the context of high levels of violence against women and vulnerable adults.
label: Home Office

text: Maintain current fireworks regulations and the 120dB maximum noise limit Keep current firework laws and the 120dB limit. Existing rules balance tradition, safety, and public joy. We believe that further noise cuts are unnecessary and would harm the UK firework industry and businesses.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Review barriers & fund accessibility pathway for M.E & Chronic Illness patients We would like the government to work with people with Myalgic Encephalomyelitis, and those with similar levels of chronic illness, to identify the barriers to accessing healthcare.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Protect Online Privacy – Ban Charging Users to Reject Tracking Cookies Make it illegal for websites to charge users for rejecting tracking cookies. Businesses should not exploit consent by forcing users to choose between paying or having their data tracked.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Increase max sentence for injury caused due to dangerous driving to 10 years We want the government to change the law on dangerous driving. We think current sentences are too soft for the serious effects dangerous drivers can cause to victims.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Issue a formal UK Government apology to the victims of the Tinker Experiment We call upon the UK Government to apologise for its role in the Tinker Experiment. We also want the Government to recognise the intergenerational trauma caused to families within the indigenous highland traveller community.
label: Scotland Office

text: Review and refund overcharged UK Student and Child Student visa fees International students who paid UK Student visa fees from Autumn 2023 onwards were overcharged £127-£161, confirmed by a House of Lords Committee. The Home Office's own refunds policy allows claims within 5 years but affected students have never been officially notified.
label: Home Office

text: Make a new Family Visitor visa for close non-EU relatives of UK residents We urge the Government to make a new family visitor visa for close NON-EU relatives of UK residents who are visiting the UK for 6 months or less. We want it to be faster, cheaper, and recognise family ties - unlike the current Standard Visitor visa which we feel treats relatives like tourists.
label: Home Office

text: Reverse decision to increase the cap on bus fares from £2 to £3. People are struggling to make ends meet and the £2 bus ticket cap has been a lifeline to many, particularly in rural communities.
label: Department for Transport

text: Prevent arms sales to the UAE following reports of UK arms being used in Sudan There have been reports of UK manufactured small-arms target systems & British-made engines for armoured personnel carriers being found being used by the paramilitary RSF in Sudan. The British government must not approve sales to the UAE as we believe there is a risk they could pass them to the RSF
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Do not ban mobile phones in schools for students over KS3 The government is moving toward a legal ban on mobile phones in schools. We think that while this is agreeable for perhaps Key Stage 3 and below, it is simply ridiculous at a certain age. People who are able to vote in general elections by the end of this year, are treated like children.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund lowering the age for a smear test to 16 years old I would like government to fund the NHS so the minimum age for a smear test is lowered, to prevent women from having cell changes at a younger age leading to cervical cancer or even vulva cancer.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require medical history to be listed on horse passports I want greater protection for horse welfare and for buyers from neglectful sellers within the equine world; where profit exceeds care. Legal requirement for all medical history to be listed on a horse passport to make it harder for sellers to be deceitful.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Create an inclusive special envoy for home educating families Create a special envoy for home educating families, who would be a mediator between Government, officials and the Home Education Community, and suggest amendments to the Children’s Wellbeing & Schools Bill. This special envoy should include home educating parents.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund new reservoirs to increase future water supplies England faces growing pressure on its water supplies due to factors like population growth, climate change and rising demand. The Government estimates 5 billion litres more water per day will be needed by 2050. Substantial additional water storage capacity will be needed to meet this challenge.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Fund greater police presence in bike theft hotspots There have been increased reports recently of violent bike theft in Richmond Park, Regents Park and other public spaces. The victims of such incidents may be fearful for their lives and may not have the courage to cycle again. This is abhorrent.
label: Home Office

text: Suspend MCA plans to remove Coastguard Rescue Officer remuneration Require the Maritime and Coastguard Agency to suspend its plans to remove remuneration for Coastguard Rescue Officers and move to an expenses-only model, pending an urgent legal, equality and operational review.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review Equality Act 2010 to protect Transgender, Non-binary & Intersex people Launch a review into updating the Equality Act 2010 to explicitly improve protections for transgender children and to include intersex and non-binary adults and children.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Do not put transgender people into prisons of their birth sex The Government has said it is reviewing transgender prisoner policy following the recent Supreme Court ruling. We think the Government should rule out putting trans people in prisons of their birth sex.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Hold a referendum in Wales on abolishing the Senedd and Welsh Government To hold a referendum in Wales on whether to abolish the Senedd and Welsh Government and return the government of Wales to Westminster.
label: Cabinet Office

text: We call on UK Government to provide sex crime victims with free legal support We call on the UK Government to set out in statue that sex crime victims are a vulnerable group from first police contact, and grant them a legal representative at the taxpayer expense.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Immediately tighten immigration requirements Require all new & existing visa holders including BNO visas, applicants & dependants to: Live 10 yrs in the UK to apply for ILR; Pay NHS & state school fees; Earn £40k pa + £20k for each non-working dependant; Be professional; Work 3 yrs with ILR in the UK to apply for citizenship; Meet Eng level C1
label: Home Office

text:
Ban cousin marriages We call upon the Government to introduce legislation banning cousin marriages.
Marriage is already illegal between siblings, so why not cousins?
label: Ministry of Justice

text:
Legalise adult adoption We think it is time for adult adoption to be legalised in the UK.

We believe amending this law would offer individuals the opportunity, as a legal adult, to sever connections with absent, abusive, or otherwise unsuitable parents.
label: Department for Education

text:
Legalise pepper spray as a method of self-defence

 We want the government to legalise pepper spray as a method of self-defence to improve the safety of women. It was reported in October 2024 that since 2020, 25 women have been violently killed in Northern Ireland. Many other women are attacked and sexually assaulted.
label: Home Office

text: Give home fee status to students who came as dependents & with no settled status Change the law so that all students who came to the UK under the age of 18 on a dependent visa, but without settled status, are eligible for home fee status at UK universities.
label: Department for Education

text: Publish framework to remove VAT on donations of medicines Patients with rare cancers face limited treatment options. VAT should not create another barrier to accessing possibly life-extending medicines offered free of charge. We ask the Government to publish their plans on removing VAT on medicines donated via compassionate-use and early-access schemes.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Take action to improve waiting times for access to work applications Some people with disabilities are waiting over 6-months for Department of Work and Pensions (DWP) to contact them to discuss the support they need to obtain or stay in paid work or set-up their own businesses.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Only resident British citizens over 18 should be allowed to vote in elections. Restrict voting rights to only resident British citizens aged 18 or over for general elections and local elections in England.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Increase funding and support for animal rescue and rehabilitation organisations. We want the UK Government to provide substantial financial support to animal rescue organisations, invest in rehabilitation programmes, and promote public awareness campaigns to alleviate the strain on these vital services.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Review accountability & evidence standards in children’s social care Launch a review into children’s social care services in England which includes looking into strengthening evidence standards for decisions affecting families, improved independent review rights and correction processes for inaccurate records.
label: Department for Education

text: Only UK residents who pay or have paid PAYE can vote in general elections We think only UK resident's, who pay or paid PAYE should have the right to vote in general elections. We think this government is not acting in the best interest of its people, who built the country and economy.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Create an Emergency Services medal for members that are injured on duty I propose a medal for Emergency Service workers that are injured on duty resulting in medical retirement. I would also ask that Emergency Service members that have been medically retired due to injuries received on duty prior to the creation of such a medal be eligible.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Ensure Disabled Residents Can Access Their Own Homes We urge HM Government to enforce s.36 and Schedule 4 of the Equality Act 2010. Some landlords are not currently making reasonable adjustments to communal areas when critically needed, leaving disabled residents vulnerable and at risk of injuries.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Fund free British Sign Language Courses for deaf people and their friends/family I am profoundly deaf. I have hearing aids and I can lipread. This is still not enough in circumstances like noisy environment and at home too when I choose to have hearing breaks, which many deaf people will do.
label: Department for Education

text: Increase funding for Endometriosis care and support We want more funding for specialists and resources for faster diagnosis and treatment for endometriosis and expand support services and fertility support. We want further investment in research to improve diagnostic tools and develop treatments. This could reduce NHS waiting times.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Increase the Council Tax Single Person Discount from 25% to 50% Amend Council Tax legislation to increase the Single Person Discount to 50% for all single-adult households. We believe this will ensure fair taxation for people living alone.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Lower the voting age to 16 for general elections We believe 16 and 17-year-olds have no say in their own future. Despite the profound impact that government policies could have on our lives, we feel the voices of our generation remain unheard. According to the Office for National Statistics, there are 1.6 million people aged 16-17.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Deport all asylum seekers that have broken the law We think that by breaking the law, they prove that they are of a criminal mindset & allowing them to continue living in the UK may feed into their criminalistic mindset.
label: Home Office

text:
Increase the UK national speed limits Change restricted road speeds that are 20 zones to 30 mph
Change Single carriageway A road speeds from 60mph to 80mph
Change Dual carriageway A road and motorway speeds from 70mph to 100mph
label: Department for Transport

text: Reinstate capital punishment for rape or for serious sexual assault Every day another person is raped or sexually assaulted resulting in physical and emotional trauma, in some cases transmission of diseases or unwanted pregnancy.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban the Shaving of 90% of Tail Hair from the Draught Horse Breed. It is common practice among those who show heavy horses to shave/clip up to 90% of a horse's tail, thinking it shows off the horses' hindquarters to better advantage. We think it is cruel and unnecessary to deprive a horse of its natural tail, and want this archaic practice to be banned.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Increase Universal Credit savings limits in line with inflation We ask the Government to increase the £6,000 and £16,000 capital thresholds to the value these had in real-terms when they were set in 2006; introduce automatic annual uprating to maintain their value; and set proportionately higher capital thresholds for joint claims than for single claimants.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Allow parents to take their children out of school for 5 school days in a year Currently attendance is high on the agenda for Ofsted and schools. If a parent wants to take their child away, parents can be fined. We would like the government to authorise parents to take their own children away on holiday when they want, for up to 5 days.
label: Department for Education

text: Hold a review into alcohol home delivery and safeguarding of vulnerable adults Commission a review into safeguarding gaps in the home delivery of alcohol. It should examine enforcement of the Licensing Act 2003 for delivered alcohol, doorstep intoxication checks, and the regulatory accountability of online delivery platforms.
label: Home Office

text: Introduce local authority run permit system for homeless outreach services Introduce permit system for organisations delivering homeless outreach services. We think a permit system overseen by local authorities could ensure a better regulated provision and ensure service standards, preventing the delivery of such services being banned due to poor practice of some services.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Suspend parental rights when arrested on suspicion of murdering the child We call on the government to suspend all parental rights when a parent is arrested upon suspicion of murdering their child.  We believe once they are arrested, they should not, for example, have the right to be involved in funeral arrangements.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Strengthen sentences for death & injuries caused by criminal use of vehicles We ask the UK Government to review the law and introduce stronger offences and sentencing where people are seriously injured or killed by offenders using stolen or illegally ridden vehicles.
label: Home Office

text: Introduce a minimum trainee teacher wage equivalent to Teaching Assistant salary We want the Government to introduce a minimum trainee teacher wage that is equivalent to a Teaching Assistant salary. Many trainees work full-time while paying £9,250 in fees, making teaching inaccessible for many. We believe this could ease teacher shortages and the financial strain on trainees.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund hair removal on the NHS for women with PCOS / hirsutism The government to take a stand on women's health, hair removal for hormonal conditions should be considered a form of treatment, like medication would be for other health conditions. PCOS and hirsutism is uncontrollable and is a huge self confidence issue for many people.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund accommodation for all prison leavers We call on the Government to fund accommodation for everyone leaving prison so they are not released directly on to the streets and therefore put at a much greater risk of re offending.
label: Ministry of Justice

text:
Tell Us Once to inform NHS of deaths, review comms with bereaved people
 We ask the Government to add the NHS to the list of organisations notified of deaths by the Tell Us Once service. We also want them to require a review of and improvements to all NHS services' communications to ensure communications with bereaved families are coordinated and informed.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reduce bus fare cap to £1.75 for journeys less than 5 miles & freeze for 3 years Review the national bus fare cap and reduce for shorter journeys. Currently the cap is £3 for a single, which means passengers may be paying £6 a day return. Reduce the cap for shorter journeys (under 5 miles) to £1.75 and freeze the current £3 limit for at least 3 years for journeys over 5 miles.
label: Department for Transport

text: Have a new referendum on EU membership I want the government to offer the people of the UK a further opportunity to reconsider the position of our communities leaving the EU.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Introduce a referendum to decide: maintain or abolish the inheritance tax. I am writing to propose a public referendum on the inheritance tax, allowing citizens to vote on its retention or abolition. We think this initiative would empower the electorate to voice their opinions on a significant issue that affects many families.
label: HM Treasury

text: Automatic right to appeal for people convicted of murder under joint enterprise The government needs to make changes with joint enterprise law. People should get fair justice. We are all human beings. The government needs to let all people who are convicted of murder under joint enterprise to automatically be able to appeal their conviction charge and sentence.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Require CCTV in all care settings. We want the Government to require CCTV in all care settings. Adults/children receiving care must be protected from abuse and neglect, and we also believe it will help protect staff. We think CCTV will help keep our most vulnerable safe. Safety must come first.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund more doctor postgraduate training posts in the NHS We call for immediate action to address what we see as a catastrophic failure in postgraduate medical workforce planning, which has left many doctors unable to access training.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Create a law to protect the neon sign making industry Introduce a 'Neon Signs Protection Act' or similar, to protect the neon sign making industry. This would mean that only products that are made from glass tubes and filled with an inert gas (mainly neon and argon) can be labelled, promoted and sold as a neon sign.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Ensure provision of emergency stoma kits in supermarkets and shopping centres We want the Government to help people who are in a situation with their stoma bags not feel embarrassed by mandating that emergency kits are available in supermarkets & shopping centres, like sanitary products. There are more people with them now. Maybe a card to ensure they are entitled to them.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require police to attend all welfare calls I would like there to be a rule where police have to attend to people if they get a welfare call of someone vulnerable or in a bad mental state without judgement.
label: Home Office

text: Call a general election if a government breaks an election manifesto promise We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation that would trigger an immediate general election if a governing party breaks a commitment set out in its election manifesto.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Fund direct discounts on repair bills for clothing & footwear We call the UK Government to introduce a British Repair Bonus: a practical, people-first discount that makes repairs more affordable for everyone. Modelled after France’s repair bonus, we want a government-backed discount applied, which is directly deducted from the repair invoice.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Fund a 30-35 Railcard We call on the Government to fund a railcard for adults aged 30-35.
label: Department for Transport

text: Exempt Lifelong Warfarin Users from NHS prescription charge We want lifelong warfarin users to be exempt from NHS prescription charges. Patients with mechanical heart valves must take warfarin for life and have no choice but to remain on this medication.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reopen BNO applications for those born before 1997 Reopen BNO applications and expand the BNO scheme to benefit those born before the 1997 handover of Hong Kong who were minors at the time. I think that those born before 1 July 1997 in Hong Kong whose parents held BNO status and who were minors at that time should receive fair treatment.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Make all households with income under £200,000 eligible for free childcare Under current UK policy, families where each parent earns just under £100,000 totalling nearly £200,000 are eligible for 30 hours of free childcare. In contrast, a single-income family earning just over £100,000 does not qualify for this benefit.
label: Department for Education

text: Introduce law to allow voters to recall local government councillors At present only MPs can be recalled by their electors in specific circumstances. There is no mechanism for voters to remove local councillors. We think there needs to be legislation covering all elected local government representatives and have unacceptable non-attendance as a reason for a recall.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Amend the Health and Safety Act to make mental health training mandatory We urge the Government to amend the Health and Safety Act to require all workplaces to provide mandatory mental health awareness training, to ensure that mental health is given the same priority as physical health and safety, helping to create healthier and more productive work environments.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Abolish Business Rates for Early Years Nurseries in England Scotland and Wales have abolished business rates for nurseries, so we think England should follow suit.
label: HM Treasury

text: Fund nirsevimab for extremely premature babies’ protection prior to discharge Babies can be seriously ill after catching RSV, and can be dealing with the effects for a long time after. Pregnant women are immunised from RSV from 28 weeks to help protect babies. We think all babies born before 28 weeks should be offered nirsevimab.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Seek to form a free movement union and passport across CANZUK We urge the UK Government to seek to negotiate a CANZUK Union passport with Canada, Australia and New Zealand to ensure free movement across the four nations. As key Anglosphere nations with shared heritage, we believe it would let citizens live, work and travel freely, while strengthening ties.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Fund breast cancer referrals for all patients regardless of age & family history Fund urgent breast cancer referrals for any patient presenting breast cancer symptoms to a GP and ensure they are automatically put on the urgent referral pathway, regardless of their age or family history.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Restore the Age-Related Personal Tax Allowance for Pensioners We call on the Government to reintroduce the age-related personal income tax allowance for people of State Pension age, setting it at 110% of the full annual new State Pension and increasing it automatically each year in line with the Triple Lock State Pension.
label: HM Treasury

text: Call a public inquiry into Chinese influence on UK politics & democracy We are concerned about reported efforts from China to influence democracy in the US, UK, Europe and elsewhere. We believe we must establish the depth and breadth of possible Chinese influence campaigns in the UK.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Introduce Law as a GCSE subject Introduce GCSE Law to the national education curriculum. I feel the current curriculum can sometimes fail to inspire and motivate students.
label: Department for Education

text: Ask NAO to investigate any errors in CMS arrears from system migrations We call on Parliament to request the National Audit Office (NAO) to conduct an audit of all arrears transferred between CSA and CMS (1993–2025), with results made public. Contractor data handling and verification must be transparent, and arrears checks kept active during any upgrades.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Review NHS prescription exemption rules for lifelong neurological conditions We call on the UK Government to review and update the NHS medical exemption list to include lifelong neurological conditions requiring continuous medication, including Multiple Sclerosis (MS).
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund heart ultrasounds as part of NHS health check for those aged 45+ We call on the Government to fund heart ultrasounds to check cardiovascular health, as part of the NHS health check for over 45s. A British Heart Foundation study has shown an increase of an 18% spike in cardiovascular disease related deaths among working-age adults.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Improve Monitoring and Early Detection for Endometriosis Patients in the UK We call on the UK Government to review current monitoring practices for people living with endometriosis and introduce improved long-term care pathways, including appropriate access to MRI scans and other diagnostic tools when clinically needed.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Government to require all car park operators to provide contactless payments We want the Government to amend its code of practice so that people can pay car parking charges by card. Car park operators who only take payment through an app cause significant problems for many people who have issues with their mobile phone service.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Introduce 25% commission rate cap for private hire (ride hailing companies) We ask the Government to introduce regulations capping ride-hailing platform commission at 25% per trip and require transparency in fare and commission structures. Drivers are told lower fares improve rider affordability, yet high rates of commission impact fair earnings and transparency.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Fund NHS Prostate Risk Questionnaire at age 45 Fund the NHS to send a Prostate Risk Questionnaire to people at age 45, assessing prostate cancer risk and guiding them to monitor symptoms, speak to a nurse, or see their GP.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require there to be general election to replace a Prime Minister We call upon the UK Government to introduce and pass legislation that makes it illegal for any political party to remove or replace an elected Prime Minister without a General Election.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Ban face coverings in all public spaces to tackle anti-social behaviour Ban face coverings in all public spaces to tackle intimidating anti-social behaviour and harassment. Those in breach of this ban should pay a fixed penalty notice of £5000 or serve 6 months in prison. People wearing face coverings for genuine religious or health reasons should be exempted.
label: Home Office

text: Fund crisis support signs on motorway and railway bridges  Fund signs with local crisis support info and helplines on motorway and railway bridges. Work with relevant campaigns and organisations to ensure signs are safe, effective, and help people in crisis find local, face to face support.
label: Department for Transport

text: Create a Renewable Open Work Permit for Sponsored Workers Create a renewable Open Work Permit for sponsored workers so they can change employers without needing new sponsorship. The Government says workers can change sponsors, but in reality few employers offer sponsorships. With ILR moving to 10–15 years, workers should not stay tied to one sponsor.
label: Home Office

text: Review the DVLA (Driver & Vehicle Licensing Agency), including digitalisation Review the DVLA and its treatment of customers from disadvantaged groups. Review how the DVLA could be modernised to ensure it delivers an efficient, fair service that is fit for 2025, saving costs along the way.
label: Department for Transport

text: Deny asylum applications & return migrants if they arrive from a safe country Deny asylum applications from illegal migrants arriving from a safe country & return them to the country from which they departed.
label: Home Office

text: Reform Child Maintenance: Introduce a set weekly rate per child Replace current income-based percentage system with a standardized set weekly rate per child. We think this would ensure all children receive a fair & consistent amount of support, regardless of their parent’s employment status or career success, while preventing excessive charges on working parents
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Review motorcycle access to bus lanes Launch a review into motorcycle access to bus lanes, which looks into requiring councils to publish safety data and justifications for restrictions, and introducing consistent national guidance that improves safety, reduces conflict and supports predictable road layouts for all riders.
label: Department for Transport

text: Introduce a total ban on any fox killing and mandate non-lethal management Ban all fox killing/injuring in the UK, including for "control." Amend the law to mandate humane, non-lethal deterrents (fencing, tech, guardian animals) for farmers and ban any lethal control or culling. We must transition from what we see as extermination to coexistence. Protect our wildlife now.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require all social housing providers to publish floor plans for accessible homes We call on the Government to require all social housing providers and local authority housing registers to publish floor plans and key accessibility measurements for any property advertised as accessible or suitable for disabled applicants.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government
