text: Launch a review into resourcing & behaviour policies in Multi-Academy Trusts We call on the Government to launch a review into Multi Academy Trusts (MATs) to investigate pupil wellbeing & behaviour policies. We are deeply concerned by what we feel is a lack of accountability, with many trusts operating with little transparency and a non-functioning complaints procedure.
label: Department for Education

text: Require schools to deliver boxing-based activities in PSE and health curriculum Young people face growing pressures affecting mental health and decision-making. We want the government to require structured programmes in schools that combine emotional awareness, discipline and decision-making skills, including safe boxing-based training to build resilience and self-control.
label: Department for Education

text: Give the UK a General Election annually on the first Thursday in every April We think this would give democracy back to the people of the UK if a government is not making the changes the public expect or if not delivering their manifesto; they can be removed to avoid the extended damage the current system allows.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Review PIP eligibility criteria and award payments based on medical diagnoses We believe many conditions should receive Personal Independence Payments (PIP) that currently do not. Disabled people can incur additional costs and we feel the assessment criteria does not take that into account.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Conduct a review into women's confidence in Judicial handling of Rape Recent high profile cases have been met with shock, anger and dismay. We are calling on the Government to review women's confidence in judicial handling of rape and particularly look at the Judicial Discipline guidance issued in July 2024.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Create and fund a national holiday and respite grant scheme for disabled adults Create and fund a national grant scheme so disabled adults on low incomes anywhere in the country can get accessible holidays and respite breaks. This should be funding for several short trips or one longer holiday (UK or abroad) and can pay for more than one support worker’s travel & accommodation.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Government to do more to protect victims of false allegations We want the Government to impose shorter time limits on pre-charge bail and introduce strong minimum penalties for those making false allegations. We think it is important that the due process and rights of the accused are protected, and that there should be a system to support those falsely accused
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Immediately close all asylum hotels & deport all illegal migrants living there The Government pledged to close down asylum hotels in its manifesto for the 2024 General Election.
label: Home Office

text: Statutory right for domestic abuse victims to separate from joint mortgages Create a statutory right for domestic abuse victims to unilaterally separate from joint mortgages, with specific protections against arrears, damaged credit and their abuser refusing to pay, sell or cooperate; ensuring a joint mortgage cannot be used as a tool of post-separation economic abuse.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Fund £10,000 armed forces funeral grants & pension inheritance rules We believe veterans who serve for decades deserve dignity and pension protections like some other pensions. Many don't receive death payments to help with funeral support and often pensions can’t pass to dependent adult children, leaving families insecure and reliant on charities.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Make social class a protected characteristic under the Equality Act The government should amend the Equality Act 2010 and make social class a protected characteristic.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Replace the VAWG strategy with a VAP - Violence Against People strategy We call on the Government to replace the Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG) strategy with Violence Against People (VAP) strategy to ensure Government policy, funding and support protect all victims of violence, abuse and coercive control equally, regardless of sex, based on evidence and need.
label: Home Office

text: Review Landlords' Rights and Fair Balance in the Private Rental Sector We call on the Government to introduce a faster, more efficient possession process where landlords have legitimate grounds for repossession, strengthen protections against late rent payments, rent arrears, and property damage, and ensure the courts resolve housing disputes promptly and fairly.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Issue guidance encouraging compassionate leave for companion animal bereavement We ask the Government to recognise companion animal bereavement by introducing guidance encouraging employers to allow compassionate leave when an employee experiences the death of a pet. This would help ensure employees are treated with understanding during a difficult time.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: No 'Pay per Mile' on EVs and Hybrids in 2028 - just £200 VED  Scrap the 3p pay per mile tax on EVs and 1.5p per mile on Hybrids entirely, & charge every driver the flat rate of £200 in VED instead.
label: Department for Transport

text: Give children 5 school days of "bookable" leave per academic year  To enable children to spend time away from school with family. These could be for day trips, holidays that are affordable or just to reinforce the love and care that children need from their guardians, as we believe families are crucial to a functioning society and supporting those bonds is key.
label: Department for Education

text: Student midwives & nurses: fund childcare & stop treating loans as income for UC Support student nurses and midwives by allowing them to claim 30 hours free childcare and excluding student loans from Universal Credit (UC). We believe current support isn't enough to live, travel to and park at full-time placements, or care for dependents. Its forcing many to leave their courses.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Create Multidisciplinary NHS services for hEDS and associated conditions. We want the Government to work with NHS England to establish multidisciplinary specialist services and national care pathways for people with Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (hEDS) and associated conditions, ensuring coordinated care and reducing delays across multiple specialties.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Make sonographers a protected, regulated profession with qualifications & checks Make it a legal requirement that anyone practicing in the UK as a sonographer must have passed accredited exams and hold relevant qualifications. They must be registered with an accredited registration body and undergo regular assessments while practicing.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review compensation schemes for businesses affected by HS2 construction We ask the Government to launch a review of compensation schemes for businesses  along the HS2 route that are suffering serious financial harm due to ongoing construction. Road closures, reduced access, noise, and disruption are driving away customers and putting many livelihoods at risk.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Ban people from flying drones over police stations and private properties Create a specific law to ban people from flying drones over police stations and private properties. We think this causes a breach of the peace to law abiding citizens and police officers.
label: Home Office

text: Give parents who split up automatic 50/50 shared care of their children Parents should get 50/50 shared care of their children without lengthy court hearings if no safeguarding issues & both families can provide care. Currently I feel parents have to fight for more or any care, using time & money better spent on the children, negatively affecting the parent & children.
label: Ministry of Justice

text:
Make it mandatory for all food outlets/restaurants to offer gluten free options We call for:
1. At least three clearly labelled gluten-free option on every menu.
2. Staff training on gluten-free preparation and cross-contamination prevention.
3. Transparent ingredient labelling for all menu items.
4. Commitment to inclusivity for people with dietary restrictions.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require social housing landlords to ensure properties have a C EPC rating We want the Government to include social and council properties in their plan to improve the EPC rating of all rental properties by 2030. This was set out in the Government's 'Plan for Change' and we feel there should be equal treatment for all tenants.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Review protections for England’s National Parks from industrial infrastructure Review protections for England’s National Parks from industrialisation caused by large infrastructure projects. Stop private companies from damaging the environment, through projects not in keeping with local areas, even where biodiversity net gain might be demonstrated.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Make Gender Neutral Toilets a legal requirement in all public areas I want the government to require ender neutral toilets to be provided in public spaces around the UK, including education institutions and shopping outlets.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Review regulation of water companies We want the Government to review regulation of water companies through Ofwat. We feel that Ofwat need stronger powers to stop any water bill hikes unless companies show service and environmental improvements.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Government to fund shortfall for Science and Technology Facilities Council We want the Government to ensure sufficient funding beyond 31 March 2028 for the Science & Technology Facilities Council through the UKRI so that it no longer requires funding cuts which imperil key scientific research projects & establishments, such as Jodrell Bank Observatory & e-MERLIN project.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Exit ECHR & do not pay families of failed asylum seekers up to £40k to leave UK Stop the pilot scheme to pay families of failed asylum seekers up to £40K to leave the UK. In our view, Government cannot be allowed to pay people who have not gotten asylum with our taxpayer money. There is a cost of living crisis, and we think we need money for defence. We should also exit ECHR.
label: Home Office

text: Do not use any taxpayer funds on asylum appeals. Charge the individual We want the government to charge individuals for asylum appeals and not to use any taxpayer funds.
label: Home Office

text: Do not lower or remove the £20,000 annual cash ISA allowance We think it is vital the British people have the flexibility to save or invest their money in the way they see fit. We think that many people may be risk averse to investing in stocks and shares ISAs, want to have a safer vehicle to store their funds, and not want to invest long-term.
label: HM Treasury

text: Government to set out plans for reducing rail fares The government recently announced a rise of up to 4.6% in rail fares, explaining that people are willing to pay for a good service. We believe that fares for commuters are far too high and not sustainable for working people.
label: Department for Transport

text: Require park home site owners to allow individual water meters Require park home site owners to allow individual water meters, read such meters and provide bills for each homes usage.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Act to improve patient safety, staffing & accountability in NHS hospitals We want Government to ensure the introduction and enforcement of  minimum safe staffing levels in NHS hospitals, strengthen accountability for poor patient care and set up a review of discharge practices.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Make it illegal for drivers to idle engines outside schools. We call on the UK Government to make it illegal for drivers to keep car engines running while stationary outside schools, and to introduce penalties or mandatory environmental awareness courses for those who do.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Hold a referendum on the Chagos Deal & scrap it if the public votes “no” If the majority votes “no”, then the UK Government should cancel the deal and instead, work with Mauritius to ensure security in the Indian Ocean without transferring the islands.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text:
New rules for migrants who arrive without ID or outside official entry points We think there should be two options for illegal migrants:
• 1: Deportation to country of origin within 28 days
• 2: Transfer to designated 3rd country within 60 days; No pathway to return to the UK; Basic living conditions.
Both to entail biometric processing, with costs borne by the individual.
label: Home Office

text: Ban the sale and release of exotic and native waterbirds Ban all breeding, sale and release of exotic and native water birds. We think birds may be mis-sold by breeders, which could lead to charities having to step in and rescue birds that are put in danger when released in insecure locations with unsuitable conditions by inexperienced owners.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require family judges to complete LGBTQ+ family sensitivity training Make LGBTQ+ family sensitivity training compulsory for judges before sitting family cases, developed with LGBTQ+ family charities. We believe this could help to address any unconscious bias and protect the rights and welfare of children and parents.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Remove the statute of limitations on reporting childhood domestic abuse Currently there is a statute of limitations on domestic violence in the UK. A victim of domestic abuse has 6 months from formally reporting an offence of domestic abuse to the police to initiate prosecutions and two years from the date of offence to prosecute the abuse.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Include the Lord's Prayer in the national curriculum I call on the Government to include the Lord’s Prayer in the national curriculum. I believe that the power in prayer cannot be underestimated and that we should start embracing our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ once again.
label: Department for Education

text: Cap political donations at £1000 & fund a £4 civic voucher for voters Pass a law which caps political donations at £1,000 per year from any individual, company or union. Introduce and fund £4 civic vouchers per voter each year, which citizens can direct to their chosen party as a donation. We believe democracy should be about people, not pounds.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Dual Cab pickup trucks keep commercial status beyond April 2025 Keep the commercial status of dual cab pickup trucks rather than re-classifying them as passenger cars, for those using them for agriculture or construction. They are so important.
label: HM Treasury

text: All wastewater to be filtered of chemicals, pharmaceuticals & microplastics We want the government to pass legislation to require all commercial and utility wastewater to be more comprehensively filtered to help remove more harmful chemicals, pharmaceuticals and microplastics before it enters the environment.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require MPs to evidence all contributions in Parliament and introduce penalties I think that MPs should be required to substantiate claims/statements made in Parliament. This could help ensure that MPs prioritise evidence based decisions, ensuring integrity and credibility by requiring independent, unbiased, peer-reviewed scientific evidence for all parliamentary contributions.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Protect Skilled Care Workers Affected by Sponsor Licence Revocation Grant care workers affected by sponsor licence revocation a 1–2 year transition visa to secure alternative sponsored employment, with no recourse to public funds, and protect housing and children’s education during this period.
label: Home Office

text:
Keep 5-year ILR for Skilled Workers & dependents who come before April 2026
 We want the Government to keep the 5-year ILR pathway to settlement for people on Skilled Worker visas, and their dependents, who enter the UK before the changes come in (April 2026).
label: Home Office

text: Mandate a lifetime driving ban for causing death by dangerous driving Change the minimum penalty so anyone convicted of death by dangerous driving faces a lifetime driving ban. Dangerous driving includes drinking/drugs, using mobile phone, excessive speeding. This selfish behaviour endangers lives and we think it must have severe, permanent consequences.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Fund more early intervention support for people struggling with mental health We think the government needs more NHS early intervention support services nationwide, in order to support people when they first notice the signs of poor mental health.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require CCTV cameras in all SEN schools and settings such as transport Many parents of SEN children are terrified of something happening to our children. We urge the Government to require cameras to be installed in all SEN schools, transport and other SEN settings to protect our children who are non-verbal or/and have limited communication.
label: Department for Education

text: Remove transgender content from RHSE curriculum We don't think children should be taught about transgender issues. We are concerned this could lead to children, who can be easily influenced, making life changing, irreversible choices.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund affordable unilateral bras on the NHS Fund affordable unilateral bras on the NHS. While some retailers offer post surgery bras designed to hold prostheses, bras for women with a single mastectomy who choose to remain flat on one side are much harder to find and often cost more.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require businesses pay a 50% deposit to contracted sole traders/small businesses Change the law to require businesses to pay a 50% deposit for services when working with freelancers, sole-traders and small businesses who cannot exist in credit or have 'accounts' like bigger companies. The remaining 50% should then be paid within 30 business days.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Review and reform Plan 2 student loan repayment terms Review Plan 2 student loan repayment thresholds and interest rates, including the impact of frozen thresholds. Assess whether current terms are fair, transparent, and proportionate, and consider reforms so repayments reduce balances and better reflect graduates’ ability to pay.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund teacher training for mental health first aid and suicide prevention Government to fund Mental Health First Aid Training and Suicide Prevention Training for all Primary and Secondary School Teachers
label: Department for Education

text: Apply an income tax rate of 99% to MPs' additional incomes Tax any income MPs get other than their Parliamentary Salary at a rate of 99%
label: HM Treasury

text: Set national planning rules to ban incinerators near facilities for children We are calling on the Government to introduce national planning safeguards that prevent waste and clinical waste incinerators being built within a specific distance from schools, nurseries, and playgrounds.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Increase Statutory Maternity Pay - 90% of Wages from 6 Weeks to 16 Weeks Increasing time with a newborn in the first 4 months can boost bonding, support emotional/brain development, aid breastfeeding, reduce parental stress and postpartum depression risk. We think extending SMP at 90% gross wage to 16 weeks further enables parents to fully utilise this critical period.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Cap Out-Of-Hours Veterinary Fees to Prevent Pet Abandonment Introduce regulations to cap charges for essential veterinary emergency treatments carried out outside normal working hours, ensuring fees are fair, transparent, and proportionate, by scrapping excessive mark-up prices.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Allow Vehicle Excise Duty (road tax) to be charged on a pro-rata daily basis Change Vehicle Excise Duty (VED) rules so tax is calculated and refunded on a pro-rata daily basis rather than by full calendar month, including when vehicles are sold or taken off a Statutory Off Road Notification (SORN), so motorists pay only for the days they own and use a vehicle.
label: Department for Transport

text: Increase the Personal Allowance to £16,000 and link it to inflation We call on the Government to increase the Personal Allowance from £12,570 to £16,000 and automatically uprate it each year in line with inflation (CPI), so people on low and middle incomes don’t pay more tax in real terms when living costs rise.
label: HM Treasury

text: Change review process for ongoing benefits for people with lifelong disabilities Allow workers in the DWP to review the available case notes for people who have lifelong disabilities rather than require people with lifelong disabilities and their carers to attend repeated reviews.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text:
Fund the creation of bike lanes for all main roads I want the government to give local councils more money to be able to create a safer environment for cyclists. 

I want them to give funding so that all main roads have bike lanes.
label: Department for Transport

text: Remove the triple lock commitment on pensions and tie increase to inflation only We feel the triple lock on pensions is unaffordable and unjust. We think tying the increase in pensions to inflation only could ensure the living standards of those reliant on the pension are protected, and would be more affordable.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Give UK citizens the right to veto laws by national referendum We urge the Government to create a law where if one million citizens sign a petition within six months of a law being passed, a binding national referendum must be held, and if voters reject the law, it must be repealed. We believe this would return democratic power to the people.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Give families an additional tax-free allowance for each child Introduce a tax-free allowance for each dependent child under 18, in addition to the personal allowance, and ensure it is given to the parent with primary day-to-day care of the child.
label: HM Treasury

text: Review court system to address trial delays for rape and sexual abuse We want the Government to review the court system in order to better prioritise and protect victims of rape and sexual abuse by preventing postponements of trial start dates. Victims can be left in limbo for months or years, which can cause further trauma and deny timely justice.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Require NHS hospitals & clinics to provide after-treatment surveys I urge the Government to require NHS hospitals and clinics to provide end of treatment surveys to patients or families at the end of care/treatment. I would like this to be sent to an independent review board and assessed so that any serious complaints are dealt with properly.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review current legislation and regulation of gambling adverts I think that gambling is a major problem in the UK and regulation on TV adverts seems very loose, with a quick "be gamble aware" at the end. I would like the Government to review current regulation for gambling adverts on television. A review could help reduce the levels of problem gambling.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Do not apply retrospective ILR rule changes to spouses on family visas We call on the UK Government to ensure that spouses who have entered or applied to come to the UK via family visas are not unfairly affected by retrospective changes to rules relating to Indefinite Leave to Remain.
label: Home Office

text: Ban all gambling advertisements Ban all adverts that promote gambling on tv and in media.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Make face coverings illegal Ban all face coverings hiding facial identity. With the introduction of identity cards, we think face coverings should be made illegal except in times of national health crisis
label: Home Office

text: Reschedule psilocybin from Schedule 1 to 2 to allow for use in medical research We ask the UK Government to reschedule psilocybin, moving it from Schedule 1 to Schedule 2 of the Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001, to allow it to be used in clinical trials.
label: Home Office

text: Increase the installation of solar panels on commercial rooftops and carparks. We think the Government should introduce legislation so that outdoor car parks of a certain size include solar carports and EV charging facilities, similar to a law already passed in France. We also want the government to make it easier for commercial premises to install solar panels on rooftops.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Require gaming developers to make games adaptable for disabled users Require gaming developers to make their games adaptable for disabled users. For example have racing games compatible with a gaming steering wheel for those with cerebral palsy or similar conditions.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Ban breeding & use of doves & pigeons at weddings, funerals & sex reveal events Legislate to prevent breeding of doves and pigeons intended for release at weddings/funerals and make it illegal to pay to release birds at such events. Many of these birds are unable to navigate their way back home and as they are domesticated, they may not survive in the wild after being released.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Make Inclusive Playgrounds Mandatory in All New and Upgraded Parks  No child should be left out of play because of disabilities. We want the UK Government to make sure it is mandatory for all new and upgraded parks to have inclusive playgrounds and be accessible to every child.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Enable parents to register birth and death of babies carried beyond 24 weeks We ask the Government to change the law so parents can register the birth and death of babies carried beyond 24 weeks, even if they passed earlier. Families deserve recognition and dignity, not the miscarriage label, for the babies they carried and gave birth to.
label: Home Office

text: Introduce Stamp Duty relief for domestic abuse survivors forced to relocate Require the Government to introduce Stamp Duty Land Tax relief for people who are forced to leave their main home because of domestic abuse and purchase a replacement home for their safety.
label: HM Treasury

text: Ban adoption & the removal of children from their birth parents We call for a complete ban on adoption and any legal activities that aim to take children away from the care of their birth parents. The Government should provide services to support families and end any discrimination or human rights abuses.
label: Department for Education

text: Give leaseholders a right to force a buy-back after serious mismanagement To introduce legislation giving leaseholders the right to compel a freeholder, intermediate landlord or management company to buy back their property at the higher of the current market value or the original purchase price, where a tribunal finds serious breach of lease or mismanagement.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Provide a 'Home Care Allowance' as an alternative to funded childcare Introduce a Government-funded 'Home Care Allowance', equivalent to the value of funded childcare, for parents who are entitled to but choose not to claim funded childcare hours or Tax-Free Childcare so they can care for their child at home.
label: HM Treasury

text: Reform statutory time limits for all offences involving child victims under 16 Review and reform statutory prosecution time limits for all offences involving victims under 16. A review could consider extending or removing time limits where delayed disclosure, safeguarding investigations, or multi-agency child protection processes may prevent prosecutions.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: No More Patchwork Paving: Change the resurfacing rules for utility companies. Amend the law to require utility companies to fully resurface, at their own cost, the entire width of the pavement/road rather than just the strip they dug up. Local authorities can be left liable for repairs or injury compensation after the post-works guarantee period has elapsed.
label: Department for Transport

text: Introduce minimum hours of driving lessons before practical driving test The Government should review the issuing of driving licenses and introduce a legal requirement for all learner drivers to complete a minimum number of professional driving lesson hours before being allowed to take the practical driving test.
label: Department for Transport

text: Use a permanent implanted tracker for murderers released on licence I would like to see a permanent implanted tracker in perpetrators of murder released on licence, and an app that those affected by their crimes can use to track their whereabouts at all times.
label: Home Office

text: Increase statutory maternity pay. I want statutory maternity pay to be raised because of the cost of living. Having a baby doesn't mean bills don't need to be paid. Bills stay the same but often people's income goes down after having a baby.
label: HM Treasury

text: Fund and distribute a leaflet on climate change to every UK household This leaflet would contain an evidence-based and impartial account of the reality of climate change. It should set out what is known of its causes and its likely effects on UK households under a number of scenarios for future levels of greenhouse gas emissions.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Increase the minimum sentence for those found guilty of rape to 15 years Currently the minimum sentence for people convicted of rape is typically 4 years. I would like that to be upped to a minimum of 15 years.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban and criminalise all abortions. Choose Adoption and Save Children’s Lives The Crime and Policing Bill includes a clause which would mean that in respect of any law involving abortion, a woman would not commit an offence if acting in relation to her own pregnancy. We did not ask for this. It was not in any manifesto. We demand that abortion be abolished and criminalised.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Introduce legislation to ensure national marking of Remembrance Day We call upon the House to debate and introduce a specific Act of Parliament to legally protect all established provisions and customs of the national Remembrance Day (11th November and Remembrance Sunday) events.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Conduct a review into the long-term effect of section 28 We want the government commit to launching a full review into the impact of Section 28 on LGBTQ+ individuals. This could include its contribution to physical and mental health struggles, as well as the long-term harm caused to those raised under its enforcement.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Create the Department of Government Efficiency Create The Department of Government Efficiency (DGE) focused on optimising the operations of public services in the UK, ensuring that tax revenue is spent as effectively as possible and brings real benefits to British citizens.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Reintroduce the death penalty for Treason, Rape, Murder, Terrorism & Espionage I call on Parliament to reintroduce the death penalty for the most heinous crimes. Our justice system should reflect the gravity of deliberate murder and terrorism. We believe we must protect our citizens, uphold accountability, and ensure that the severest crimes receive the severest punishment.
label: Home Office

text: End the freeze on income tax thresholds & adjust annually, indexed to inflation The fiscal drag hits lower- and middle-income earners the hardest. We call on the Government to unfreeze income tax thresholds and index them to inflation. We believe this will make the tax system fair, let workers keep a fairer share of their earnings, boost the economy, and help families.
label: HM Treasury

text: Cap the Indefinite Leave to Remain fee at £3000  We feel that increasing ILR fees risk financial hardship for families as they must save for the fee with the high cost of living. We want the Government to consider the value people with visas bring to the economy. We believe the UK is losing valued people because of increasingly high fees.
label: Home Office

text: Require anti-spiking measurers, increase spiking support and awareness Require CCTV in all bars, clubs, and pubs, fund spiking prevention tools (drink covers, testing kits), require staff training, introduce stricter penalties for perpetrators, fund victim support services, launch public awareness campaigns, and promote innovative anti-spiking technology.
label: Home Office

text: Ban the Production and Sale of Lab-Grown Meat We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation banning the production, sale, and importation of lab-grown (cell-cultured) meat for human consumption, following the precautionary approach already adopted by countries such as Italy.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Update school uniform guidance to prioritise comfort for students in England We urge the Government to update guidance on school uniforms in England, so that it prioritises comfort and addresses: breathable fabrics, flexible designs, and seasonal options. We believe comfortable uniforms help students focus, feel confident, and learn better in school.
label: Department for Education

text: Review protections for NHS skilled worker visa holders We urge the Government to launch a review into protections for NHS Skilled Worker visa holders who have made significant contributions. We are concerned many face losing jobs and visas due to NHS cuts. Protections and allowing redeployment without extra visa fees could help retain vital staff.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Make "One-Punch" Killings Carry Harsher Sentences We are calling on the government to introduce specific legislation that ensures stronger and more consistent sentencing when a death results from an extreme act of violence like a single punch. Similar laws are already in place in Australia called the Coward Punch Laws.
label: Home Office

text: Make it an offence to publish suspect details before they are charged We want publishing details of a suspect before they have been charged with a crime to be an offence to protect innocent people being destroyed by false allegations. Public naming before charge can cause irreversible harm to innocent people. Some people lose their jobs reputations & mental wellbeing.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Introduce a Presumption of Equal Parenting Time in Family Law We want the Government to legislate to establish a presumption of equal parenting time following separation, unless there is clear evidence that it would not be in the child’s best interests. We think this would help ensure children maintain meaningful relationships with both parents.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Do not extend the BBC TV license fee to streaming services It has been reported that the Government is considering extending the BBC TV license fee to active subscribers of popular streaming services such as Netflix as an example. We believe this is unfair and that the Government has no rights to extend what we think is an unfair charge.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Revise the eVED Taxation on Plug-in Hybrid Vehicles (PHEVs) We call on the Government to revise the proposed eVED charge to prevent 'unfair' double taxation. PHEV drivers pay a flat 1.5p/mile even on petrol miles, where they already pay 53.95p/L fuel duty. We believe this discriminates against those who adopted hybrids in good faith to reduce emissions.
label: Department for Transport

text: Publish a timetable and approval pathway for supervised self-driving systems. Publish a timetable and approval pathway for supervised self-driving systems in GB.
label: Department for Transport

text: Make St George’s Day a Bank Holiday for people in England We believe it is time that England celebrates St George’s Day by having a Bank Holiday as other nations celebrate theirs. We believe England should be proud of St George’s Day.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Ban the sale of disposable BBQs during periods of high wildfire risk We want to ban businesses from continuing to sell disposable BBQ equipment to the public while the business is located in an area with a high wildfire risk. At present, businesses sell these to consumers despite the real risk they can pose of starting wildfires when used irresponsibly.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Ban chewing tobacco to prevent cancer and litter We would like the Government to ban the import and sale of chewing tobacco products to and in the UK. Chewing tobacco can cause cancer and we feel that the spitting in residential streets and shopping areas causes a great deal of litter.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Government to mandate brownfield development targets for local councils We believe that in order to meet government housing targets and protect greenfield land, the government should legislate to ensure that local councils are bound by law to develop housing on brownfield sites.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Write off all plan 1 Student Loans after 25 years Write off all plan 1 student loans including those paid out before 1st September 2006 after 25 years. Currently the write off date for those who were paid their loan before 1st September 2006 is when they are 65 years old.
label: Department for Education

text: Reintroduce the death penalty for people found guilty of terrorism I think that any terrorists who kill on UK soil, land, sea or air space should be face the death penalty.
label: Home Office

text:
Ban non-recyclable plastic packaging and products.
 I want the government to pass a law so all products and packaging that companies produce are recyclable.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Require enhanced DBS checks for ALL employees in contact with vulnerable people We want the Government to make enhanced DBS checks a legal requirement for ALL employees who come into contact with children and vulnerable persons.
label: Home Office

text: Reduce spouse visa income requirement from £29k to £20k Lower the spouse-visa income requirement to £20,000 to reflect real UK wages. We ask the Government to protect the right of British citizens to live with their families, uphold the UK’s principles of fairness and family unity, and ensure immigration rules do not contradict those values.
label: Home Office

text: Mandate trauma-informed training in justice, healthcare, education & social care Introduce legislation to require professional bodies to include accredited trauma-informed training as a mandatory requirement for professionals in justice, healthcare, education & social care. Embed into standards, inspections & safeguarding frameworks to ensure consistent understanding of trauma.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Require neurodiversity education for children in schools I would like children to be educated on how autism feels for autistic children. I think it would create a level of understanding on why children with autism might be (for example) stimming in the corner of the classroom.
label: Department for Education

text: Require Rapeseed Oil to be listed as an allergen on food packaging We want  the Government to ensure that Rapeseed Oil is listed as an allergen on food packaging. Many brands have switched to Rapeseed without labelling it as a recipe change & this is causing a health issue as many people find they are unable to consume the same foods without stomach upset.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Ensure parity of esteem between mental and physical health services The principle of achieving parity of esteem between mental and physical health services was established through legislation by the Health and Social Care Act 2012. We think that realising this objective requires more funding for mental health services, a goal that we think is far from being realised
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund free period pads We urge the Government to provide funding to ensure that period pads are free in England.
label: HM Treasury

text: Ban alcohol displays at checkouts and entrances in all supermarkets We want legislation that requires supermarkets to sell alcohol only in one designated area, away from entrances, aisle ends, and checkouts. This could support people in recovery, reduce triggers for addiction, and limit exposure to children and vulnerable individuals.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Review DWP guidelines for DLA Higher Rate Mobility component Review DWP guidelines for the DLA Higher Rate Mobility component, to ensure the assessment explicitly recognises that autistic children who lack spatial and danger awareness, and risk bolting or self-harm MAY meet the criteria for "virtually unable to walk" due to severe safety risks.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text:
Establish and fund a National Defence Reinvestment Programme
 We urge the Government to launch a National Defence Reinvestment Programme, beginning with an initial capital investment equivalent to 5% of GDP. We are concerned the UK has become dangerously underprepared after decades of under-investment in defence (the so-called post–Cold War “peace dividend”).
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Require domestic cats to be kept inside April-September and wear belled collars We require domestic cats to wear quick release multi-belled harnesses or belled collars all the time, when cats are venturing outside, and/or be kept house bound between the start of April, right through to the end of September, annually.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Commit 1% of government spending to development of space activities We want a penny out of every pound spent by the government to go towards space. We think that the majority of the new spending should be on developing space resources and working towards the colonisation of space by the UK, in collaboration with our international partners.
label: HM Treasury

text: Introduce a super visa for parents to join the family the same as Canada Introduce a super visa like in Canada which allows parents and grandparents to stay with family in the UK without having to travel every 6 months back to their home country. We think it may be difficult for them to travel frequently and better to spend time with their grandchildren.
label: Home Office

text: Ban the sale and use of rat poison due to the negative impact on wildlife The Rodenticide Stewardship Scheme (RSS) was created in 2015 to reduce wildlife being exposed to toxic anticoagulant rodenticides. Exposure has unfortunately risen, as these poisons are found in our water, birds and fish. We need urgent regulatory change to ban these products.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Stronger penalties for animal cruelty and stricter regulations on animal sales Every year, countless animals suffer at the hands of people who intentionally harm, neglect, or kill them. While the Animal Welfare Act increased maximum penalties in England and Wales, we think too many offenders still face minimal consequences — sending the message that animal lives don’t matter.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Legislate to ban participants wearing face coverings at demonstrations Government should introduce legislation to make it an offence to attend a demonstration or counter-demonstration wearing face coverings. All participants should be showing their faces, or, be arrested so that they can be identified.
label: Home Office

text:
Ban the sale of small animals from pet shops and third-party sellers in the UK Ban the sale of small animals from pet shops and third-party sellers in the UK including hamsters, gerbils, mice, guinea pigs, and rabbits.
After two of our shop bought Guinea Pig's died within a week of each other, an outbreak of Strep across 433 UK stores was publicised.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Require all end parking spaces to be for disabled parking Require every end space in all car parks, including supermarkets, retail parks and council car parks, to be reserved for disabled parking where safe and practical. This provides vital side access for wheelchair users and carers to open doors and transfer people safely.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Adjust Child Maintenance Payment assessment to account for living costs We urge Government to revise child maintenance calculations to reflect net incomes after essential living costs. We believe this would ensure a fair and balanced system that supports both children and non-resident parents.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Decriminalise not having a TV licence People should not face criminal charges or fines for not having a TV licence to pay for the BBC channels. People should have the right to opt out in favour of paying for their preferred subscription channels and streaming services.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Fund free BSL courses for all deaf individuals and their friends and family I am profoundly deaf. I have hearing aids and I can lipread. This is still not enough in circumstances like noisy environments and at home too when I choose to have hearing breaks, which many deaf people will do.
label: Department for Education

text: Hold a referendum on a future UK Security/Defence pact with any European country The Government is committing billions of taxpayer money to defence, such as to support Ukraine, and may commit to a potential security or defence pact with the EU, or group of European countries. We believe such a pact is not in the national interest and must be subject to a referendum.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Review NHS guidance on iron deficiency for women Iron deficiency is one of the leading contributors to the global burden of disease, disproportionately impacting reproductive age women. We think iron deficiency is often overlooked because blood counts or ferritin is in “normal range” and NHS guidance should be reviewed to support women's health.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Government to issue public solar and wind power forecasts The Government should issue 3-day solar & wind power forecasts to help ease the energy crisis. We believe these will help the public maximize their domestic power instead of wasting it. By timing usage with these peaks, they can reduce the energy crisis's impact & lower national costs for everyone.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Introduce 18 year residency and English language requirements to vote in general The Government should legislate so that you must have been resident in the UK for a minimum of 18 years and be able to show a degree of proficiency in the English language in order to register to vote in General Elections.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text:
Set dates when fireworks are allowed. When October hit, fireworks start day and night until January.
We want the government to choose selected dates e.g. Diwali, 4th of July, New year's Eve, etc. To approve as recognised for fireworks and prohibit fireworks out of these dates.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Mandate petitionable new elections if govt has under 25% UK electorate support Introduce legislation requiring an immediate general election if a government is elected with support from less than 25% of the UK electorate, and at least 10% of UK electorate sign a verified petition calling for its removal, which would be binding.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Mandate Body Cams for staff who work with those with communication difficulties We ask that the use of body-worn cameras for staff who work with those who have communication and severe learning difficulties, for example in schools, be made mandatory to help prevent any abuse and provide evidence when needed.
label: Department for Education

text: Require airlines provide spaces for passengers to stay in their wheelchairs Require airlines to provide safe, secure spaces on planes where wheelchair users can remain in their own wheelchairs during short-haul and long-haul flights.
label: Department for Transport

text: Make parental alienation a criminal offence We want the Government to make Parental Alienation a criminal offence. We believe deliberately turning a child against a loving parent is emotional abuse. The law should make it an offence, train professionals to identify it, and hold offenders accountable to protect children’s rights.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Base the High Income Child Benefit Charge (HICBC) threshold on household income The aim of this petition is to request the government to change the threshold for the High Income Child Benefit Charge (HICBC) from the current individual £60K income to a household income of £120K.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Review of Universal Credit and Job Centre Operations We urge the UK Government to review Universal Credit and Job Centre operations. We believe there are issues with delays, sanctions, and support which can negatively impact claimants. We want to see improvements in staffing, payment resolutions, and help for disabled and vulnerable people.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Fund free hospital parking for NHS staff and students on placement We want the Government to fund free hospital parking for staff and medical & dental students working in NHS hospitals on placement during working hours and ensure they are protected from parking penalties at all times, including when they are required to work beyond their scheduled hours.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund access for all women to a genetic blood test for breast cancer risk genes Fund a national NHS screening programme offering all women the opportunity to be tested for BRCA1 and BRCA2 gene mutations. This could be offered alongside routine cervical screening appointments, such as at a woman’s first smear test or at her next scheduled appointment.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Resentence IPP prisoners; end indefinite licence and limit recall We call on the Government to make arrangements for a resentencing all on IPP sentences, to fixed-term sentences with clear release dates. It must end indefinite licence periods for all, and reform the threshold for recall so only those who have reoffended or who present a serious risk are recalled.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Levy per carcass to fund independent continuous abattoir CCTV monitoring Effective, independent, real time observation required with costs funded by a levy per carcass.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Make Saint David's Day (Wales) and Saint George's Day (England) Bank Holidays I think Dydd Gwyl Dewi (Saint David's Day) on 1st March in Wales and Saint George's Day on 23rd of April in England should be made to be bank holidays. I believe these dates are important for the people of the respected nations, and are a day of celebration that should be open for everyone to enjoy.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Remove the ban on semi automatic firearms over .22 calibre. Remove the ban on semi-automatic firearms over .22 calibre to allow for more freedom within the firearms community.
label: Home Office

text: Require bars, pubs and clubs to have CCTV covering all areas surrounding toilets I believe it should be a legal requirement for CCTV to cover all areas of the venue. This includes stairwells/corridors leading up to toilet facilities to monitor the safety of customers. This could help prevent spiking and other forms of assault or support in the prosecution of the attacker.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Mandate hip scan offer for newborns with a family history of hip problems (DDH) Require the NHS to automatically offer a hip ultrasound scan for all newborn babies if there is a known family history of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) or related hip conditions on either parent’s side.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reinstate the policy to deport asylum seekers to Rwanda On taking office this Government cancelled the Rwanda plan and promised to 'Smash The Gangs'. The annual number of illegal migrants crossing the channel was higher in 2025 than in 2023/24, and we think the gangs have not been smashed. We would like the Government to reinstate the Rwanda plan.
label: Home Office

text: Fund more training for teachers on neurodivergence We want the government to fund more comprehensive training programs for teachers on how to effectively support and engage neurodivergent students in the classroom.
label: Department for Education

text: Require businesses to offer interviews to care leavers meeting minimum criteria We ask Government to introduce a national policy so medium and large employers offer care leavers a guaranteed interview for any role where they meet the essential criteria, ensuring fair access to work and consistent opportunity.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Make it a specific criminal offence not to notify the authorities of a death I would like it to become a specific criminal offence to not report a dead body or a death if you are in the company of said individual when they pass or if you are aware of one.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Conduct a review of routes into work for new graduates. We believe that many graduates, myself included, who spent £27k+ on university are struggling to find jobs. Entry-level roles often demand experience, which feels unfair, as we're constantly rejected for lacking it. We need opportunities, yet many of us lack industry connections.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text:
Require all police forces to review serious cold cases within 5–10 years Require all police forces in England and Wales to review serious cold cases within 5–10 years. This should be called 'Stacey’s Law’.

End the postcode lottery, protect vital evidence, give families a fair, timely chance at justice.
label: Home Office

text: Put all proposals for closer ties to the EU to a referendum Hold a referendum on proposals for closer ties to the European Union, and commit to holding a referendum on any future proposals for closer ties, including if the government decided it wanted the UK to become a full EU member state.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Ban AI advertisements The government should create legislation to prevent businesses using generative AI for advertisements, including medical advertisements.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Retain 5-year ILR Pathway for LGBTIQ+ Refugees in the UK The Government’s new asylum policy proposes replacing the current five-year refugee leave with temporary 30-month grants and delaying eligibility for settlement to 20 years for those on the new core protection route. We believe these changes will disproportionately impact LGBTIQ+ refugees negatively
label: Home Office

text: Create legal definition for Maternity Nurse role We call on the Government to set out a legal definition for the non-medical role Maternity Nurse, as the name for the role of caring for parents and babies, privately in the home.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Give permits for parent and child bays to stop the misuse of these spaces I am calling on the government to introduce a permit that allows access to parent and child parking bays from 20 weeks of pregnancy until the child turns 8 years old. Pregnant individuals and parents of young children may face mobility and safety challenges that require accessible parking.
label: Department for Transport

text:
Repeal laws that restrict the right to free speech in the UK Repeal these laws where they create speech based offences:
- Public Order Act 1986
- Malicious Communications Act 1988
- Terrorism Act 2000
- Communications Act 2003
- Racial and Religious Hatred Act 2006
- Terrorism Act 2006
- Criminal Justice & Immigration Act 2008
- Online Safety Act 2023
label: Home Office

text: Require all public places to have toilets accessible with a medical card Require all places that serve the community i.e garages, shops give access to customers to use a toilet and anyone with a medical card, such as a ‘Just can’t wait’ card, can use any toilet they need.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Make all types of animal snares illegal in England At the moment self-locking snares are illegal, since the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981, but I think that free-running snares should also be illegal, as they are in Wales and Scotland.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Repeal UK Laws Restricting Speech & Pass 'Free Speech Act' like US 1st Amendment We call on the Government to repeal restrictive speech legislation - including sections of the Communications Act 2003 and the Public Order Act 1986 – and pass a “Free Speech Act” mirroring protections and rights guaranteed by the First Amendment of the United States Constitution.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Require supermarkets have someone on tills at all times Require superstores always have a till or two open so disabled people, people with mental health problems and older people don’t need to struggle during the early hours to get their shopping.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Reduce the immigration health surcharge for family visas We want the IHS to be reduced to its previous rate of £624 per year for people living in the UK on a family visa. We believe that the IHS, which was increased by the previous government, has been set too high for family visas.
label: Home Office

text: Hold a review into the effects of parental alienation on families We are calling on the UK Government to launch a review into parental alienation, examining its scale, how courts and services respond, and the impact on children. The review must deliver clear reforms to protect parent-child relationships and ensure fair, evidence-based decisions.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Reduce fuel duty and remove VAT on petrol and diesel The Government should reduce fuel duty and remove VAT from petrol and diesel to make fuel more affordable for drivers across the UK.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Ban the sale of vapes in stores located in properties with residential units  We believe the recent fire in Glasgow Union Street highlights the dangers of Vape stores. In this case there were no casualties but this resulted in a fire requiring several fire engines, and we think this could have had far more serious consequences and has impacted so many businesses.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Government to enhance powers of the Environment Agency against waste offenders We want the Government to enhance the powers of the Environment Agency to allow for the quick shutdown of sites that violate regulations. Increased penalties and fines for non-compliance should also be considered as a deterrent.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Mandate police to use S61 to move illegal encampments from unauthorised sites Mandate police to use Section 61 (CJPOA 1994) to move illegal encampments as soon as relevant legal thresholds are met. Police must direct trespassers to leave, arrest those who refuse, and seize caravans and vehicles used in the occupation, without discretion.
label: Home Office

text: Make "ghost jobs" illegal Ghost jobs are advertisements for positions that are not currently open or that the company has no intention of filling. We think that ghost jobs create stress, waste time, increase unemployment benefit costs, give a false indication of the job market and artificially inflate companies market value.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Mandate First Aid & mental wellbeing training for all school staff I would like the Government to change the law to make it a statutory requirement for all school employees (teaching, non-teaching & support staff) to be trained in emergency first aid and mental wellbeing.
label: Department for Education

text: Ban culling of hatched male chicks. We believe chicks do not need to hatch only to be killed within hours. We believe there is no longer any need to cull hatched male chicks, the technology exists via in-ovo sexing which we feel needs to be mandated.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Provide funding to separate Gynaecology/women’s health from Maternity services Invest more money into Gynaecology services to make them separate from Maternity and stop 1000s of women who are struggling with infertility or miscarriage going through the heart ache of having to share clinic spaces or wards with pregnant women or parents to be.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require criminal trial juries to provide reasons using a verdict questionnaire Introduce legislation requiring criminal juries to complete a structured verdict questionnaire detailing the factual reasons for their decisions, learning from international models to ensure a transparent, appeal-resilient justice system.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Create a searchable register of those convicted of serious animal cruelty Create a register of those convicted of serious animal cruelty, which can be searched by potential employers etc to avoid these people working in inappropriate areas.
label: Home Office

text: Review the use of retail businesses as cover for illegality We urge the Government to launch a public inquiry into the legitimacy and legality of the huge number of barbers, nail bars, car wash, vape shops and similar outfits already established, and springing up in towns throughout the country.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Ban the sale and use of indoor fireworks We call on the UK Government to ban the sale and use of indoor fireworks. Although classified as F1, they emit flames and sparks that can pose a serious fire risk in enclosed spaces. We believe a ban would help prevent avoidable fires and reduce pressure on fire and rescue services.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Create a bank holiday on 12 July 2027 to celebrate the unification of England Create a one off bank holiday on Monday the 12th of July 2027, to celebrate the 1100th anniversary of Athelstan being recognised as the first ruler of a unified Kingdom of England.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Fund support for elderly or unwell parents who are carers for disabled children  We want the Government to provide more support to parents before they pass or become seriously unwell. Some parents are carers until their end of life, they might have the worry of who will continue to care for their children after they pass. We feel better policies & support need to be provided.
label: HM Treasury

text: Require all public places to have allergy medication & EpiPens We urge the Government to require all public places, such as cafes, restaurants, shops, businesses and schools, to have first aid boxes which contain EpiPens and allergy medication, as we believe allergic reactions are a life-or-death situation.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Replace the word "prostitute" in legislation with "sex worker" Just change the wording in law/legislation from prostitute to sex worker.
label: Home Office

text: Establish welfare body to end horse deaths in racing now Create an independent welfare-focused body empowered to implement measures that eliminate deaths of horses in racing immediately.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Fund more schools for children with special and additional needs I think the Government should look at converting disused buildings into schools for children's with additional needs or use the space the schools have to add a unit on. I feel there's not enough out there. I think special needs children are being forced into mainstream schools and are struggling.
label: Department for Education

text: Commit to not increasing taxes or imposing additional taxes on landlords We urge the Government to formally commit to not imposing tax increases or additional taxes on landlords to help protect current rental markets and tenants.
label: HM Treasury

text: Establish a cap on Homes of Multiple Occupancy (HMO) in stressed communities We call on the government to set a firm planning cap - to be adhered to by local authorities - on the level of flatlet and HMO development of a maximum 10 per 1,000 population. We believe this would help ensure that community infrastructure, character and cohesion are not stressed or destroyed.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Make funeral directors a regulated profession We believe the funeral industry must be regulated as there are a lack of government regulations for setting up a funeral business, meaning owners don't need to meet specific requirements.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Abolish the Office of the Children’s Commissioner We call on the government to dissolve the Office of the Children’s Commissioner. We think it is not independent enough from government and risks becoming politicised.
label: Department for Education

text: Review and reform child custody arrangements Change the default child custody contact arrangements to be 50/50 shared contact and living. We feel that the current system leads to disputes and can leave children without access to one parent.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Conduct review of sudden alopecia cases, diagnosis and patient support We call on the UK Government to review diagnosis of, and care for rapid-onset alopecia areata, including severe forms resulting in total hair loss.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text:
Hold a referendum to decide if the UK should leave the ECHR. Hold a referendum to decide if the UK should leave the ECHR.
We ask the government to arrange a public referendum on the UK’s membership in the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR).
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Review suitability of NHS mental health services for Neurodivergent people At present, I believe people with Autism, ADHD and other Neurodivergent conditions do not receive appropriate Mental Health treatment and care they need and deserve through NHS Mental Health services. All NHS Mental Health services must be suitable for Neurodivergent people.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Abolish 10 year spouse route and replace with one 5 year route to ILR Provide a single, UK Spouse visa path to ILR for all eligible couples; abolish the 5-year/10-year split and cap renewal costs. We believe this will be fairer.
label: Home Office

text:
To legally ensure that allergen-friendly food is always available in airports Airports should have at least one facility which holds food that can safely
cater to people who have medical dietary requirements related to the 14 main allergens.Travelling can be long and exhausting,it’s worse when you have to worry about whether you can safely eat, meaning some can’t eat at all.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require coconut be labelled as an allergen on food packaging Require coconut be labelled as a mandatory allergen on all food packaging. Any product containing coconut must clearly list it. Other countries, including the US and Canada, already require this. Clear labelling could protect children and adults at risk of life-threatening reactions and death.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Increase funding to £20m yearly for male suicide prevention & support. Increase funding to £20m per year for the UK. Increase support, prevention & awareness. As its not spoke about enough.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Pay compensation to families of wronged Sub-Postmasters/mistresses  We believe that those families affected by this situation should be compensated and offered help and support.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Fund treatment for R-CPD on the NHS I would like government to fund the NHS to provide the treatment for Retrograde Cricopharyngeus Dysfunction (R-CPD). We feel that this disorder impacts lives daily and is beginning to be taken seriously in the medical world.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban the sale of single-use plastic drinks bottles in UK schools We want the UK Government to ban the sale of single-use plastic drinks bottles in all primary and secondary schools, and require schools to provide sustainable alternatives such as refill stations and reusable bottle schemes.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Ban gambling advertising on TV We would like the government to step in and ban advertising on TV of all gambling and gambling sites. At present, it feels like there are so many adverts trying to get people gambling.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Increase defence spending to a minimum of 3% of GDP with immediate effect. We think we must bolster defence given the Russia Ukraine war. We believe that we mustn't think that when the war ends things will go back to how they were before. We think we will need to revert to previous levels of spending, for example in the mid 80's we spent 5% of GDP on defence!
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Exempt all social care providers from employer NI contribution rise We call on the Government to exempt all social care providers from the 2025 increase in employer National Insurance. We believe that as a result of this rise, the social care sector is now collapsing, and providers are closing weekly resulting in vulnerable people losing access to care.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Keep two-child benefit cap for fairness and sustainable public spending I want the government to keep the two-child benefit cap to support fair and sustainable welfare spending. Retaining the cap will help manage public finances responsibly and ensure that benefits remain targeted and effective for those most in need.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Establish national UFO reporting office & cooperate with other countries on UFOs We think the UK public deserves clarity on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAPs), also known as UFOs. The US has held hearings, passed laws, and created offices to investigate UAPs. Yet the UK remains silent.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: UK to propose Palestinian statehood at UN and press US to support it Fly UK leaders to the US to support a renewed 1967-based resolution for Palestinian statehood at the UN, urge the US to support it, and promote fair talks to help ensure security and sovereignty for both Israel and Palestine.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Fund paid placement or bursaries for medical students and improve conditions Fund paid placements or bursaries (like for some other allied health students), for medical students, as well as funded travel and accommodation during their placements. We also call on the NHS to set minimum standards for safe rota limits including protected rest, and fund mental health support.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review the NHS breast screening age Review NHS breast screening and ensure women with possible breast cancer symptoms, including those mistaken for menopause, receive timely investigation regardless of age.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review & reform the per pupil funding formula to support rural & coastal schools Schools in coastal and rural areas often receive less funding because they have fewer pupils. They may be forced to become academies or even close because the funding formula doesn’t cover costs. Therefore, we ask the government to use a different funding method that allows them to function well.
label: Department for Education

text: Reduce the time of day that fireworks can be set off to between 5pm & 8pm Reduce the time in which fireworks can legally be set off to reduce the nuisance & detrimental effect on animals & vulnerable members of the community.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Reduce the school week to three days a week Government and parliament need to lower children's school days per week from 5 to 3 to allow them to still enjoy their childhoods.
label: Department for Education

text: Cap legal fees for divorce cases and remove or reduce VAT Divorce can be stressful and costly. I think lawyers’ hourly fees are too high and should be capped, e.g. £250/hr. Legal help in divorce feels essential, so VAT should be exempt to ease the financial burden.
label: HM Treasury

text: Government to set up and fund an Emergency Services Covenant Trust We are asking the government to establish and fund an Emergency Services Trust, similar to the Armed Forces Covenant Fund Trust, which will provide funding to Emergency Services charities for treatment, rehabilitation and recovery services.
label: Home Office

text: Pause military support for Ukraine and hold a referendum The government has spent billions supporting Ukraine in the conflict. We believe this has no strategic or economic interest to the UK and that it’s adversely affected the cost of energy and of living. There should be a pause in the policy until there is a national debate and referendum on the issue.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Reverse new Dual Nationality entry requirements We want the Government to overturn the new UK entry requirements for Dual Nationality UK persons to visit their home, their heritage and their family introduced in February 2026.
label: Home Office

text: Establish a specific offence and sentence for Murder, Desecration & Concealment  Judges currently use their discretion when sentencing in cases involving murder, desecration and concealment. We want there to be a new standalone offence of Murder, Desecration and Concealment, with its own mandatory minimum custodial sentence.
label: Ministry of Justice

text:
Create a National Strategy for Childhood Apraxia Of Speech (CAS) We want the Government to create and fund a National Strategy for CAS, which should include:
- Increase education of CAS.
- Set up and fund a working group of experts and families to advise Government.
- Create a strategy across health and education sectors, similar to autism and dyslexia.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text:
Cyclists to be licenced, registered to be on the road and have insurance 1 All adults cyclists to have some kind of registration for their bikes like other road users
2 All adult cyclists to have valid insurance while on the road just like other road users
3 Cycling test to raise safety awareness and while on the road
4 Fines to be issued for not complying with this
label: Department for Transport

text: Seek agreement to protect refugees and restore humanitarian access in Libya We call on the UK Government to work with international partners to strengthen protection for refugees, asylum seekers, and migrants in Libya and to seek to ensure humanitarian organisations have safe and sustained access to provide assistance.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Legal requirement to respond to job applicants after interview Make 'ghosting' job applicants illegal after an interview. Job applications are time consuming for applicants. Some companies interview applicants and then provide no response. Companies should be required to provide interview feedback within a reasonable time frame
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Lower pension age for physically demanding jobs to 62 Introduce a reduced state pension age of 62 for people who have worked long-term in physically demanding occupations.
label: HM Treasury

text: Ban plastic stickers on fruit and vegetables sold in the UK We urge the Government to ban plastic stickers on fruit and vegetables sold in the UK. We believe they are not recyclable and contribute to microplastic pollution, and that there may be compostable or laser-etched alternatives. We believe the UK should follow France & New Zealand in doing this.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Review and reform how NHS Health Boards share, access & communicate patient data I'm calling for urgent review and reform of how NHS boards share, access, and communicate patient data. I want stronger requirements to ensure that they communicate transparently and share patient records effectively to prevent any risk of missed diagnoses, failed care, and delayed interventions.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Legalise and fund medical cannabis cafés for medical patients Some medical cannabis patients may be isolated and fearful despite having legal prescriptions. We want the Government to legalise and fund safe, regulated cafés where patients can use their medication, access support, and feel part of a community without stigma.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Introduce guidelines for disclosure photos of criminals We call on the Government to introduce new guidelines regarding disclosure of photos of criminals used by the police to disclose an image of a criminal to a victim of crime or their families.
label: Home Office

text: Create the right to examine council witnesses in moving traffic contraventions Millions of Penalty Charge Notices are sent out to motorists each year. We believe it is a human right to have the opportunity to question the evidence including by requiring the attendance of the author of a witness statement pertaining to a traffic  camera.
label: Department for Transport

text: Fund NHS pathways & mandated training for Pelvic Congestion Syndrome (PCS) We call on the Government to fund a clear NHS clinical pathway for PCS that bridges the gap between Gynaecology and Interventional Radiology.
