text: Fund school bus service for all Primary & Secondary state schools students We propose the funding of a shared school transport service (e.g., buses/vans) to provide safe, efficient, and eco-friendly travel for all school children. We believe such a service would bring significant benefits to our community like it is in other countries.
label: Department for Education

text: Extend the theory test expiry date from the current 2 years to 3 years I would like the Government to extend the theory test expiry date from the current 2 year period to 3 years. I believe extending this would be fair and just. Extending it could help the DVLA deal with the Covid backlog and third parties booking lots of slots and selling them on at higher prices.
label: Department for Transport

text: Allow child maintenance payslip deductions without notifying the paying parent Change the law to allow the Child Maintenance Service to issue calculations and apply deductions directly from wages without notifying the paying parent. This could rely on HMRC, employer and DWP records alone without needing to identify a “last known or notified address”.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Seek to establish an audit with France on expenditure securing our borders Seek to establish an independent audit in cooperation with France to help ensure transparency, accountability, and proper use of taxpayers’ money. Since 2014, the UK has given France hundreds of millions to manage Channel crossings, but there’s little public information on how it’s been spent.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Allow motorcycles in all UK bus lanes where taxis are permitted Require all highway authorities to allow motorcycles in any bus lane that already permits taxis. Update DfT guidance to make motorcycle access the default, ensure consistent rules nationwide, and amend traffic orders and signage accordingly.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review treatment of ARFID and access to NHS eating disorder services In many cases, support from NHS eating disorder services is not given to people with ARFID. We think this support is crucial and should be mandatory. If left untreated, ARFID can be life threatening. People can miss out on education and life events, and can lack energy to do basic daily activities.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Establish an official annual Women’s Health Awareness Week in England Women's health campaigns across England are fragmented, with no national platform to unite them. We call on the UK Government to establish an official annual Women's Health Awareness Week, delivering on its own Women's Health Strategy and matching other countries like the US, NZ and Australia.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund childcare for working parents immediately after maternity leave ends We want the Government to change the Funded Childcare for Working Parents scheme in England so eligible parents can access their childcare hours immediately after maternity, paternity, adoption or shared parental leave ends, rather than waiting until the next school term.
label: Department for Education

text: Legalise and regulate e-scooters & e-bikes exceeding current limits for road use Introduce a regulated framework allowing privately owned e-scooters and higher-speed e-bikes on roads, with a two-tier system: low-speed devices with basic registration, and higher-speed devices requiring a simple licence, ID and annual fee, with clear safety and enforcement rules.
label: Department for Transport

text: Require & fund the assignment of a caseworker to every domestic abuse victim Victims of domestic abuse are often required to navigate police, courts, housing and family law alone. Many are penalised for not understanding complex legal systems or procedures. A dedicated case worker could provide continuity, guidance and support from first disclosure to case conclusion.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Raise e-bike speed to 20mph, power to 1000W, throttle to 15.5mph Raise e-bike maximum speed limit to 20mph, power to 1000W for hills, & throttle to 15.5mph. We think current 250W/15.5mph limits hinder commuters, disabled riders, and cargo use. We believe this could lead to safer, greener, more active travel, cut emissions, and help stop illegal modification.
label: Department for Transport

text: Create a Cold War Medal for veterans who served in the cold war. Create a medal representing service given during the cold war which can be awarded to all cold war veterans. It was a very tense time in our history. Many lost their lives during this time.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Extend legal regulation of the teaching profession to teaching assistants  Extend Teaching Regulation Agency powers to Teaching Assistants so they are subject to the same professional misconduct regulations as qualified teachers, allowing the Teaching Regulation Authority (TRA) to investigate serious safeguarding concerns involving all teaching assistants.
label: Department for Education

text: Ban the use of AI in job recruitment processes We ask the Government to enact a law which bans the use of artificial intelligence tools in job recruitment processes.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Give Next of Kin Named on Death Certificate Automatic Access to Medical Records Amend the Access to Health Records Act 1990 so that the next of kin named on the death certificate has the legal right to access the deceased person’s full medical records, without needing to be the executor, administrator of the estate, or prove a legal claim. Families deserve peace of mind.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Stop VAT being added to Private school fees Stop the charging of VAT on private schools fees. Government funds free schools, so therefore I think it should also be supporting private schools that hard working parents scrimp to pay for! I think supporting private schools increases places and facilities offered to state schools!
label: HM Treasury

text: Require all new homes to include a swift brick Mandate that all new homes are built with one nesting brick which in short is a hollow brick with an entrance hole. Swifts are suffering from a lack of nesting, and we believe this would give them thousands of nests with the Government planning to build so much new housing.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Make conscription a condition of citizenship for migrants who entered illegally We may be sending troops to Ukraine and possibly other places. Our Armed forces are short of personnel. We think a period of serving in the armed forces should be a condition of gaining British citizenship for those who entered the country illegally.
label: Home Office

text: Allow UC claimants with start-up-businesses to receive payments for 3 years Change the law to allow people on Universal Credit who start and run a business to continue to receive payments for 3 years. This could give them time to build income and stability before benefits are reduced. This could encourage self-employment, growth, and independence from Universal Credit.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Recognise garlic and onion allergies within UK food allergen regulations Garlic and onion allergies can cause severe reactions, but they aren’t recognised in current allergen rules. This means restaurants and food labels often don’t list them, putting people at risk. Recognition would improve safety, awareness and consistency.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Stop the use of taxis for asylum seeker transport We call on the government to stop the use of taxis for asylum seeker transport.
label: Home Office

text: Review and reform Cafcass to address systemic failings and protect families We think Cafcass fails children and families, showing a lack of balance, ignoring evidence, and enabling abusers. Section 7 reports may be inaccurate, professional assessments dismissed, and complaints ignored. Victims may face retraumatisation, while staff may make harmful decisions.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Require schools to allow children to use the toilet at all times I would like the government to require schools to allow children to use the toilet at all times.
label: Department for Education

text: Review transparency and standardised labelling for pet food Review transparency of pet food labelling rules so consumers can make informed choices. Manufacturers should disclose individual ingredients, the proportion and origin of key ingredients, standardised nutritional information, and notify customers when recipes materially change.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Introduce a Publicly Accessible Sex Offenders Register Introduce a public Sex Offenders Register. We believe "Sarah’s Law" is too reactive, and that communities deserve a proactive "right to know". In our view, transparency must outrank offender privacy and we demand an official, searchable database to empower parents and enhance safety.
label: Home Office

text: Introduce 10 year minimum sentence for rape, sexual assault & child sexual abuse Campaign to improve justice for rape by introducing a minimum sentence of 10 years to reflect the severity of rape and sexual assault. Help strengthen public confidence to protect the most vulnerable.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Bring back 75% business rates relief for retail, hospitality & leisure sectors Business rate increases and business rate relief reductions come into effect in April 2026. We urge the Government to increase business rates relief back to 75% for retail, hospitality & leisure. We are concerned increases could lead to business closures, substantial job losses & empty properties.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Increase funding for medical research on women's anatomy Prioritise and allocate more funding for medical research on women's anatomy. We believe this will help to ensure a future where women’s health is understood, valued, and advanced for generations to come.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text:
Significantly increase dedicated funding for endometriosis - Increase ring-fenced funding for endometriosis research through UK research bodies.
- Support the development of faster, non-invasive diagnostic methods.
- Invest in better treatment options and long-term care strategies.
- Improve education and training for healthcare professionals.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Seek to work with the EU to develop European alternatives to key US products Seek to cooperate with the EU to examine areas where we rely upon American products and services and work to remove those dependencies.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Increase the maximum sentence for coercive control to 10 years Increase maximum sentence for coercive control to 10 years. We want the law to truly reflect the damage this abuse causes. Coercive control can destroy lives, isolate victims, erode their freedom, and leave lasting emotional scars. Many survivors never fully recover.
label: Ministry of Justice

text:
£1000 fine for loud exhaust pipes & seize vehicles of repeat offenders Increase the on the spot fine from £50 to £1000 for any motor vehicle being used on a public highway with an illegally loud & modified exhaust system.

To seize and destroy the vehicles of repeat offenders.
label: Department for Transport

text: Make it a legal requirement to report cat collisions and cover vet fees I propose that the government enforce a new law that requires all drivers involved in a cat collision to report it to the police and also be legally required to cover all veterinary expenses caused by the collision. Cats are loved pets too. Cats’ lives matter just as much as any other animals.
label: Department for Transport

text: Making Veteran Status a Protected Characteristic Make veteran status a protected characteristic under UK equality law. Veterans should be protected from discrimination in employment, housing, healthcare and public services because of their veteran status. Recognise and protect those who served.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Add Biomedical Scientists to the immigration salary list Recognise Biomedical Scientists as a shortage occupation and adjust immigration rules. Add them to the immigration salary list to lower salary thresholds for visa extensions.
label: Home Office

text: Move Tax Bands in line with minimum wage increases Review and change tax bands in line with minimum wage increases. Since freezing the bands, minimum wage has increased by 28.5%. The tax bands should have moved by same amount or minimum wage should not have increased.
label: HM Treasury

text: Review of support for widows and widowers with children under 18 Increase financial support for widows and widowers with children under 18, and allow them to automatically access Pupil Premium and Early Years Pupil Premium Funding.
label: HM Treasury

text: Do not describe sexual abuse of children as "grooming" by "grooming gangs" I want the Government and Parliament to stop using the words "grooming" and "grooming gangs". I feel they are euphemisms being used in official publications to describe horrible, violent sexual abuse of children including rape, torture, kidnapping and imprisonment.
label: Home Office

text: Cap public electric vehicle (EV) charging station rates. Current prices for public electric vehicle (EV) charging stations can be triple the cost of domestic electricity. This would make the cost per mile for many EV's higher than the diesel/petrol equivalent vehicle. The Government should set a maximum charge for public EV charging stations.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Protections for Migrant Workers in the Care Worker Visa Sponsorship System (COS) Implement protections for migrant care workers whose Certificates of Sponsorship are cancelled due to employer misconduct. Require inspections of care providers, establish penalties for fraudulent operators, allow affected workers to switch sectors, and provide temporary visa extension.
label: Home Office

text: Create a more inclusive sign for disabled toilets and require universal use Make disabled signs on toilets more inclusive to people with hidden disabilities. I have a stoma bag and I have the right to use disabled facilities but I am verbally attacked and abused by members of the public for doing so. We need to include everyone not just people in wheelchairs.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Ban the use of facial recognition software & require consent for biometric data We call for a law to make the use of facial recognition technologies by all actors, including police and security services, illegal. Such a law should require written consent for the collection of any biometric data, with full right of deletion preserved.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Legalise Wild Camping In England I ask the Government and Parliament to create a legal framework that allows responsible wild camping across England
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text:
Reinstate the hard shoulder on all smart motorways. Since smart motorways have done away with the hard shoulder, people have lost their lives in collisions resulting from being stranded with nowhere to go.
Safety bays are no use if your car suddenly cuts out or has a tyre blow out.
label: Department for Transport

text: Set a 6 month waiting time for autism diagnosis & increase funding Some children may be waiting over three years for autism assessments. Delays rob them of vital early support.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Polluter levy on companies whose products make up most litter Introduce an annual independent nationwide litter audit to identify the brands and products most commonly found littering the UK’s streets, parks, countryside and waterways and introduce a polluter levy on the 100 companies whose branded products are found most frequently.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Do not introduce a Brexit 'reset' bill Immediately stop any actions that help to reverse the outcome of the Brexit referendum.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Launch a review of the UK construction industry Launch a review of the UK’s construction industry, including the work environment, wages and recruitment, and legislation that could protect earnings that may be lost as a result of weather conditions, along with any money owed.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Reform the petition system: Parliament vote at 1M signatures & referendum at 5M Reform the petition system so that petitions reaching 1 million signatures trigger a parliamentary vote on the issue within 6 months, and petitions reaching 5 million signatures trigger a national referendum. This can help ensure the public’s voice leads to action, not just debate.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
label: Cabinet Office

text: Fund a national rollout of free-to-use Calisthenics Outdoor Gyms We urge the Government to fund the rollout of free-to-use outdoor gyms for bodyweight strength training, also known as Calisthenics (derived from Greek, meaning beautiful strength), as we believe there are hardly any Calisthenics outdoor gyms.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Fund stab vests as standard PPE for all prison officers We want the Government to provide prison officers with stab vests as part of their Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban all developments in high wildlife areas In 2014 it was reported that earth had lost 40% of its wildlife in the previous 40 years. Many species have become red-listed. We think all developments should be banned in high wildlife areas such as forests, woodland and green belt land.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Convene relevant parties to seek agreement on international regulation of AI We believe there has been too much talk about regulation of AI and not enough action. The Government should host a meeting of fellow Governmental officials, relevant NGOs and Senior Executives from the top AI labs to discuss and propose a set of international AI regulation principles.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Government must abolish Ofsted I want the Government to abolish Ofsted.  I believe the existence of Ofsted is the single most limiting factor in progressing education within this nation. Removing what I believe is its toxic influence would allow schools to thrive.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund free bus travel for all post-16 students We want the Government to fund free bus travel for post-16 students. We want free reliable travel for all post-16 students.
label: Department for Transport

text: Diabetes should not prevent someone serving in the British armed forces Diabetics should be able to join the military due to the modern technological advances that occur everyday. Managing the condition is second nature to most diabetics therefore I believe it should not be considered a risk as those who are insulin dependent know how to handle it and live with it.
label: Ministry of Defence

text:
End the tax threshold freeze to stop potentially pushing families into poverty 1. Legislate that, from April 2031, all income tax thresholds will rise automatically each year in line with CPI inflation or average wages (whichever is higher).
 
2. Apply a one-off sharp upward correction in 2031 to restore the real value lost over the decade — not a token increase.
label: HM Treasury

text: Replace First Past The Post with a transferable voting system We ask for the replacement of the current voting system with a transferable where the electorate will indicate preferences for up to 3 candidates and candidates are eliminated until one has over 50% of the remaining votes. This could ensure all votes cast are fully counted and be more representative
label: Cabinet Office

text: Mandatory anti-spiking measures in all nightclubs and bars Mandatory ID checks for everyone that enters a nightclub either manually or by an electronic system. Mandatory staff training for spiking awareness. Mandatory anti-spiking tools provided at every nightclub. Mandatory bag and pocket searches. Minimum of 1 trained welfare staff on shift at all times.
label: Home Office

text:
Independent Body to deal with misconduct in Public Services & training Abolish existing internal misconduct processes and establish an independent body to investigate all misconduct in public and emergency services.
Require all public & Emergency Services to have external non biased Whistleblowing workshops.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Review UK immigration policies, including a cap the number of people arriving  I would like the government to undertake a review into and be transparent about what checks and balances are in place so that this country can manage immigration sensibly. We think the review should consider whether there should be a cap on the number of people arriving.
label: Home Office

text: Require convicted domestic abuse offenders to be placed on a national register Create a national register for people convicted of domestic abuse offences, with appropriate safeguards, to help protect future partners and improve public safety. Domestic abuse often involves repeat offending.
label: Home Office

text: Continue the national Free School Meals voucher scheme for school holidays Continue to give the national free school meals vouchers. These vouchers are vital for some parents on low incomes but the Government has now ended the scheme.
label: Department for Education

text: Abolish fees for passport name changes Abolish fees for people who change their name on their passport due to marriage, divorce, gender reassignment, estrangement, or escaping domestic abuse, where the change is supported by official documents such as a marriage certificate or deed poll.
label: Home Office

text: Ban anyone convicted of serious criminal offences from standing in elections People with serious criminal convictions are allowed to stand for election for councillor after five years and once they leave prison, for MP. This includes terrorism, violence, sexual offences and fraud. We believe public office is a privilege, not a right, and should meet higher moral standards.
label: Cabinet Office

text:
Review and reform administration of Universal Credit & compensation Universal Credit was established to help provide financial stability & support to those in need.
However, we believe mounting evidence & widespread testimonies are revealing that injustice, financial distress, & systemic mismanagement have become pervasive experiences for claimants nationwide.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Extend the Fuel Duty Freeze for Motorists For At Least Two More Years Extend the temporary cut on fuel duty for motorists, set to end in March 2026 for a minimum of 2 more years, ensure fuel duty rates for motorists continue to stay frozen at the current headline rate during this period and set clear targets for further freezes in the future.
label: HM Treasury

text: Ban High-Silica Engineered Stone Worktops. We want high-silica engineered stone worktops banned due to the risk of silicosis resulting from silica dust particles. This stone is a common product in the market in the UK. Engineered stone is banned in Australia.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Change the legal driving age to 15 I think the government should change the legal driving age to 15 because the legal age to drive is 17 and I think both 15 and 16 year olds will be able to drive.
label: Department for Transport

text: Lower universal credit earnings threshold (the AET) for single parents Many single parents are struggling to find more hours or new jobs that work around school holidays, resulting in pressure from the job centre with weekly phone calls / meetings. It is difficult to find holiday clubs for over 5’s in many areas which adds more pressure on the parent.
label: Department for Education

text: Review use of the '"Child in Need" label by social workers & local authorities We think the government should have a full, urgent review of how safeguarding applies to disabled children. We want respect and compassion for parent carers doing their best under impossible circumstances.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Facilitate a referendum on Scottish independence We believe Scotland deserves independence.
label: Scotland Office

text: Mandatory life sentence for involvement in trafficking women & children for sex We ask the Government to take the lead in tackling human trafficking, in particular of women and children for sexual exploitation. We ask for the institution of mandatory life sentences for anyone involved in these crimes to deter those operating at all levels of human trafficking networks.
label: Home Office

text: Ban the use of all Single-Use Plastics Ban use of all single-use plastics, including food packaging and product wrapping. We think this would reduce waste, protect the environment, and encourage manufacturers to adopt sustainable alternatives like plant-based or cornstarch solutions.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Guarantee 100% Pension Transfer to Surviving Spouses We call upon the Government to enact legislation that guarantees surviving spouses receive 100% of their deceased partner’s pension—whether state, occupational, or private—without any reduction, delay, or discretionary limitations.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Exempt first time buyers from stamp duty We urge the Government to remove stamp duty for first-time buyers to allow them to get onto the property ladder. Many first-time buyers have to cope with inflation and rising costs of properties, which are extremely difficult, and then pay stamp duty on top of hard-earned money saved after tax.
label: HM Treasury

text: Introduce targeted coastal trawling bans to protect ecosystems & reduce erosion We call on the Government to establish 0–6 nautical mile exclusion zones for bottom-contact fishing in key UK coastal areas. We think this will allow kelp and seagrass recovery, strengthen natural defences like saltmarsh and dunes, and reduce coastal erosion and flood risk sustainably.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Stop criminalisation of parents who take children abroad due to domestic abuse 75% of 'child abductions' involve mothers. Most are taking their child back to their country of origin and have experienced Domestic Abuse (DA).
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban all electric scooters on public roads We ask the Government to ban e-scooters on public roads due to the increasing number of accidents, injuries and fatalities. They pose serious risks to riders, pedestrians and other road users. Stronger regulation and enforcement is urgently needed to protect public safety.
label: Department for Transport

text: Require & fund local councils to provide public toilets Introduce a duty that every council should be compelled to provide a public toilet service which can meet the needs of the entire population. The government should allocate sufficient funds to local councils to carry out these obligations.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Review communication of diagnostic results in cases of suspected cancer Review the communication of diagnostic test results that indicate suspected cancer, and ensure NHS providers are making urgent suspected cancer referrals where national referral criteria are met.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Create a £5,000 tax-free allowance for online marketplace income We want the UK Government to create a £5,000 annual tax-free allowance for income earned through online marketplaces and side hustles, including eBay, Vinted, Depop and similar platforms.
label: HM Treasury

text: Review the use of digital technology in schools Following the example of Sweden, we want the UK Government to review how digital technology is used in UK schools and restore a better balance between screens and traditional learning, include more use of printed books, handwritten work, and focused reading time, especially in early education.
label: Department for Education

text: Require cosmetic surgeons to hold a GMC-approved specialist qualification Require clinicians carrying out cosmetic procedures to hold a GMC-approved specialist qualification for surgical intervention for the area of the anatomy that they are treating.  A new law should ensure that any clinician carrying out surgery should have a GMC-recognised specialist qualification.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban supermarkets from throwing away or destroying unsold safe food Supermarkets should be made to either significantly reduce the price so food gets sold before closing time, or donate it to charities and food banks. They should be banned from throwing food into waste if there are other options, if the food is safe and hygienic under FSA guidance.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Require that photo ID and fingerprints are taken prior to the purchase of knives I feel the law needs to be changed regarding the purchase of knives. I believe that when purchasing a knife, photo ID should be held on record and finger prints taken, to reduce the lives lost to knife crime.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text:
New road safety legislation for cyclists & mandate safety gear and reg numbers We want the Government to introduce laws regulating the behaviour of cyclists on the road. This should include making it an offence to:
•            Using a mobile phone whilst cycling
•            Not stopping at traffic lights and pedestrian crossings
label: Department for Transport

text: Hold a referendum on the proposed ban on new ICE cars in 2030 I request a referendum regarding the proposed ban on the sale of new Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) cars by 2030. I think this referendum is crucial to ensure public opinion is considered in this significant transition, balancing environmental goals with economic and social impacts.
label: Department for Transport

text: Require elected public office holders to identify their role on social media Require elected public office holders, including MPs, councillors and mayors, to clearly state their official role in their social media profile name.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Negotiate with Ireland reciprocal visa free tourism travel for all residents Seek an agreement with the ROI government to allow non-UK/ROI/non-visa residents of UK and ROI travel within CTA for short stay and tourism purpose without the need for a visa from each other. The population of Non-British / Irish / EU citizens in UK and ROI is over 4% of the total population.
label: Home Office

text: Scrap either EV pay-per-mile tax or Vehicle Excise Duty for EVs. Don't have both From 2028 electric car owners will pay BOTH VED car tax and 3p per mile. We think this will punish working people and families resulting in around £300 extra for 10000 miles on top of £195 VED tax for many EVs. It's not like the electricity to charge the car hasn't already been taxed.
label: HM Treasury

text: Ban both private and public use of fireworks & replace with cleaner alternatives Ban the sale and use of fireworks at public and private events. Instead, allow organised eco-friendly displays like drone shows, as adopted in countries such as the Netherlands.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Launch a review into imposing stricter moped sale & licensing regulations We urge the Government to launch a review into introducing stricter regulations governing the process of obtaining a moped licence and the private sale of mopeds.
label: Department for Transport

text: Include Mindfulness in the Curriculum for Schools Childhood trauma can impact adult mental health and criminality. Mindfulness in schools could help build resilience and prevent long-term issues by intervening early.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund awareness & training for Heparin Induced Thrombocytopenia Thrombosis We urge the Government to fund a national campaign to raise awareness of Heparin’s potential side effects, and to fund training programs and continuous medical education which include comprehensive information on the drug’s side effects and their management.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Decriminalise the possession and use of marijuana & cannabis products in the UK We urge the Government to review the classification of marijuana and decriminalise the possession and use of marijuana and cannabis-related products in the UK. We believe people shouldn’t be prosecuted or fined for what we believe is a private act of intoxication in their homes or public.
label: Home Office

text: Require time & space for Muslim children to pray at school & education We want the government to require schools to have a designated room & adequate time in the school day (if outside break times) for Muslim children to carry out prayers. Ablution (cleansing the body) is required before praying. We want education to be rolled out on this in schools to remove stigma.
label: Department for Education

text: Mandate the installation of solar panels on all new buildings The government has pledged to construct 1.5 million homes by the end of this parliament. We think there should be legislation that all of these new homes must have solar panels. We think this must be incorporated into building regulations in the same way that insulation requirements already are.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Ban ambient music in public places We think hospitals and public transport should be places of calm. We think private concerns which we all must use, such as supermarkets, should also be prohibited from playing loud music.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Make lying or spreading disinformation in public office a criminal offence We want the Government to make it a criminal offence if a person or persons in public office has/have knowingly lied and/or spread disinformation and/or suppressed factual information.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Fund wildlife vet care and give rehabilitators access to medicines. We want the Government to amend the Veterinary Medicines Regulations to allow qualified wildlife rehabilitators regulated access to essential medicines, and to work with the RCVS to establish a funded framework requiring vets to cooperate with recognized rescues on long-term treatment.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Review and improve safeguarding for children before and after adoption Review and strengthen safeguarding for children before and after adoption by improving multi-agency working, recognising professional judgement alongside evidence, and considering routine and unannounced welfare visits before Adoption Orders.
label: Department for Education

text: Create a legal entitlement to two weeks’ paid bereavement leave for employees We call on the Government to create a legal entitlement to two weeks (10 working days) of paid bereavement leave for employees, which can be taken flexibly and in separate periods where needed, to ensure consistent protection for bereaved workers across the UK.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Chemical castration for all those convicted of child sexual abuse We think that for all those found guilty in cases of child grooming and sexual abuse, along with a custodial period, they should be chemically castrated to help prevent repeating this behaviour.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Increase the statutory paternity leave allowance for fathers of multiple births We believe the Government should increase paternity leave allowance for fathers of multiple births, such as in the case of twins or triplets. We think it’s unfair that fathers are expected to return to work after two weeks in the event of multiple births.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Hold a public inquiry into the work of the Family Courts We think there are huge inefficiencies in the family court system. We think this leads to delays, incorrect appointments, wrong outcomes and lack of contact between parents and children. We believe hundreds of thousands of people are affected.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Include British Citizens Studying Medicine Abroad in NHS Training Prioritisation The Government should work to ensure the inclusion of British citizens who studied medicine abroad in internationally recognised institutions, in the NHS foundation and specialty training prioritisation, so they are not treated the same as overseas applicants without UK ties.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban holiday companies from implementing price hikes during school breaks We feel that families (be that single parent families, one income families or other less fortunate families) are being squeezed by holiday companies with price increases in the school breaks. We feel this is unfair.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Hold public inquiry into racial hatred in England since 2012 We think public attitudes have shifted amid a constant stream of misinformation about minorities and immigration, and that politicians, public figures and so-called "news" channels now lie with impunity.
label: Home Office

text: Make politicians legally responsible for their election promises Require all individuals standing for public office to sign a legal declaration to say that if elected, they will carry out their duties with honesty and integrity and fulfil their promises to the electorate. Otherwise, I think they should be held criminally liable.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Require media retractions be made as visible as original headlines or articles We think media companies should not be allowed to get away with printing false, misleading and malicious headlines, only to hide the retractions on interior pages or fine print some days later. Retractions should have to have the same prominence as the original headline or article.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Allow the Police to use the public genealogy databases to investigate cold cases We want law enforcement agencies to be given permission and access to the public genetic genealogy databases; to investigate cold cases.
label: Home Office

text: Review Investigative and Prosecutorial Standards in Sexual Offence Cases We call for a review into the investigative and prosecutorial practices in sexual offence cases to ensure fair evidence standards, proper disclosure, and accountability, protecting the integrity of the justice system for all.
label: Home Office

text: Increase domestic violence maximum sentences and penalties & reform bail laws We call on Parliament to increase domestic violence maximum sentences and strengthen bail laws by banning bail to high-risk and repeat offenders. Increase penalties for repeat abuse and restraining order breaches to prioritise victim safety. Risk assessments should be required before release.
label: Ministry of Justice

text:
Make Medicine Prescriptions Free for Asthma Pump Users This petition is very simply calling for the UK Government to give all people with Asthma an exemption from paying the prescription fee.
More than three-quarters of people with asthma who pay for their prescriptions said they struggle to afford them, according to a recent report by Asthma UK
label: Department of Health and Social Care
Cabinet Office

text: Require a UK wide referendum before donating £10 Million or more to any country Before any UK government can donate more than £10 million to any foreign country there should be a UK national referendum held and the result should be legally binding.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Ban intelligence services use of public personal data for creating/training AI Prevent government intelligence services from taking personal data from the internet and other public places and using it to create and/or train artificial intelligence/ algorithms/information technology of any kind.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Require an expert to examine a pet before seizure under the Dangerous Dogs Act Stop the police taking family pets without an expert there to examine the pet. I think this causes unnecessary stress for all involved and I believe the condition a lot of these animals get returned in is disgusting.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Regulate small animal breeding We want the Government to regulate small animal breeding that would protect small animals from over breeding and coming to harm. We want there to be the same standards as there is with dogs as there are a large amount of small animals in rescues.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Allow for shorter visa extensions & HIS refunds for migrants nearing ILR We want the Government to allow migrants and dependents who are close to qualifying for Indefinite Leave to Remain to be able to apply for shorter visa extensions and receive a refund of Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) payments that is proportionate to their time left before receiving ILR.
label: Home Office

text: Remove cursive handwriting from the expected standard for primary school I would like the Government to change how children in primary can reach the expected and greater depth writing standard by removing the factor that they must write in cursive handwriting.
label: Department for Education

text: Allow National Lottery funds to support social housing Allow National Lottery funds to support social housing at social rent, whether provided by local authorities, community land trusts, housing co-operatives, or other not-for-profit providers. Change the rules relating to the principle of additionality to allow this.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Outright ban on all XL Bully dogs We think the 2024 ban that allowed existing XL bully dogs to hold an exemption certificate is clearly not working given the continuing number of serious attacks. We think that the dogs are clearly not suitable for domestic settings and need to be destroyed.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Fund cervical screening every 3 yrs or more frequently, lower minimum age to 18 Reduce the age at which routine cervical screening is first offered, to 18. Require routine testing every 3 years, fully funded, rather than 5 years, for non HPV positive individuals and increase funding for more frequent testing.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Scrap the policy to ban the sale of new Petrol and Diesel Cars from 2030 We believe the Government's policy of banning the sale of new petrol & diesel cars after 2030 in favour of EVs is totally unworkable. We are unclear about how people who park their cars on the street & people who live in high rise flats will be able to charge their EVs with leads running everywhere
label: Department for Transport

text: Reduce vehicle tax rates by 50% for vehicles registered up to 31 March 2017 Reduce vehicle/road /VED tax by at least 50% for cars registered up to 31 March 2017. In our view, the current costs are not realistic, unfair, and extortionate and further promotes the disposable, uneconomic car culture that results from serviceable vehicles being scrapped.
label: HM Treasury

text: Prevent people with serious criminal convictions from becoming local councillors We call on the Government to prohibit people convicted of serious criminal offences from standing for election as local councillors.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Fund more, newly designed knife banks outside every police station I want a newly designed knife bank outside every police station. I think it should be designed to accommodate the large machete type zombie blades that is on our streets, not the small post box type knife bank that you find outside some police stations
label: Home Office

text: Fund recovery wards in hospitals for mothers that have newborns in NICU Fund separate wards for mothers who have babies in the NICU where they don’t have to watch other mothers bonding with their babies. It could be a space for women in the same position to seek comfort and reassurance from each other.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review the UK Novel Foods Regs to allow medical mushrooms for human consumption Modernise the UK Novel Foods Regulation so traditional natural products with a history of safe global use can be sold without authorisation. The framework should reflect modern science, cultural diversity, consumer choice and fair access for small UK producers; not an arbitrary 1997 cut-off.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Establish a new Independent Complaints Process for Serving Police Officers Amend the Police Reform Act 2002 to create an independent complaints process for police officers which would allow them, whether victims, suspects, or whistleblowers, to raise concerns about their force without those matters being referred back internally.
label: Home Office

text: Stop arms sales and any military support to Ukraine and Israel. We demand the government cease all arms sales to these countries along with any military support. We believe we should end our part in the pain and destruction inflicted by war, and that we should not support weapons but instead, invest the money in our own citizens and services.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: All negotiations with the EU must be debated and voted on by Parliament We believe any changes to the UK's relationship with the EU must be debated and voted on by Parliament before being agreed. We think this would ensure that any decisions made are subject to parliamentary sovereignty and consider elected representatives’ views.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Fund spiking testing in A&E and in walk-in sexual health clinics Fund greater access to testing for spiking victims, to allow the scale of the spiking cases to be quantified, truly analysed and tackled. We think this should be available in hospitals and sexual health clinics to help understand, deter and tackle spiking.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require all companies to declare microplastic levels in their food & drinks We urge the Government to require all companies to publicly identify and declare the amount of microplastics in their food and drink products, so people can make an informed choice about whether to consume products that may contain high levels of microplastics.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Fund Rent payments for Working Care Leavers in Supported Accommodation We think care leavers aged 18+ in supported accommodation should have their rent funded if they are working or on apprenticeships. They are encouraged to not be NEET yet we think the current system punishes those trying to become independent and may force some into poverty.
label: Department for Education

text: Require a Public Referendum Before Deploying Troops or Bombing Campaigns Abroad  Pass a law requiring a public referendum before any military action on foreign soil, including troop deployment, bombing, and covert operations. This would ensure real democratic control and help prevent unnecessary, harmful conflicts driven by political, corporate, and geopolitical interests.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Raise the minimum legal age to make adult content to 25 We think the minimum age to become a content creator in the adult industry should be raised to 25 to protect the welfare of young adults.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Ban MPs having second jobs whilst in office I believe Members of Parliament should not be allowed to hold second jobs of any sort whilst holding Office.
label: Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

text:
Enact the Socio-Economic Duty of the Equality Act 2010. To enact the Socio-Economic Duty of the Equality Act 2010.
This requires public bodies to consider inequalities resulting from socio-economic disadvantage when making certain decisions. Successive governments have not enacted the Duty.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Ban local authorities from approving driven piling near existing homes We ask the government to change planning legislation and national planning policy so that local planning authorities cannot approve the use of driven piling near existing residential properties as part of the planning process.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Require lie detector tests for victims and people accused of sexual offences Make it mandatory that all accusers and those accused of sexual offences, however minor or major the offence, are required to take a lie detector test.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Require a referendum for any policy that breaches the governments manifesto The government should not be able to act in away which goes against their manifesto pledges. We believe the manifesto is what drives the people to vote for government. If the government wishes to break the manifesto then we the public should have a vote in a referendum.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Fund training on Neurofibromatosis and Functional neurological disorder Fund training for doctors to further understand the basics of Neurofibromatosis and function neurological disorder so patients can receive better help without needing to be transferred to a specialist which could be miles away.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Stop Child Maintenance if parents are denied access to their children We believe that parents, often Fathers, across the UK are paying child maintenance while being unfairly denied access to their children and we want this to change.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Amend the Pet Abduction Act 2024 to remove exemptions for having lived together We want the government to amend Sections 1 and 2 of the Pet Abduction Act 2024 to remove the exemptions from committing an offence which rest on the fact of having lived together
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Change the rule on admissibility of recorded evidence in domestic abuse cases We want the Government to create a presumption of admissibility for recordings submitted as evidence by victims to the police relating to domestic violence in order to help protect victims from further abuse.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Introduce a minimum 6-month grace period for UK dual citizen travel rules. Require the Government to introduce a minimum 6-month grace period before enforcing new travel rules requiring British dual citizens to use a UK passport or certificate of entitlement, allowing sufficient time to obtain documentation before travel and avoid disruption to existing travel plans.
label: Home Office

text: Require a National Insurance number to access any NHS treatment We believe anyone wanting free medical attention or treatment from the NHS should only qualify if they or their parent or guardian have a National Insurance Number. Without this, we believe they must be required to pay for their treatment.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Change Sexual Offences Act rape definition to include any assault by penetration I want the government to change the Sexual Offences Act legislation to redefine all penetrative assault as rape and the offenders should be prosecuted as such. We think labelling it as penetrative assault undermines the victim’s reality of the harm and impacts caused.
label: Home Office

text: Require Latino/Hispanic option in the ethnicity section for official documents We want the government to require that a Latino box is included in the ethnicity section of every government document in the way that different Asian and Black ethnicities are often represented.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Require full public consultation on proposed PIP reforms in the Green Paper The Government must include all proposed changes to PIP in the Pathways to Work Green Paper in the consultation, including the four-point threshold rule for PIP. The significant reforms will directly impact disabled people.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Ban the import of foie gras into the UK We believe the production of foie gras involve cruel methods: it is produced by force-feeding ducks or geese, which may cause severe distress, organ failure, and a dramatically reduced quality of life. We believe this practice is inhumane and any foie gras products must be banned.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require Property Management Companies to Publish Management Annual Accounts The Government should require all property management companies responsible for issuing service charges in residential apartment complexes to publish annual management accounts within 12 months of each financial year end and publish them on a publicly accessible portal, similar to Companies House.
label: Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

text: National guidelines to standardise burial fees and ban non-resident surcharges  We want the Government to issue national guidance to local authorities to ensure fair and consistent burial charges across the country and remove “non-resident” surcharges.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Fund free NHS dentist treatment for all UK Citizens During times such as the currently financial crisis many people including those who work full time are struggling to excess dentist treatment due to the cost. Make it free for all UK citizens to access.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Seek free movement agreement with Australia, Canada & New Zealand We want the Government to negotiate with the governments of Australia, Canada and New Zealand with a view to establishing the free movement of our collective citizens between these countries.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Ban Private Dog Breeding and Strengthen Penalties for Animal Cruelty We urge the UK Government to ban the private breeding of dogs and allow only registered charities to breed dogs for rehoming. Additionally, we call for stricter minimum sentences for those convicted of animal cruelty, ensuring more consistent punishment and stronger deterrents.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Add a “None of the above” option to ballot papers for all elections We urge the Government to pass a law which adds a “None of the above” option at the bottom of all ballot papers in local and general elections, which we would like to be counted alongside votes and published in the results.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Redirect some foreign aid to fund services for British children We call on the Government to redirect a portion of overseas aid—particularly the £18 billion already committed to Ukraine—toward supporting the future of British children.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Create a tax on clothing that contains micro-plastics To aid in combatting the issues of plastic pollution and fast fashion, we urge the Government to implement a tax on clothing containing microplastics. With this, we aim to encourage clothing companies and brands to stop partaking in fast fashion and promote sustainability.
label: HM Treasury

text: Reverse the burden of proof in relation to consent in sexual assault cases We want to place the burden of proof on the defence, to prove, on the balance of probabilities, that they did have consent.
label: Home Office

text: Ban all UK economic & charitable activities with all illegal settlements We call on the Government to bring forth legislation that will prohibit all economic and charitable activities, including any trade and investment, with any illegal settlement in territories deemed occupied under international law.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Equal Parental Leave for Fathers: Reform UK statutory Paternity leave Policies We want the Government to introduce equal statutory parental leave for fathers, matching statutory maternity leave duration. We think this would ensure fathers can fully support their partners during recovery, bond with their children, and promote equality in caregiving and workplace rights.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Require schools to ringfence SPP and report how it helps service children. Introduce rules so SPP (Service Pupil Premium) is used specifically for service children, tracked clearly, overseen by a designated lead in each school, and used to provide targeted support that helps them thrive during parental deployment and improve their wellbeing and learning outcomes.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund research into improving maternal health outcomes for black women in the UK We are calling for the Government to increase funding into research focused on maternal health outcomes for black women, including improved data collection and transparency around maternal outcomes.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund private financial planning support for terminally ill patients We want the Government to fund private, face-to-face, one-to-one support for all terminally ill patients so that they can have help to organise their financial and legal affairs as part of palliative care, with access to appropriate support and referrals.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Raise Rent a Room Scheme tax-free threshold to reflect inflation & housing needs Increase the Rent a Room Scheme tax-free threshold from £7,500 to at least £12,000 per year and introduce automatic index-linking to inflation.  Public policy benefits are: Increase housing supply; neutral/low cost (uses existing homes); economically fair; administrative ease; supports workers.
label: HM Treasury

text:
Improve access to Parliament’s work for people with learning difficulties We want the Government and Parliament to change so that we can participate in their work.

We want to change the law in the Equality Act so that this must happen.

See this petition in Easy Read: https://www.inclusionlondon.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Parliament-E-petition.pdf
label: Cabinet Office

text: Create a Shariah-compliant Alternative Student Finance Option Introduce Alternative Student Finance for those who are unable to take out the traditional interest-bearing student loan
label: Department for Education

text: Introduce legal standards for hedgehog houses Introduce legal design and build standards for hedgehog houses. This would ensure those which did not meet the standards could not be legally sold.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Launch a national awareness campaign on sepsis & emergency responses We are calling for greater awareness, earlier recognition and faster treatment of sepsis – a life-threatening condition, by launching a national awareness campaign. We hope it will prevent loss and heartbreak. We believe sepsis should be treated as an emergency.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Conduct a review into the treatment of white people by the police  We call on the government to conduct a review into whether there are internal or external factors that are impacting police services and how they respond to white people, particularly if the police are discriminatory towards white people.
label: Home Office

text:
Add the Progress Pride Flags to the flags that don’t require permission There are rules about the flags that can be flown without local planning authority consent.
 
The Rainbow Flag is already listed, subject to certain restrictions. We would like the Progress Flag & its Intersex inclusive version to be listed too, allowing organisations to demonstrate inclusiveness
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text:
Stop Means Testing Pensioners and increase the State Pension. We demand the government stop means testing pensioners, that we think is a degrading and humiliating practice. We also think the state pension should be increased.

We believe that for too long, our elderly have been portrayed by media as merely burdens on the NHS and the modern welfare state.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Reduce the UK Census closure period from 100 years to 80 years We request the Government to reduce the UK Census record closure from 100 to 80 years, retaining safeguards for sensitive information, enabling families, genealogists and researchers to access vital historical records earlier while balancing privacy with the legitimate public interest.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Create a tax-free overtime allowance for overtime worked above 40 hours per week We want the Government to introduce a change to Income Tax so that genuine overtime worked above 40 hours per week is tax free, up to a set cap. This should apply only to hours worked above a person’s normal contracted hours. The policy should also comply with existing working time law.
label: HM Treasury

text: Introduce a rent cap on student accommodation Introduce a rent cap on all student accommodation across both private and corporate providers to address excessive pricing, ensure equal access to higher education, and reduce the mental health impact of financial strain on students.
label: Department for Education

text: Provide funding for all schools to have a social worker I think that all children deserve to have access to an independent person who they can share their worries and fears with as they need within their school days not having to wait to fit criteria set by others and disturbing their life creating differences between them and other children.
label: Department for Education

text: Require insurers to verify animal boarding licences before providing insurance Legislate to require insurers to verify animal boarding licences before issuing or renewing insurance cover for animal boarding businesses. Insurers should be responsible for checking licences are valid, current and relevant to the activity being insured.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Government must abolish IPSA We believe MPs should be stopped from claiming tax-payer-funded & none-means-tested perks & allowances which we feel contrasts hugely with the means-tested and limited support available to the public.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Create a visa route for Palestinian Orphans and Simplify Adoption Processes We think the Government should establish a clear and accessible process for bringing orphaned babies to the UK, ensuring that prospective adoptive parents, charities, or other responsible entities can apply for visas on their behalf.
label: Home Office

text: Make Black history part of the curriculum in all schools We think that the celebration of Black history in England should not be relegated to one month a year and should be made mandatory across all schools in England from ages 8-16. It should not be separate history because it is a part of British History.
label: Department for Education

text: Reverse the withdrawal of funding for security and leadership apprenticeships Reverse the withdrawal of funding for key security and leadership apprenticeships. Maintain funding for relevant programmes, consult with industry, and ensure apprenticeship policy supports sectors facing rising pressure due to for example crime and operational risks.
label: Department for Education

text: Ban aspartame in our food and drinks I call on the government to ban the additive aspartame/E951 in food and beverages. I think that the precautionary principle should be key to safeguard public health.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Regulate “Counsellor” and “Psychotherapist” as protected statutory titles Introduce statutory regulation for counselling and psychotherapy, with protected titles for “Counsellor” and “Psychotherapist”. Anyone using these titles must meet statutory standards, register with an independent statutory regulator, and be subject to complaints and fitness-to-practise processes.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Change the statutory term ‘Special Educational Needs’ to more inclusive language Change the term “Special Educational Needs (SEN)” in education legislation and statutory guidance to more inclusive, modern terminology such as “Additional Learning Needs” or “Learning Needs”, including in the SEND Code of Practice and relevant education law.
label: Department for Education

text: Amend the home buying process in England to align with Scotland We ask the UK Government to reform property law in England to align more closely with the Scottish model. The process in Scotland makes offers legally binding earlier, which we think helps reduce fall-throughs and creates a more secure, fair process for all.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Grant home fee status to UK & EU nationals who live in the EU The Government should grant British citizens living in the EU and EU nationals the right to qualify for home fee status at English universities, even if they have not spent the 3 years before the start of their university term living in the UK.
label: Department for Education

text: Legislate to release the 1951 census in 2032 instead of 2052 Legislate to allow the release of the 1951 census details in 2032 instead of 2052 due to there being no censuses available in 1931 and 1941. This would mean that many families could find answers to genealogical questions that currently have no answers and no means of finding the answers elsewhere.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Amend UK trade agreements with the Faroes to protest dolphin hunting & killing We call on the UK Government to review and amend trade agreements with the Faroe Islands. The Grindadráp involves driving dolphins and whales into shallow waters where they are horrifically killed. The practice goes against all marine mammal protection law in the UK.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Introduce laws to allow children to use puberty blockers, choose gender & names Introduce laws and safeguards to make sure that transgender children are legally able to use puberty blockers (but not undergo surgery until 18) and are able to change their names legally themselves. I want the government to ensure they are protected from transphobic parents or guardians.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Only allow a change of prime minister through a general election Pass a law to ensure that if a Prime Minister leaves office a new general election is held.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Introduce a Minister for Deportations at the Home Office Introduce a dedicated Minister for Deportations at the Home Office, with their own team and budget, focused solely on deportations.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Mandatory minimum sentences for offences relating to indecent images of children We call on the Government to increase the mandatory minimum sentence for all offences relating to indecent images of children to at least 15 years.
label: Home Office

text: Don't reduce the number of trials by jury There have been reports that the Government may reduce the number of trials by jury. We believe we must retain the right to trial by jury to prevent miscarriages of justice.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Government funding for home-educated children: ensure fair educational support. We urge the Government to provide financial support to home-educating families, similar to per-pupil school funding. This could help cover educational materials, resources, and extracurricular activities, ensuring equitable access to quality education for all children, regardless of environment.
label: Department for Education

text: Commission an inquiry into wrongful convictions & the current appeals process The current appeals system provides for errors in law and/or evidence that was not available at trial. We are concerned that many people have been found wrongly convicted after years of imprisonment.
label: Ministry of Justice

text:
Implement a mandatory DNA register for everyone born in or arriving in the UK. The implementation of a mandatory DNA database could help solve crimes more quickly and aid in the resolution of unclosed cases.
It could also be an aid in removing potential suspects from police workloads if they aren't a DNA match.
label: Home Office

text: Make Universities free for all We want to make Universities accessible for all, as we think higher education should be a right not a privilege for the wealthy. End tuition fees at Universities and make higher education free and accessible for all—no debt, no barriers, just a world of opportunities.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund Child Contact Centre visits for parents Some individuals are ordered by the courts to attend a child contact centre for supervised or supported contact. We feel this should be funded by the Government.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Provide funding to increase capacity for employment tribunal hearings Employment Tribunals are severely under-resourced, leaving claimants and respondents waiting up to 5 years for hearings. We call on the Government to invest sufficient funding to increase judicial resource into the ET system, and publish a clear, time-bound plan to reduce waiting times.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Mandate Social, Emotional, and Mental Health informed school behaviour policies Set out guidelines and legally mandate SEMH-informed school behaviour policies. This should include replacing punitive discipline with early intervention, stopping exclusions which we see as punishing mental health struggles, enforcing trauma training for staff, funding better mental health support.
label: Department for Education

text: Review and strengthen child car seat law We want the Government to review current child car seat law to strengthen it. We believe the current law is derived from outdated research. Recent research has suggested that the law should be updated, better protecting children on every journey.
label: Department for Transport

text: Detain anyone arriving in the UK illegally We believe that anyone arriving into the UK illegally should be detained in the hotel/migrant accommodation until they are deported as they have arrived without the proper documentation. Such accommodation could include temporary camps.
label: Home Office

text: Add Zambia to the list of 'designated countries' for driving licence exchange Add Zambia to the list of countries authorised to exchange their domestic driving licences for a United Kingdom driving licence.
label: Department for Transport

text: Update the Highway Code Rule 243 to forbid parking/stopping on private driveways Update Rule 243 of the Highway Code to forbid parking or stopping on private driveways. The rule currently pinpoints 12 places not to stop or park, but absent from the list is parking on someone else’s driveway.
label: Department for Transport

text: Introduce a free UK visa or other evacuation route for refugees from Gaza I want the UK Government to introduce and fund a free visa or evacuation route for refugees from the conflict in Gaza, including families, so that they can escape the violence and live in safety. I believe that thousands of lives could depend on action like this.
label: Home Office

text: Ensure the renewal of LPWGS beyond March 2026 without any caps There is uncertainty over the Listed Places of Worship Grant Scheme. It has been vital in guaranteeing urgent/necessary conservation/repair work to thousands of historic churches. The Government should extend the scheme beyond March 2026 and ensure no caps are put in place.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Fund a national lymphoma awareness and early diagnosis campaign Fund a national lymphoma awareness campaign with the aim of increasing public awareness of the signs and symptoms of lymphoma so that people are better able to recognise unexplained or persistent symptoms and seek medical advice.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Make Makaton Training Mandatory In Care, Education & Extracurricular Settings Make Makaton Level 1 training compulsory for people working in care, education and extracurricular activities.
label: Department for Education

text: Abolish vehicle excise duty on battery electric vehicles We want the Government to abolish vehicle excise duty on electric vehicles. My car emits 0 co2 and weighs 1345kg. My VED is £200 pa. My friend's petrol car emits 128 g/km co2 and weighs 2080kg. Her VED is £170. I do not know how this can be considered fair.
label: HM Treasury

text: Withdraw from jurisdiction of European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) We believe the ECtHR is outdated and does not look at the rights of both sides, and will overlook the rights of everyone it effects while it blocks dangerous people being deported.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Make It Compulsory for All Antifreeze to Contain Bitterant Make it a legal requirement for all antifreeze products sold in the UK to contain bitterant (such as denatonium benzoate).
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Raise the income tax allowance from £12,570 to £18,000 A previous petition asking to raise income tax allowance to £20,000 was debated in May. The government said this would cost them funding to support hospitals, schools and other public institutions which I think sounds fair. I think raising it to £18,000 will leave the govt funding it still needs.
label: HM Treasury

text: Remove priority need requirements from homelessness legislation. Change legislation regarding provision of accommodation for rough sleepers. Treat rough sleeping as a priority need in itself. We think not being able to go to the toilet or attend to basic personal hygiene is a priority need.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Withdraw from the ECHR and replace with domestic human rights legislation We believe withdrawing from the ECHR is necessary to ensure national security and protect British citizens from harm. The ECHR has repeatedly limited the government's flexibility to enforce robust immigration policies to deport illegal immigrants and criminal foreign nationals swiftly.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Remove requirement to be 10-year seizure & medication free for HGV & PSV license Remove requirement for people diagnosed with epilepsy to be seizure and medications for seizures free for 10 years to hold a licence for group 2 drivers (HGV & PSV). We believe that the individual case should be assessed to see by their medical teams to hold such a licence.
label: Department for Transport

text: Extend Paid Maternity Leave to 18 Months to Support Child Development. We, the undersigned, respectfully petition the Government to extend paid maternity leave until a child reaches 18 months of age, and to provide parents with the opportunity to remain at home with their babies for longer during this critical period of development.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Introduce a contribution-based asylum scheme for residents with 3+ years in UK I want the Government to Introduce a contribution-based asylum route for people living in the UK for 3+ years, including long-pending asylum families, legal entrants who later overstayed, UK-born children and their parents, subject to identity checks, good character and proof of residence.
label: Home Office

text: Legislate to require tech companies to offer parental controls for under 17's We urge the UK Government to require tech companies to offer parental controls for all users under 17, based on agreed standards. These controls should, at a minimum, manage screen time, app use, and content access.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Review the rules on suspending SIA licenses We want the government to review the rules on suspending worker's SIA licenses following an allegation of assault. We believe that licences should not be suspended unless the holder is formally charged with any allegations.
label: Home Office

text: Require fines instead of points for drivers exceeding speed limits by up to 5mp Drivers should be fined instead of given points for exceeding any speed limit by up to 5mph, with the amount being similar to charges for parking violations.
label: Department for Transport

text: Law to allow families to request compulsory assessment when addiction risks life The Government should pass a Substance Abuse and Addiction Act. It should let families, with medical evidence and court oversight, request compulsory assessment when severe addiction risks life, ensure quicker treatment, better integrated services, more safeguards, and lawful early intervention.
label: Home Office

text: Fund every GP to have a dedicated Chronic Pain/Fibromyalgia Practitioner. We want the Government to fund a minimum of one Fibromyalgia pain management practitioner in each GP surgery.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban financial lobbying from groups linked to states facing active ICJ cases Legislate to ban groups with financial links to states facing active litigation at the ICJ from lobbying MPs and All-Party Parliamentary Groups. This includes a ban on MPs and APPGs accepting funded hospitality, travel or other gifts from these lobby groups.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Family parking space badges for children up to 12 and fines for illegitimate use Create a badge system similar to the blue badge that will allow families with children up to 12 years old or pregnant mothers to be the only ones allowed to use parent parking. Introduce fines for individuals who break the rules and park there without a child or who aren't pregnant.
label: Department for Transport

text: Give Coroners Discretion to Restrict Press Access Give coroners discretionary powers to restrict press access when they judge an inquest as sensitive, and where reporting may cause unnecessary harm or distress to bereaved families. This should not prevent transparency of proceedings and an open justice process.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Amend the Nursery Milk Scheme to fund alternatives for children with allergies Allergic toddlers often sit with nothing to drink while peers have free milk unless parents pay a c£307/yr "allergy tax" for safe cartons which can create a large financial penalty or can leave vulnerable toddlers with a nutritional deficit. The scientific consensus now shows plant milks are safe.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Raise the age of consent to 18 with peer exception for 16-17 year olds Set the legal age of consent at 18. Allow a “close-in-age” or “peer” exception: 16–17 year olds can consent only with other 16–17 year olds.
