Make it illegal for any adult (18+) to engage in sexual activity with someone under 18, unless they had an existing sexual relationship from age 16/17.
label: Home Office

text:
Fund extensive support for victims of grooming gangs Fund:
At least 12 months of fully-funded specialist trauma therapy
Access to funded therapeutic retreats
Ring-fenced personal funding (housing, debt, education, etc.)
Oversight by an independent Survivors’ Panel with real power
Automatic, non-means-tested support via a dedicated national fund
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Nationalise all public utilities: water, energy, telecoms, postal and buses We want the government to nationalise all public utilities: water, energy, telecommunications, postal and buses.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Issue guidance on handling specialist disability buggies on public transport Government to issue national guidance on how specialist disability buggies used as essential mobility aids must be handled on public transport, including mandatory staff training and consistent policy across operators. There should be no difference in priority between these aids and wheelchairs.
label: Department for Transport

text: Require galleries segregate artists' sale proceeds, protect them from insolvency We urge Parliament to enact legislation requiring UK art galleries to segregate artists' sale proceeds into separate, protected trust accounts. We think this is essential to prevent commingling, ensure funds are not lost in gallery insolvencies, and safeguard artists' livelihoods.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: End Capital Gains Tax on cryptocurrency gains Capital gains tax is applied to the gains of those that take the chance on gambling their life savings (which may be already taxed) on a very volatile market. We think the UK government needs to understand the impact this is having on the UK crypto market; and abolish taxing people on crypto gains.
label: HM Treasury

text: Introduce scheme for reduced or free public transport fares I believe that there should be a government scheme to make public transport fees reduced or free across the country, in addition to the existing bus fare cap.
label: Department for Transport

text: Classify beverages at or below 0.5% ABV as alcohol free Change the law so any drink at 0.5% ABV or below can be labelled “alcohol-free”. At 0.05%, the UK’s limit is the strictest in the world. The Government has consulted twice and committed to it. Stop consulting and act.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ensure every UK Armed Forces veteran funeral is offered Armed Forces recognition We ask the UK Government to create a national framework so every UK Armed Forces veteran funeral is offered recognition from the Armed Forces community, such as a standard bearer or veteran representative.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Establish a 'Less Scroll, More Soul' Bank Holiday: An Offline 'In-Community' Day We think the country urgently needs a breather: an annual reset for our overwhelmed, disconnected lives. A day to log off, look up & reconnect. A government-backed opportunity to build awareness of the grip tech has on us & remind us of what matters in a healthy society: people, place and presence.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Ban all types of wire snares We think snares are cruel, outdated traps that cause immense suffering to wildlife and pets. They can be indiscriminate, sometimes catching non-target animals, including protected species. We think the government should ban the use, sale and possession of animal snares to prevent unnecessary harm.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require key worker housing eligibility to include frontline charity workers We believe key worker housing scheme providers should be required to include frontline charity workers in eligibility criteria for key worker housing schemes, in the same way as certain essential public sector workers.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Do not give £50m of aid for Syrians We do not think that the £50m of international aid for Syrians (announced recently) should be provided. We think it should be spent on the UK instead.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Make the state pension the same as the minimum wage for a full time worker Make the state pension the same as the minimum wage for a full time worker.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Tax banks to recoup the £23bn they lost taxpayers in the banking crisis To recoup the outstanding/lost £23bn from the financial/banking sector, following the bailout during the financial crisis. We think this should be recouped through emergency taxation on banks, and that this could be used to fill what has been described as £22bn black hole in public finances.
label: HM Treasury

text: Put British companies first: only tender government contracts to UK companies We think the UK Government should ensure all UK government contracts go to UK companies. We think all governments should put their own people first and this will boost the UK economy in lots of ways.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Change the earliest days of ILR application from 28days to 180days before 5years I want the government to change the ILR application from 28days to 180 days before 5years. It is a great privilege to live here permanently. Applying earlier helps people in their plans and help to attain permanent stay before visas expire and reduces the tension of applying 28days before 5years.
label: Home Office

text: Fund research into the causes, treatment & medical training for Fibromyalgia I would like the Government to invest in research into the causes of Fibromyalgia, and fund better training for all health professionals who may encounter sufferers and a better care pathway that is more effective and accessible to Fibromyalgia patients.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Apologise and hold inquiry into ESN schools in the 1950s to 1980s From the 1950s through to the 1980s, thousands of children were labelled “educationally subnormal” and removed from mainstream education. Many of these children were misclassified due to flawed testing, cultural bias, racism, poverty, and low expectations within the education system.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Require government departments to publish annual reports on digital projects Make it law that all government departments publish annual reports on digital projects. These must explain why each website, app or campaign exists and what it costs. Named senior officials must be accountable. No project should go live unless it meets government accessibility standards.
label: Cabinet Office

text:
Give legal gender recognition to non-binary+ people What I want the Government/Parliament to do:
 - For nonbinary+ people to have Legal Gender Recognition (for people to be able to put N/A or none of the above or X etc on legal documents)
- Marriage/Civil Partnership labels to be other than bride or groom
- Legal gender-neutral titles (such as Mx)
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Allocate share of per-pupil education funding to support home-educated children We believe home-ed families should receive a share of per-pupil funding to support resources as home-ed children are entitled to a suitable education, yet families currently receive no direct funding, despite the state saving thousands of pounds when a child is educated outside the school system.
label: Department for Education

text: Expand menstrual health education & early screening for conditions I feel too many people suffer in silence from conditions like endometriosis and adenomyosis without knowing what they are. Some data suggests that in the UK 1 in 10 women are affected by endometriosis, it takes on average 8 yrs 10 months to diagnose, and only 50% of 16-24-yr-olds know what it is.
label: Department for Education

text: Require employers to notify all interviewees of their hiring outcome The law does not legally require employers to inform interviewees if they are unsuccessful. This "ghosting" can cause stress for job seekers. We call on the Government to require employers to notify all job candidates of their application’s outcome after an interview, even if it is automated.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Cut FLR(FP) waiting times for people with British children or British partners Reduce delays in Further Leave to Remain (Family and Private life) applications for parents of British children and partners. Some families have waited over 12 months despite paying £5,000+ including for the Immigration Health Surcharge and usually having no access to public funds.
label: Home Office

text: Create national "Low Demand School Hubs" for students with EBSA, ODD, and PDA The Government should provide funding and a national framework for "Low-Demand School Hubs" specifically designed for students with Emotional Based School Avoidance (EBSA), Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD), and Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA).
label: Department for Education

text: Fully fund tuition fees for all healthcare-related degree programs Fund healthcare tuition fees and reintroduce living grants. The NHS spends £2bn+ on agency staff while students work thousands of clinical hours for free. We think we must remove debt barriers & placement poverty to stop dropouts, end the staffing crisis, and ensure the NHS is staffed for the future
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Legislate to reduce motorcycle noise to lower, standardised levels Bring in a law requiring all motorcycles to have their exhaust noise silenced to standardised levels, without any exceptions for existing machines.
label: Department for Transport

text: Allow conjugal visits with spouses for prisoners incarcerated for 3+ years Allow prisoners who have been on incarcerated for 3+ years to have conjugal visits with their spouse. They must be married to do so. You can’t change partner with whom you choose as your person to have the conjugal visit with.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Make it a criminal offence to mislead or lie in public office We think misleading or telling lies to the public in public office should be criminalised. Public servants should function at a higher standard, and we think parliamentary standards alone haven't solved issues.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Provide grants of £25,000 for independent tackle shops. We urge the Government to make £25,000 digital transformation and viability grants available. We believe this support would protect the heritage and sustainability of these shops as vital cultural and community assets.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Mandate collection & publication of criminals’ immigration status & nationality We call on the Government to mandate the collection and publication of all crime statistics broken down by immigration status and nationality for the past 5 years, including data on illegal immigrants and asylum seekers, in the interest of transparency and public accountability.
label: Home Office

text: Mandate wheelchair-accessible emergency safety zones in motorway barriers We ask the Government to require National Highways to install wheelchair‑accessible emergency gates, ramps or lowered alcoves along motorway barriers, especially where no hard shoulder exists. The Department for Transport should update the DMRB to ensure disabled drivers can also reach safety.
label: Department for Transport

text: Prohibit HMO licences being granted for properties near schools So that migrants cannot be housed in HMOs located near or next to schools.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Fund more research into gynaecological health from current 2.4% Only 2.4% of public research funding goes to women’s gynaecological health and childbirth. I would like to see this massively increased and much more importance placed onto it.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Capital punishment for those convicted of terrorism, murder or intentional harm We want the government to reinstate capital punishment for those who have committed terror offences, murder or intentional harm.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Review the family court system for removing children from their guardian We urge the Government to launch a review of the family court system in England and Wales, and the guidance on when a child should be removed from there guardian.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: UK to join the joint statement on ECHR interpretation We believe delay on legal reform risks the same failings seen in the ECHR’s Swiss climate ruling. Nine democracies have published a statement supporting ECHR interpretive reform. We think the UK should act now to protect national law from judicial overreach and ensure democratic accountability.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Review and publish government guidelines/procedures for state visit invitations The Government should review and publish any government guidelines and procedures relating to the issuing and revoking of invitations for state visits.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Create a public holiday in November to honour and remember our veterans We feel that a 2-minute silence on 11/11 at the 11th hour to honour those who fell in the line of duty (making the ultimate sacrifice for our country) and those who put their lives on the line every day still is not enough.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Amend Health and Safety at Work Act to include the provision of defibrillators This petition calls on the UK Government to review and update the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 to explicitly include the provision and consideration of automated external defibrillators (AEDs) within workplace and public health and safety requirements.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Make it illegal to fire any kind of gun within 15 miles of a residential home We call on the Government to make it illegal to fire a gun of any kind unless you are police within 15 miles of anyone’s residential home.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Hold a referendum on Reintroducing the Rwanda scheme. We think the current government are failing to deal with illegal immigration effectively. We think the Rwanda scheme should have a chance to work. The laws are in place and we think Rwanda are happy to take immigrants while they await processing.
label: Home Office

text: Require licenses to use an electric bike or electric scooter Make Licenses mandatory for all users of E-Bikes or E-Scooters so they cannot ride them on the road if they don’t have a license.
label: Department for Transport

text: Ban all charging for the use of public lavatories. We call on the Government to amend the Public Health Act 1936 to forbid any local authorities from charging for use of public lavatories or passing ownership to anybody which does not provide free public lavatories.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund free rail travel for Armed Forces veterans and a nominated companion We ask the Government to fund free rail travel for everyone eligible for a Veterans Railcard, replacing the one-third discount. We also ask that a veteran's nominated companion, such as a spouse or partner, be entitled to free rail travel when travelling with the veteran.
label: Department for Transport

text: Add Pet Heat Safety Warnings to UK Met Office Extreme Heat Alerts We call on the Government to work with the Met Office to include pet heat safety advice in all official extreme heat warnings. This should include guidance on avoiding dog walks in dangerous temperatures, hot pavements, preventing heatstroke and when to seek urgent veterinary care.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Abandon the Chagos deal We call for the Chagos deal to be scrapped in its entirety, and for the United Kingdom to retain its current sovereignty over that territory.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Require background checks before customers can purchase an animal Before anyone buys a pet from a pet shop or breeder, they should be checked if they have all necessities beforehand and have the correct funds + household to look after the pet. They should also make sure that the person doesn’t live with any abusive people so the animal isn’t at risk.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Amend divorce law to protect survivors of spousal sexual abuse Change the law so that in cases where one spouse has been convicted of rape or other serious sexual offence against the other, the survivor is legally safeguarded from any financial claims made by their abuser in divorce proceedings.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Establish a workplace wellbeing rating and require workplaces to disclose them We call for mandatory workplace culture and wellbeing ratings to be established, similar to food hygiene ratings, and for each employer to publicly disclose them. We think that if we require food safety transparency, why not mental health?
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Ban single-use expanded polypropylene packaging In October 2023 the government banned expanded polystyrene cups and take away food boxes. Some manufacturers have now started using expanded polypropylene boxes.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Ban all mid-terrace houses from becoming HMOs We urge the Government to ban all mid-terrace houses from being converted into Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs).
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Reinstate full HS2 route to Manchester & Leeds to combat regional inequality. I want the Government to extend the HS2 project from London to Manchester and Leeds. The Government should also improve rail infrastructure in the North. I believe this is vital to boost connectivity, bridge rural-urban divides, reduce poverty, and future-proof the rail network.
label: Department for Transport

text: Legally require ministers to seek expert advice from the UN Human Rights Office Legally require ministers to seek and consider advice from relevant human rights experts at the UN Human Rights Office before introducing significant counter-terrorism measures, expanding counter-terrorism powers, or proscribing organisations under UK law.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Stop the move to mandatory weekly food waste collection I want the Government to reverse its decision to mandate weekly food waste bin collections.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: New Law on adoption and muzzling of greyhound dogs We call on the Government to introduce a new law to:
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Ban the use and sale of methyl methacrylate in the nail industry Ban the use and sale of methyl methacrylate in the nails/beauty industry. Methyl methacrylate (MMA) has been associated with health issues such as contact dermatitis, asthma, allergies, permanent nail damage and numbness in fingers. We think it poses a risk to public health.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Amend terror law to remove "damage to property" as an element of terrorism We think terrorism law should only be used for serious offences, not to police non-violent actions and protest. We think acts that only involve damage to property in ways that are not directly harmful to human health or life should not be governed by terrorism law.
label: Home Office

text: Legislate to upgrade all B class license holders to include the C1 category We urge the Government to pass a law where in the same way people with a B class (car/van 3.5 tonne) driver’s license are automatically entitled to a B+E category (car/van and trailer) license, people with a B class license can be automatically entitled to a C1 (7.5 tonne) license.
label: Department for Transport

text: Reinstate the death penalty for child murderers There is no room in society for child murderers. We call on the Government to introduce legislation to reintroduce the death penalty for those convicted of the deliberate murder of a child.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Raise higher rate tax threshold to £60k, and raise yearly in line with inflation This petition asks the Government to increase the higher rate income tax threshold from £50,270 to £60,000 now and going forwards introduce automatic annual increases to the threshold in line with inflation.
label: HM Treasury

text: Exempt all female hygiene products from tax We think it's unfair that there can be a price difference between male and female hygiene products. Females often have to pay more for hygiene products because they are targeted towards women with pink and purple packaging. We therefore call on the Government to exempt such products from tax.
label: HM Treasury

text: Hold a referendum on planned changes to trial by jury We believe the Government has no right to abolish or restrict trial by jury without a referendum.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Reallocate illegal migrant spending and use money to fund other things Reallocate the billions spent on housing and supporting undocumented or illegal migrants, and instead use that money to fund reductions in council tax and invest in the UK, including housing, the NHS, youth programmes, small businesses, and support for low-income British families.
label: Home Office

text: Ban the use of sound-emitting cat deterrent devices Some children and young adults (and some older adults too) can hear 'ultrasonic' cat deterrents. We think that the noise they emit is loud, uncomfortable, and constant. We think it violates people's right to a quiet enjoyment of their home.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require asylum claims to meet the same evidential standard as other routes We ask the Government to require asylum claims to be assessed against the same standards of verified identity, evidence and background checks as other legal immigration routes, ensuring fixed decision timeframes, enforced removal after failed appeals, and a review of accommodation costs and impact.
label: Home Office

text: Mandate alcohol breathalyser and drug swab tests in House of Commons MPs should be banned from taking part in proceedings if they are found to be under the influence of drugs or alcohol whilst at work. Mandatory drug and alcohol testing is common in many professions. This is important for MPs as they are making decisions that shape the future of the nation.
label: Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

text: Hold Developers More Accountable in New Builds to Help Protect Nature  We believe major property developments must protect existing trees, hedgerows, ponds, meadows, and other natural features, and developers who break planning rules should be held more accountable.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: NHS for Pets Create a system whereby animal owners can access free medical care for their pets and not pay extortionate prices by private practices.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require parliamentary candidates publish five years of tax returns The Government must update election laws, governing who may stand as a UK parliamentary candidate. The new requirement is as follows; to have their name included on the ballot paper, parliamentary candidates must publish their tax returns from the previous five years, or be disqualified.
label: Cabinet Office

text:
Introduce new written Bill of Rights, allow citizens to call binding referendums The new Bill must state:
Any issue can be forced into a National Referendum (NR) if citizens get enough signatures
1 or more NR must be held each year
No issue is immune to change by NR
Parliament must obey NR decisions within 2 years or call general election
The Bill can only be changed by NR
label: Cabinet Office

text: Ban Scissor Traps for Moles and impose fines Ban the use of scissor traps for moles and impose a large fine on anybody using, distributing, or buying scissor traps in the UK. The Government and Parliament need to treat using scissor traps as a serious offence against animal rights and animal cruelty.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Remove all alcohol venues from the UK Parliament We believe all alcohol venues in Parliament should be immediately removed. We believe Parliament should be a serious place of work where important issues are addressed, like other workplaces, alcohol consumption should be limited and there should be no sale of alcohol in the UK Parliament.
label: Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

text: Reduce excise duty on cigars and pipe tobacco Decrease the excise duties on cigars and pipe tobacco to be in line with current minimum EU duties. Use of these products seems much lower than vaping and cigarettes and for that reason I think they should be taxed less, as I think they are unappealing to younger audiences.
label: HM Treasury

text: Ban greyhound racing in England We believe greyhounds deserve protection, not exploitation for profit. Greyhound racing causes injuries and deaths to dogs every year. Wales has committed to banning the sport and Scotland is ending it.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Increase national single-carriageway, dual-carriageway & motorway speed limits Increase respective speed limits on appropriately-engineered single carriageway, dual carriageway & motorway class roads to 70mph, 80mph & 90mph respectively.
label: Department for Transport

text: Hold a referendum on the future funding model of the BBC The BBC is a public corporation established by Royal Charter, operating as a public service broadcaster funded primarily by the UK television licence fee. It is independent of the government but accountable to the public. As such the public should have final say on any new funding model.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Create a formal appeal process for Coroners’ inquests We want the Government to introduce legislation creating a clear right of appeal against Coroners’ inquest conclusions, allowing families to challenge findings where there are errors of law, procedure, or failures to properly examine state involvement or evidence.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Require public service broadcasters to give proportional coverage to all parties We urge the Government to pass a law which requires all public service broadcasters, including the BBC, to be required to give media coverage to political parties that is proportional to the number of MPs they have in the House of Commons.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Impose sanctions on Israel unless Gaza blockade is lifted In May, the World Food Programme said that 470,000 people in Gaza were facing catastrophic hunger. The blockade needs lifting so food and water can reach Gaza.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Fund free prescriptions for people living with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) We want the Government to add IBD, including Crohn’s and colitis, to the list of conditions eligible for free prescriptions in England, and to fund this. People with IBD need lifelong medication. We think this change would ensure fair access to essential treatment and reduce financial pressure.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Retain Disabled Students’ Allowance (DSA) assistive technology funding We’re calling on the Government to protect Disabled Students’ Allowance (DSA) assistive technology funding and reject plans to restrict support to “exceptional circumstances” only. These changes risk widening inequality and must be evidence-based, not cost-driven.
label: Department for Education

text: Stop all legal immigration to UK for workers earning less than £80000 a year Suspend all immigration to UK for at least 5 years for workers earning £80,000 or less to reduce pressures on the economy, social housing, the NHS, schools and other resources.
label: Home Office

text: Introduce the care home fees cap for personal care costs A care cap was due to come into force in England in October 2025. It would have meant that no one would have to pay more than £86,000 in England for their personal care. This was postponed and finally abolished by the previous and current governments. I feel strongly that it should be implemented.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban vaping in public places Ban vaping in public places, especially public houses and beer gardens, to help protect people with asthma, COPD, sarcoidosis an other lung diagnosis. I don't see why people vaping have the right to pollute my air space.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund increased access to menstrual products to address period poverty  The government should expand free menstrual product programs beyond schools and colleges to include community centres, food banks, and other public spaces. We believe menstruation has effectively become a luxury that countless individuals simply cannot afford.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Provide funding for public outdoor 10m diving platforms Provide funding to build outdoor high-diving platforms to provide safe legal sites for diving, reduce trespass, and promote outdoor sport. Inspired by Europe, these facilities could support recreation, training, events, and community wellbeing.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Lift Sanctions on Iran and Restore Trade Relations We call on the UK Government to lift sanctions on Iran, work with international partners, including the European Union, to reverse the snapback of JCPOA-related measures, return to the nuclear deal, and restore lawful trade and economic relations with Iran.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Ban councils from using third party litter enforcement companies Councils often employ third party companies to hand out fines for the dropping of litter. These companies are driven by profit. We want this practice to end and councils must employ their own enforcement employees.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Make it illegal to keep or sell social animals like guinea pigs alone We call on the government to introduce legislation preventing pet shops and breeders from rehoming social animals, such as guinea pigs or rabbits, without a suitable companion. Owners must keep these species in compatible pairs or groups, with exceptions only for bereavement or planned re-pairing.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: National measures to prevent people leaving dog faeces on the streets. We are calling for the Government to require schools to educate children, from infant school age, on the dangers of owners not picking up their dog's faeces. We also want the Government to increase default fines and give more funding for local authority enforcement.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Review sentences and punishments for sexual assault and rape cases Introduce stronger sentences for sexual assault and rape on par with manslaughter and murder. Review training for investigators to ensure better survivor support and a justice system that ensures accountability, deterrence, and long-term public protection.
label: Home Office

text: Review how the Home Office deals with False Domestic Abuse Claims to get ILR A BBC investigation raised concerns that the UK Home Office have granted settled status to migrants based on insufficient evidence when applicants claimed they had experienced domestic abuse.
label: Home Office

text: Introduce regulations governing media reporting of abuse of women and girls Abuse, assault and harassment of women and girls is a serious issue, one that has been described as a "national emergency". One in 12 females in the UK are victims, and a staggering 97% of women aged 18-24 have been sexually harassed. Yet media reporting of the issue normalises and trivialises it.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Impose criminal penalties on companies advertising Ghost Jobs The government should impose criminal penalties on companies advertising ghost jobs. I have applied for roles that were never real, wasting time, effort, and money. This is deeply unfair when so many of us genuinely want jobs. Graduates are tired of applying and we are getting nowhere.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Reduce Fuel Duty to below £0.20 per litre The Government should fund a reduction in fuel duty to below £0.20 per litre. This could help young people become more mobile – particularly in areas where public transport is insufficient- allowing them to get jobs further away and access recreational activities.
label: HM Treasury

text: Keep Sex Offenders on license and the register for life Keep all registered sex offenders on license and on the register for life. We believe it will help protect survivors and potential victims.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Repeal the Investigatory Powers Act The Investigatory Powers Act gives the government additional powers to access encrypted data, which we feel threatens privacy and security. This petition calls for the repeal of this Act, as we believe it undermines individual freedom, risks data security, and could set a dangerous global precedent.
label: Home Office

text: End public funding for faith schools Stop taxpayer funding for faith-based schools. Instead, ensure all state schools are secular, where we believe children from all backgrounds can learn together without division by religion or culture.
label: Department for Education

text: Ban hormone and endocrine disruptors from all menstrual products Introduce a law making it illegal for any period products—including pads, tampons, and reusable wear—to contain hormone disruptors. The government must mandate independent safety testing and set legal toxic limits to protect highly absorbent vaginal tissue from exposure.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Negotiate exemption to the 90/180 Schengen travel rule for professional drivers We call on the UK Government to negotiate an exemption from the Schengen 90 days in any 180-day period rule for UK professional drivers, including HGV (lorry) drivers and PCV (coach and bus) drivers, when travelling for work purposes.
label: Department for Transport

text: Waive UK visa fees for overseas teachers coming to work in the UK We believe the UK’s education sector is in the grip of a significant recruitment and retention crisis. Not all students have the subject specialists they deserve. We believe overseas teachers play a vital role in bolstering our falling teacher numbers; yet may be expected to pay to do so.
label: Home Office

text: Mandate specialist input for neurological NHS continuing care assessment panels Mandate clinical specialists such as neurologists on assessment panels for complex neurological conditions. We believe many with complex neurological conditions (Posterior cortical atrophy, Parkinson's, MND, atypical dementias) can face systemic refusal of NHS Continuing Healthcare (CHC) funding.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ban LGBTQIA+ conversion therapy Ban the use of conversion therapy intended to change the sexual orientation or gender identity of members of the LGBTQIA+ community. We believe all forms of “conversion therapy” disrespect the equal moral value of LGBTQIA+ people and violate specific protected areas of liberty and equality.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Fund programme to humanely relocate seals found in rivers Through no fault of their own Seals appear to be entering UK rivers more and more, which can impact fish stocks there.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Extend the Adoption Support Fund to include adults up to 25 without an EHCP The adoption and special guardianship support fund (ASGSF) is currently available for children and young people up to and including the age of 21, or 25 with an education, health and care plan (EHCP). We think it should be eligible for all adopted adults up to the age of 25.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require trauma-informed guidance and training in rape investigations and trials Require police and prosecutors to have more extensive trauma training to help them consider evidence in rape cases in a trauma-informed way. Include the psychological, physical and functional impact of the offence. Provide guidance to juries on the impact of trauma.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Review CMS to be calculated on both parents’ income, including investments Currently the non resident pays the resident parent. We think both parents’ income, including investments, and income, claimed from self-assessments, should be included in the child maintenance calculation, with the higher earning parent contributing more towards the costs of raising the child(ren).
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Mandate all teachers in mainstream schools receive SEN & mental health training Fund mandatory SEN and mental health training for all teachers. We are concerned that many children with special educational needs are being failed, as mainstream staff often lack the skills and qualifications to support pupils with social, emotional and mental health needs.
label: Department for Education

text: Increase Government funding for children’s homes & the young people living there We would like the government to increase funding for children’s homes to ensure that the young people have the support they need to pay for things such as their food shopping, clothes, toiletries, phone bill, and anything else they need.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Mandate funding of active travel provision as part of any transport projects In light of the Chancellor's recent announcement of funding for transport infrastructure, we call for new legislation mandating funding for active travel provision alongside funding for transport projects, built at the same time as any transport improvements or construction.
label: Department for Transport

text: Exempt medically discharged Commonwealth service people from immigration control I would like automatic, continued exemption from UK immigration control for all Commonwealth citizens serving in the UK's armed forces, when they're medically discharged. I've personally experienced challenges of medical discharge from the Royal Navy, and feel compelled to advocate for change.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Automatic Deputyship to parents once child with disabilities turns 18 We urge the Government to automatically grant Deputyship to parents of children with disabilities once they reach adulthood. We think this change would eliminate complex legal processes, ensuring continued care, while reducing financial and emotional burdens on families.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Funding for ASD and ADHD assessments for children within 18 months of referral We think funding should be provided so children have ASD (Autism) and ADHD assessments completed within 18 months from initial referral.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Compulsory immediate prison sentences for people convicted of rape I want the government to stop suspended sentences and community service being given as punishment for rape. For victims, the effects of rape can be life long and can’t be erased.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Increase penalties for motor vehicles that exceed legal noise pollution levels We ask the UK Government to introduce stricter penalties for excessive vehicle noise, including modified loud exhaust systems and unnecessary use of car horns during night hours. Excessive noise from vehicles is a growing problem in many communities across the UK.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review how to help keep children with families, with funding for early support We think children should stay safely with their families whenever possible. The government must review how to do this, fund better early help, respite, and practical support, reduce any unnecessary court removals, and ensure decisions to remove children are only a last resort with full transparency.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Update UK e-bike laws: allow 750W, 20mph limit and throttle use. Modernise e-bike law by raising motor power to 750W, increasing assisted speed to 20mph and permitting throttle control. Update regulations so e-bikes remain legally classed as bicycles, without licences or insurance, while keeping safety rules and existing road standards.
label: Department for Transport

text: Allow unpaid trainee teachers on placement to access 30 hours of free childcare Many trainee teachers work 40+ hours per week on placement; cannot access 30 hours of free childcare per week. Trainee teachers who work on full-time placements can be excluded from vital support, forcing families to struggle and careers to stall.
label: Department for Education

text: Provide Fully Funded Armed Security for Jewish Public Buildings  We call upon His Majesty’s Government to urgently provide funding for armed security (police or military presence) at Jewish public buildings – including schools, synagogues, and community centres.
label: Home Office

text: Increase funding for mediation and arbitration in family courts We urge the Government to increase funding for non-adversarial solutions such as mediation and arbitration. We hope that this may result in more transparency, fair processes, and a shift towards shared parenting, ensuring children’s best interests are the primary focus.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Remove age verification introduced by online safety act We call on the Government to remove the age verification requirements introduced by the Online Safety Act, as we believe that parents should be in charge not the companies as it can be wrong and restrict the wrong people!
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Children of sex offenders/domestic abusers to change name w/out parental consent I want children of sex offenders or domestic abusers to have the ability to change their name even if they are under 16. This is to prevent them from being identified as the child of a sex offender, as they may be viewed differently in social settings.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Halt the EU Reset Agreement We think the recent EU reset agreement undermines the democratic will of the British people and the principles of national sovereignty. We think the Government is breaching sovereignty of the UK Parliament.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Review laws allowing perpetrators of domestic abuse legal access to children I would like the government to conduct a comprehensive review of existing laws and amend them so as to close any loopholes that may allow perpetrators to manipulate legal systems and gain access to children and previous victims of domestic violence.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Require all schools to let pupils wear their own clothes on Monday and Friday I urge the Government to require all schools to let pupils wear their own clothes on Monday and Friday, as I believe having to wear a uniform all week is uncomfortable and annoying for students. I believe this could make students happier and put more effort into their work.
label: Department for Education

text: Require licences to use air rifles  I would like for all air rifle owners to have to have a licence to use their weapon even if they are under 12foot/pound.
label: Home Office

text: Entitlement to bereavement leave after baby loss in first 24 weeks of pregnancy. If a miscarriage happens in the first 24 weeks of pregnancy, there's currently no entitlement to statutory maternity, paternity or parental bereavement leave, I believe people should be entitled to this regardless of when the baby was lost.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Use new questions on local election ballot papers to trigger a general election Questions should be added to local election ballot papers in England about how the current government in charge of the country is doing Eg. Q1. Is the current Government following their manifesto they were elected on (A) YES or NO. Q2. Do you have confidence in the current government (A) YES or NO
label: Cabinet Office

text:
Lower the age for Cervical Screenings from 25 to 21 Lower the NHS cervical screening starting age from 25 to 21, a change that we believe could save numerous lives and spare families from devastating loss.
The NHS currently recommends cervical screening starting at the age of 25. However, some countries begin screening at 21.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund free NHS prescriptions for students and under-25s in England Extend free NHS prescriptions in England to students and everyone under 25, recognising the financial vulnerability of young people and bringing England closer in line with the rest of the UK.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Cap car insurance premiums for under-21s Car insurance costs for many drivers under 21 in the UK have become excessive, exclusionary, and unsafe. Basic insurance quotes for young drivers aged 17-20 can be between £3,000-£5,000 or more per year, making legal driving unaffordable for many despite holding a valid driving licence.
label: Department for Transport

text: Do not include partner's income in calculation of disabled people's UC claims We want the government to completely remove the policy that stops disabled people who are living with/married to their partners from receiving their out-of-work benefits. The claimant's income must not include the partner. We believe this is dangerous and puts people at risk of financial abuse.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Seek to rejoin EU single market I would like the UK Government to start discussions with the European Union to seek to rejoin the EU Single Market and to make rejoining the EU Single Market a priority for the UK Government, and to aim rejoining the Single Market within 12 months.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Child against parent violence to be recognised as domestic abuse & more support I want the Domestic Abuse Act to be amended to recognise that child against parent violence by under 16’s is still a form of domestic violence.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Review diagnosis of blood cancer in young people Young people with leukaemia are often misdiagnosed as symptoms are mistaken for more common illnesses, and cancer is considered unlikely. The Government should review NHS guidance and training for healthcare professionals and access to blood tests when blood cancer is suspected.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review Existing and Proposed Low Traffic Neighbourhood (LTN) Schemes Conduct an independent review of existing and planned LTNs to assess their impact on congestion, emissions, local businesses and all residents. Require transparent consultation, proper impact assessments and consideration of alternative safety measures before further schemes are approved.
label: Department for Transport

text: Require employers have monthly menstrual 1-3 day leave policy We want the government to require workforces to allow women to have 1-3 days leave per month (outside of holiday and sick leave) during their menstrual phase.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Introduce stand alone law protecting absolute right to free speech Currently the UK protects freedom of expression under Article 10 of the ECHR through the Human Rights Act, but this right is not absolute and can be limited by law. We think this should be changed so the UK has a defined law on free speech which is not based on the HRA, but is a stand alone law.
label: Home Office

text: Continue to support fostering for looked after children in compulsory education Change fostering regulations so children remain fully supported until the end of year 13. We think current arrangements can force independence on their 18th birthday, and that children born early in the academic year are disadvantaged & discriminated against compared to peers born later in the year.
label: Department for Education

text: Restrict free access to public services to UK citizens only We urge the Government to restrict free access to public services, eg NHS and education, to UK citizens only. We believe illegal migration will always be an issue due to taxpayer-funded public services. By changing this, we believe we will lose appeal to asylum seekers.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require all nursing and care homes have to have air conditioning We want the government to make it law that air conditioning must be installed in all nursing and care homes. With climate change and temperatures increasing, we feel we need to ensure the vulnerable are not left in uncomfortable, hot rooms.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require and fund all serving Police Dogs to have adequate protective equipment. UK government to mandate that all police dogs are equipped with appropriate, high-quality protective equipment tailored to their specific roles & environments.  We call for dedicated funding to ensure that all police forces can obtain the necessary protective gear without financial constraints.
label: Home Office

text: Ban people from pulling out last minute in social housing exchanges When doing a house exchange with someone, one person might be allowed to change their mind at right up until moving day. This should not be allowed, people are packing, changing schools, etc., and then other person pulls out. Once papers are signed is when there is no changing minds about the swap.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Pass lifetime office bans for MPs & Lords who are guilty of financial misconduct Pass a law so MPs who are found guilty of financial misconduct under the law or in accordance with the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards and the Committee on Standards.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Require fireworks to be sold only through the fire service with registration Require consumer fireworks to be sold only through the fire service, with purchasers registering in advance using valid photo ID. Profits from these sales should go towards support for firefighters and their families.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Create a scheme for refugees from Palestine and Israel to come to the UK We wish for the innocent people suffering from the Palestine and Israel conflict to be able to seek refuge in the UK to protect their rights, such as that to safety. We wish for an acknowledgement for their safety as victims of conflict.
label: Home Office

text: Stop breed-specific legislation and euthanising banned dogs. We want to put a stop to banning dog breeds. We think only owners should be held accountable for their dogs. We do not want dogs to be euthanised. We think it is up to the owner to get training for their dog and take proper care of it.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Call a vote of no confidence in the Government We want a vote of no confidence in the Labour Government and then an immediate General Election if they lose.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Fund free self-defence classes for young girls We would like to see funding to help young girls learn to defend themselves in local council/community spaces. Classes could be once or twice a week.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Nationwide vote to decide London's mayor London is the capital city of our great nation, we believe there should be a nationwide vote for who runs it, as what happens in London, has a knock on effect for the rest of the country.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Amend standing orders: give right of reply to any MP/party mentioned in Commons Amend the standing orders to give an automatic immediate right of reply to any MP or any party mentioned in any statement, question or answer in the House. We think this will deter MPs and Ministers from using parliamentary business to attack opponents.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Ban mid-contract price hikes on mobile phones and home broadband A contract is a contract so how can it be right that greedy companies can put prices up mid term? It needs looking at as we believe this surely shouldn't be legal.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Require cemeteries to give more rights to family members to erect a headstone We think family members should be able to give a loved one a headstone, including where they are not the owners of the plot. At the moment they may not be able to unless certain circumstances are met.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Require non-smartphone alternatives for real word services provided on apps Many companies are using apps to fulfil physical services. For example, parking payment, etc. Some of these apps do not have a physical alternative.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Require shops to give away same-day expiring food before shop closing I want the Government to introduce a policy requiring all supermarkets and food retailers to give away food items that expire on the same day, free of charge, starting at least 1.5 hours before store closing. We think this should be a national standard.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Delay introducing Making Tax Digital until more support for the Self-Employed We ask the Government to delay Making Tax Digital for the self-employed until free software is provided, clear public guidance is given, and fair exemptions are in place for those with low income, poor digital access, or limited IT skills.
label: HM Treasury

text: Fund an information campaign for GPs on the 2 prostate cancer referral routes We want the Government to fund an NHS information campaign that raises awareness amongst GPs and instructs them to tell patients of suspected prostate cancer about the two referral routes (NICE & PCRMP routes).
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review protection for survivors of post-separation domestic abuse Review protection for domestic abuse survivors awaiting court proceedings. This should include cases of post separation abuse, indirect & direct online harassment and abuse, coercive control, and improved safeguarding restrictions for individuals awaiting trial for serious domestic abuse offences.
label: Home Office

text: Legislate to allow a public vote on MPs' pay rises Legislate for a public vote on whether MPs should receive a pay rise. Pay rises in employment are usually based on achievements in work that are paid for by the employer – in this case the public. As employers (the public) we believe we have the right to deem if it's necessary for a pay rise or not.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Legislate to require all invoices to be paid within 21 days of receipt Pass a law which requires all UK and foreign businesses, local authorities and government institutions to pay all invoices within 21 days of receipt in the UK.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Fund cancer immunotherapy treatments beyond 2 years for everyone We ask the Government to fund cancer immunotherapy beyond 2 years for all patients. We believe treatment should be based on medical need and effectiveness, not time limits. This could improve survival, fairness, and quality of life for people living with cancer.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Decriminalise and legalise Magic Mushrooms Decriminalise and legalise the consumption, picking and purchasing of psychoactive mushrooms such as liberty caps and gold caps. Not only should people have the right to these important mushrooms, but we think it would also reduce the amount of money going to violent drug gangs.
label: Home Office

text: Establish a Legally Managed & Owned HSE-Registered Electrical Safety Scheme Require all electrical scheme operators to function under Health and Safety Executive (HSE) legal oversight. The scheme should be called Electrical Safe, you could see Electrical Safe NICEIC or NAPIT, for example.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: CPR training to be mandatory for all employees in the workplace As a registered nurse, the knowledge and skills of Basic Life Support are taught throughout our training. However, I have seen how most of the general public do not have the knowledge or confidence to deal with a life threatening situation.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Minimum pay of £15/hour for Care Assistants in the private sector and care homes Long hours with little pay. We are Carers, nurses, advisors, friends, family. We endure heartache when your loved one's pass but we have to be brave and carry on. We think minimum wage is not good enough and we need higher rates of pay.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reinstate the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) to support farmers and nature Reinstate the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) to help farmers transition to regenerative agriculture, improve soil health, protect biodiversity, and strengthen UK food security. We believe that this scheme for sustainable farming and nature recovery was cut without warning, putting this at risk.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Offer asylum for Transgender, Non-binary, & Intersex US Citizens & use diplomacy We believe that beginning with Executive Order 14168, the US is targeting transgender, non-binary, and intersex Americans. We do not agree with these actions, and are concerned they could escalate.
label: Home Office

text: Urge the Spanish government to discourage octopus farms It has been reported that in Spain, there have been attempts to establish a commercial octopus farm. We are concerned this could give octopuses lives of misery and we would like the government to apply pressure to the Spanish government to prevent octopus farms from being created.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Ban the sale and hiring of e-scooters across the country by 2028 We would like the Government to ban the purchase & hiring of e-scooters throughout the country. We believe e-scooters are dangerous for both the riders & road users. Hireable e-scooters are a problem, as they can be used and then discarded in roadways, pathways & sometimes on people's properties.
label: Department for Transport

text: Abolish seasonal clock changes & keep the UK on a fixed time all year-round Pass a law to end the practice of seasonal clock changes and commit to a stable, consistent time that does not changes with the seasons. The Government should adopt a permanent, fixed time year-round, either GMT or BST, and scrap the twice-yearly seasonal clock change.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Require councils to review social housing tenancies People are being left without support, while some social housing tenants remain in subsidised homes despite earning high incomes or no longer meeting the need criteria.
label: Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

text: Only introduce digital id cards for non-uk nationals We want the government to re-think the idea that IDs for UK nationals could help reduce illegal immigration. We think that if non UK nationals all had to have an ID to confirm residency, then they could be approached to confirm ligitamcy.
label: Home Office

text: Enforce Contact Within 30 Days, Outlaw Parental Alienation, fast track hearings Introduce legislation to require interim contact to be restored 30 days after an application for child arrangements. Criminalise parental alienation and require such hearings to be fast tracked.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Create a national pet health service for veterinary care We call on the government to establish a service to provide free basic and emergency vet care, such as vaccinations and neutering. We think pets improve public health, and some animals are even used as medical aids yet vet costs are rising fast and becoming unaffordable for many.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Implement a ‘Statutory Dependents Pay’ for being off with your sick child I’d like the government to implement a ‘Statutory Dependents Pay’ for parents who have to take time off work if their child is poorly. This could be like ‘sick pay’, but for parents who have to go off work with their sick child. I'd like it to be more consistent than sick pay and start from day 1.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Regulate all mental health Therapists  We want the government to ensure all mental health therapists are qualified and regulated.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Separate Church and State End the role of Established Churches in the United Kingdom and abolish the positions of the Lords Spiritual in the House of Lords.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Require the use of renewable energy only to power the national grid Require the sole use of renewable energy sources to power the national electricity grid so that 100% of electricity generated in the national grid is from renewable energy sources.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Create fund to celebrate 100th anniversary of women fully achieving the vote We call on the Government to create a fund of £10million to help celebrate the 100th anniversary of women achieving the vote on equal terms with men in 1928.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Recognise nonbinary gender identities in law and in official identity documents Make nonbinary gender markers possible on any official document where a gender marker is required, e.g. passport, gender recognition certificate, marriage documents, death certificate.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Ban the use of electronic device loudspeakers in public & require headphone use Ban any use of electronic device loudspeakers in public places, such as using your loudspeaker for phone calls, private conversations, videos, music, social media, etc, to protect others who don’t wish to listen to the content they’re playing.
label: Department for Transport

text: Require health professionals to always inform partners of HIV diagnoses I want the government to create a law to ensure partners of those with HIV are safely informed regardless of patient consent. I believe this would prevent HIV being used as a weapon and stop the spreading of HIV ensuring healthcare professionals manage cases with accountability and care.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require an election if 70% of the government manifesto isn’t delivered Create a law requiring governments to deliver at least 70% of their clear, measurable manifesto pledges within a Parliament. If they fail, a general election must be triggered, with delivery independently verified.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Automatically revoke spousal visas from abusive partners in the UK We call on the Government to create a law that automatically revokes the spousal visa of any person who abuses their partner while on a spousal visa. We believe abusers should not benefit from UK residency. We feel immigration rules must protect victims and not shield abusers.
label: Home Office

text: Keep the LCWRA Universal Credit component for under 22's Keep the Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity (LCWRA) component for under 22's. Why should someone who is 22 and living with cancer be entitled to LCWRA support, where someone who is 20 and living with cancer isn't. We call on the LCWRA component for 18–21-year-olds to remain.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Create a law introducing specific offence of manslaughter by drug supply Create a law introducing specific offence of manslaughter by drug supply. This could address the supply of drugs which cause death by overdose and hold the suppliers responsible for involuntary manslaughter.
label: Home Office

text: Mandate sanitary bins in public loos for those with a colostomy bag It’s necessary to not ostracise people that have a colostomy bag and allow them to use general facilities if disabled toilets are not available. Every toilet for customers in a venue/business and public loos maintained by local authorities should be required to have a sanitary bin.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Require essential services to have phone and face to face options The Government should require essential services, including the NHS, banks, utilities and public bodies keep telephone and in person access. Digital only systems risk excluding older, disabled and low income people who cannot reliably use online services.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Review the driving test booking process, ban resales at inflated prices & bots We believe the Government needs to find a way to reduce the backlog of driving tests. We want the Government to review the process for booking driving tests, ban the resale of tests at inflated prices and the use of automated bots to buy tests.
label: Department for Transport

text: Require schools to allow students to wear skirts Some schools are removing skirts entirely from uniforms, erasing choice under the guise of equality. We think this isn’t inclusion, it’s control. Let’s stand together and demand that this be debated now.
label: Department for Education

text: Revoke Parental Responsibility & Rights from Sexually Abusive Parents Revoke parental responsibility and rights from parents who sexually abuse their children. We need to be our children's voices and protect them at all costs.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban Applied Behaviour Analysis Therapy designed to reduce Autistic Stimming The Government should ban Applied Behaviour Analysis Therapy (“ABA”), for the purpose of reducing soothing “stimming” behaviours in people with autism spectrum disorder.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Introduce compulsory voting I think that the Government should introduce compulsory voting in the UK for general elections.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Ban public transport from operating without working AC when it is 25°C+ Ban public transport from being in operation without working air conditioning on board when outside temperatures reach 25°C. There should also be inspections for compliance with this ban and a website reporting vehicles in operation without fully working air conditioning.
label: Department for Transport

text: Ban the sale and planting of invasive cherry laurel (Prunus laurocerasus) Add cherry laurel to the list of invasive plants banned from sale and planting in the UK. Launch a strategy to tackle the spread of this invasive exotic shrub across our natural environment.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Change the maintanence loan for weekend students to be available Many students cannot study during weekdays due to work or childcare, especially single parents. The Government should reform maintenance loans to support weekend and flexible learners equally. Fair access to funding would help more people enter education and improve their future.
label: Department for Education

text: Ban training generative AI with creative works without artists' consent The government should make it illegal for AI developers to train generative AI models on creative works - such as art, music, writing and film - without the creator's explicit consent. Artists deserve control and fair compensation for the use of their work.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Legalise UK Citizens copyright to their own likeness & bio-data Introduce legislation to grant every UK citizen full ownership of their likeness, including their face, retina, voice and body data to ensure no system or company can replicate or use these without consent.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Make it a criminal offence to enter a domestic dwelling without permission Make it a specific criminal offence for individuals or groups to enter someone's home without the home owner or legal tenant's permission.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Fund and implement A Universal Basic Income (UBI) We believe that we are in an era of economic uncertainty, growing inequality, and job insecurity and it is time for Parliament to introduce a Universal Basic Income (UBI). Some Economists argue, UBI is not just a welfare measure, it is an investment in people, and a foundation for economic security.
label: HM Treasury

text: Remove visa requirements for non-UK spouses of UK citizens to visit the UK We urge the Government to remove visa requirements for non-UK spouses of British citizens when they come to visit the UK, such as for a short stay with family. We feel that the cost of visas for non-UK spouses often outweighs the cost of travel.
label: Home Office

text: Provide free school meals to all school children I would like the Government to fund free and nutritious school meals to all children attending school. I believe that many school meals are expensive and of poor quality. Many students cannot leave school during lunchtime and have to eat what’s being served at school.
label: Department for Education

text: End the Use of Bearskin in the Kings Guard Headgear The Ministry of Defence must find suitable faux-fur alternatives for the King's Guard headgear that fulfil the necessary criteria. Currently, the hats require Black Bear Skin, costing over £2000 each, making them both expensive and ethically questionable.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Reinstate the NI Legacy Act protecting veterans from prosecution Give veterans the same protection from prosecution as given to suspected IRA terrorists by Tony Blair's amnesty.
label: Northern Ireland Office

text: Require a full and independent enquiry before any hospital job cuts We call on the UK Government to immediately halt any existing consultations on hospital job cuts, such as those taking place in Cornwall,  and instead require a full independent enquiry before any hospital job cuts. We believe cuts can undermine patient care and weaken essential support systems.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Limit Lord Mayor Tenure to Two Terms Limit the number of terms an individual may serve as Lord Mayor or Mayor to two terms in any local authority by amending existing local government legislation and requiring councils to update their standing orders accordingly.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Require people who run over cats to stop and to report it, and impose fine We call on the Government to introduce a fine for people who run over cats as Owners have to pay vet bill no fault of their own. We think it’s not right, and think a fine should be introduced even if it’s only a £50 fine
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Fund and require early assessment, treatment and education on severe period pain Fund and require the NHS to assess all severe period pain early, providing faster referrals, diagnostic tests, specialist treatment, and staff training. Expand menstrual health education in schools, including on severe period pain, to help conditions be identified sooner and reduce suffering.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Make Remote Working a Legal Right Where Roles Can Be Performed From Home Grant employees a legal right to work from home where their role can be performed remotely and performance standards are met. Employers must provide clear, evidence-based reasons to refuse, rather than relying on preference or assumption. This right should be enforceable in law.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Commission a strategic review into social work pay, wellbeing and regulation. We call for an independent review of the social work sector to address stagnant pay, outdated mileage rates, and excessive hours. Critically, the review must investigate Social Work England’s fitness to practise timeframes, which leave professionals unable to work for years pending completion.
label: Department for Education

text: Seize all Russia-linked shadow fleet tankers The UK Government should seize all tankers in Russia’s Shadow Fleet – ships that are avoiding international sanctions by transporting oil with false flags, with communications off, without proper insurance, and sometimes in a dangerous state of repair.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Classify affordable housing as critical national infrastructure Classify affordable housing as critical national infrastructure to address the lack of supply of safe, accessible and affordable housing. This single action could allow for long-term investment and planning to provide a fundamental human need: shelter.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Do not fund officers to patrol French beaches for illegal small boat crossings We want the government to stop giving France millions to police their own beaches to reduce illegal small boat crossings.
label: Home Office

text: Mark 30 years of DDA: Make all public buildings flat threshold The disability discrimination act promised disabled people equality of access yet 30 years later still some public buildings, like 10 Downing Street, have steps and visitors may using face portable ramps that we think are embarrassing.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text:
Random Microchip Checks and Harsher Penalties for Abandoning Cats We call on the government to introduce random home microchip checks and harsher penalties for those who abandon cats and kittens.

We think stronger laws and proactive measures would ensure accountability, protect vulnerable animals, and prevent cruelty, ensuring offenders are held responsible.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Introduce new rules for B2B sales of telecommunication contracts We call on the UK Government to introduce an immediate, mandatory 14-day cooling-off period for all business telecommunications contracts sold over the phone. Furthermore, we demand a review of the regulatory oversight and enforcement against predatory sales tactics.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Review legal & social care use of ‘parental alienation’ and impact on families Review cases where ‘parental alienation’ has been used as a reason to place children in foster care or placements, or to provide custody to parent who has been accused of abuse. Ensure that children are heard, and end use of these concepts in courts, criminal investigations & social work practice.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Expand the Great British Energy-funding for solar schools to every school We want the government to invest in solar schools. From the existing scheme, 100 schools have installed solar and 250 schools are expected to save £200 million in energy bills. We want every school to have this opportunity.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Align Plan 2 student loan interest rates with Plan 5 (RPI only). We call on the government to remove the +3% 'real' interest rate from Plan 2 loans and cap interest at RPI, as is the case for students who started after 2023.
label: Department for Education

text: Include the Royal Family, Household & Duchies in the Freedom of Information Act Legislate to bring the Royal Family, the Royal Household, the Duchy of Lancaster, and the Duchy of Cornwall within the scope of the Freedom of Information (FOI) Act 2000. We think this would help to modernise constitutional transparency, safeguard privacy and increase trust in the British Monarchy.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Require employers give employees 3 months sick pay when cancer is diagnosed I want the government to have a policy in place to help all cancer patients financially. I feel that for the first couple of months, cancer patients need to focus on their diagnosis. Having 3 months of full sick pay in place could allow them to focus on what they are dealing with.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Ban councils considering PIP/DLA as income for council tax reduction schemes Stop councils including personal independence payment/DLA as income for council tax reduction schemes.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Make the pensions of former Prime Ministers performance-based I think the government must be held accountable, should deliver upon manifesto pledges and should lead by example. I propose pensions for former PMs be performance-based, starting at basic state pension with extra points awarded for the general state of the country upon retirement from office.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Review how to close the gender health gap and improve women's healthcare I want the government to hold a review into how to close the gender health gap, and prioritise women’s health and wellbeing more both in workplace & personal life. This should consider how women suffering from endometriosis & other conditions affecting women should be given help, support & education
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Do not bring forward the rise in state pension age to 68 The Government must halt any plans for an earlier State Pension age rise to 68.  Data suggests that healthy lifespans are falling. We believe it is unfair to force millions who started work at 16 to work longer despite declining health & Ministers must protect workers, and keep the timeline.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Define anti-Christian hostility & issue guidance for schools, police & business Define “anti-Christian hostility” mirroring the 2026 anti-Muslim hostility definition and appoint a tsar to oversee it effectiveness. Mandate school guidance on bullying, require police to record incidents as anti-Christian hostility hate incidents, and issue guidance for Christian businesses.
label: Department for Education

text: Reverse the decision to abolish the Hereditary Peers The Government and Parliament should reverse their decision to abolish the 92 Hereditary Peers in the House of Lords, and should instead review and dismiss the number of Life Peers that have been appointed by political leaders. We believe these are purely political appointments, not based on merit.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Ban Supermarkets from selling fresh produce in plastic & require it to be loose Bring in legislation (like in France) to ban supermarkets from selling fresh produce in plastic packaging. If it is necessary to have products in packaging, make it paper.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Expel all US diplomatic and military personnel from the UK We urge the UK Government to expel all US diplomatic personnel from all US diplomatic missions in the UK, alongside expelling US military personnel and aircraft from RAF and other UK military bases.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office
