text: Ban AI-generated images in the advertising of beauty and cosmetic products Introduce legislation banning AI-generated or AI-altered images in the advertising of beauty and cosmetic products, requiring realistic, truthful visuals that show real results on real people, to prevent misleading claims, protect consumers, and stop the spread of visual misinformation.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Require NHS to use pulse oximeters accurate for all skin tones Ensure all NHS pulse oximeters are independently tested and certified to be accurate for all skin tones. Update NHS procurement and clinical guidelines so only inclusive devices are used, with a full transition to validated models by the end of 2026.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Compel residential care homes in England to publish their tariff of room charges We urge the Secretary of State to use their powers under the Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014, to compel residential care homes in England to publicly display an itemised tariff of fees for rooms and service charges, very similar to those displayed in hotels.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review the tax affairs of all sitting MPs for public peace of mind Government or Parliament should initiate a review of the finances of all sitting MPs for all years they have sat in office. The review should make sure they were conducting themselves according to the law regarding taxation, including with regards to their assets.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Modernise treason laws to include terrorism and wilful betrayal of the state. Treason legislation to be updated in line with wilful acts against the UK. Modern threats such as domestic terrorism, joining proscribed terrorist organisations acting against the UK, coercion with a hostile state to harm the UK and betrayal of public mandates all to be considered as modern treason.
label: Home Office

text: Require pickup of packaging boxes by companies making repeat deliveries We want the government to pass legislation that requires corporations/companies which deliver to the same addresses on a regular basis (defined as more than twice a month) to pick up and recycle their own packaging.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Ban palm oil I want the importation and use of palm oil to be banned. Palm oil production is one of the leading causes of deforestation.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Abolish the House of Lords We believe the House of Lords should be abolished, and replaced with a elected Senate, which will use Proportional Representation (PR) as its system for electing members.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Review evidence underpinning recent tax reforms affecting independent schooling Commission an independent review of the evidence underpinning tax reforms implemented in 2025 affecting independent schooling: VAT on fees & removal of charitable business-rates relief, including their cumulative effects, assumptions & forecasts, assessed against evidence since reforms took effect.
label: Department for Education

text: Publish assessment of China’s Ethnic Unity Law & transnational repression risks We call on the Government to publish a standalone assessment of whether China’s Ethnic Unity Law increases the risk of transnational repression for UK residents, and for the assessment to provide recommendations on measures to protect those who could be at risk.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Ban AI usage in education by teachers and students To impose a consequence or discouragement for teachers who are using AI to educate, provide feedback and mark students work. Encourage educational lessons on the harms behind AI and when it should be used. Give records to students who are found to be repeatedly using it in their education.
label: Department for Education

text: Launch an inquiry into road maintenance & publish road tax spending We would like the Government to launch an inquiry into awful road conditions and what can be done to make them more reliable in the future. The inquiry should investigate the materials and companies involved in building roads, and finding better solutions, as we feel our roads are not suitable.
label: Department for Transport

text: Ban MPs from accepting any gifts or donations from businesses and individuals Politicians are lawmakers and should be held to the highest standards of integrity. Yet MPs are currently allowed to accept gifts, hospitality, and donations from businesses and individuals. We think that even when declared, this can create a clear conflict of interest and undermine public trust.
label: Cabinet Office

text:
Update Vaccine Damage Payment Scheme to reflect inflation and disability costs
 Increase the Vaccine Damage Payment Scheme (VDPS) payment, last set at £120,000 in 2007, to reflect inflation and the real cost of living with severe vaccine injury, and ensure it is reviewed regularly to remain fair and up to date.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Require child maintenance payments to increase by inflation & review enforcement We call the Government to review and look into reforming Child Maintenance Service (CMS). We believe the current payment system does not reflect the true cost of raising children, especially in the current cost of living crisis.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Condemn human rights violations in Pakistan and consider how to support victims There are serious concerns about human rights violations and political persecution in Pakistan. We want the Government to condemn this, and to consider what they could do to help victims.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Ban sunbed use due to health risks + the large cost to the NHS from skin cancers Ban sunbeds outright due to the high risk of health risks and the cost that skin cancers and related health complications cost the NHS in which sunbeds are a major contributor.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Review access to Hormone Replacement Therapy for Transgender Youth I want Government to review access to Hormone Replacement Therapy for young transgender people. I want HRT to be easier to access, because of the mental health effects that people can face when they don’t receive gender affirming care.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund routine breast screening invitations to women beyond the age of 71 Women stop receiving 3 yearly invitations for breast screening at the age of 71. We believe most are not aware that they can still request a 3 yearly breast screen from their GP.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Rescind the Discharge of Local Planning Authority Functions Regulations 2026 The draft Town and Country Planning (Discharge of Local Planning Authority Functions) (England) Regulations 2026 remove the ability for district councillors in planning committees to give input on almost all planning applications.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Make consent training mandatory at all universities The OfS found that 1 in 7 students experience sexual assault, with over half occurring in university settings. We believe consent training should not be optional and the Government needs to make it a legal requirement for universities to provide consent training to every student.
label: Department for Education

text: Hold a referendum regarding UK withdrawal from the 1951 Refugee Convention  To combat false and unwarranted bogus asylum applications which we believe make up a significant proportion of all current applications, give the British public a referendum on withdrawal from this treaty which we think is outdated and flawed & only benefits nations other than the British public.
label: Home Office

text: Universal basic electricity allowance for all households, with usage thresholds Set into law that all households be given free, basic electricity allowances, eg 4kWh daily, funded by energy companies through a series of energy use thresholds, where cost per kWh increases (for electricity, oil & gas). Capped for households with high energy use for legitimate health reasons.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Make any sexual contact with an animal a criminal offence We think the government should recognise gap in current law regarding bestiality and change it. They should make it law that any sexual act with an animal is illegal.
label: Home Office

text: Ban parents from using their children to create social media content We want the government to bring in legislation to protect children used by parents for content creation. We think this could protect them from abuse, exploitation and exposure to paedophiles.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Legalise the picking, buying, selling and consumption of psilocybin Mushrooms To legalise mushrooms that contain psilocybin which we believe have great opportunities for mental health treatment and are fun and life changing.
label: Home Office

text: Ban all ticket touting and reselling of tickets for higher prices I want the government to crack down on concert and sports ticket touting. I think it's disgusting to rip off fans who genuinely love the enjoyment of going to a concert or sports event. I believe the government should bring in tougher laws and protections for fans.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Ban the use of audible propane bird scarers We think audible propane bird scarers, known as gas gun bird scarers, should be banned due to their disruptive nature. While used by farmers to scare birds away, we feel they cause significant noise pollution, disturbing residents, animals, and passers by.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require people over 70 have a compulsory eye tests every 2 years to drive We want the government to introduce legislation to require all people over 70 to have a compulsory eye test every 2 years. We want it to be made mandatory for GP’s or Opticians to notify DVLA if a person’s eyesight does not meet the minimum requirements to drive a car.
label: Department for Transport

text: Remove VAT from pet veterinarian bills Many pets and pet owners suffer from not being able to afford simple medical care. In a nation that has a state-funded, free to use, national health service, I think it is immoral to tax medical treatment for animals. Please remove VAT from vets bills.
label: HM Treasury

text: Cap car insurance prices I believe there should be a cap on how much companies can charge on car insurance.
label: Department for Transport

text: Ban the sale of caged birds. Please support a ban on the sale of caged birds. We think confining birds in small cages ignores their need for space, social interaction, and freedom to fly, harming their welfare. Let’s end this outdated practice and prioritize the humane treatment of animals.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require taxi & rideshare apps to disclose if a vehicle is wheelchair accessible Require taxi and ride-hailing transportation services to display a clear 'Disabled Taxi' option to allow users to request a wheelchair accessible vehicle if one is available.
label: Department for Transport

text:
Extend Working Time Regulations to contracted freelance workers Mandate that freelance contracts must abide by the following Working Time Regulations:

• Maximum of 48 hours/week
• Right to rest
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Require labelling of natural rubber latex used in food packaging Require clear labelling where natural rubber latex is used in food packaging materials, including packaging seals and cold-seal adhesives, so consumers with severe latex allergy can make informed choices.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require Directors be responsible for and minimise company’s environmental impact We call on the Government to amend the Companies Act 2006 to require the Director to not just promote the success of the company and have “regard to” the company’s impact on the environment, but to mandate that the Director must demonstrably, in all decisions, minimise impact on the environment.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Formal recognition of climate-displaced people within the asylum system Amend immigration and asylum law to establish a clear legal status for people displaced by climate change, provide access to protection comparable to refugee status, and create defined humanitarian pathways and resettlement schemes for climate-displaced people.
label: Home Office

text: Suspend Council Tax collection in areas with delays to Local Elections Local elections delayed in some UK areas leave councils operating without a renewed mandate. Residents should not be required to pay council tax to a council past its elected term. Government must suspend council tax collections in areas where elections are postponed & reinstate once a vote is held.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Tv-licence holders to be able to demand refund We call on legislation to be introduced to enable tv license payers to be able to demand a 50% refund if the BBC is found to have breached its Charter and not provided an on-air public apology.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Suspend all immigration for one year and review current laws and policies Suspend all immigration for one year. Review current laws and policies to work on a comprehensive plan to reduce immigration and repatriate illegal migrants.
label: Home Office

text: Require all children’s play centres to provide two dedicated SEN sessions a week We want the government to require all children’s play centres to provide at least two dedicated SEN sessions per week — one on a weekday and one at the weekend. We want them to be held at reasonable, accessible times to support neurodivergent children and their families.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Provide funding to make all asthma-related medication free on prescription We call on the Government to provide funding to make all medication related to asthma free of charge on prescription. This would include inhalers, pacers, and breathing treatments.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Make it illegal across the country to park on and obstruct the pavement. We want the government to make it illegal and fine cars or vans that are parked on and obstruct a pavement.
label: Department for Transport

text: Create a SEND access fund within the Every Child Can enrichment programme We call on the Government to create a dedicated SEND access support fund within Every Child Can & related enrichment programmes. This fund should be available to eligible community organisations & children’s activity providers when a child with SEND needs additional adult support to participate.
label: Department for Education

text: Ban public use of fireworks on New Year’s Eve & promote quieter alternatives We ask the Government to ban the use of fireworks by members of the public on New Year’s Eve, and to promote safer, quieter alternatives for celebrations, such as professionally organised drone light displays accompanied by music.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Ban spikes on residential shared fences for the safety of wildlife and pets Ban spikes on residential boundary fences.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Require employers to provide retail security staff with stab-proof vests We want the Government to require all retail employers to provide in-house security staff with stab-proof protective vests, as part of their duty of care under the Health and Safety at Work Act, to help reduce injuries and improve safety in stores.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Review timing of child contact centre referrals at family court Review the need for early intervention through contact centres at the point when court applications are made. We think this could help ensure children maintain relationships with both parents while legal processes are ongoing.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban ROTL & early release for offences related to death of a child We want the Government to legislate to ban the early release and Release on Temporary Licence (ROTL) of anyone convicted of child cruelty in cases where a child has died, causing or allowing the death of a child, or manslaughter where the victim is a child.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Declare a one-off bank holiday if England win the World Cup We call on the Government to declare a one-off national bank holiday on the Monday immediately following the World Cup Final, should the England Men’s Football Team win the tournament.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Make St George’s Day a national bank holiday in England every year Make St George’s Day (23 April) a national bank holiday in England each year, recognising England’s patron saint and bringing England in line with other UK nations that already have national day public holidays.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Cut Fuel Duty by 20p per Litre to Reduce the Cost of Living. We call on the UK Government to cut fuel duty by 20p per litre to ease the cost of living. Lower fuel prices would reduce everyday costs, support workers who rely on driving, and help bring down prices across the wider economy while still earning estimated £20bn in tax revenue.
label: HM Treasury

text: Enshrine in Law Access to Hormone Replacement Therapy for Transgender Adults It has been reported that NHS England is to lead a review into the ‘effectiveness’ of medications for Trans adults. The Government should commit to enshrining the right to medical care for Trans Adults in line with the scientific research that supports Transition.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review evidential threshold in emotional and financial domestic abuse cases In our view, prosecutors too often rely on visible injury or direct financial control when considering whether the evidential threshold has been met in domestic abuse cases. We therefore ask for a review of the statutory guidance on the evidential threshold in domestic abuse cases.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Nationalise public utilities & set up a committee of the public to oversee them Nationalise the country’s utility supply infrastructure. Bring under governmental control the infrastructure of providing and distributing water, power and connectivity services. Consider a rotational committee of residents, akin to jury service, to oversee national services outside of politics.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Ban factories from producing single use plastic bottles for still drinks Ban factories from producing plastic bottles with still drinks in them and instead use recyclable cartons.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Change the law to allow under 16's to be recognised as victims of domestic abuse We want the government to amend the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 so children under 16 who experience abuse at the hands of a parent or partner can be legally recognised as victims of domestic abuse. Every child affected deserves to be heard, protected, and supported in law and through services.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Redirect weekly Asylum Support Spending to Pensioners & Disabled People We urge Parliament to reduce spending on asylum hotels housing, legal aid, and administration, and to redirect this funding to support pensioners and disabled citizens, to improve welfare & address urgent social care needs across the UK.
label: HM Treasury

text: Ban labels from saying "may contain" regarding allergens The government should require food manufacturers to clearly declare whether their products contain peanuts and other common triggers of anaphylactic reactions. This bill should ban the vague phrase “may contain…”, which we think puts lives at risk.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Review funding for our police services I believe a review of police funding is crucial as funding impacts public safety, community trust and resource allocation. I think a review could help ensure a balance between effective law enforcement and addressing social issues, fostering transparency and accountability while shaping policies.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Require e-bike riders to be licensed & regulated like mopeds We call for e-bike riders to be required to hold a valid license in the same way as moped and light motorcycle drivers. We also call for e-bike riders to be treated equally to moped drivers for road offences under the Road Traffic Acts.
label: Department for Transport

text: Implement regular checks on the legal status of all visa holders in the UK. We call on the Government to establish a system for conducting regular checks on UK visa holders to ensure they maintain their legal status and comply with UK immigration law. We think this should include periodic assessments to verify ongoing eligibility and adherence to immigration regulations.
label: Home Office

text: Review handling of complaints by public bodies and their transparency levels We call on the UK Government to thoroughly review complaint-handling practices within public bodies and introduce stronger enforceable safeguards to ensure transparency, accountability, and proper record-keeping.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Review and reduce the proposed £2.20 per 10ml Vaping Products Duty I want the Government to review and reduce the proposed £2.20 per 10ml vaping duty. I believe this level is excessive, could raise prices sharply, harm small businesses, and risk pushing people back to smoking or unsafe black-market products.
label: HM Treasury

text: Make abortion and bodily autonomy a legal right Abortion is still regulated by law, not protected as a right. Every woman and pregnant person deserves the freedom to make decisions about their own body — free from interference.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund the construction of more detention centres for illegal migrants We would like illegal migration to be solved, and we believe the only way it can be solved is by deporting all illegal migrants. In the meantime, we urge the Government to fund building more detention centres in old military barracks or empty buildings that are far away from towns and cities.
label: Home Office

text: Make it a specific criminal offence to lie about being bitten by a dog When people falsely accuse dogs of biting them dogs could be wrongly seized or even killed. This puts strain on dog owners, police and tax payers.
label: Home Office

text: Review and reform education system based on Finland's to improve accessibility I want the government to review, learn from and adapt principles and pedagogy from Finland's education system to reform our own. Remove standardised tests until age 16, relax the curriculum for more flexibility for individual schools and teachers, limit homework, increase play and exploration time.
label: Department for Education

text: Introduce mandatory anti-bullying programmes in schools I urge the Government to introduce mandatory anti-bullying education programmes in schools. These programmes should promote awareness, provide support, and create safe environments for students, helping them understand the importance of kindness and tackling bullying.
label: Department for Education

text: Review law around consent and disclosing sex or trans identity We believe the law needs reviewing regarding consent in rape cases & disclosing birth sex. We are concerned that there could be insufficient protections against criminalisation for trans &  non-binary people who are questioning their gender & are not ready to have a conversation about their gender.
label: Home Office

text: Reduce time & improve conditions for guinea-pigs in quarantine after entering UK We urge the Government to revise guinea-pig quarantine from non-EU countries, reducing it from 4 months to 1 due to low rabies risk. We also request indoor facilities with proper hideaways to ensure their comfort and well-being, as current conditions can cause stress and health issues.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Government to urge Israel to withdraw from Lebanon  We call on the UK Government to urge Israel to withdraw from Lebanon, stop occupying Palestinian land, and respect the rights of Lebanese and Palestinians.  We believe this would ensure justice, peace, and recognition of their biblical heritage.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Set minimum MP attendance requirements and automatic by-election if not met Introduce a minimum level of attendance of an MP in the House. In our view, this is the role they were elected to perform by their constituents, and therefore a minimum attendance level should be required. If levels fall, the constituents should be able to remove them as an MP through a by-election.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Improve accessibility of nightlife venues for disabled people We call on the Government to tackle accessibility barriers within nightlife venues and to propose measures that promote consistent, meaningful accessibility practices across the sector.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Reduce school to 4 days a week and have optional extra activities Reduce the school week to 4 days. Have optional extra-curricular activities at the end of the day to help children with exams. Students with disabilities could have optional clubs on the day off to build skills that could benefit their education.
label: Department for Education

text: Allow the Commissioner for Standards to investigate MPs' constituent casework The Procedural Protocol in respect of the Code of Conduct for MPs should be amended to allow the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards to investigate MPs' dealings with their constituents.
label: Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

text: Ban the use of prong dog collars I would like the Government to take action on the use of prong dog collars by introducing a ban and issuing fines to those who use them. We also think dogs should be taken away from their owners if they repeatedly offend.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Introduce Albanian GCSE and A-levels We ask the Government to introduce GCSE and A-Level qualifications in the Albanian language. Many children attend Albanian supplementary schools and would benefit from a nationally recognised qualification in their mother tongue.
label: Department for Education

text: Fund community-led mental health services and preventative care Fund community-led mental health services, supporting people and their families to have autonomy over their own care. We believe that funding community initiatives can help prevent the systemic failures that lead to mental health issues.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Ensure Equal Access to NHS Fertility Treatment for Same-Sex Couples Establish national NHS standards to ensure same-sex couples can access funded fertility treatment without the burden of self-funded IUI cycles. We call for an end to the postcode lottery, a review of eligibility for those with existing children, and expanded access to options like reciprocal IVF.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Do not introduce licensing for gamebird shooting We think sustainable game shooting is making a major contribution to nature recovery and rural livelihoods across the UK.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Give people a vote of confidence in their MP 18 months after a general election Give people a vote of confidence in their MP 18 months after a general election. If fewer than 326 MPs from the governing party/parties win their confidence votes then a general election should be held in six months’ time.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Require Disclosure of All Pesticide Residues and Processing Aids on Food Labels All residues and processing aids used at any stage of the food production and supply chain must be clearly and fully disclosed to consumers on product labelling, including the amount of agents used during farming, processing, preservation, or packaging that remain in or on the final food product.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Fund free bus passes for all carers of disabled people Amend the English National Concessionary Travel Scheme, Transport Act 2000 and relevant legislation, and fund mandatory free bus passes for all carers of disabled people. There are disabled people who cannot travel without their carers and we think carers should be able to travel with them for free.
label: Department for Transport

text: Shut down the UK Government and Parliament Petitions system Stop funding the UK Government and Parliament e-petitions system and shut it down. We believe it's a waste of taxpayer money, that it consistently ignores public feedback, and that it enacts not enough real change. Shut it down.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Remove Sugary Foods from School Menus in England to Promote Children's Health. We urge the Government to amend the School Food Standards to remove high-sugar items like puddings, jellies, and cakes from school menus and offer nutritious alternatives such as fresh fruit, yoghurt, or low-sugar options instead.
label: Department for Education

text: Ban indoor fireworks, sparklers and pyrotechnics in public venues We are concerned with the safety of fireworks, sparklers and pyrotechnics in public venues following recent mass casualty events in Europe. We would like to see tighter regulation and ban on indoor fireworks, sparklers and pyrotechnics.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Prohibit restaurants from including tips on bills Prohibit restaurants adding tips or “service charges” to bills, even if they are optional.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Review SATs and GCSEs to reduce exam reliance and increase inclusive assessment. We think high-stakes exams affect children’s mental health and disadvantages many pupils, especially those with SEND, and negatively impact attendance and inclusion. A review is needed. More project-based and continuous assessment could create a fairer system where all children thrive and succeed.
label: Department for Education

text:
Improve safety for E-Bikes and E-Scooters to reduce injuries • Make helmets mandatory
• Introduce drink/drug limits, with enforceable testing powers
• Raise minimum age FOR USE to 18
• Cap rental e-bike/scooter speeds at 12 mph nationwide
• Require safety inspections and minimum maintenance standards
• Strengthen penalties against dangerous riding
label: Department for Transport

text: Keep the 5-year Indefinite Leave to Remain ILR for ex-Gurkhas & their families We want the UK Government to keep the current 5-year Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) pathway, for ex-Gurkhas who left the armed forces post 1997, their spouses, and family members. Gurkhas have served Britain with loyalty and deserve fairness, stability, and respect for past commitments.
label: Home Office

text: Amend Prison Rules to give a statutory minimum of 2 hours daily out-of-cell time Amend the Prison Rules to require that every prisoner is guaranteed a minimum of two hours out-of-cell time each day.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Make it illegal for a child to be left home alone before a specific age We want the government to make it illegal for a child to be left home alone before a specific, appropriate age and consequences for parents found breaking the law. Currently the law does not say a specific age when a child can be left on their own.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Improve regulation of letting agents including new statutory regulator We believe there is an urgent need for better regulation of letting agents. We think the current system is broken, and that it seems to protect system abusers, not victims.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Establish an Independent Inquiry into alleged Sexual Abuse in the Armed Forces We think the government should set up an independent inquiry into allegations of sexual abuse in the Armed Forces.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Introduce mandatory extreme-weather safety protections for delivery workers Introduce mandatory national extreme-weather safety standards for delivery workers, including severe-weather risk assessments, temperature monitoring inside delivery vehicles, reduced workloads and clear rules to modify or suspend outdoor deliveries when conditions become unsafe.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Remove the need for planning permission for external shutters on properties If residential properties could install wooden external shutters covering windows and doors, without planning permission, it would remove the need for expensive aircon units, cooling houses in heat waves but also help warm houses in the winter.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Introduce a Mental Health Duty Law Introduce a Mental Health Duty requiring institutions with power over people's lives such as workplaces, schools, healthcare, housing, justice & public services to proactively protect mental health. Require inspections, ratings & real consequences for non-compliance. Don't wait for people to break.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Make students studying less than 35 hours a week eligible for carers allowance The DWP states that anybody in “full time” education, even if they only attend classes 2-3 days a week, is not eligible to receive carer's allowance. We believe this is unsustainable. Anyone attending classes for less than 35 hours a week (equivalent to a full-time job) should be eligible.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Scrap Payments on Account and increase self-employed personal allowance to £20k Self-employed create jobs & drive growth, and we think the Payments on Account would be better invested in businesses. If we are late to pay it we pay interest, which we think is unfair! We call on the Government to scrap it and to raise the Personal Allowance to £20k for self-employed.
label: HM Treasury

text:
Release unredacted medical records to Nuclear Test Veterans. The MOD should release, without redactions, medical records relating to nuclear test veterans.
This government should formally acknowledge and apologise for any effect nuclear radiation has had on the people who took part in experiments and their children and grandchildren.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: More funding to strengthen youth homelessness prevention methods We call on the government to increase funding to support young care leavers.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund wheelchairs and changing places facilities for beaches We would like the government to fund better basic disabled facilities for beaches. By that we mean at least one beach wheelchair and a changing places toilet along with it. We have found some beaches have one or the other but a lot of disabled people need both.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text:
Levy Water Companies to Fund Year-Round Water Testing to Safeguard Public Health Year-round, real-time water quality testing for all UK rivers, lakes, and seas.
Levy Polluting water companies to fund improved testing infrastructure, monitoring, and public alerts (“polluter pays” principle).
Enhance public health protections.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Fund free bus travel and increase rail fare discounts for those 22 and under We want the Government to introduce free bus travel for all young people aged 22 and under, and to increase the rail discount available to this age group. We do not think that the £3 cap on bus fare cap is enough. We think it prices out many young people.
label: Department for Transport

text: Prevent Sex Offenders from Applying for Removal from the Sex Offenders Register In July 2012, the Sexual Offences Act 2003 was amended to allow certain convicted sex offenders to apply for removal from the Sex Offenders Register 15 years after release. I respectfully urge this amendment be repealed to protect the public.
label: Ministry of Justice

text:
Grace period for UK Tax Residents to Report Worldwide Income and Assets Requesting the Government to create a short-term grace period for UK tax residents to report worldwide income and assets without penalties.
We think HMRC should provide clear guidance and support to help people comply and avoid unexpected tax bills.
label: HM Treasury

text: Place a ban on party whips in Parliament Parliament should ban party whips in the House of Commons.
label: Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

text: Review police pursuit rules to ensure proportionality and safety We believe police pursuits can pose high risks of serious injury/death to drivers, passengers bystanders. One of the duties of the police is to prioritise the preservation of life. A review should investigate whether rules on police pursuits reflect this duty of care and commitment to public safety.
label: Home Office

text: Allow people with Coeliac Disease into the UK Armed Forces Anyone suffering with a gluten intolerance cannot join the UK armed forces. However, the Army, Royal Navy and RAF cater for those requiring Halal, Kosher and Vegetarian meals. We see this as discrimination against those with a food intolerance which can be managed and not life threatening.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: Ban water company shareholder dividend payments if they pollute in dry weather Water companies should be banned from paying dividends to their shareholders when they report that they're discharging untreated sewage, either raw or diluted, into the environment during normal rainfall as defined by the World Meteorological Office.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Extend the Driving Theory Test Expiry date We believe learner drivers are being penalised having to retake their driving theory test due to long waiting times for practical Driving Tests. The Government needs to extend the 2-year rule, or consider abolishing the expiry altogether.
label: Department for Transport

text: Fund free female sanitary products in Public Restrooms We urge the Government to provide funding so that all female sanitary products are free and accessible in public restrooms.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Require registration and regulation of all private domiciliary carers in England We ask the Government to require all English domiciliary carers to undergo mandatory registration, enhanced DBS checks & minimum training requirements. English private carers are not currently required to register with a regulatory body, undergo enhanced DBS checks or meet minimum training standards
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Increase funding for mental health services for the LGBT+Q community We think more money for mental health services in the LGBT+Q community-is needed right now. We are worried that suicide rates may be rising fast in our community.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Fund and Improve Mental Health Service transition into the Community Fund an improved mental health service enabling a seamless transition from acute crisis care (Home Treatment/Rapid Response) and community support. Establish a statutory "Continuity of Care" guarantee with a safety/care plan before a patient is discharged from intensive services.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text:
Fund more support for student midwives We want the government to increase financial support for student midwives. 
 
We also want student midwives to have:
 
- Access to free childcare initiatives
- Exemption from hospital car parking costs
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Introduce a mandatory driving test for moped/small motorcycle users I urge the government to require all moped and small motorcycle users to pass a mandatory practical and theory driving test before they can ride on a public road to ensure that all road users possess the necessary knowledge and skills to drive safely and responsibly.
label: Department for Transport

text: Declare a state of emergency to prioritise climate action We believe that climate change poses an urgent and unprecedented threat to the UK's environment, economy, and public health. Rising temperatures, extreme weather events, and loss of biodiversity are already affecting our communities, and vulnerable groups can face the greatest risks.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Fund ADHD/Autism Burnout Support in all GP Surgeries Before and After Diagnosis Fund support for ADHD and autistic burnout so it’s available through GP surgeries for people both before and after diagnosis. Many people struggle to understand and manage their symptoms, including overwhelm, exhaustion, brain fog, emotional difficulties, and loss of everyday functioning.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Provide Government funding, resource grant & guidance for home-schooled children We are asking for the government to introduce financial and resource grants for families who choose elective home education for their children. Currently, many parents do not have support, nor direction on where to start with home-schooling alongside carrying the full financial burden.
label: Department for Education

text: Review current sentencing guidelines and immigration laws Review sentencing guidelines and immigration laws to ensure the victims’ role in sentencing is strengthened & sentences given based on crime committed and not personal background. We want the Government to ensure serious foreign offenders are able to be deported promptly after serving their sentence
label: Home Office

text: Reform the Mental Health Act to remove the detention of autistic people The Government has promised to reform the Mental Health Act; we feel they have failed to do so. Meanwhile, autistic people have been forcibly detained and may spend years in unnecessary restraints, over medicated and isolated. We want the Government to release them into residential homes.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Recall the mayor of London mid-term: amend the GLA to include recall provisions Amend the Greater London Authority Act of 1999 to include recall provisions so that if a certain % of London voters decide to enact a recall - a new election is held.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Require NHS hospitals to provide discharge support for sepsis survivors We want the Government to require NHS hospitals to provide mandatory, standardised discharge support for patients recovering from sepsis, including written information, follow-up guidance, red flags for post-sepsis syndrome and access to rehabilitation and mental health support services.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Evacuate 50 Gazan children with complex trauma injuries to the UK Nearly 4,000 children are in need of medical evacuation from Gaza. We are asking only for 50 children with life-threatening conditions to be medically evacuated to the UK for medical treatment.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Introduce a healthcare worker tax relief scheme for NHS and supporting staff. Introduce a tax relief scheme for NHS healthcare workers and private staff supporting NHS services, including higher tax-free allowances, reduced National Insurance, and tax-free overtime to improve retention, recruitment and morale.
label: HM Treasury

text: Increase the personal tax allowance for single adult households to £15,000 Revise the tax free allowance for single adult households increasing from £12,570 to £15,000.
label: HM Treasury

text: Make conflict of interest a criminal offence for MPs and Peers Make it a law that any MP or member of the house of lords should not have a conflict of interest in any law, guideline or deal to be presented to the government. They should not have any links to businesses that will profit from new contracts from the above mentioned including company shares.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Let the NHS Recruit Australian & NZ Specialists: Cross-Recognise Qualifications The NHS is short 7,000+ medical staff and 52% of advertised vacancies go unfilled, mostly for lack of applicants. Many specialists want to come to the UK from Aust and NZ but they currently face a very difficult and costly 4+ year approval process.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Grant Malaysian Driving Licence Conversion We urge the Department for Transport to allow direct conversion of Malaysian driving licences.
label: Department for Transport

text: Ban balaclavas to prevent crime I want the government to totally ban balaclavas. I do not think there is any need for them because we do not have arctic conditions in this country. Stop people from selling them and arrest and fine people who are found wearing them.
label: Home Office

text: Stronger Product Safety & Copyright protection on Non-UK E-Commerce Platforms Introduce laws requiring overseas e-commerce platforms selling to UK consumers to meet all UK safety standards, remove unsafe or copyright-infringing products quickly and face penalties for non-compliance. Strengthen enforcement of such laws to help protect consumers, small businesses and creators.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Any crime involving a knife to get a minimum 10 year custodial sentence Young people, in particular, are often both victims and perpetrators of knife crime. We think this highlights the urgent need for targeted interventions. We think the emotional and societal costs of knife crime are profound, affecting families, communities, and the fabric of our society.
label: Home Office

text: Require VED Expensive Car Supplement threshold to be uprated with inflation Require the £40,000 Vehicle Excise Duty Expensive Car Supplement (ECS) threshold to be uprated annually in line with inflation and apply the uprated threshold to hybrid as well as electric vehicles. £30–32k in 2017 is very often £40k+ today, without being higher spec or more luxurious in real terms.
label: HM Treasury

text: Reverse the visa brake on student visa applications from Afghan nationals Reverse the visa brake on Afghan student visa applications. In 2025, only 277 Afghan students received UK visas, 0.07% of all student visas. This is not an unsustainable crisis. We ask the Government to restore fair, safe educational pathways for students fleeing Taliban rule.
label: Department for Education

text: Make voting compulsory in the UK 55% of the electorate did not vote in the last general election in the Blackpool South Constituency.
label: Cabinet Office

text:
Make public inquiry recommendations legally enforceable Amend the Inquiries Act 2005 to:
– Require formal government responses to inquiry recommendations within 12 months
– Legally mandate implementation plans
– Establish independent oversight to monitor progress and ensure meaningful accountability
label: Cabinet Office

text: Require local authorities to fast track Blue Badges for seriously ill children Require local authorities to fast track the application process for Blue Badges for children diagnosed with cancer and other serious illnesses. Consider allowing medical professionals to confirm eligibility so that families could receive temporary or emergency badges without delays.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Negotiate with EU to end the 90 day limit on staying in Schengen area countries We want the government to negotiate with EU to end the 90 day limit on staying in Schengen area countries without a visa. We think this rule detrimentally affects many people as well as and the relationship between UK and EU.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Extend the Skilled Worker visa grace period from 60 days to 12 months The 60-day grace period can be too short to find new sponsored work. Recruitment and sponsorship often take months, some employers may wait until after probation. Extending it to 12 months could reduce hardship, protect children's education and help retain skilled workers who contribute to the UK
label: Home Office

text: Mandatory safeguarding alerts for repeat injuries in children under 10 Government to mandate an NHS-wide alert if a child under 10 presents twice in 12 months with suspicious or non-age-appropriate injuries. This alert should trigger an immediate independent skin check and the alert should remain visible to all GPs and hospitals, regardless of where the child is seen.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Amend adoption/kinship care laws to protect privacy rights of adult adoptees Amend the Children Act 1989 and adoption guidance to explicitly state that local authorities cannot contact or assess an adopted person to act as a kinship carer for a biological sibling they have no prior relationship with unless the adoptee has explicitly opted into a contact register.
label: Department for Education

text: Raise SEND funding by £10 billion & stop all new SEND reforms Every SEN child has a right to a fair education and the right the support, and we are concerned that if funding is not increased and if the new government reforms are introduced, this won’t happen.
label: Department for Education

text: Review decision to end the ECO scheme, assess the economic and social impact Review and pause the planned ending of the ECO scheme until a full impact assessment is completed, including effects on employment, industry capacity, fuel poverty and delivery of net-zero targets.
label: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

text: Allow Skilled Worker visa holders to work up to 40 hours in secondary employment Allow all Skilled Worker and Health Care visa holders to legally work up to 40 hours per week in secondary employment. This will support essential sectors, reduce staff shortages, and increase tax revenue for the UK
label: Home Office

text: Amend law to allow advertisement of cancer treatments in clinical trail stage Amend existing legislation to allow the publication of advertisements for cancer treatments that have passed Phase 2 clinical trials. We believe this would give people more choice and more chance to find new treatments not available through the NHS.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Publish detailed regular account of all public spending on asylum seeker support The government must publish frequent, up-to-date, full accounts of all taxpayer funds spent on asylum seekers, including accommodation, goods, services, subsistence payments, all other related expenses, and details of specific goods purchased.
label: Home Office

text: Require election & manifesto pledges to be implemented and legally enforced We think any promises or gestures made to obtain voters during an election run-up including in the party manifesto, to have to be acted on and upheld / made law once in power. So no U turns can be made when in power, which would lead to the acting government / individuals to be removed from power.
label: Cabinet Office

text:
Grant asylum to White South Africans and provide emergency support We believe the Government should:
1) Recognise the treatment of White South Africans
2) Grant & fast-track asylum for White South Africans, who we consider are facing discrimination & violence
3) Provide emergency support to those affected
4) Push South Africa to do more to protect their rights
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Ban higher car insurance premiums for young and new drivers We want the government to introduce regulations to require car insurance companies to reduce the cost of insurance for new drivers, particularly those under 25, by offering need-based pricing models.
label: Department for Transport

text: Government to provide information about objects flying above US airbases in UK Recently, it was reported that flying objects were making incursions into airspace above US airbases located in the UK, with what I believe appears to be minimal effective deterrence. The UK government must be as transparent as possible with what it knows about these craft.
label: Ministry of Defence

text: We Want Affordable Housing for All. We request for the government to statutorily provide a decent, high standard of affordable housing for everyone. Presently, some people cannot afford housing, as they need to save up deposits and we think the rents are too high.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Require retailers to name the courier service they use Mandate retailers to name the courier service before selling to a consumer so that an informed choice can be made by the consumer. The courier service stated should also be the one making the delivery and it should not be allowed for it to be sub-contracted to another courier service.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Link tax threshold increases for pensioners to the triple lock for pensions We are concerned that the triple lock rise in UK State Pensions could pull those with a small pension into paying tax. We believe that if the triple lock was to rise by, for example, £400 above the tax threshold, that the tax threshold for pensioners should rise by £400.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Mental Health Act to cover severe substance use if life-threatening We call on the Government to amend the Mental Health Act to include severe substance use disorder. Currently, this alone does not meet the threshold for detention. If a person is deemed to have mental capacity, they can refuse treatment even if their addiction is causing life-threatening harm.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Reduce VAT for hospitality from 20% to 13% permanently  Reduce the standard rate of VAT applied to hospitality businesses (including restaurants, cafés, pubs and accommodation) from 20% to 13% on a permanent basis, to reflect the sector’s cost structure and to support business viability following recent fiscal changes.
label: HM Treasury

text: Fund new-born screening and more treatment for MPS Hurler syndrome Improve early diagnosis and access to treatment for children with MPS Hurler syndrome, including clearer referral pathways and new-born screening, so children are not diagnosed too late to benefit from treatment.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Put pressure on Saudi Arabia regarding executions and death penalty We urge the UK Government to use its influence to press Saudi Arabia to end executions for drug-related offences and crimes committed by individuals as children, and to impose a moratorium on the use of the death penalty generally.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Cap cost of prison phone calls to 5p per minute & free weekly allowance I want the Government to make prison phone calls affordable by capping costs at no more than 5p per minute and introducing a free weekly call allowance for all prisoners. Communication is a right, not a privilege — we feel that no one should be priced out of staying connected to loved ones.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Recall of MPs Act to cover MPs excluded from parliamentary estate for 60 Days+ Amend the Recall of MPs Act to trigger a recall petition for any MP banned from the Parliamentary estate and inactive for 60 days without in-person voting or participation in debates, questions, or committees, ensuring constituents can call a by-election.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Government to review NHS agenda for change. I would like the government to review the NHS agenda for change and consider changes to better represent the nursing care delivered today.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Establish a National Freshwater Resilience and Stewardship Strategy Establish a National Freshwater Stewardship and Resilience Strategy including an independent review of water governance, use, allocation, storage and major water users; independent regional catchment networks; and a Citizens' Assembly to support immediate actions and shape long term reforms.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require medicinal (pill) packet producers to provide a recycling scheme for them The recycling of medicinal (pill) packets is costly and difficult to do due to their composition.  If the manufacturers of pill packets were made responsible for recycling used packets, there would be a greater chance of less impact on the environment and/or more sustainable packaging being used.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Require over 65s to retake the hazard perception test every five years I would ask the UK Government to require driving license holders, upon reaching 65 years old, to retake the hazard perception section of the driving theory test. They would then continue to be re-tested every 5 years.
label: Department for Transport

text: Ban MPs & Ministers from using a 'disappearing message' function on work phones In order for complete transparency to the UK taxpayer, and to speed up any possible future police enquiries, all MPs' and Ministers' work phones & other devices should not be allowed to have the 'disappearing messages' feature.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Set Up Statutory Independent Advocates for Bereaved Families Of Homicide Victims Create a statutory right for families of homicide victims to have a state-funded Independent Advocate. They must be independent of police and legally empowered to act as a proxy for complex administration, including CICA claims and IOPC proceedings.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban perpetrators of domestic violence from living in same city as their victims I want people who have been convicted of domestic violence to be banned from the same cities as their victims. They should not be allowed to wander the same streets or live their life as if they’ve done nothing wrong. It should be an automatic ban.
label: Home Office

text: Reject Lords amendment on age checks to the Children’ Wellbeing & Schools Bill The Government should reject the Lords amendment to the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill requiring the Government to introduce "highly effective" age assurance measures to stop under-16s using social media.
label: Department for Education

text: Require tax agents to share liability for errors in tax returns they prepare Introduce legislation so that any person or company preparing and submitting tax returns on behalf of others is jointly liable for penalties, interest, and losses arising from errors caused by their negligence, misrepresentation, or failure to meet professional standards.
label: HM Treasury

text: Replace age verification process set out in Online Safety Act to voucher system We the undersigned wish for the government to change how online age verification is currently handled because we have serious concerns about online security and the potential for fraud as a result of the current implementation requiring websites to do their own checks, often with data sent abroad.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text:
Allow Skilled workers to work unlimited extra hours with other employers Review the rule that skilled workers can only work a maximum of 20 extra hours out of their sponsored employment.
Most skilled migrants aim to maximize their earnings to support their families, but their sponsors may be unable to provide additional work beyond the contracted hours.
label: Home Office

text: Make it illegal for sound to be played on public transport without headphones. Make this behaviour to be classed as anti social behaviour.
label: Department for Transport

text: Tougher Penalties for drivers with loud cars We think there should be tougher penalties for people driving loud cars that are above the legal noise limit.
label: Department for Transport

text: Increase statutory paternity leave from two weeks to four weeks. I want the statutory two weeks of paternity leave to be extended by two weeks, to four weeks.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Ban the removal or felling of ancient trees We would like the Government to ban the removal or felling of all ancient trees. We believe these trees are valuable and precious and we need them now and for future generations. Therefore, they should have full legal protections.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Create a government body dedicated to safeguarding parental rights  Create a new government body which helps safeguard parental rights, including helping fathers, some of whom are paying child maintenance, to see their children.
label: Department for Education

text: Ban all plastic in food and drink packaging Ban plastic packaging.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Oppose revised guidelines on New Medicine Service Subcontracting for Pharmacies We believe that the NMS helps patients newly prescribed medication for long-term conditions by improving understanding, managing side effects, and enhancing adherence. We urge NHS England to reconsider NMS subcontracting in pharmacies, as it improves patient access and supports pharmacists.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Exempt all registered motorcycles from paying Vehicle Excise Duty We urge the Government to exempt all registered motorcycles from paying the Vehicle Excise Duty (VED). We believe accidents are being caused by the state of the roads, including delamination of the road surface but motorcycles don't have the weight to severely damage the roads.
label: Department for Transport

text: Review measures to tackle tax evasion and end offshore tax loopholes We call on the Government to review UK tax evasion laws & close offshore tax loopholes used by the ultra-rich. Increase funding for HMRC's tax evasion unit, enforce 15% global minimum tax, create a public register of offshore holdings & strengthen tax laws to ensure billionaires pay their fair share
label: HM Treasury

text: Require all workplaces to have Neurodiversity Advocates We think that every workplace should be required to have a number of people trained up on neurodiversity, reasonable adjustments, communication, sensory safe spaces and generally just being a voice for someone who may not be able to provide their perspective.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Fund at home smear test kits for females when requested. Outside routine screening, currently you cannot request an at home smear test kit on the NHS. There are reports of this becoming available on the NHS but we think the Government should provide funding so that females can request a yearly test if they want it.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Legislate for the repair of potholes within a time frame in the UK. Set legislation for National Highways and local councils to repair and make safe every pothole found on roads, dual carriageways and motorways, within a specific time frame. This should link to a transparent public national reporting system to track progress and accountability.
label: Department for Transport

text: Make courier service disclosure mandatory in online transactions Every day, countless consumers across the country are frustrated by failed delivery attempts, undelivered packages, or damaged/lost goods. We believe this frustration arises from a lack of transparency during online transactions, specifically about the couriers tasked with delivering our purchases.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Create a primary care scrutiny committee to assess the current GP crisis We call on the government to set up a parliamentary committee for General Practice for urgent cross party analysis.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: National rough sleeping programme: permanent, safe accommodation and support I want the Government to implement a national programme to eliminate rough sleeping by providing permanent, safe accommodation and access to support services for all individuals experiencing. Offer mental health support, addiction recovery services, and employment assistance.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Prohibit recording frontline workers without consent We want the Government to make it illegal to film individuals on the front lines without their consent. We feel this step is vital in protecting frontline workers from exploitation and potential harm resulting from unsolicited recordings.
label: Cabinet Office

text:
Ban smoking and vaping in public spaces Ban smoking and vaping in all public spaces.

Smoking has been proven to have numerous detrimental effects, especially to children.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Protect Free Speech in Public: Amend the Public Order Act 1986 We believe that Section 5 appears to be the go-to legislation for potentially malicious arrest and prosecution. It requires no actual complainant or victim. To make an arrest, police simply have to believe that someone (incl. themselves) could be caused harassment, alarm or distress by words spoken.
label: Home Office

text: Fund free school meals for all children up to the age of 16 The cost of food is rising daily and many families are struggling. We believe this can be addressed by giving all children up to the age of 16 free school meals. Families will save at least £199 a year per child per year & this would help with the cost of living crisis. Help support all families!
label: Department for Education

text: Disability Confident must prove outcomes or employers lose the badge Require an independent audit of disabled workforce representation, retention, and progression as a condition of retaining Disability Confident accreditation, with status revoked where unmet. Require DWP to report audit outcomes to Parliament. Embed both in the Disability Confident scheme overhaul.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Require the NHS to offer full body (head to toe) MRI scans for cancer patients My dad developed kidney cancer during lockdown. After having his left kidney removed, we were told that chemotherapy wouldn’t be needed because the cancer was to be gone with the kidney. Just a few weeks later, nodules were found on his lungs. He collapsed and we found it had spread to the brain.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Repeal the Internal Markets Act 2020. We call on the UK Government to repeal the Internal Markets Act 2020, because we think it undermines devolution and the ability of the Scottish Government, Senedd Cymru and the Northern Ireland Assembly to legislate effectively in their devolved areas.
label: Cabinet Office

text: Fund all payment fees for EpiPens and asthma inhalers Fund all payment fees for EpiPens and asthma inhalers to make them free of charge. These medicines are critical for managing life-threatening conditions and are required for immediate emergency treatment. We believe it is unreasonable for such essential medication to come at a cost.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Detain all illegal migrants in military barracks until they are assessed Require all illegal migrants to be detained and confined to military barracks until they have been assessed, as we believe this is paramount to keeping the British people safe.
label: Home Office

text:
Urge the UK Government to support peace and aid for Sudan We call on the UK Government to take urgent action to help bring peace and deliver humanitarian aid to Sudan.
Millions of people are suffering as the conflict continues, with many displaced, injured, or facing starvation.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text:
Protect & reinstate funding for arts & humanities in higher & further education Reverse funding cuts to arts and humanities subjects in higher and further education.
Increase funding to protect art schools and creative courses from closure.
label: Department for Education

text: Cancel the UK-India Free Trade Agreement due to Indian purchases of Russian oil We urge the UK Government to cancel the UK-India Free Trade Agreement as punishment for India buying Russian oil, which we believe is helping fund Russia’s war against Ukraine. We believe the FTA should only be renewed if India halts all purchases of Russian oil.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Include asexuality as a protected characteristic in the Equality Act 2010 Include asexuality in the Equality Act 2010 to prevent discrimination
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Require all elected public officials have a clean enhanced DBS prior to start We think we need to restore faith in politics, both locally and nationally. Nurses, teachers, doctors, carers; each require enhanced criminal background checks to enable them to help people. We think that these standards should also apply to elected officials.
label: Home Office

text: Require employers to notify unsuccessful job candidates and give feedback Implement a law where if someone applies for a job and they are not successful, the applicant is notified of this by the prospective employer with relevant feedback.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Cap tuition fees at £3000 retrospectively & write off the resulting student debt We want the Government to retroactively cap tuition fees at £3,000 for all Plan 2 loans and Plan 5 loans. We call for all balances to be recalculated to this level, with the excess principal and all associated interest cancelled to restore financial fairness to an entire generation.
label: Department for Education

text: Automatic 50/50 custody for separated parents without a criminal conviction Require that separating parents both automatically have equal, 50/50 time with their children, unless a parent has a relevant criminal conviction. We think children need both parents and it would help stop parental alienation, and having parents in a child's life helps them better progress in life.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Ban the use of therapy notes of rape survivors in court proceedings We’re calling for urgent reforms in the criminal justice process for rape survivors especially in the period after victims give video-recorded evidence. We feel that survivors should be able to access therapy without fear it'll be used against them in court. Justice processes must be trauma-informed
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Make misogyny a hate crime. Make it a hate crime for a person to be hateful and prejudiced towards women before we lose more lives.
label: Home Office

text: Make it illegal for the media to shame victims of romance fraud We believe it should be illegal for the media to use victim-shaming language in their headlines and news reports. We think that doing so is secondary victimisation, which includes harassment and discrimination, that the media should be held accountable for.
label: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

text: Ban male chick culling in egg production The UK egg production industry kills millions of male chicks per year by either gassing or maceration.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Allow self-employed single parents to claim childcare as business expense Amend HMRC rules to allow self-employed single parents and self-employed households to deduct registered childcare and holiday club costs as an allowable business expense on their Self Assessment tax returns.
label: HM Treasury

text: Legislate to give funeral processions legal right of way Amend the Road Traffic Act 1988 to protect funeral corteges. Make it an offence to cut into a procession or overtake it in built-up areas, and require drivers to give right of way at roundabouts and junctions to corteges if safe to do so and to advise them refrain from overtaking.
label: Department for Transport

text: Introduce a Statutory Right to Independent Legal Review for Bereaved Families Grant bereaved families the right to an independent judicial review of police and CPS actions following a homicide acquittal. This must apply when clear CCTV evidence exists, forcing a public report detailing why the prosecution failed, ensuring any systemic flaws are exposed.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Abolish 0.5% Stamp Duty Reserve Tax on UK-Listed Equities In order to promote more investment in UK industry by domestic & international investors the government should remove the current 0.5% Stamp Duty Investment Tax on UK listed Equities.
label: HM Treasury

text: Hold a referendum before changing the State Pension Age Hold a referendum before changing the state pension age.
label: Department for Work and Pensions

text: Require political adverts to be truthful & factually accurate Electoral law doesn’t require claims in political campaigns to be truthful or factually accurate. We think this must change to ensure that citizens can trust what they see broadcast, on billboards or in any written media and to prevent falsehoods swaying votes of the British public.
label: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

text: Make it easier to obtain a licence to produce/grow medical cannabis We feel that it is currently extremely difficult to apply for a controlled drugs licence to grow cannabis high in THC for medical use in the UK.
label: Home Office

text: Remove bedroom tax We think the government should remove the bedroom tax because we feel it places an unfair burden on families and individuals. Many people rely on housing benefits to help cover their rent and we think the bedroom tax reduces this support without considering their specific needs.
label: HM Treasury

text: Ban rodent traps that kill or hurt mice and other rodents We want the government to ban mouse or rodent traps that kill or hurt mice or rodents so people use capture and release traps instead. We think that traps that kill or hurt rodents are inhumane.
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Require schools to teach students about knife crime as part of the curriculum We want the government to raise awareness about knife crime and add it to the primary and secondary school curriculums. We think this could help the knife crime rate go down and make children aware so when they grow up they might be less likely to do it.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Increase maximum animal cruelty punishment from five years to eight years We believe that animal cruelty is a huge, growing problem that we think isn’t being addressed as harshly as necessary. Therefore, we think we need to fight for harsher animal cruelty sentences (increased by three years).
label: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

text: Fund free period hygiene products via the NHS for all who need it We think the Government should fund an NHS scheme where individuals should be able to sign up to receive free essential period products each month, as we think access to basic period hygiene should be available to everyone who needs it.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Establish a capacity limit for trains. For Health and Safety we would like a capacity limit bringing in and this not to be left to the train operating companies’ judgment. We believe this could reduce the possibility of injury or fatality from a users experience at the moment in time.
label: Department for Transport

text: Allow under-25s to undergo cervical screening on request I believe individuals should have the ability to discuss their concerns with a healthcare professional and make an informed choice about whether screening is right for them, rather than being restricted solely by age. Due to me losing my dad to cancer I'm extremely scared of getting cancer.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Demand financial compensation from the US & Israel for damage to our economy The US and Israel attacked Iran while US-Iranian negotiations were ongoing. We believe this war of aggression has had widespread global consequences, increased the cost of fuel, and places our economy, security, and way of life at risk. We require compensation for these effects on our country.
label: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

text: Prevent fuel companies increasing prices as soon as oil prices rise. The Government must pass a law that stops fuel companies increasing the forecourt prices as soon as it is mentioned that oil prices are rising. The fuel at the pumps and storage tanks were purchased at a lower price, so we think there is no reason to increase so quickly. This must stop now.
label: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

text: Increase the UK inheritance tax gift allowance in line with the US We call on the UK Government to reform the current inheritance tax gift rules (where only £3,000 is exempt each tax year before the seven-year rule applies)
label: HM Treasury

text: Do not introduce any new taxes or increase any existing taxes We urge the UK Government not to introduce any new taxes or to increase existing taxes. Ordinary citizens are already facing unprecedented financial pressures, yet there are reports that Government continues to seek additional ways to tax incomes, savings, property, fuel, and everyday essentials.
label: HM Treasury

text: Fair Chance Hiring: Make Blind Recruitment Law We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation requiring all employers in the public sector to use blind recruitment at the initial application stage. This means removing names, dates of birth, schools, and other identifying details before shortlisting candidates.
label: Home Office

text: Fund a volunteer force to patrol our borders from illegal immigrants As illegally entering the UK is a criminal offence, we believe citizens have a right to arrest perpetrators where the Police are unable to prevent the offence from taking place.
label: Home Office

text: Introduce whole life tariffs for under 18s who commit murder We call upon the government to change the law so that whole life tariffs can be introduced for murderers who are under 18.
label: Ministry of Justice

text: Require all healthcare environments to be wheelchair accessible To make it a legal requirement for all healthcare facilities to be fully accessible for wheelchair users. We think all MRI facilities should have plastic wheelchairs available, staff should be trained to assist patients with mobility impairments and accessibility protocols should be reviewed.
label: Department of Health and Social Care

text: Review strategy for youth crime & anti-social behaviour, and increase funding We call on the Government to review how to address youth crime and anti-social behaviour to ensure that there are meaningful and immediate consequences for offenders and that prevention, education, and intervention are prioritised. We also urge the Government to increase funding.
label: Home Office
